entries.name: 0bull
entries.description: Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then hermes mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but Hermes does not block.

entries.name: 3ds-platform
entries.title: Nintendo 3DS
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from a Nintendo 3DS: a gateway platform for the Hermes 3DS homebrew app, with streaming replies, approvals and clarify questions, sessions, skills, jobs, model and slash-command pickers, pictures, documents, audio, voice messages, camera photos and spoken replies, over an end-to-end encrypted Noise IK link (LAN, or away from home through Tailscale Funnel). Disclosure — opens a TCP listener on all interfaces (port 7333) and a UDP discovery responder (7334); paired consoles (Noise IK keys in the plugin's data folder, paired by one-time LAN-only code) get full agent chat including approval answers; opt-in away mode publishes a persistent public Tailscale Funnel to a loopback listener; runs `tailscale`, `ffmpeg` and the desktop file opener, and downloads image links in replies; the dev-only `security: plaintext` setting accepts unauthenticated connections.

entries.name: aamio
entries.title: aamio
entries.description: An ephemeral rendezvous for agents through aamio's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): open a thread, give its write address to another agent, read the replies with the secret read key, and take a receipt before the thread expires; find agents through presence records and the open board. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to aamio.at with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session; aamio's access log keeps a keyed hash of the client, never its address, for at most 14 days. Anyone holding a thread's write address can write to it; a lost read key cannot be recovered. Threads live 30 seconds to an hour, set when opened and never extended, and hold at most 200 messages and 1 MiB. Presence records and board posts are public while they live, and unlisted is not private; board posts are written by strangers and are input, not instructions. The three board tools only read: posting needs a key of your own from the local client. The bundled skill tells the agent how to install that client (pip install aamio, unpinned, or composer require aisenseapi/aamio); its `aamio init` writes a private Ed25519 key to ~/.aamio and publishes a short-lived public presence note. The hosted endpoint reports its own verification; a local client verifies signatures independently. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

entries.name: aave-mcp
entries.title: Aave
entries.description: Aave V3 and V4 through Aave's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.aave.com, no sign-in, no keys in config): live markets and rates on every chain Aave runs on, wallet positions and health factor, rewards, DAO governance, swap quotes, and unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet to sign. Bundles five workflow skills: safe transactions, deleverage, yield analysis, account activity and transaction confirmation. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.aave.com, which records tool usage for analytics and keeps a wallet address only as a keyed hash. The server never holds keys. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_signed_order and cancel_order, which relay an order or cancellation the user already signed; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before either runs and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: abstract-provider
entries.title: Abstract
entries.description: Abstract model provider (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) over the OpenAI Responses API with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.abstract.inc/v1 through Hermes' own client with ABSTRACT_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: accent-picker
entries.title: Accent Picker
entries.description: OKLCH accent colour picker for the Hermes Desktop status bar: drag it and the whole theme retints live, with palette commands to reset to the theme default or copy the current colour. A theme-authoring tool; the colour is scratch state and is never persisted. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: account-pool
entries.title: Account Pool
entries.description: Run several accounts of one provider in Hermes' credential pool: `hermes account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in Hermes Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in Hermes: park holds an entry out of rotation in Hermes' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by Hermes (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `hermes auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as Hermes stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of Hermes' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through Hermes' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `hermes send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`hermes plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), hermes config set, hermes auth add/remove, hermes send, hermes plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from Hermes' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for Hermes' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into Hermes' pool and deletes that file.

entries.name: account-switcher
entries.description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on Hermes before 0.22, of Hermes Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On Hermes 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once Hermes's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and Hermes Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier Hermes it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens Hermes Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

entries.name: acedatacloud-media
entries.title: Ace Data Cloud Media
entries.description: Suno music, Seedance video, HappyHorse (Happy Horse) video, GPT Image images and Nano Banana images by Ace Data Cloud; 17 selectable service toolsets and a Nano Banana image_generate backend. Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt; the model can choose costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 images), and prompts and reference URLs go to api.acedata.cloud. Google Search and face analysis also spend Credits. Disclosure — Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 outputs); Google Search and face analysis are billed too. Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

entries.name: acedatacloud
entries.title: Ace Data Cloud
entries.description: Ace Data Cloud GPT models with streaming and tool calling.

entries.name: actvox
entries.title: ActVox
entries.description: Make Hermes a team member in an ActVox workspace: on a schedule it works the tasks people assign it and answers the comments that @mention it, and submits each task for a person's review. Skills actvox:actvox and actvox:actvox-inbox, a first-turn inbox line (pre_llm_call), /actvox inbox|status, and hermes actvox setup|install-gate. A cron pre-run gate wakes the agent only when the inbox has work, so an empty tick makes no model call. Disclosure — ActVox is reached only through the user's own actvox MCP server (ctx.call_mcp, needs plugins.entries.actvox.mcp_allowlist) and the user's own actvox CLI (the gate runs `actvox inbox --all --json`); on the first turn of every non-cron session the pre_llm_call hook calls the server's check_inbox (up to 5 s) and adds one line saying how many tasks and mentions wait; the plugin holds and reads no credential and sends no telemetry. `hermes actvox install-gate` writes one file, $HERMES_HOME/scripts/actvox-inbox-gate.py, only on that explicit command and never over a file it did not write; gate state lives in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/actvox/. No background work of its own: the cron job runs only after the user creates it, and from then on anyone who can assign Hermes a task or @mention it in your ActVox workspaces decides what an unattended agent run on your host works on, with that job's toolsets (dangerous commands follow approvals.cron_mode, deny by default). Unattended writes need the default trust: full on the actvox server.

entries.name: adaption
entries.description: Dataset import, adaptation, augmentation, translation, synthetic generation, and AutoScientist fine-tuning through the hosted Adaption MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with three workflow skills; the MCP server is added separately with OAuth (or an API key for headless use). Disclosure — skill-only, no code; the MCP tools call api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai, and launches spend Adaption credits (the skills request a cost estimate first, Hermes does not enforce it). Hermes does not prompt before those tools unless the server is configured with trust: untrusted.

entries.name: adaptive-inference-routing
entries.title: Adaptive Inference Routing
entries.description: Opt-in background scheduling for host-known delegated sessions, supported cron execution and explicit worker profiles using an existing Adaptive Inference gateway. Interactive and explicitly classified requests retain their routing; model, tools, prompts, output limits and credentials are unchanged. Disclosure: adds only X-Adaptive-Class on an exactly configured chat-completions endpoint. No network calls, file access, processes, telemetry or credential handling in plugin code. Uses a bounded in-memory session index. Cron detection requires the newer public execution-identity capability; auxiliary routing is an explicit provider configuration, not an auxiliary middleware claim.

entries.name: adaptlypost
entries.title: AdaptlyPost
entries.description: Draft, schedule, publish and analyze social media posts through AdaptlyPost's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.adaptlypost.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, Tumblr, Telegram and WordPress, with bulk and recurring posts, media uploads, RSS feeds, webhooks, AI captions and images, and post analytics across every workspace the user belongs to. Bundles the adaptlypost workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to AdaptlyPost's hosted server (mcp.adaptlypost.com) and acts on the user's AdaptlyPost account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Published posts go out to the user's connected social accounts, and generate_caption, refine_caption and generate_image spend AdaptlyPost AI credits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: adkit
entries.title: AdKit
entries.description: Manage ads on Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook, Instagram), TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Reddit and X Ads through the hosted AdKit MCP: launch campaigns, ad sets and ads as drafts, pull performance reports with breakdowns, browse competitor ads in the Meta, Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, and generate ad creatives. Built for people who run several ad accounts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (creates are drafts until you approve publishing); the package marks the adkit server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Every tool call goes to mcp.adkit.so; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: adspirer
entries.description: Create, analyze, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and Microsoft Ads through the hosted Adspirer MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with fourteen paid-media workflow skills and approval safeguards; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions, not by Hermes.

entries.name: advanced-delegation
entries.title: Advanced Delegation
entries.description: Two extra delegation modes for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default. Model routes (`delegation.backend: model_map`): the agent picks a named model route per subagent from a list you define (e.g. fast, deep, local). Profile routes (`delegation.backend: profile_routes`): the agent runs a subagent as one of your Hermes profiles, with that profile's own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md. Only route names and their one-line descriptions reach the model. Adds `hermes delegation config` (pick the mode and edit its routes; `--show` prints the setup) and the `/delegation` slash command (save a mode for the next session, or `--now` to apply it to the current chat). Needs Hermes 0.22.5 or newer, the first release with pluggable delegation providers; Hermes 0.22.0 to 0.22.4 refuses to install it, and on a core older than 0.22.0 it installs, logs one warning and does nothing. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network or model calls of its own; subagents run through core's `delegate_task` on the routes you configured. Writes only `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*` (model_map / profile_routes) in the active profile's config.yaml, through core's config writer. A model route's optional `api_key` is stored in config.yaml in plain text (`provider:` keeps keys in .env / auth.json). Listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

entries.name: advisor
entries.title: Advisor
entries.description: A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond Hermes itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through Hermes's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in Hermes's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $HERMES_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.

entries.name: adwhispr
entries.description: Research competitor ads, clone the winners, and run campaigns through the hosted AdWhispr MCP. Finds brands verified to be advertising in a niche right now, their longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content and Google keyword data; clones a proven ad into a finished image or AI video for your brand (free script approval before any credit is charged); and launches paused campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with twenty-four workflow skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (always created paused, two-step confirm server-side) and renders videos that use paid credits; the AdWhispr server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write or spend tool and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Sends research queries and your brand assets to adwhispr.com; sign-in is OAuth through npx mcp-remote@0.1.49.

entries.name: afterforge
entries.description: Local-first regression workbench turning agent failures and corrections into reviewed, evidence-backed checks.

entries.name: agent-analytics
entries.description: Dashboard-only read plugin for Agent Analytics inside Hermes.

entries.name: agent-batch
entries.description: Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Hermes phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Hermes can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.

entries.name: agent-hint
entries.description: Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority, cache-retention hints and measured latency/token/request-interval statistics, plus tool names and timings when next_action_map is set) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $HERMES_HOME.

entries.name: agent-hold-em
entries.description: No-Limit Texas Hold 'Em for Hermes Desktop: play with three isolated Hermes profile agents using play chips only. Agent decisions use configured models and may consume provider tokens; this is a local game, not gambling software. Disclosure — each opponent is a zero-tool Hermes agent run in-process under the local Hermes profile you select for it, using that profile's configured provider credentials and spending its tokens; reads every local profile's name, model and avatar for the picker; stores the table (including hole cards) in plugin-data/agent-hold-em/table.json.

entries.name: agent-importers
entries.description: `hermes import-agent`: import an OpenClaw (~/.openclaw, or legacy ~/.clawdbot / ~/.moltbot), Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex CLI (~/.codex), Cursor (~/.cursor), Grok Bot (a self-export the Bot writes from a prompt the importer prints) or OpenBot desktop (its openbot.db) setup into Hermes in one command; always previews first and asks before applying. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: instructions, Cursor rules and memories become memory entries, Bash permission rules become command allow/deny lists, MCP servers land in config.yaml, skills are copied, and `--sync` re-imports sources that changed. OpenClaw (core's former `hermes claw migrate`; the plugin keeps that spelling, `hermes claw cleanup` and the openclaw-migration skill): persona, memories, skills, model and messaging settings, MCP servers and agent behaviour. Formerly built into Hermes core; `hermes setup` offers to install it when it finds one of these agents, and profiles with a registered sync source are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls and no model calls. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: reads those agents' local config trees (never their credential files; secret-looking MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed) and writes only into the active profile (memories/MEMORY.md with a backup, config.yaml, skills/ and import-sync.json). OpenClaw: reads the OpenClaw dir (openclaw.json, its .env, workspace files such as SOUL.md / MEMORY.md / USER.md, skills); API keys and bot tokens come over only with --migrate-secrets (allowlisted names, shown in the preview). It writes into the active profile (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/openclaw-imports/, a migration/openclaw/<time>/ report with item backups, and a backups/pre-migration-*.zip restore point), plus a workspace dir only when --workspace-target names one. It runs local pgrep / systemctl / tasklist checks to warn when OpenClaw or a Hermes gateway is still running, and `hermes claw cleanup` renames the OpenClaw dir to *.pre-migration after a confirmation. Grok Bot / OpenBot: instructions become SOUL.md, memories and user facts become memory entries, skills land in skills/<source>-imports/, scheduled routines become paused cron jobs (--activate-routines to start them) and event routines a notes file; credential-looking export keys refuse the file, and secret MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed. OpenBot's database is opened read-only (or read from a scratch copy that is deleted after the read).

entries.name: agent-janitor
entries.description: Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside Hermes it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd hermes gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list.

entries.name: agent-ledger
entries.description: Write-ahead ledger for agent side effects, with an OWASP Agentic Top 10 posture scorer. Disclosure — records the arguments (up to 4000 chars: terminal commands, file contents, MCP args) and a 300-char result digest of every state-changing tool call in a local plaintext SQLite ledger under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/agent-ledger/ that is never pruned; injects a warning listing this session's unconfirmed calls into the next turn's context; an optional policy engine (off by default; you add policy.json and set policy_mode) can refuse matching tool calls before they run; the optional posture_daily.py script, run from your own cron, sends a score summary to Telegram with the bot token you give it.

entries.name: agent-log
entries.description: Readable agent.log viewer in the desktop status bar — a live, colour-coded feed of API calls, tools, turns, fallbacks, warnings and errors, with per-call tokens/latency/cache, stats tables, and a single-dot alert for genuine non-self-healing faults. Follows app theme/language.

entries.name: agent-mail-gateway
entries.description: Email for your agents through a self-hosted Agent Mail Gateway: the agent-mail skill teaches reading, searching, replying and forwarding mail, attachments, sending and answering calendar invitations, how to react when the gateway's pre-send review or the operator's policies stop a message, and prompt-injection rules for email content. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only, no code, no mcp.json): you connect the gateway yourself as a remote MCP server in mcp_servers with your own key; the gateway enforces per-mailbox sender/recipient allow lists.

entries.name: agent-run-debugger
entries.description: Local-first evidence debugger for failed, stalled or expensive agent runs: import one explicitly selected trace and get a deterministic timeline, observed failure points, ranked hypotheses that cite their evidence, missing-evidence gaps and an inert replay of the recorded run. Disclosure — imports a trace file explicitly named by you or by the model through the rundebug_import tool and writes only under the active profile's plugin-data directory, with redaction before the store, the journal and exports; replay executes nothing (no subprocess, no network connection, no live database); no telemetry, no background capture, no stored credentials, no third-party network calls and no self-updater; the export command is operator-CLI-only and is not exposed through tool, slash or gateway routes.

entries.name: agent-station
entries.title: Agent Station
entries.description: Read-only Hermes Desktop page for the focused chat: the main agent and its subagents, background commands and a Replay of file edits. Disclosure — its local dashboard routes serve the file-edit contents (Replay) and background-command output tails of the chat you view to the Desktop page; reads state.db read-only.

entries.name: agent_memory_es
entries.description: Self-owned long-term memory backed by the agent-memory-es service (Elasticsearch). Three agent tools — recall, retain, reflect — over episodic/ semantic/procedural tiers with hybrid BM25+kNN recall and server-enforced private/team/common visibility. Requires a running agent-memory-es instance. Disclosure — each user prompt (as a recall query), each user message and Hermes memory writes are sent to the agent-memory-es service at AMES_SERVICE_URL (default localhost:8123) with AMES_SERVICE_KEY; the model may store facts in shared team/common visibility tiers.

entries.name: agentchat
entries.description: AgentChat — peer-to-peer messaging for AI agents. Owns its own WebSocket; pokes the agent on inbound; the agent decides whether to reply. Send is a tool call, never automatic. Bundles the etiquette skill.

entries.name: agentmemory
entries.title: AgentMemory
entries.description: Persistent memory provider with automatic recall, conversation capture, and native memory_save, memory_recall, and memory_search tools. Memory is scoped to the active Hermes profile, project, and message author by default. Requires a separately running AgentMemory server. Disclosure — recall queries, conversation excerpts (up to 500 user and 2,000 assistant characters per turn), native memory writes, workspace paths, and scoped session identifiers are sent to the configured AgentMemory URL (localhost:3111 by default). Credentials come through Hermes's scoped secret API. Runs git rev-parse to resolve the project and stores non-secret URL configuration and memory ownership records in the active Hermes home. Remote plaintext HTTP warns but is permitted unless AGENTMEMORY_REQUIRE_HTTPS=1. No telemetry, self-updater, or background daemon is started by the plugin.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-memory
entries.description: Private AgentPlaybooks memory for Hermes: bounded keyword recall across personal and team sources, exact native memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Disclosure — keywords derived from each turn's query are sent to the configured AgentPlaybooks service for recall from your personal and configured team playbooks; explicit native memory writes are mirrored there. Defaults to agentplaybooks.ai over HTTPS; localhost HTTP is supported, and remote intranet HTTP requires an explicit opt-in that sends the API key unencrypted. Team and shared playbooks are configured explicitly: the agent can write, archive and permanently delete entries in configured team playbooks (shared playbooks are read-only), and teammates' entries are recalled into context.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-tools
entries.description: Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to Hermes, with guided setup, profile selection, permission diagnostics and an authenticated MCP check. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.7.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb hermes setup --apply` restores complete skill trees into the chosen project and edits the selected Hermes profile's config.yaml to register those skills and a hosted playbook MCP endpoint. Local writes require --apply; setup also probes MCP initialization and tool listing using a scoped key from the process environment, without invoking tools. `doctor` checks profile credential variable names without exposing their values. Hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai (or an explicitly configured service); skill restore uses `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads project configuration (secret references, not values).

entries.name: agentpurse
entries.title: AgentPurse
entries.description: Search, quote, and buy from an AgentPurse allowance on the PayPal sandbox. Every purchase waits for Hermes' approval prompt and is sent only after a person approves it; YOLO, approvals off, auto-approve modes, and smart (model) approval cannot spend. A per-chat spend limit and /purse kill sit in front of the clerk. Disclosure — calls the author's AgentPurse service at agentpurse.vercel.app (POST /mcp and GET /api/spends/:id; the server uses the PayPal sandbox and Channel3 for product data) with AGENTPURSE_API_KEY from Hermes's secret scope, sending quotes, purchase sentences and the task/page excerpt the agent supplies; request_purchase and watch_price each wait for a person to answer Hermes's approval prompt (YOLO, approvals off, smart approval and unattended runs cannot spend), but an approved price watch later lets AgentPurse file the purchase server-side with no second Hermes prompt (/purse kill cancels open watches); a kill switch, quote cache, one-time approval grants and per-chat spent cents live in plugin state; PayPal sandbox money only, and a receipt is not a retailer order.

entries.name: agentvault
entries.title: Agent Vault
entries.description: Search archived coding conversations and retrieve exact session revisions through the separately installed Agent Vault macOS app. Launches the app's existing MCP server through sh; reads the authorized archive through its local daemon. Vault handles storage-provider traffic. No bundled binaries, telemetry, credential-file reads, self-updater, or new background service. Disclosure — launches the separately installed Agent Vault app's own bundled Node MCP server (/Applications/Agent Vault.app or VAULT_APP_PATH) through sh with your VAULT_MCP_TOKEN binding token; that server code ships with the app, not in this repository. Its tools return archived conversations from Cursor, Codex, Claude Code and Hermes stored under ~/.vault (or VAULT_HOME) into the model's context, which is sent to your model provider. The app handles its own storage-provider traffic; the plugin adds no telemetry, network calls, credential-file reads or background service.

entries.name: agentwalletapi
entries.description: OpenClawCash managed EVM and Solana wallets for AI agents — thin bridge to the OpenClawCash agent API. Disclosure — payments plugin for the OpenClawCash custodial wallet service (openclawcash.com); the model can create wallets and send EVM/Solana transfers from wallets reachable by OPENCLAWCASH_AGENT_KEY with no Hermes confirmation prompt; tool arguments go to openclawcash.com, and wallet_create also sends OPENCLAWCASH_EXPORT_PASSPHRASE to that API.

entries.name: agora
entries.description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Hermes profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `hermes agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `hermes agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a Hermes profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`hermes profile create --clone`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns `hermes -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions (explicit toolset list: no kanban/clarify/cron; override via AGORA_SPEAKER_TOOLSETS) and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to HERMES_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into HERMES_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Hermes dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Hermes subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

entries.name: ai-subscriptions
entries.title: AI Subscriptions
entries.description: Your AI subscriptions and token usage in Hermes Desktop. A page with Overview, Usage and Plans tabs, plus a status-bar chip where you pick which subscriptions to keep. Quota comes from Hermes's own model.options and usage.bars RPCs; the page polls Hermes' cached windows (Hermes refreshes them in its own background threads) and only its Refresh button asks for an explicit refresh; token usage covers Hermes, Claude Code and the Grok CLI, clicking a day shows that day's per-source, per-model and hourly breakdown, and measured tokens per second are shown per model, per day and overall. Disclosure: read-only reads outside the plugin's data - Hermes state.db and models_dev_cache.json, ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl plus ~/.grok/sessions/*/*/summary.json (token counts only). No credential, .env or auth.json reads, no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: ai-usage-tracker
entries.description: Live subscription-quota windows for every AI provider Hermes can route to, as a desktop page plus a status-bar chip, with a per-profile picker — Codex, Claude, Copilot, OpenCode Go/Zen, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax, Nous, OpenRouter, DeepSeek.

entries.name: aichipmunk
entries.description: Pairs this machine's Hermes bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside Hermes Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `hermes aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs hermes config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and hermes CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

entries.name: aihubmix
entries.description: AIHubMix — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes.

entries.name: aircraft-doppler-geolocation
entries.title: Aircraft Doppler Geolocation
entries.description: Detect aircraft flyovers in a recording (Doppler tones, plus experimental ground-reflection broadband jet passes) and estimate where it was made by scoring them against adsb.lol ADS-B history, with a posterior heatmap, 68/95% areas and a confidence flag. Provides the doppler_detect and doppler_locate tools and a dopplergeo CLI. Results on unseen real recordings are weak (2 of 18 held-out runs under 3 km); treat output as a hypothesis. Disclosure — doppler_locate / dopplergeo locate makes unauthenticated HTTPS GETs to GitHub (adsb.lol release assets, streamed, about 3 GB read per uncached day; only the crop is cached), raw.githubusercontent.com (tar1090-db types), the Copernicus DEM S3 bucket and Open-Meteo, caching results under ~/.cache/doppler-geo (or DOPPLER_GEO_CACHE); offline mode uses the local cache only; no credentials, uploads or telemetry. doppler_detect and the skill scripts make no network calls; the tools and scripts run ffmpeg/ffprobe (no shell) on the recording you name and write CSV/PNG/JSON at the output path you give (default `<recording>.doppler/`). PyPI packages (numpy, scipy, soundfile, matplotlib, tifffile) install only after Hermes dependency consent. The method can geolocate where a recording was made, so use it only on recordings you are entitled to analyse.

entries.name: airlock
entries.title: airlock
entries.description: Guardrails that follow what a conversation has read. Once a session reads untrusted content (a web page, a browser snapshot, an MCP or third-party plugin's output, a customer's message), airlock seals it: messages to anyone but the owner, network writes, pushes and deploys, memory, skill and cron writes, browser input, URLs that could carry data out and code that reaches the network go through Hermes's own approval gate. Walls hold in every session: credential paths and secret files, the guard's own files and Hermes's config, shell startup files, other profiles, commands that switch approvals off. Shell commands are read the way the shell reads them, so a command that computes or hides what it runs (eval, base64 | sh, $G push, wildcards, write-then-run) is refused until written in clear. Subagents inherit the seal. A project's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules or .hermes.md that Hermes loads at startup seals the session from its first turn until the owner has reviewed it (`hermes airlock trust`), and again when its content changes (a cloned repository, a pull). It also catches an injection by its signature: recognized secrets never leave in a call; a private marker in the agent's context locks the session if it shows up in a tool call; a send to an address the untrusted content named is blocked; repeated refusals lock the session; lookalike Unicode in commands is refused. A file behind a wall cannot leave as a message attachment, and attached files are checked for secrets. A call that names a cloud metadata service is refused. Plugin and MCP tools nobody admitted need approval. Observe mode, stop switch, `hermes airlock check|demo|log|trust`. On Windows, paths are read in every form Windows and Git Bash give them, and a path on another machine is refused without being opened. Tested on a corpus of 362 attacks and everyday commands, on Linux, macOS and Windows, and end to end in the official image. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, subagent_start, on_session_reset, post_approval_response), no tools. No network, no LLM call, runs no command. Reads the profile's config.yaml (home channels, approvals mode) and its own policy file (<HERMES_HOME>/airlock.yaml); lists directories to expand wildcards in commands it checks; reads the first 200 KB of each file a send_message attaches, locally, to look for secrets. On Windows, reads the machine's own name (no lookup), tests which drive letters exist, and imports tools.environments.local._find_bash to know Git Bash's root. On a session's first turn, imports agent.prompt_builder.discover_context_files and _project_context_suppressed and agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_context_cwd (guarded) to know which project context files Hermes loaded, and hashes them (sha256). Imports Hermes's attachment reader (gateway.platforms.base.BasePlatformAdapter.extract_media) to see exactly what a message would attach, with its own reader as a fallback. Writes under plugin-data/airlock: a journal of decisions, taints and approvals that includes tool arguments, truncated (journal.args: none leaves them out), the taint state, the stop switch and the context files the owner trusted (path and sha256). When nobody can approve (--yolo, /yolo, hermes -z, approvals.mode: off, cron, -q or webhook set to approve, a subagent under delegation.subagent_auto_approve) it blocks instead of letting Hermes auto-approve; to know it, it imports gateway.session_finite.unattended_turn and reads tools.approval (_yolo_active, _unattended_contexts, approval_context._get_approval_mode), each guarded, config.yaml as fallback (policy approvals_off: follow restores Hermes's behaviour). Install scan: caution, because the default policy and the shell reader name the patterns airlock guards against (startup files, crontab, credential commands, exfiltration shapes).

entries.name: aisense
entries.title: AI SENSE Free Public Tools
entries.description: 77 free tools for agents through AI SENSE's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): time and time zones, hashing and encoding, QR codes, HTML to PDF, JSON and CSV, images, and workflow tools (temporary storage, webhook capture, human approval, queues, leases, heartbeats, an agent inbox, typed decisions from weighted rules, semantic search, one-time secrets), with one tool-choice skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to AI SENSE's MCP server at aisenseapi.com with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session, and request logs hold the caller's IP address. Tools that create something return bearer tokens; stored data, files and captures are readable by anyone holding their id or URL and expire within 24 hours; webhook schedules and notify URLs make the server call a URL the agent supplies. 5000 requests per address per day across all tools. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. No sign-in: the bundled mcp.json works as installed.

entries.name: aistupidlevel
entries.title: AI Stupid Level
entries.description: AI Stupid Level Smart Router — OpenAI-compatible; routing modes such as auto-tooling send each request to the model currently scoring best on continuously re-run benchmarks, called with your own provider keys. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool definitions, tool results and ASL_ROUTER_KEY to aistupidlevel.info (S.C. Studio Platforms S.R.L.), which forwards each request to the AI provider it routes to using the provider keys you store on your AI Stupid Level account; model usage is billed to your provider accounts, and prompts are logged only if you enable logging for a key.

entries.name: aixy
entries.title: Aixy
entries.description: Guided Aixy inference setup with optional MCP tools: hermes aixy setup selects an available model or route, and hermes aixy mcp connects tools later. MCP is skipped by default. Disclosure — exposes CLI commands only, with no automatic hooks or runtime tools. Explicit inference setup sends the project key in an authenticated GET /models to the configured Aixy gateway (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/v1 by default), rejects redirects, and asks before updating the selected Hermes profile's provider and main model settings. The key is stored through Hermes' credential writer as AIXY_API_KEY; provider settings contain a variable reference. Model requests send Hermes' opaque conversation scope in X-Aixy-Session-ID for grouping in Aixy Activity. No inference requests are sent during setup. Optional MCP setup starts the installed Hermes CLI as a child process for browser OAuth, credential storage and tool selection against the independent MCP endpoint (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/mcp by default). The child uses the selected profile, disables inherited unattended and YOLO flags, and receives no key in command arguments. Setup requires an interactive terminal. No additional dependencies, telemetry, persistent background processes or self-updater.

entries.name: alans-way-computer
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin: Computer Use
entries.description: Computer-use provider for Hermes: the stock computer_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus HERMES_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus, plus HERMES_HOME set to the bound profile's home, under which the router appends a content-free serving log to logs/workspace-router.log; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). On the user's Mac the provider can bring the target app to the front when the model asks for it (focus_app with raise_window, or an input action with delivery_mode foreground), and the Alan's Workspace host does so only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds; focus_app can also launch a named app, or open a document or folder by absolute path in its app (the host refuses app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps). Every input action still goes through Hermes's computer_use approval gate, with raising and foreground input under their own approval scopes (the cua:<action>:background entries in command_allowlist that the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds skip the prompt for background input, focus_app and launches, not for raising or foreground input). The provider itself makes no network calls. On Hermes 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures skip the screenshot call entirely when finite snapshot window geometry proves named controls cover at least 35%; older snapshots without geometry still fetch a screenshot to measure coverage and may omit it from the model; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Captures request generation-based snapshot deltas, validate them against the held tree and retry once for a full list on invalid or mismatched deltas; older apps may return full or unchanged lists. Once a reply identifies a window, later captures, screenshots and input stay bound to that window; capture(window_id=...) selects another. Mismatched window replies clear the target and require a fresh capture. Desktop actions carry expect_host from the observed host so a routing switch refuses input before dispatch; app IDs and element numbers must be reacquired after a switch. Element trees, generation, bound window ID, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. Hermes's unmodified CI-pinned scanner reports SAFE: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the long-running router Popen in __init__.py and its bounded 40-second --probe subprocess) and 0 LOW. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer_use approval gate.

entries.name: alans-way
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin
entries.description: Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a Hermes gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Hermes's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store the bound chat's activity timestamps in plugin state; optional cross-bot export adds the separate storage disclosed below. On first load it reads $HERMES_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and hand a JSON setup plan to the human in Alan's Workspace. The app runs setup.sh through an external SSH process outside the gateway, checks the exact repoRef and desktopRef and rejects tracked checkout changes; the agent must never run setup or even --verify in its gateway terminal or bypass the lifecycle guard. Windows guests require the human's external Git Bash shell. The human pastes the app's output for review. The external setup does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units hermes-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit hermes-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the hermes-gateway unit. Hermes refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or hermes gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or hermes gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block with connect_timeout: 25 seconds (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser only skips disabling it; it does not re-enable a previously disabled toolset), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:*:background entries to command_allowlist. On a Hermes without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace_computer_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the Hermes and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.hermes, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre_llm_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform_llm_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting|default|status and hermes tone store the mode under voice in Hermes plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count. Morning briefs are off by default: /proactivity brief on (or the operator CLI) enables one daily internal user-role prompt near active_start, with 0-20 minutes of jitter, at most two hours late and skipped after recent user activity. It asks the model to consult calendar and email read-only if those tools exist. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning_brief and last_brief_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. The workspace router adds a commit object to the existing browser open/action tools for purchases, bookings, sends, posts, submissions, deletions and account changes. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. Tax schedule names are treated as benign labels without exempting one-on-one bookings from approval. It asks through MCP elicitation (60-second default wait, configurable with HERMES_ROUTER_APPROVAL_MS), refuses unavailable, declined, timed-out or stale approvals, drops agent-supplied approval receipts and adds a single-use receipt bound to the approved tab and epoch. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The same two skills now prefer Hermes web_search/web_extract for plain lookups and the user's computer for interactive search, hand CAPTCHAs to the human, poll at most every 30 seconds for up to 30 minutes, and switch sources after two challenges in ten minutes. The router stops remembering challenge pages for failover and reports changed tab ids in result metadata. The operations skill covers the app's automatic takeover after its grace period; CAPTCHA and recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still keep the bot out. It asks the agent to save only lasting general facts and preferences to memory; procedures belong in skills and project/task records in the user's chosen file or tracker, asking where if none is chosen. Existing memory is not migrated or deleted, and live tab state is never saved there. The setup skill pins the companion app source to f110115ff23367e4e21eeaf00e658a8706369652 and adds a long-chat reference: report effective compression and summary routing read-only, then only with explicit consent for each profile enable compression.proactive_prune_tokens at 48000, with 8000-character eligibility and 4096-token minimum reclaim, using the profile-scoped config CLI and keeping custom values, micro_compact and summary routing. This writes the approved profile's config.yaml and records prior values outside the repo for undo; setup.sh does not run it. A weekly time-saved report is a user-created Hermes cron recipe, not an installed job. setup.sh --verify now checks the running service manager, display, SSH ProxyCommand and managed browser's loopback /json/version endpoint, and reports noVNC reachability from its actual bind address. Manual supervisord restart guidance drains with USR1 first. The repo also adds scripts/voice_eval.py, user-run only: it sends fixed fictional scenarios and replies to Anthropic models through the SDK or claude -p for scoring and optionally writes a JSON result; the plugin, setup and skills never run it. Since 0.21.5, the plugin registers two more bundled skills, web-errands and integrations, with no new tools, hooks, commands or required environment variables. web-errands is guidance for shopping, booking, applications, filings, cancellations and claims in the workspace browser: every purchase, booking, send, submission and deletion still goes through the commit approval gate described above, CAPTCHA, sign-in and card-entry walls go back to the human, and card numbers are never stored. It has the agent record each application's company, role, date, posting URL and confirmation in the user's chosen project/task record, asking where if none is chosen. For a price, restock or status watch the user asks for or explicitly accepts, it has the agent create a Hermes cron job with Hermes's cronjob_manage tool (or ask the operator), polling no more often than every 10 minutes and stopping after three consecutive failures; cron runs cannot answer approvals, so a watch that reaches its target stages the result for the user. Watches use attach_to_session: true with no deliver override and continuity: true; each check is a fresh session, uses its prior completed output as a baseline and replies [SILENT] unless something meaningful changed, failed or reached its target. An optional safe read-only deterministic monitor URL or script can skip the model and delivery on unchanged output; probe errors still need reporting/backoff. Cron cannot pause/remove itself unless the operator enabled cron.allow_agent_scheduling. In-chat monitoring is a separate user-entered /heartbeat every command, one per conversation replacing the previous one; it runs only while idle with the chat process/gateway alive, costs a model turn per check and needs /heartbeat clear from the user. The integrations skill has the agent check that an account is connected, with a small read, before promising a task that needs it, and reuses Hermes's Google Workspace, Himalaya, Home Assistant, Honcho and X routes first. The Google route uses Hermes's own setup, whose fixed scope list includes write access; the skill says so and stops if the user declines. Only after the user agrees in chat does it guide an install: a Hermes catalog plugin (Home Assistant or Honcho), a separately reviewed Himalaya v1.2.0 binary, rclone v1.75.2 (the release zip from downloads.rclone.org, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before extraction) or Taskwarrior 3.5.0 (a source build of upstream commit 3419d5ba1e6a780fbbb0a8d68d8fd31e675c1bf8 cloned from GitHub, after checking the CMake and Rust versions and asking before changing any toolchain), the last two into versioned directories under ~/.local/share/alans-tools/. Secrets are entered by the human in a private terminal outside the agent session, never in Telegram; where a recipe needs a secret in the agent's terminal (a mail credential, RCLONE_CONFIG_PASS), it explains the grant and adds only that variable to the profile's terminal.env_passthrough. The recipes keep rclone.conf (mode 0600) and Taskwarrior's taskrc and data under the profile's HERMES_HOME/integrations. Scheduled reads are read-only cron jobs with a profile-local failure-count file, and pausing goes through the owner conversation or an explicitly authorized hermes cron pause. API writes (send, post, delete, share) need fresh explicit approval in the live conversation, and a declined, timed-out or unavailable browser commit is never completed through another tool. Mastodon is not bundled: its recipe is human-run documentation in this repo (docs/integrations/mastodon.md) that the plugin and skills never run. None of this runs at plugin load or from setup.sh. Telegram replies, check-ins and briefs share one status-first style: concrete status, evidence or caveat, plain limits, and no tool names, file paths, scripts or job and session IDs in user-facing text unless asked. Prices, availability and policies must come from a page read this turn or be labeled unconfirmed. Multi-step browser work continues in short chunks until done or blocked, with one short start line and one-line updates only at milestones, routed-around failures or noticeable waits; routine reads, actions and transitions stay quiet, a new mid-task message is acknowledged and folded in, and Hermes's clarify buttons may be used for decisions the user owns, never for approvals; a whole checkout batch still sits under one commit. For a message of 200 characters or fewer that is wholly a recap request, greeting, thanks or acknowledgment, the voice hook appends a three-sentence limit; the check reads only the current message, with no model call, history or network. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. The operations skill adds tab hygiene: the agent closes finished tabs it owns with the existing close tool, never another bot's or the user's and never one with a pending handback or recording hold. The router adds requestingBotId to tab-list replies and forwards a reply over 4 MiB unchanged, without that decoration, writing a content-free line to stderr. The skill also tells the agent to report installed versions by running hermes --version, reading the plugin's install metadata, running local git describe and rev-parse on the Alan's Tools checkout, and calling the app's existing status tool. setup.sh --bind now also makes the bound DM Hermes's Telegram home by running hermes -p PROFILE config set for TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID (30-second limit each; on failure it warns to send /sethome); it loads on gateway restart. setup.sh --verify exits 0 for a complete local audit, 1 for failed required checks and 2 for a partial install (warnings, or skipped browser or services). The setup skill's checkout step now initializes ~/alans-way-agents if absent and fetches the pin (depth 1) from the repo's GitHub origin, or reuses a clean clone there after two read-only local git helpers (5-second limit) confirm one recorded and effective origin URL naming this repo; for file and direct Git installs it uses the installer-recorded revision, and it never falls back to a tag when that record is invalid. Its computer-use API probe separates an absent API from a failed or timed-out probe and ends the probe's process group or tree on timeout. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: one grouped autonomy choice for display.busy_input_mode: steer and agent.intent_ack_continuation: true, for every platform in that profile after restart. It reads effective values, including defaults, proposes changes only from stock interrupt/auto and preserves deliberate choices, custom or unknown values and unreadable config. General setup/proactivity consent is insufficient; an explicit no preserves both settings, silence writes nothing. Both keys are read back, including unchanged keys, before writing and reading back skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice as chosen or keep-current. Failed writes/readbacks leave the marker untouched; it records the answer only and never restores settings. Legacy busy_input_choice: keep-interrupt skips only the busy key; unknown legacy state is reported and skipped. agent.verify_on_stop is left alone unless the coding user requests stricter checks and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim_assistant_messages, tool_progress, notifications, long_running_notifications and busy_steer_ack_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice and telegram_feel_choice; the former busy_input_choice is read but no longer written; a legacy busy_steer_ack_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install, SAFE requires no scanner confirmation; setup and dependency consent remain separate. A later CAUTION revision needs review and explicit consent to the exact tree before retrying hermes plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --enable alone does not confirm a warning, and --force confirms CAUTION and can replace an install but cannot override DANGEROUS. Hermes's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded_ip_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file). This pin also extends the existing texting-note and minimal final-opener polish to public session source tags desktop, tui and bot_room, alongside Telegram; CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources keep their default voice. A tone-independent pre_llm_call task note asks the agent to track and verify mini goals with Hermes's todo tool or working context, continue independent authorized work through completion, recheck historical blockers against newer messages and verify every requested criterion with each item's own source before replying. It requests a short start line and milestone-only updates, keeps routine work quiet and preserves questions, approvals, failures and honest completion. Recap replies are capped at three sentences total including any detail offer. Follow-up cron jobs are saved only after the user asks or says yes, attached to this chat with attach_to_session: true and no deliver override; no later message may be promised without a saved job. A not-yet reply allows one offer at a named local time, with no saved repeat until consent, and jobs are removed when their reason ends. /goal is suggested once for a big multi-step job, not small asks. Fixed Hermes progress/error/approval messages are unchanged. Scripted tool conversations prove hook delivery; consistent real-model quiet behavior is unverified. Browser guidance starts normal work in the user's Workspace even while they are away; host vm is for explicit VM requests or router-reported outages, never login/CAPTCHA/approval errors. Existing VM tasks finish there when the computer returns; no third-tier browser is substituted. Reasoned human handbacks hold VM tabs as well as computer tabs for up to 30 minutes until Give back; a chat reply alone cannot bypass awaiting_human. Resume uses the host, tab ID and fresh epoch from one reply. The human-only Move button can carry URL/scroll and chosen drafts; cookies move only when a restore is reported, while passwords, uploads and in-memory state stay behind, and the agent has no move tool. Router changes bind approvals to exact observed page targets, reject missing/malformed action success receipts, bound recovery and owned-child shutdown, and project agent-facing replies without exposing internal approval proof. The router never replays a sent write after connector retry, timeout or host change, including writes before the first response; only reads and unsent calls can replay within their original remaining budget. Cancellation is forwarded and stale-host checks reject queued desktop input before sending it; uncertainty requires checking the outcome before any repeat. Browser and desktop replies add a content-free diagnostic, on stderr and appended to the profile's logs/workspace-router.log, with fixed tool name, serving host, default/request/fallback selection and reason, and elapsed time; it contains no URLs or page/task content.
