Idle direct SSH probes can discover a recovered computer sooner without moving an active VM task. Cross-bot proactivity adds the cross_bot_ask tool and pre_tool_call/on_session_end hooks; no middleware, required secrets or direct network destinations are added. Optional cross-bot proactivity is off by default, configured with the same explicit absolute shared root and designated primary in each participating profile, then enrolled per bot through /proactivity cross on (activation in a running gateway needs a restart). Only completed user/final-assistant exchanges from each enrolled bot's bound owner Telegram DM are exported: at most four recent exchanges and 2 KiB per digest, expiring after 24 hours per exchange. There is no historical backfill or export of groups, other chats, attachments, reasoning, tool history, cron, check-ins, briefs, child or imported turns. Exchanges that appear to contain credentials or payment details, or match operator redact terms, are skipped entirely before truncation; sanitization cannot detect every secret. Only the designated primary receives other enabled profiles' fresh digests during permitted check-ins, including user-requested /proactivity now; its own digest is excluded and exports are JSON-escaped as untrusted observations, bounded to 32 KiB across 16 profiles. Ordinary turns receive no digests or dispatch permit; separately consented helper results can arrive there as disclosed below. Briefs and cron receive neither. The primary may automatically schedule one read_only or draft_only cross_bot_ask with fresh target evidence per check-in into another enrolled bot's existing bound DM; replies appear there with primary attribution, and only separately consented short outcomes can return to the primary. The receiver needs its own gateway-injection permission and verified routing, observes pause/hours/busy settings, and starts no spontaneous secondary check-ins. Queued asks are at most 800 characters, expire after two hours and are deleted before injection; sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed, with no replay, delivery-receipt store or result polling. Result sharing is separately off by default, including for existing cross-bot users: /proactivity cross results on must be chosen in both bound owner DMs. Only future asks can return a sanitized Done/Blocked summary of at most 280 UTF-8 bytes, correlated to one ask, with the same two-hour expiry measured from ask creation. The private shared results.json stores up to 64 pending/running/completed records with profile identities, enrollment generations, ask IDs, timestamps, prompt/session-correlation hashes, status and summary. Results are consumed once before exposure at the primary's next ordinary owner turn or permitted check-in, as untrusted helper reports rather than independently verified facts. There is no wake, retry or delivery guarantee; a crash or helper restart can lose an outcome. /proactivity cross results off purges pending outcomes; cross off also revokes the choice. Copied outcomes can persist in chat/provider context after expiry or opt-out. Attempts are limited to four per rolling day gateway-wide, two per target and 60-minute target spacing. The plugin-owned POSIX shared directory uses mode 0700 and files 0600: digests and queued bodies, persistent enrollment/generation and eligibility/heartbeat records, body-free turn/attempt hashes retained for 48 hours, one-use check-in permits and imported-session locks expiring within 30 minutes. Session locks contain the exact session key and ask ID and survive restart until session end, expiry or opt-out. Pruning runs on activated startup, before store access and every 60 seconds while connected; offline expired files can remain until an activated profile prunes them. Dormant profiles do no cross-bot store access. /proactivity cross off immediately stops sharing, receiving and dispatch and purges that profile's digest, permits, locks and pending asks; body-free records remain until expiry and scheduler roles revert on restart. Only the operator can enable or expand sharing; the model may disable it. Launch-gateway profile routing policy is read through public configuration/home-scope APIs; no Hermes session DB or credential store is read for export. Imported sessions block terminal/code, desktop actions, delegation, messaging, scheduling, further cross-bot asks and unknown connectors; reviewed reads/drafting and existing gated browser actions remain allowed. Browser approval, CAPTCHA and ownership gates still apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Copied context goes through the configured model provider and target Telegram delivery and may remain in Hermes history, API-content sidecars, compaction and memory-provider records, including Honcho when configured, and model-provider retention after expiry or opt-out. The instruction not to save other bots' excerpts is model policy, not enforced deletion; the plugin performs no memory-provider writes. No new direct network endpoint or telemetry is introduced. Optional integrations use the user's selected Google Workspace API, IMAP/SMTP mail service, Home Assistant instance, Honcho API, X API or rclone cloud/WebDAV/S3 endpoint; browser errands contact user-selected sites. Honcho can receive conversation turns, derived conclusions, peer/session IDs and version/OS/plugin headers. Native tools retain their own profile-scoped credentials, including Google client/token/pending OAuth files and encrypted rclone provider tokens; the plugin does not create a separate credential store. Setup downloads also reach GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com, the official Tailscale installer, configured distro package repositories and the npm/Playwright distribution, in addition to Google and rclone downloads already disclosed.

entries.name: alice-voice
entries.title: Alice Voice Input
entries.description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for Hermes, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.

entries.name: ample
entries.title: Ample
entries.description: Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps Hermes builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, Hermes home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in Hermes's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to Hermes's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.

entries.name: anatomy-museum
entries.title: Anatomy Museum
entries.description: Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in Hermes" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or Hermes data are sent.

entries.name: ando-platform
entries.description: Connect a Hermes agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $HERMES_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start Hermes turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's Hermes cache); hermes ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.

entries.name: android-emulator
entries.description: Control a headless Android emulator from Hermes — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.

entries.name: anki
entries.title: Anki
entries.description: Create, search, and review Anki flashcards from Hermes through the local AnkiConnect API: adds notes to a deck (creating it if needed), searches the collection, lists due cards, and grades reviews. Writes to the local Anki collection and changes scheduling only when its tools or /anki command are used. Requires Anki desktop with AnkiConnect (add-on 2055492159); no telemetry; optional API key via ANKI_BRIDGE_API_KEY.

entries.name: antenna
entries.title: Antenna for Hermes
entries.description: Signed messaging with paired Hermes and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).

entries.name: antigravity-agy
entries.description: Run Hermes on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Hermes tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Hermes. Fails closed on any non-Hermes tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

entries.name: antigravity-duet
entries.title: Antigravity Duet / Duffy Queue & Ruflo Swarm Controller
entries.description: Autonomous background task queue (DAAK Duffy / Duet Do-For-You worker) with Human-in-the-Loop approval gates (duet_queue tool, /duffy and /duet commands), Ruflo multi-agent swarm orchestration (ruflo_swarm tool), and multi-model Antigravity CLI quota fallback worker (gemini-3.8-flash-high -> claude-sonnet-5-5-high -> gemini-3.1-pro-high -> claude-opus-5-5-high -> gpt-oss-120b-medium). Disclosure — when the optional background worker or the ruflo_swarm tool is used, the plugin runs the locally installed agy or ruflo CLI under its existing sign-in (counting against the user's subscription) with the Hermes process environment; the worker you start with `python3 -m daak_duffy worker` serves a token-protected dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8899; the plugin never reads, copies, links, or modifies any OAuth token files, keychains, or .env secrets.

entries.name: antigravity-oauth
entries.description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `hermes auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx hermes-antigravity-oauth`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Hermes system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

entries.name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Runs Hermes on an Antigravity subscription via the agy CLI. Streams progressively and opts into host streaming when the profile declares it; persists trajectories via agy --conversation (239k); discovers models per account; maps effort; reports /usage quota; aborts native tool steps. Windows console children spawn with CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Inference and /usage reads count against your subscription; links the antigravity-oauth-token into a private temp HOME deleted on close; probes keyring presence (Secret Service, Keychain, Credential Manager), reading no secrets; symlinks ~/Library/Keychains on macOS; never writes vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking env vars before spawning agy (ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT allow-list); ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR writes every prompt to disk. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list) and disables agy's background auto-updater in its child environment. Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

entries.name: anyapi
entries.title: AnyAPI.ai
entries.description: AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.

entries.name: anyrouter
entries.description: AnyRouter — one API key for many models through an OpenAI-compatible gateway. The /model picker lists only tool-capable routes, and meta-models like anyrouter/hermes auto-route across top models with fallback. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/hermes is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model, not a Nous Research model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds Hermes attribution headers.

entries.name: anysearch
entries.description: AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).

entries.name: aphrodite
entries.description: CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled. Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_hermes + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the Hermes home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).

entries.name: apify
entries.title: Apify
entries.description: Apify, the largest marketplace of tools for AI: discover, run, and collect results from thousands of ready-to-run Actors, from the comfort of your agent, plus an Apify backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract tools.

entries.name: approval-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of Hermes's approval prompts (dangerous commands, protected writes, MCP consent, smart-mode verdicts): /approval-log shows how often each rule asked, how many prompts were approved, denied or left unanswered, and how long a person took to answer, per rule, per surface or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /approval-log recent lists the newest decisions (ten, or up to 100 with /approval-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes decision metadata (session id, surface, rule label, answer, timings; no command, description or session key) to plugin-data/approval-ledger/approvals.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer or change an approval; no network

entries.name: ard-kit
entries.description: Agentic Resource Discovery — search a local tool catalog by intent and inspect an entry to get its invoke command. Ships the ard-registry skill plus an stdio MCP server (ard_search / ard_inspect / ard_verify); stdlib only, the run stays local. Disclosure — no network egress, no API keys and no environment variables read by the MCP front, which ranks a catalog JSON on disk; no catalog ships in the repo, so the first call returns an explicit error naming the `python -m ard_kit.catalogize` command that builds one.

entries.name: artifact-relay
entries.description: Publish and read private Markdown or HTML reports through your Artifact Relay server.

entries.name: artifacts
entries.title: Hermes Artifacts
entries.description: Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to HERMES_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential HERMES_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Hermes secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Hermes read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Hermes write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: artil
entries.title: Artil
entries.description: Give Hermes agents their own email inbox, phone number, and workspace accounts to work directly with customers, teammates, and other agents. Disclosure — runs the bundled Artil CLI (`artil internal hermes-channel`) while the gateway is listening, which holds a connection to Artil and turns email, SMS, Telegram and team Message-URL messages to the agent account into agent runs with the gateway's tools; who reaches the agent is decided by the agent's "Who can wake the agent" page in Artil and by Hermes's ARTIL_ALLOWED_USERS / ARTIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS allowlist or pairing (hermes gateway setup writes those to .env); message text and replies go through Artil's servers; the Artil sign-in stays in the CLI's own ~/.config/artil.

entries.name: ascii-worlds
entries.title: ASCII Worlds
entries.description: Koi and jellyfish drawn live in text glyphs for Hermes Desktop. Choose how many and their colours in Settings -> Plugins -> ASCII Worlds, and optionally let them swim across the whole window. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network access.

entries.name: aside-browser
entries.description: Use the signed-in Aside browser as Hermes's browser when the Aside CLI is installed. Disclosure — runs the local aside CLI to drive your signed-in Aside browser (page text, screenshots, Aside memory, model-written JavaScript via aside_repl) without a Hermes approval prompt; Aside's permission level is a user-only setting (default ask) that covers aside_exec only. Optional pre_tool_call hook blocks Hermes' built-in browser tools while Aside is ready when browser_policy is always. Reads Aside's settings.json for the model list; no telemetry.

entries.name: astro-agents
entries.title: Astro Agents
entries.description: Verifiable planetary timing data for market analysis and backtesting through the Astro Agents MCP server (24 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://astro-agent.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): geocentric and heliocentric positions, declination, Gann planetary lines, a to-the-minute event calendar (ingresses, stations, eclipses), sky analogues and crypto token launch charts and synastry, plus full Western and Vedic astrology (birth chart, transits, synastry, kundli D1-D60, dashas, doshas, KP, yogas, panchang, Gun Milan), computed from the NASA/JPL DE440 ephemeris with no LLM; every result carries a SHA-256 hash. Data for your own analysis, never a trading signal or forecast. Bundles the astrology skill (when to call which tool, input conventions). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call sends the dates, times and coordinates it is given to astro-agent.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. 1 free call per client on the $0.01-0.02 routes only (REST, MCP or A2A); every other route, finance included, is always paid. Over MCP a paid tool returns a standard x402 offer (USDC on Base or Solana) and is paid per call only if the user's own x402 MCP client signs it, or with prepaid credits when the user sets an X-Credits-Token header; the package holds no wallet, key or token.

entries.name: athena
entries.title: Athena
entries.description: The local AI-app store for Hermes: browse a constantly growing catalogue of apps, install an app from any git repository, launch it, read its logs and stop it. It declares HF_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN so Hermes offers to set them, and reads each one through Hermes' own secret route rather than scavenging another program's token store. An app is handed a credential only after you approve that app, as an environment variable for the life of its process - never written to disk and never sent anywhere by Athena itself. Apps run on your machine on loopback; third-party install scripts run as you, and the README states the network endpoints, the WSL/QEMU command paths and the GitHub publish path in full. The panel and the CLI are two doors into the same engine. Agent control is in active development. Disclosure — installs apps by cloning third-party git repositories and running their own install and launch scripts on your machine as you (each install and first launch asks through Hermes' approval prompt); provisions a pinned app engine from npm at setup after consent; hands HF_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN to an app only after you approve that app, as an environment variable of its process; sends the GitHub token only to GitHub hosts; can manage WSL/QEMU machines and publish your store to a GitHub repository you name.

entries.name: athletedata
entries.title: athletedata
entries.description: The athlete's own training and health data from 39 apps (Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, Hevy, Apple Health, Intervals.icu and more) through athletedata's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.athletedata.health/mcp): activities, training load, HRV, sleep, readiness, nutrition, body composition, race predictions, and structured workouts pushed to the athlete's watch. Bundles one skill that tells the agent when to use it. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.athletedata.health and needs an athletedata account (paid, 7-day free trial) with its API key in ATHLETEDATA_API_KEY; the athlete's health and training data is returned from that server. Write tools (push a workout to the watch, log food, create a Hevy routine) change the athlete's own accounts; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: atmorouter
entries.title: AtmoRouter
entries.description: AtmoRouter — OpenAI-compatible gateway; one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Grok models, with the /model picker fed by the live GET /v1/models catalog. Disclosure — sends your prompts, conversation history, tool definitions, tool results and ATMOROUTER_API_KEY to atmorouter.dev, which forwards each request to the upstream infrastructure serving the chosen model; that infrastructure's location and retention vary per model and zero retention is not promised (AtmoRouter states it keeps metadata, not prompt or response content, in its usage records and does not train on API content; https://atmorouter.dev/privacy). Usage is billed per token from a prepaid AtmoRouter balance (USDC on Solana or QRIS); prices vary by capacity tier and a request can route to any listed tier, including tiers above official pricing, unless you set maximum prices under Budgets; failed upstream requests are not billed and the plugin itself makes no payments.

entries.name: aurora-design-system
entries.title: Aurora Design System
entries.description: Two offline tools plus four skills that make a Hermes agent build real web UI with the Aurora CSS design system: aurora_search returns the family, the pack and the real markup of any of 2,223 documented objects from a bundled census; aurora_validate checks a page against that census (invented classes, packs used but not linked, gradients, !important, hand-written colours, duplicate headings, missing attribution) and returns failures and warnings in milliseconds. No network, no subprocess, no writes, no hooks. Disclosure — the bundled skills have the agent run `curl`/`git` against api.github.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net (Ntizar/Aurora) to resolve the current release, build pages that load their CSS from cdn.jsdelivr.net, and require the attribution footer `Hecho con ❤️ por David Antizar` and Spanish copy on every page (`aurora_validate` fails pages without the footer); `aurora_validate` reads any HTML path the agent passes.

entries.name: author-feed
entries.description: Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. It reads public posts and profiles from the Bluesky social media network, which is built on the AT Protocol (atproto), without signing in. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. hermes author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run hermes author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with hermes cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall.

entries.name: auto-pin
entries.description: Automatically pin every new interactive session (desktop, CLI, TUI) and the branches you fork from them. Cron, one-shot, subagent and messaging sessions are left alone, and unpinning a session sticks. Disclosure — on each new desktop/CLI/TUI session it sets the session's pinned flag in Hermes's session database (state.db) through the shared SessionDB handle, and records each automatic pin in $HERMES_HOME/auto-pin/ledger.txt; no network, no tools.

entries.name: aux-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of Hermes's auxiliary LLM calls (titling, compression, vision, approval): /aux shows tokens, time and failures per task, model, provider or day, or lists the newest calls (ten, or up to 100 with /aux recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded. Disclosure — writes auxiliary-call metadata (ids, models, timings, token counts, no prompt or response text) to plugin-data/aux-ledger/calls.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: b64-ref
entries.description: @b64: context references that decode encoded text for the model: @b64:<value> takes base64 (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), hex (0x48656c6c6f, 48:65:6c, \x48\x65), percent-encoding or a data: URI, told apart by the value's shape or picked with base64:, base64url:, hex: or url:, and attaches what it holds: text as text with control and invisible characters escaped, JSON pretty-printed, gzip and zlib inflated in memory (at most 1 MiB, one layer), and binary named by its format (PNG and GIF with their size, JPEG, PDF, ZIP, ELF, SQLite and more) with a hex dump of its first 128 bytes; notes point out a value that was cut short, padding that is off, a second layer of encoding and a JWT inside; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's base64, json, urllib.parse and zlib; nothing decoded is run, opened or saved; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what it decodes, but the @b64: reference and the decoded contents become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only values you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @b64: reference provider.

entries.name: background-review-watch
entries.description: Status-bar chips for the background self-improvement review and batch context compaction: review running/done/stale with live elapsed time, a turn-countdown fill bar to the next nudge, an always-visible compaction chip (compacting/done/failed/stale with committed reduction or failure class), reply-guard recovery and review-overlap diagnostics, and a Settings page that tunes both orphan ceilings. Disclosure — renderer-only; polls filtered read-only tails of agent.log via host.logs to parse lifecycle markers; listens for review.summary/message.start/message.complete events; stores three small plugin-storage records (settings + last compaction + last review); no network calls beyond the local gateway, no credential access, no self-update.

entries.name: backupdrill
entries.title: BackupDrill
entries.description: Back up a Supabase project to your own S3, R2 or B2 bucket with the open-source backupdrill CLI (the Postgres database, plus Storage files once their S3 keys are set), then restore the snapshot into a throwaway Postgres in Docker to check it comes back. Disclosure — a skill only, with no Python, hooks or server: it has the agent run npx -y backupdrill@2.7.1 in shell commands, which npx downloads from npm on first run. The CLI connects to the user's Supabase project and their own bucket, and a drill pulls a postgres image from Docker Hub. The connection string and bucket keys stay in a .env.backupdrill file the user fills in; each command loads it in a subshell and never prints it. Nothing is sent to BackupDrill.

entries.name: basekit
entries.description: Read-only live Base (chain 8453) intelligence — gas and real USD cost estimates, wallet portfolios, decoded transaction receipts, token facts with proxy detection, and windowed transfer/approval reads — plus a desktop pane, status-bar chip and a standard-library-only core with no PyPI dependencies. Disclosure — sends the wallet addresses, transaction hashes and token addresses you ask about to public Base RPC endpoints (base-rpc.publicnode.com, mainnet.base.org, base.drpc.org, base.meowrpc.com; a custom rpc_url still fails over to these), prices to coins.llama.fi and api.coinbase.com, and to api.etherscan.io only when a Basescan key is set; a pre_llm_call hook adds one line of live Base state to turns that mention Base or crypto terms (off with inject_chain_context); keeps a local read ledger in its plugin-data folder; no signing, no keys, no telemetry.

entries.name: beam
entries.title: Beam
entries.description: Move data across cloud storage and exchange end-to-end encrypted messages, files and media between agents with Beam Network (Bittensor SN105).

entries.name: bento
entries.description: Bento (bentonow.com) email marketing: subscribers, tags, fields, events incl. $purchase, stats, draft/scheduled broadcasts and transactional email, with dry-run + human-approval gates on every send. Native Python plugin, no dependencies. Disclosure — sends real email (bento_email_send, bento_broadcast_schedule), and events, purchases and consent changes can trigger Bento Flows that email people; calls only app.bentonow.com (an operator base_url override is limited to https *.bentonow.com or loopback) with the BENTO_* keys from the profile .env; no telemetry, no self-update; T2/T3 calls go to the Hermes approval prompt, which asks no human under YOLO, approvals.mode off, or cron/single-query/unattended mode set to approve. T3 sends then still need a dry-run confirm token and hard guards, but T2 writes (events, purchases, consent, bulk upserts) need no token unless safety.tier2 is token_only; T1 writes (tags, tag/field definitions, drafts, upserts up to bulk_threshold) are never gated and still run under environment=disabled; environment=staging does not block sends, only environment=disabled blocks T2/T3.

entries.name: better-capabilities
entries.description: Delete and package skills, browse their markdown files, and save per-profile on/off presets from one Settings page. Disclosure — deleting a skill from its page moves the skill folder out of `<HERMES_HOME>/skills` (on Windows to the Recycle Bin by running `powershell.exe`, elsewhere to `<HERMES_HOME>/better-capabilities-trash/`); applying a preset switches skills, toolsets and agent plugins on or off, including for other profiles the preset names.

entries.name: better-session-appearance
entries.description: Set a color for each session and show an idle glyph to make rows easier to scan.

entries.name: betterdb
entries.description: BetterDB long-term memory provider — semantic recall on Valkey / valkey-search via the betterdb-agent-memory SDK. Completed turns are embedded and stored in a vector index; the next turn recalls the most relevant memories with a composite similarity/recency/importance score. Explicit betterdb_remember / betterdb_recall / betterdb_forget tools. Disclosure — turn text and tool-stored facts are embedded through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint you configure (embeddings_base_url, default api.openai.com) and written to the Valkey instance you point it at; plaintext http:// to a remote host is refused. Opt-in, off by default: a discovery marker (set discovery=true to let BetterDB Monitor enumerate the tier) and SDK usage analytics (set telemetry=true).

entries.name: bharatcode-provider
entries.description: BharatCode (bharatcode.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider — free student tier, native /model integration. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and BHARATCODE_API_KEY go to bharatcode.ai (BharatCode, India), which processes prompts through third-party inference partners, some outside India; outside paid Pro (complimentary or referral Pro included) BharatCode may retain private prompt/response logs for debugging, abuse review and product quality, and even on paid Pro a flagged account can have a time-limited sample of up to 100 prompts and responses captured for security review.

entries.name: bilinc
entries.title: Bilinc
entries.description: Hosted memory for Hermes with a full history: see what your agent remembered, when it changed and why. Recalls relevant memories before each turn, adds bilinc_recall, bilinc_remember, bilinc_revise and bilinc_forget tools, and mirrors Hermes built-in memory writes. Maintained by ReARC Labs; free plan available. Disclosure — recall queries (the text of each message, when auto_recall is on), tool arguments, mirrored built-in memory writes, the Hermes session id and, only if memory.bilinc.capture_turns is turned on, each turn's user and assistant text are sent over HTTPS to bilinc.space under your BILINC_API_KEY; requests carry User-Agent bilinc-hermes/<version> and X-Bilinc-Client: hermes-plugin headers. Secret-looking strings are redacted before sending. Recall and writes run on background threads inside Hermes; no separate process, local database or telemetry.

entries.name: billing
entries.description: Nous Portal usage widget for the Hermes desktop statusbar — remaining credits plus plan-usage percentage, with portal detail on hover.

entries.name: biomimetic-brain
entries.description: Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

entries.name: birkin-mnemosyne
entries.description: Local Markdown memory provider with multilingual lexical recall and profile-local durable notes. Writes are limited to primary agent contexts: create-only notes plus preview-by-default archive and restore, which never delete files. Uses published birkin-mnemosyne 0.9.0 with compatible updates below 1.0; no API key, network service or telemetry. Session handoff capture is opt-in. Native Hermes memory files remain separate.

entries.name: blackbox
entries.title: Agent Blackbox
entries.description: Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `hermes blackbox setup` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Hermes homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `hermes blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700.

entries.name: blender
entries.title: Blender
entries.description: Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Needs Git and uv; Blender 5.1+ is not needed at install. The skill opens Blender itself when a task needs it and, after you agree, installs Blender and Blender Lab's MCP add-on. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; the skill starts Blender with online access for that session only (your saved preference is unchanged), and the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password, so any program on this computer can use it while Blender is open; only after you agree does the skill download Blender from download.blender.org (about 400 MB, about 1.5 GB unpacked), check it against blender.org's sha256 list and install it in your own folder without administrator rights (Linux ~/.local/opt, macOS ~/Applications, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation; never over an existing Blender), and download the v1.0.3 add-on, check its hash and install or enable it; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.

entries.name: blinkenbar
entries.description: Dense, animated supercomputer light banks driven by system telemetry and live agent activity in Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: boardstate
entries.title: Boardstate
entries.description: A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live Hermes data, in the dashboard and Hermes Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/HERMES_NODE_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under HERMES_HOME/boardstate-state/. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from Hermes internals (web_server._SESSION_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

entries.name: bot-activity
entries.title: Bot Activity
entries.description: Live per-Bot activity timeline for Hermes Desktop: turns, tool calls (arguments, result, duration), approvals and Group Chat streams, grouped by Bot or by Group Chat, with one-click tracking for new Bots. Disclosure — local only, no network or telemetry; records every Bot profile's turns, assistant replies, tool arguments and results, approval commands and Group Chat streams (redacted with agent.redact, capped per field, 3-day / 20k-row retention) into one SQLite file shared by all profiles under plugin-data/bot-activity; reads each Bot profile's state.db, profile.yaml and config.yaml read-only; Track now / Update runs `hermes -p <bot> plugins install <same source> --ref <same sha> --enable --yes-deps` (or copies the plugin and runs `plugins enable`) in the Bot profiles you track, never re-enabling one you disabled.

entries.name: bot-cabinet-v2
entries.title: Cabinet
entries.description: Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a Hermes profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that Hermes's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates Hermes profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.hermes/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private Hermes modules (hermes_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a Hermes update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

entries.name: bot-forge
entries.description: Say "make me a <role>" and your agent spawns a complete Bot Mode Bot — name, face, SOUL.md, memory, tools, skills, routines, gateway — tested, with rollback. Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. Disclosure — spawns the hermes CLI to create and run Bot profiles under HERMES_HOME/profiles/, and installs its own small companion hook plugin (bot-forge-marks, two hooks, no tools) into each Bot profile it manages, enabling it in that profile's config.yaml; never the root profile. Disclosure — when a Bot journals a blocked/failed entry, the plugin emails its title and summary to your own address via the SMTP account in Hermes' EMAIL_* settings (TLS verified; off with notify_blocked or notify_email false); adopt_bots (off by default) installs the companion hook into every profile on load.

entries.name: brain-graph
entries.description: Local Markdown vault for Hermes Desktop — notes, wikilinks, search, recycle bin, and an interactive graph.

entries.name: brave-search
entries.description: Brave Search API tools for live web search inside Hermes

entries.name: breeze-tts
entries.title: Breeze Blue TTS
entries.description: Breeze Blue text-to-speech as a Hermes voice provider (tts.provider: breeze-blue), driven by the Breeze Blue Developer API. Voices come from the Breeze console — stock, cloned or designed — and the provider speaks whole replies through text_to_speech and read-aloud, with mp3 (default), wav, flac, opus, aac or pcm output, so Opus voice notes work on messaging platforms. No new Python dependencies: the plugin posts directly to the ElevenLabs-shaped endpoint. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice id and model, and your BREEZE_API_KEY (header xi-api-key) to api.breeze.blue, or to BREEZE_BASE_URL when you set it; synthesis is billed to your Breeze Blue account; generated audio is written to Hermes's audio cache; the text is not logged; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry. Not implemented: realtime/WebSocket streaming (voice-mode replies are spoken sentence by sentence instead) and voice listing.

entries.name: brethof-brain
entries.description: brethof-brain long-term memory provider — the memory's briefing in the system prompt at session start, ambient recall on every turn, every turn archived; one memory shared with the user's other agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more). Sends each turn to the user's own brethof-brain memory (on their machine at 127.0.0.1:8610, or hosted at memory.brethof.cloud). Needs a brethof-brain account. Disclosure — sends every user prompt and each turn's user and assistant text, with your API key, to the brethof-brain server you configure (default a local box at 127.0.0.1:8610; hosted at memory.brethof.cloud), and puts the server's returned briefing and recall text into the system prompt and each turn; reads BRETHOF_BRAIN_* from $HERMES_HOME/.env and ~/.brethof-brain/config.json.

entries.name: bridge-adapter
entries.description: Generic JSON-file-based bridge adapter. Bridges self-register via a registry/ manifest (presence = registered, rm = unregistered). Polls inbox/ for incoming messages, writes outgoing to outbox/. External services (imsg, Matrix, Telegram, ...) write/read JSON files in a shared directory.

entries.name: browser-toggle
entries.description: One titlebar button, next to HUD mode, that opens and hides the built-in browser: the same action as Ctrl+Shift+L. Label follows the active UI language. Front-end only: no agent calls, no network, no API keys. Disclosure — works by pressing the browser shortcut (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+L); breaks if the user rebinds it.

entries.name: browserless
entries.title: Browserless
entries.description: Run Hermes' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Hermes' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-hermes-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.

entries.name: browserpaw
entries.description: Drive your own Chrome from Hermes through a BrowserPaw MCP server you configure: 16 browserpaw_* tools for navigation, indexed DOM reading, click/fill, batch actions, screenshots and tabs. Disclosure — a thin wrapper over a BrowserPaw MCP server you add yourself (mcp_servers.browserpaw, plus plugins.entries.browserpaw.mcp_allowlist: [browserpaw]); it drives your real Chrome profile (logged-in sessions, cookies) through the separately installed BrowserPaw extension and native host on 127.0.0.1:12306, whose credential lives in ~/.chrome-mcp/bridge-token; the agent can click, fill, submit and read pages without a Hermes approval prompt unless you set trust: untrusted on that server (the README sample enables the full 50-tool profile, including in-page JavaScript, HttpOnly cookie reads and raw CDP, as native Hermes MCP tools); the optional Jev remote mode sends structured page state to TypeSafe AI or a base URL you set, and its local model download contacts hf-mirror.com/aifasthub.com/huggingface.co (probing baidu.com/bilibili.com first).

entries.name: bubblewrap
entries.description: Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), the dot entries of the home directory (credential stores always) and the Hermes home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`hermes config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) run inside the sandbox too, and because the working directory is a real host directory Hermes keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.

entries.name: bunny_space-platform
entries.title: Bunny Space
entries.description: Bunny Space gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects a Hermes profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to Hermes under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

entries.name: burnclock
entries.title: Burnclock
entries.description: Status-bar chip showing the provider balance and runway tracked by the MIT burnclock CLI, read from its local badge cache. Requires the CLI (pip install burnclock); the plugin makes no network calls and reads no credentials. Disclosure — runs a read-only shell command (cat of burnclock's local cache file) in your active local session every 60 seconds; balances come from the separately installed burnclock CLI (PyPI `burnclock`), which you configure with your provider keys and run yourself.

entries.name: by2kb
entries.description: Discover learning videos by topic, select numbered recommendations, and turn Bilibili and YouTube videos into transcripts, abstracts, and study notes using the Hermes host model. Disclosure — intercepts gateway messages with a Bilibili/YouTube URL, a "by2kb <topic>" prefix, or (for 1 h after a recommendation list, same user/chat) a bare number reply, and runs the separately installed by2kb CLI (BY2KB_COMMAND or PATH), which searches Bilibili/YouTube, downloads media and runs ASR; enrichment prompts go to your active Hermes model.

entries.name: cadence
entries.title: Cadence
entries.description: Local usage page: year heatmap, streaks from days a chat was used, model and place breakdowns, and this week against last week. Disclosure — reads the selected profile state.db read-only and runs the local cadence command through Hermes cli.exec. No network calls, secrets, telemetry, or provider logins. Not a fork of hermes-activity.

entries.name: call-me
entries.title: /call-me
entries.description: /call-me gateway: text your Hermes agent from the /call-me iPhone app, and the callme_call tool rings your phone, speaks the agent's text and returns your spoken answer as a transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the /call-me service at https://callmemcp.com/aiphone (run by the plugin author): creates one agent session, sends texts and call requests, and long-polls for replies while the gateway runs (at most one request every 3 seconds); sends message text, the text to be spoken and the destination numbers, and call audio is transcribed by the service so only the transcript comes back; the agent session token and event cursor are stored at $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/call-me/session.json (mode 600); only numbers in CALLME_ALLOWED_USERS can message the agent or be called, and inbound messages must come from that number's verified /call-me device; callme_call blocks until the call ends (300 seconds at most) and returns missed if nobody answers; no shell commands, telemetry or self-update. The /call-me iPhone app that receives the messages and calls needs a paid subscription; the plugin itself is free and MIT-licensed.

entries.name: calling-mom
entries.title: Calling mom
entries.description: Lets a cheap model run your Kanban board and calls a stronger model only where the board or the tool results show it is needed. Mom (a good, affordable model) answers stuck signals, risky commands and completion checks; olymp (the expensive heavyweight) is asked only when mom escalates a rare high-stakes case, with hard limits per card and per day. Disclosure — once enabled, the plugin observes every kanban worker tool result (hashes and counts only, logged to logs/calling-mom.jsonl). With the advisor enabled AND a board or card opted in, redacted run excerpts go through Hermes's ctx.llm to the mom and olymp models you choose; the answer is appended to the tool result and written to the card with the public kanban_comment tool. A card line verify: <command> runs an allowlisted command (no shell, scrubbed environment) for cards created by trusted creators. hermes calling-mom setup writes the plugin's own config (calling_mom.* and its plugins.entries allowlist) with the values you pick, reads delegation.backends.model_map (read-only, to offer your Advanced Delegation routes) and creates one cron job, 'calling-mom: sweep', unless you pass --no-cron; the sweep reads the kanban databases and may push metrics to Pushgateway URLs you configure (off by default). No telemetry, no credentials stored.

entries.name: camel-guard
entries.title: CaMeL Guard
entries.description: Gate sensitive tools on trusted user capabilities after untrusted tool output.

entries.name: camofox-human-auth
entries.description: Universal human-controlled authentication for Camofox Browser, powered by the Camoufox engine. Supports login, registration, SSO, MFA, OTP, CAPTCHA, and device confirmation. Requires the Camofox backend; never changes an existing Hermes browser provider automatically.

entries.name: camofox
entries.description: Camofox browser backend: browse with a self-hosted anti-detection Firefox (Camoufox, C++ fingerprint spoofing) through the camofox-browser REST server. Registers the browser_* tools (navigate, snapshot with clickable refs, click, type, scroll, back, press, get_images, vision, JavaScript console, plus cookie import when CAMOFOX_API_KEY is set) in the `camofox` toolset, with `hermes camofox setup|status`; existing CAMOFOX_* variables and browser.camofox settings carry over. Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure: one Python dependency (requests). It talks only to the Camofox server at CAMOFOX_URL (e.g. http://localhost:9377, which you run yourself: Docker or `npm start`), sending CAMOFOX_API_KEY as a bearer token when set. Page text reaches only your model as tool output; browser_vision sends the screenshot to your configured auxiliary vision model. Snapshots mask values that look like secrets (API keys, tokens), but text typed into form fields, passwords included, shows up in snapshots. Oversized snapshots and screenshots are written under the Hermes home (cache/web, browser_screenshots). Cookie import reads Netscape cookies.txt files only from browser.camofox.cookies_dir (default ~/.camofox/cookies). browser_vault fills saved passwords on the Camofox tab (sent only to a loopback or HTTPS CAMOFOX_URL). Inert on Hermes cores that still bundle Camofox.

entries.name: canadian-primary-care
entries.title: Canadian Primary Care
entries.description: Twenty-six offline Canadian-unit clinician decision-support calculators (preview). Disclosure — clinician decision-support calculators, not a regulator-reviewed medical device; runs fully offline with no network calls, stores only your favourites list in Desktop plugin storage, Copy puts the result on the system clipboard, and source citations open in your browser when clicked.

entries.name: carbonvoice-platform
entries.description: Carbon Voice gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects via Socket.IO (primary) with REST polling fallback — no public webhook or tunnel required. Persists a cursor to disk so messages received while Hermes is offline are processed on the next startup. Replies via POST /v3/messages/start, so the Her

entries.name: cartograph
entries.title: Cartograph
entries.description: Map local repositories and retrieve task-focused source excerpts with line references. Disclosure — runs the separately installed Cartograph Node CLI (no shell, bounded time/output, credential-free env) against any local directory the model names unless `allowed_roots` is set, returns source excerpts into the conversation, and caches excerpts in the plugin data directory.

entries.name: cashew
entries.description: Cashew — persistent thought-graph memory with local embeddings, organic decay, and autonomous think cycles.

entries.name: catalogo-it
entries.title: Plugin Catalog (Italian)
entries.description: The official Hermes plugin catalog in a native page (sidebar entry, route /catalogo, plus a command-palette entry) with an Italian interface and on-the-fly Italian descriptions: Google Translate first, MyMemory as a second public source, and a final fallback to the user's own local llama.cpp model. Disclosure — it fetches the public catalog feed (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) and, when you open a plugin entry, sends that entry's English description to translate.googleapis.com (Google Translate's keyless public endpoint) and, if that fails, to api.mymemory.translated.net; nothing else leaves the machine. It reads no credentials or Hermes files, and its backend route is empty. Translation runs when a plugin entry is opened, not for the whole catalog. No telemetry. UI is Italian-first with an English bundle.

entries.name: cdp-manager
entries.description: Local Chrome CDP debug ports in the status bar (probe, launch, stop, recheck) plus a managed port Hermes keeps alive and the `cdp` agent tool, which also detects and repairs a Chrome profile-picker launch (wedged/unwedge). Disclosure: launches local Chrome on 127.0.0.1 only, with per-port profiles under the local app-data directory, and closes it with a clean Browser.close; state lives in the plugin's own config file. Windows only.

entries.name: certarc
entries.title: CertArc
entries.description: Practise free scenario questions for the CISM, CISSP, CISA, AAISM and AAIA exams in Hermes, with an explanation for every option. No account or keys. Also covers exam outlines and CertArc study guides, and can link to CertArc's free assessment when you finish a set. Bundles the certarc-practice skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to certarc.com through its free no-sign-in endpoint (https://certarc.com/mcp/grok), whose tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill's assessment links carry a utm source tag, and the user opens them and signs in themselves.

entries.name: channel3
entries.title: Channel3
entries.description: Shop 100M+ products across thousands of US retailers: search, compare every store's live price, and switch variants (color, size) on inline product cards in Hermes Desktop. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted Channel3 MCP server at mcp.trychannel3.com (no account or key; free tier rate-limited per IP); search queries (and any image URL for visual search), product ids and variant selections go to it, and the Desktop cards call it directly from the app; a server-issued thread_id links searches within a conversation; product images load from cdn.trychannel3.com; Buy buttons open buy.trychannel3.com redirect links in the browser; nothing is purchased in-app and no credentials are stored.

entries.name: chat-length
entries.title: Chat Length
entries.description: Tells the user when a chat is getting too long and hands them a short opener for a fresh chat; the new chat pulls the earlier context itself via session_search, no handover document. Fill level from real provider token counts, measured against Hermes' compaction point by default; notices at 70 % and 90 % (configurable), once each per chat, re-armed after compaction, never in cron, subagent, kanban, batch or webhook runs. Notice in the conversation language, English or German. Disclosure — on the turn that crosses a threshold, pre_llm_call adds a one-turn instruction to that turn's user message (never the system prompt; replayed byte-identical, so prompt caching stays intact); post_api_request stores per-session token counts, model and provider name and which notice fired (no message content) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/chat-length/, pruned after 30 days; reads the session title read-only from state.db and the compression settings read-only from config.yaml; no network calls, no tools, no dependencies.

entries.name: chat-studio
entries.description: Offline conversation customization with one-click presets and plugin-owned settings. Disclosure — enabled by default; injects a stylesheet that restyles the Desktop chat transcript (width, fonts, spacing, optional colours) keyed on app data-slot selectors, so a Desktop update can break the styling; settings stay in plugin storage, no network.

entries.name: chatto-platform
entries.description: Chatto gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a Chatto server (self-hosted team chat) and relays messages between rooms/DMs and the Hermes agent.  Uses the Chatto ConnectRPC API (JSON over HTTP) for outbound messages and the Chatto realtime WebSocket protocol (binary protobuf) for inbound eve

entries.name: cheatsheet
entries.description: Title-bar cheatsheet. Describe what you want to do and it points to a real command or a cited passage; live slash commands and plugins, plus cited passages from this install's docs. No runtime network. No self-update. Disclosure — reads the Markdown docs shipped with your Hermes install (website/docs next to hermes_cli) through a local dashboard route and lists your commands, plugins and MCP servers via read-only gateway calls; no network at runtime (doc and GitHub links open in your browser only when clicked).

entries.name: chmod-ref
entries.description: @chmod: context references that explain a file permission mode for the model: @chmod:<mode> takes an octal mode (755, 0755, 4755), ls -l text (-rwsr-xr-x, with the file type letter and a trailing + . or @) or an st_mode as stat and git write it (100644), and attaches both forms, each class's rights in words (directory rights named as such), what setuid, setgid and the sticky bit do and where they are ignored, and notes such as a mode everyone can change, one private to the owner, or a class holding rights the class before it lacks; @chmod:"644 u+x,go-w" applies a symbolic change step by step the way GNU chmod does (u g o a, + - =, r w x X s t, copies like u=g), @chmod:"100644 100755" shows what changes between two modes, and @chmod:"umask 027" shows what new files and directories get; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a mode as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's re; it never looks at a file on disk; no network, no files read or written, no permission changed, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what you write, but the @chmod: reference and the explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @chmod: reference provider.

entries.name: chorepilot
entries.title: ChorePilot
entries.description: Your house and family chore board as Hermes tools, through ChorePilot's own MCP server on this machine, the LAN or Tailscale. Runs appliances (lights, climate, dishwasher/washer/dryer, sprinklers, vacuum and more via Home Assistant, Home Connect, MQTT or a simulator) and keeps a rotating chore board that devices verify. ChorePilot's policy decides every call: water/heat actions wait for the person's own yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent's approval queue, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available to an agent. Bundles the chorepilot:household skill. Disclosure — each tool call sends HTTP requests with the bearer token in CHOREPILOT_TOKEN to the user's own ChorePilot server at CHOREPILOT_URL, and the plugin also lists that server's tools once at every Hermes start (plain http only to loopback, private, Tailscale or .local/.lan/.ts.net addresses); chorepilot_call runs any device or chore tool the token's person may use (lights, climate, vacuum, locking and more) without a Hermes approval prompt, with ChorePilot's own policy deciding, so water/heat actions wait up to two minutes for that person's yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available; no other network calls, no files read outside the plugin, no background processes, no telemetry, stdlib only.

entries.name: chrome-tab-watchdog
entries.title: Chrome Tab Watchdog
entries.description: Conservative Chrome tab cleanup with in-process observation and browser-call leases. Disclosure — runs a background thread inside Hermes that proxies your local Chrome DevTools port (127.0.0.1:9222 → 127.0.0.1:9223, loopback only, you must point browser.cdp_url at it), injects a focus/activity listener into every Chrome page, rewrites browser_exec session names to a per-profile namespace, and a cron script you schedule auto-closes idle, duplicate and blank tabs (including tabs with unsaved text).

entries.name: chronicle
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Hermes — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.hermes/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

entries.name: chutes-provider
entries.description: Chutes model provider for Hermes Agent via API key. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CHUTES_API_KEY go to llm.chutes.ai (or CHUTES_BASE_URL), plus a GET /models catalog probe with the same key

entries.name: cjk_sanitizer
entries.description: Strip unwanted Chinese (CJK) and Cyrillic characters from LLM output. Korean Hangul and Japanese Kana are preserved.

entries.name: clack
entries.description: Encrypted agent-to-agent messaging with durable receipts and no plaintext fallback. Disclosure — sends your agent's signed identity, relay service token and end-to-end-encrypted messages the model writes to the configured Clack relay (default relay.tryclack.com); messages received from peers are untrusted input handed to the model, and their decrypted text is kept indefinitely in plugin-data/clack; Linux/macOS only.

entries.name: claude-code-theme
entries.title: Claude Code Theme
entries.description: Unofficial Claude Code-inspired theme for Hermes Desktop, with light and dark palettes, rounded composer and side-panel cards, softer sidebar and menus, and a context-window meter beside the model switcher. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic or Claude Code. Disclosure — unofficial Claude Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles native Desktop surfaces (user bubbles, composer, file panel, sidebar rows, dropdown menus) and hides the chat backdrop image; the context meter reads session.usage through the SDK; an opt-in accent setting uses setAccentOverride; no network calls of its own.

entries.name: claude-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Experimental model provider that runs Hermes turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. Requires the claude CLI installed and logged in; the plugin checks for it at load, in hermes model, in the pickers and before every request, and refuses cleanly with the install hint when it is missing. Disclosure — every turn is billed against your Claude subscription's Agent SDK allowance, and the provider inherits whatever account claude is logged into.

entries.name: cli-session-tabs
entries.title: CLI Session Tabs
entries.description: Directory-scoped native TUI tabs when the public core capability contract is advertised, with isolated tmux fallback. Disclosure — the tmux backend requires OS-installed tmux; explicit `hermes tabs` commands probe the Hermes CLI (`--help`, `--tui-capabilities`) and start private, long-running TUI or tmux/Hermes clients only when invoked, passing the selected profile and the current terminal's pane identity through a credential/bypass-filtered environment; the tmux backend stores non-secret workspace metadata in profile plugin-data and confirms closes; native-tab persistence stays in core. Does not patch Hermes or read conversations/credentials.

entries.name: clinepass
entries.description: ClinePass model provider with live model discovery and a curated fallback catalog.

entries.name: cliproxyapi-provider
entries.description: CLIProxyAPI as native Hermes model providers: discovers each CPA provider group (Claude, Codex, xAI, Gemini, Kiro and others) and registers one profile per group on the wire its CPA executor accepts (Anthropic Messages, Responses or Chat Completions), with context windows and reasoning levels from CPA. Disclosure — sends model-list and inference requests, authenticated with the API key env var you name, to the CPA base_url you configure; with an optional management key it also makes bounded read-only GETs to CPA's management API; with an optional billing route it sends inference, and a model-list GET, to the gateway URL you configure, authenticated with the gateway key env var you name. Known limit: Hermes strips from agent subprocesses only the key env vars a registered provider declares, so the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, stay readable by agent shells.

entries.name: cloudflare-sandbox
entries.description: Run Hermes terminal, file and execute_code tools in Cloudflare Containers, with the workspace saved to a snapshot when idle. Disclosure — you deploy the bundled Cloudflare Worker to your own account first; running containers is billed by Cloudflare; commands and file contents run in the container at HERMES_CF_ENDPOINT using HERMES_CF_TOKEN; the container has outbound internet by default (ENABLE_INTERNET); host env vars, skills and credentials are not copied into the container; dangerous-command approval stays on.

entries.name: cloudflare-web-search
entries.title: Cloudflare Web Search
entries.description: Cloudflare Web Search backend for Hermes' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. Disclosure — sends queries, result limits, gateway IDs, and optional BYOK aliases to api.cloudflare.com, which forwards searches to the selected provider and records them in AI Gateway logs.
