Requests can consume gateway credits or provider quota. Reads its own settings and CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN through Hermes' profile-scoped APIs. Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin.

entries.name: cloudflare-workers-ai-provider
entries.description: Cloudflare Workers AI as a Hermes model provider (`--provider workers-ai`, or Cloudflare Workers AI in `hermes model`, which asks for the token and the account's base URL): the 16 Workers AI models with function calling and 64K+ context, Cloudflare's context windows (a custom endpoint lists no models and assumes 256K for the 128K gpt-oss), reasoning effort in the form each model accepts, and a clear message when a free-plan account picks a paid-plan model. Not affiliated with Cloudflare. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); the model list and details are built in, so nothing is fetched to show them; chat requests go to the URL in CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL through Hermes' own client with CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN, both read by Hermes per profile; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: cloudgpu-provider
entries.title: CloudGPU
entries.description: cloudgpu.app models (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax) via the OpenAI-compatible API at cloudgpu.app/v1: live model list from the public /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CLOUDGPU_API_KEY go to cloudgpu.app (or to CLOUDGPU_BASE_URL when the user sets it).

entries.name: coder
entries.description: Run Hermes terminal commands in an existing remote Coder workspace. Disclosure — runs terminal commands inside your Coder workspace at CODER_URL using CODER_API_KEY; starts a stopped workspace automatically; forwards only the env vars you list in TERMINAL_CODER_FORWARD_ENV.

entries.name: codex-chat-look
entries.description: Independent Catppuccin Latte/Mocha desktop theme with peach accents, SDK-native gateway/profile switching and host-owned session density. Legacy plugin identity: codex-chat-look. No self-updater or native layout overrides. Disclosure — Desktop theme derived from FPSUnleashed's MIT-licensed desktop skin; switches gateway/profile via host.ensureAgent only on user selection and a palette command rewrites the native sessionListDensity setting; no network calls of its own.

entries.name: codex-theme
entries.title: Codex Theme
entries.description: Codex × ChatGPT inspired theme for the Hermes Desktop chat: dual light/dark palettes that follow the system appearance, graphite-on-paper typography with a 1.625 root line height (measured from ZCode's chat body) and content-spacing presets (1.5/1.625/1.75), the OpenAI radius scale (inline 4px / rows 8px / controls 10px / cards 12px / composer 20px), hairline borders instead of shadows, and an 880px reading column with 768/880/992px presets. Settings → Plugins → Codex Theme offers appearance mode, reading width, content spacing, text & code font presets, user/assistant chat bubble colors and a bilingual (EN/中文) UI as native controls; the theme paints theme-level tokens only and never writes user-configurable settings such as --chat-text-scale. v1.2.0 is a compliance release — the composer-drag and input-focus-guard features of the v1.1 line were removed because they patched prototypes and captured global events, which catalog rule 8 forbids. Disclosure — no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials; registers only through the Desktop plugin SDK (THEMES_AREA, PALETTE_AREA, ctx.registerSettingsPage, ctx.i18n), switches the active theme to Codex once on first install, and keeps its preferences in plugin-scoped ctx.storage.

entries.name: codex-truly
entries.title: Codex Truly
entries.description: Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Hermes only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through Hermes's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.

entries.name: cognee
entries.description: Knowledge-graph memory for Hermes, shared with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins: automatic recall, remember, forget, recaps and code search, on Cognee Cloud or a local cognee server. Disclosure — in local mode it installs cognee==1.6.5 and its dependencies (about 1 GB from PyPI) into a private environment, ~/.cognee-plugin/hermes/runtime, when you choose local mode (`hermes memory setup cognee` or `hermes cognee install-runtime`; never at session start), and runs a local cognee server from it (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011); a session-close watcher runs in the background; each turn plus its tool calls and results (redacted, capped) go to that server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default), or to Cognee Cloud / COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode; turns the server could not take are queued in ~/.cognee-plugin; the store lives in ~/.cognee, outside HERMES_HOME and shared across profiles and with Cognee's Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw plugins; cognee sends anonymous telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; the system prompt tells the agent to prefer Cognee memory over MEMORY.md/USER.md (COGNEE_MEMORY_STEER=false turns it off), and an answer that used recalled memory may end with a one-line Cognee credit, drawn with the Cognee logo by a transform_llm_output hook (COGNEE_PLUGIN_CITE_MEMORY=off turns it off).

entries.name: cognition
entries.description: Cognition session-end memory — facts regex-extracted from your messages at session end, stored in a local SQLite queue and JSON log under one repo label, with fetch-first merge, per-entry provenance, and budgeted prefetch (tools: cognition_search, cognition_status, read-only cognition_dream). Disclosure — saves verbatim excerpts (up to 400 chars) of your own messages that match preference/decision phrases in plain local files under HERMES_HOME/cognition/ (SQLite queue, JSON commit log) and re-injects them into later prompts sent to your model provider; the author name is read from ~/.gitconfig; the plugin makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: colorado-traffic
entries.description: Live Colorado highway events from CDOT COtrip. No API key. Default corridor is I-70 Golden to east Denver. Separates incidents happening now from scheduled work and unverified Waze reports.

entries.name: comfyrizz
entries.title: Comfyrizz
entries.description: Chat-as-frontend for the Comfyrizz film pipeline: brief, plan, revise, explicit accept, generate, CPU assemble, export, and retake. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, stdio mcp.json, comfyrizz-film skill) with the MCP server in-tree. Disclosure — the stdio server launches local Node that talks only to a loopback Comfyrizz engine URL (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL); optional Streamable HTTP binds 127.0.0.1 only when deliberately enabled and has no authentication, so any local process or web page in your browser can call its tools while it runs. Paid generation (Google Colab, Comfy API, or ComfyUI) is dispatched by the agent with an approval id it reads from the engine's spend card; the bundled skill tells the model to get your explicit yes first, but Hermes itself does not prompt before paid generation or retakes. Env vars are forwarded as ${VAR} from the user environment (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL, COMFYRIZZ_MCP_HTTP, COMFYRIZZ_TOKEN, and optional provider keys); no credentials are stored in the package. No self-updater.

entries.name: command-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the slash commands you run in Hermes (built-in commands in the CLI, built-in and plugin commands on messaging platforms): /command-log shows how often each command was used, its share, in how many sessions and when last, per command, platform, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /command-log recent lists the newest commands (ten, or up to 100 with /command-log recent 50) with the alias typed. Disclosure — writes command metadata (command name, alias typed, surface, platform, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no arguments, session key or user id) to plugin-data/command-ledger/commands.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot block or change a command; no network

entries.name: command-tray
entries.description: Session command tray — shell commands the Hermes agent ran via the terminal tool (success and failure). Desktop pane and /commands. No API keys. Disclosure — records terminal commands with exit code, workdir and a 160-char redacted output preview to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/command-tray/state.json; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API) with clipboard fallback; no network.

entries.name: commandcode-oauth
entries.description: Command Code CLI-key model provider with a live OAuth catalog property bridge, plan limits and failover classification. Disclosure — uses the CLI-internal api.commandcode.ai/alpha/generate endpoint and CLI client headers, sends the full conversation, tool schemas, cwd path and OS/Python version, and imports a static key from the read-only CLI credential file or a browser hand-off; no OAuth exchange takes place. Hermes also bundles commandcode for the documented Provider API.

entries.name: comment-scraper
entries.title: Comment Scraper
entries.description: Ask about the Reddit and Hacker News threads you exported with the Comment Scraper browser extension: list, read, search and quote them by comment number. Disclosure — starts a local stdio MCP server with npx -y comment-scraper-mcp@0.1.0, which npx downloads from npm on first run; the server only reads JSON exports in ~/Downloads and the folders directly inside it, never writes files, makes no network requests, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: compartment
entries.description: Encrypted, fully offline memory provider. AEAD-encrypted local vault (vectors included), bundled embedding model, exact hybrid search, no API key and no network at runtime. One vault shared with Claude, Cursor and any other MCP client on the machine. Disclosure — installs the full compartment engine (about 27 Python packages including onnxruntime, tokenizers, mcp and system-tray dependencies) into the Hermes venv; the provider's system prompt instructs the model to store passwords and API keys in the encrypted vault.

entries.name: completion-sound
entries.title: Completion Sound
entries.description: Pick the sound Hermes Desktop plays when a turn finishes: one of the 14 built-in presets or your own audio file (mp3, wav, ogg), with an optional different sound during night hours. Files stay in the plugin's local storage. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: composer-modes
entries.description: Cursor-style composer modes (ask / agent / plan / debug) for the Hermes desktop — the mode's operating note reaches the model inside the turn's model-facing bytes, never the bubble, transcript or session titles, and ask mode is enforced read-only on the tool side.

entries.name: composio-connections
entries.title: Composio Connections
entries.description: Connect and disconnect Composio accounts from Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard. Lists every row the Composio CLI returns, including expired, duplicate, and unaliased accounts, opens OAuth in the user's browser, and disconnects one exact account after confirmation. No agent tools or hooks. Catalog metadata uses COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY through agent.secret_scope.get_secret and requests only https://backend.composio.dev. Disclosure — inventory, connect, and disconnect run the composio CLI already logged in on the gateway; the API key never reaches the browser. Removing a Composio connection does not revoke every permission at the provider. The bundled service logos include an Ngrok mark; the plugin does not open a tunnel.

entries.name: constraint-vault
entries.description: Pins the user exact constraints (numbers, addresses, hard rules) as structured local data and re-injects them verbatim into the model context on every turn and immediately after every context compaction, with a SHA-256 hash-logged injection record, because memory providers and compression silently paraphrase or drop exact values. Not a memory provider and not a compressor: a guard layer above both. Disclosure — local code only, no network or processes; stores constraints in constraint-vault.json in the Hermes home and appends a hash record to constraint-vault-injections.jsonl on every turn; the model can pin or drop constraints through its own tools without asking, and pinned text is injected into the model context on every turn of every session until dropped.

entries.name: context-audit
entries.description: Context-window forensics: per-turn input/output token estimates, the single largest tool output of each turn, oversized tool calls (args over 50 KB), and compaction events, recorded as metadata only (tool name, byte length, ids, timestamps — never args or results) in a local SQLite DB under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/context-audit/. Adds a /context-audit slash command that prints the top 5 context eaters over a window with one mitigation per entry.

entries.name: conxt
entries.title: Conxt
entries.description: Conxt governed memory provider — recall before each turn (personal, plus a team's approved memories), conversation capture in batches, and tools to search, remember, and propose team memories that a person approves in Conxt before anyone recalls them. Disclosure — Each turn's message (first 500 characters) and the conversation's user and assistant messages are sent to the Conxt API at mcp.conxt.dev (or an https CONXT_BASE_URL you set) with your CONXT_API_KEY; tool results are not sent, but text the assistant repeats is. Every entry Hermes's built-in memory tool adds is also copied to your Conxt memory, and conxt_remember / conxt_propose send the memory text they are given. No telemetry, no shell commands, and nothing is written automatically from cron or subagent runs. Requires a Conxt plan that includes API keys.

entries.name: coreweave
entries.description: Run Hermes on CoreWeave Serverless Inference with live model discovery, streaming responses, and an OpenAI-compatible API. Disclosure — Hermes sends model discovery and chat requests, including prompts and tool results, to https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1 (CoreWeave / W&B Inference) using COREWEAVE_API_KEY; the installed provider registers a profile only and reads no credential files, starts no processes and adds no telemetry.

entries.name: corpus
entries.description: Hosted Corpus MCP (Streamable HTTP at corpuslaw.us/api/mcp) plus two bundled skills: US law search/get_node/list_coverage over 571k+ provisions, and LLC/nonprofit formation intake (requirements, compare, NAICS lookup, handoff, USDC checkout, payment_status), with account.status for quota. Filing always stays human-gated and USDC pay is email-confirmed. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); no API key needed for anonymous research. The formation skill requires fixed vendor-authored marketing copy in the first reply and before payment, and sends founder PII (name, email, phone, address) to Corpus through links and MCP tools. Intake instructions are vendored; checkout requires exact-amount confirmation from the user in the current turn.

entries.name: cortexlayer
entries.description: CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into Hermes' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence Hermes' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.

entries.name: cost-sentinel
entries.description: Live cost ledger and daily budget guarddog for Hermes Agent, per profile or fleet-wide — every LLM call is priced with Hermes' own pricing engine into a per-profile SQLite ledger plus a shared fleet ledger (all profiles of the install roll into one daily number); /cost rules the budget (set, block, warn, off, scope fleet or profile, resume, reset), the cost_report tool lets the agent read it, and the hard pre_llm_call gate stops an over-budget turn with an escape-hatch message. Desktop pane shows the gate number (fleet or profile) with a spend ring, per-model and per-day breakdowns and a status-bar budget chip. Disclosure — writes a per-profile SQLite ledger and a ledger shared by every profile of the install at <default hermes root>/plugin-data/cost-sentinel/fleet.db, which also holds the daily budget settings, so /cost set, block, resume or reset in any profile changes the budget for all profiles; rows store tokens, cost, model/provider, session/turn/request ids, platform and error type plus the first 400 characters of provider error messages, never prompt, response or tool-argument text; the hard gate is off by default, is checked once before each turn (a turn already running can overshoot), and counts calls Hermes cannot price as $0; no network of its own (pricing goes through the host pricing engine), no MCP, shell, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: courier-by-autolane
entries.title: Courier by Autolane
entries.description: Restaurant pickup delivery in Austin, Texas: the user places a pickup order, and an Autolane vehicle collects it and drives it to them for a flat fee, through Autolane's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE; the user links a mobile number with a texted code), with one ordering skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Autolane's MCP server at mcp.goautolane.com with store and drop-off addresses, the customer's name and order details, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. reserve_delivery, confirm_delivery, update_delivery and cancel_delivery book, change or cancel a real delivery and take payment; the package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Autolane's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Invite-only for now. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add courier-by-autolane --url https://mcp.goautolane.com/courier-mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: covision
entries.description: Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

entries.name: crawl4ai
entries.description: Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

entries.name: crew
entries.description: One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. A coordinator owns every card until its proof command exits 0 - one writer per card, an independent verifier, a hard token budget per card, and a live local dashboard of every card, run and tool call. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; it never approves shell hooks itself, but on a terminal offers (y/N) to open each profile's Hermes so Hermes asks for hook consent, first revoking approvals whose hook script changed; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the Hermes dashboard and a native Crew page in Hermes Desktop build that board inside the Hermes backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge, Unstuck, Retry, Proof and Stop actions, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports (with longer proof-command and summary excerpts) and questions are sent to the originating chat via hermes send, each linking its ticket id to the card on the dashboard (<dashboard>/crew?card=<id>); agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

entries.name: cron-bulletin
entries.description: Central Hermes Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

entries.name: cron-consolidator
entries.title: Cron Consolidator
entries.description: A read-only plan for tidying a crowded cron list: groups jobs whose prompts are near-duplicates or that share skills and destination or run the same script (candidates to become one job), lists clock-time jobs that fire in the same minute, jobs on a failure streak and deliveries never confirmed, and estimates the prompt tokens a merge could save from usage_audit.jsonl. Deterministic (difflib, no model call); nothing is applied. Disclosure — no network; reads cron/jobs.json (including prompts, compared but never printed), cron/usage_audit.jsonl and cron/executions.db (opened read-only) of the chosen profile, and with --profile another profile's cron folder under the same Hermes root or with --home the cron folder of any path given; the report (job names, schedules, delivery targets, up to 160 characters of a failing job's last error) is shown wherever the command runs, including messaging-gateway chats; writes nothing; runs no shell command and no background process; registers no hook, tool or middleware, only a slash command and a CLI command; no telemetry.

entries.name: crontab-ref
entries.description: @crontab: context references that explain a cron expression for the model: @crontab:"0 9 * * 1-5" (or a shortcut such as @crontab:@daily) attaches a plain-words reading ("At 09:00 on Monday through Friday."), each field on its own row, whether Hermes's /cron takes it as a cron expression (shortcuts, ? and 5#3 are not), its next five runs in Hermes's timezone setting worked out the way cron/jobs.py computes next runs, and notes on day of month OR day of week, * in the minute field, steps that do not divide the hour or day, days 29-31 and 7 as Sunday; the TUI and Desktop composer suggest examples and preview an expression as you type it. The reading comes from croniter, the library Hermes's scheduler uses. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, the system clock and Hermes's timezone setting (HERMES_TIMEZONE, else timezone from the loaded config through hermes_cli.config), using croniter (already installed with Hermes) and Python's standard library; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read, no cron job created, changed or run; the @crontab: reference and its explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @crontab: reference provider.

entries.name: crowbot-provider
entries.title: Crowbot
entries.description: crowbot.sh as a model provider: frontier models plus the uncensored open models with their refusals removed. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks or commands); requests go to https://api.crowbot.sh/v1 through Hermes' own client with CROWBOT_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: crypto-prices
entries.description: Live crypto price ticker for the desktop status bar — Top 10 by market cap, seamless marquee, custom coins & 60+ display currencies, adjustable width (CoinGecko, no API key).

entries.name: csharp-game-editor
entries.description: Give it one feature for the Unity project open in your editor, and it builds the scripts, objects and scene in one plan, stops that plan when the compile reports an error CS line, and plays the scene when the compile is clean. Disclosure — Needs MCP for Unity pinned to v10.3.0, plus git and uv. Hermes starts mcpforunityserver==10.3.0 through uvx with telemetry and the update check off. Disk reads run at once. apply_plan asks once and puts back a file the plan did not name. A plan that deletes, runs editor code, can lose unsaved work or writes outside the project asks again, and that summary is sent only when every line fits the approval card; otherwise nothing is sent and confirm_risky_plan asks. unity_docs sends the query to docs.unity3d.com after Hermes asks. unity_generate can call paid providers you configured in MCP for Unity; that call was not part of the check. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway. Only users the gateway admits can reach the tools, and this plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron and a session with nobody to answer decline. Logs stay in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-csharp-game-editor-<hash>/logs. Stop with hermes plugins disable csharp-game-editor, or hermes tools for one surface. macOS only.

entries.name: ctx_checkpoint
entries.title: ctx checkpoint
entries.description: Memory provider that archives the direct user/assistant transcript into a ctx knowledge store before every compaction, deterministically and with no LLM in the path, and hands the resulting block IDs to the compaction summary so the exact wording stays recoverable. Set up from the Desktop/Dashboard memory form or `hermes memory setup ctx_checkpoint` (ctx URL and API key, no YAML editing); compaction thresholds stay Hermes' defaults, which suit 1M-token windows. Best-effort on any supported Hermes; with compression.checkpoint_required on Hermes 0.21.1+ it uses the fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint contract (#94639) and blocks compaction until the checkpoint is durable. Optional memory layer (`memory: true`, off by default): recall before each turn, ctx_query/ctx_store/ctx_search/ctx_get tools, a mirror of MEMORY.md/USER.md, fact extraction from compacted turns, session digests and a bundled `ctx-memory` skill, over the same ctx server. Disclosure — the turns about to be compacted (tool results and system prompts excluded, secrets redacted twice) and, with the memory layer on, the mirrored memory entries, extracted facts and digests (all redacted the same way) are written through Hermes' MCP dispatch to the ctx server you configure in mcp_servers; setup, when you run it, writes memory.ctx_checkpoint and that mcp_servers entry to config.yaml and the API key to .env as CTX_API_KEY; the plugin never writes compaction settings, holds no credentials of its own unless you opt into transport: rest (CTX_KEY in .env; that client redacts the key from every error text it produces and follows no HTTP redirect), makes no other network calls and has no telemetry; with the memory layer on it keeps small dedupe state files under HERMES_HOME/ctx_state and reads state.db read-only; it imports the core modules agent.redact, agent.secret_scope, tools.registry, tools.interrupt, hermes_constants and hermes_cli.config.

entries.name: cua-spaces
entries.title: Cua Spaces
entries.description: Cua's own plugin: runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live, as a terminal backend (`hermes config set terminal.backend cua`). On Hermes 0.22.3 and later, Bot Desktop, computer_use and the browser follow the terminal into the Space too (needs the `cua` command). Disclosure — installs the `cua` Python SDK (>=0.5.0,<0.8); every command the agent runs, every file it touches, and (on 0.22.3+) every screen, click and page the agent drives go to the Space: on this machine for a local Space, or on Cua's cloud (cua.ai) or a machine you name, using the sign-in `cua auth login` saved (the plugin never reads or stores a token, and keeps CUA_API_KEY/CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN out of the Space). Windows Spaces run Hermes's tools in Git Bash, like Hermes on a Windows PC: if the Space lacks Git for Windows or Python, the plugin installs them inside the Space (pinned official installers checked against SHA-256, `winget` fallback) and adds `C:\c`-style drive aliases there. The optional `desktop` setting installs a desktop stack (VNC, Chromium, agent-browser, cua-driver) inside a Linux Space with sudo there. Nothing is installed on this machine. With the default `space: create` it makes a fresh Space per session and deletes it when Hermes finishes (`delete_on_exit`); because that Space is a disposable sandbox, Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends. A Space you name is never deleted and keeps the prompts.

entries.name: cursor-acp
entries.description: Use your Cursor subscription models (Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Composer 2.5, GPT-5.6, Grok) inside Hermes Agent via the Cursor CLI's ACP server (`agent acp`). Install with one command (`npx hermes-cursor-acp`) or `hermes plugins install cursor-acp`. The plugin rewrites `.cursor/cli.json` in an empty private workspace every run with a deny-all list (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `WebFetch`, `Mcp`) to prevent Cursor's native CLI tools from accessing host files. It includes a custom extractor that recovers both flat `{"name", "arguments"}` and inline `<tool_call>` blocks that standard regex bridges drop, retries on concurrent `set_model` calls, and reports `usage=None` so Hermes proactive context compression functions correctly. Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Hermes tool schemas and tool results to Cursor through your locally installed, signed-in Cursor CLI (`agent acp`); Cursor's own tools are fenced by a deny-all `.cursor/cli.json` that the plugin rewrites in a private workspace under `$HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-acp-workspace` on every start (a differing existing file is backed up to `cli.json.bak`), and Hermes executes every tool call under its own approvals.

entries.name: cursor-provider
entries.description: Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk; Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and Hermes keeps tool execution and approvals.

entries.name: cursor-sdk
entries.description: Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Hermes's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Hermes support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.

entries.name: custodian
entries.description: Autonomous operations monitor for a Hermes install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under HERMES_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

entries.name: custom-dangerous-patterns
entries.description: Add custom dangerous command patterns to Hermes's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; a pre_tool_call hook sends block patterns to Hermes's human approval gate and blocks deny patterns immediately. Modifies no Hermes internals.

entries.name: cut-sprite-sheet
entries.description: pixel art sprite sheet cutter. png to tileset splitter. cut pixel art into game tiles. sprite sheet from pixel png. 2d walk cycle sprite sheet. tileset cutter for pixel art. split png into sprite sheet. shore tiles tileset tool. pixel art walk cycle sheet. png sprite and shore tiles. Cuts a pixel-art png into frames. Tools: inspect_grid, slice_grid, place_kit for a 2D game. Disclosure — The png stays on this computer. Nothing is sent. No API key. No daily cap. A gateway room can call the tools. Stop them with hermes tools. One approval on one line via pre_tool_call. Choosing always covers only the same call. An oversized line writes one list file. A failed check writes nothing. Hermes yolo and approvals off skip that prompt. cron, -q, and unattended sessions default to deny. Empty, unknown, or a restrictive license is not written. Unknown text is copied and next warns. CC-BY-SA is copied and next names share-alike. No license chunk still writes and next says no rights are attached. Import once or play fails: godot --headless --editor --quit --path <project>. No solid-color box and no sound effect. Does not launch Godot or Unity. Play may write app-userdata. Uninstall leaves no cron job. Linux is untested. Unity editor 6000.6.6f1 on macOS kept the walk-sheet fileIDs after a reopen.

entries.name: darkmoon
entries.description: Triage the findings file of a Darkmoon autonomous pentest scan (JSON or SARIF): filter by severity and proof status, get a severity-sorted summary and a pass/fail gate for a release. Read-only and offline: no network, no subprocess, no credentials, standard library only. Darkmoon is open source (GPL-3.0); its web dashboard and remediation agent are Pro and are not used here. Disclosure — reads a local .json or .sarif file at a model-supplied path (10 MB cap) and returns its findings; no network, subprocess or writes

entries.name: dashboard-auth-feishu
entries.title: Feishu / Lark Dashboard Login
entries.description: Feishu / Lark OAuth sign-in for the web dashboard, admitted by tenant + open_id allow-list. Registers the `feishu` dashboard auth provider once plugins.entries.dashboard-auth-feishu.settings (app_id, tenant_key, owner_open_ids) and an app secret are configured. Disclosure — calls only the fixed Feishu or Lark authorize, token and user_info endpoints; reads HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_APP_SECRET or, as a fallback, the Feishu gateway's FEISHU_APP_SECRET, plus HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_SESSION_KEY; stores tenant, open_id and display name per sign-in in a 0600 SQLite file under plugin-data (no upstream tokens); a refused sign-in logs the tenant_key and open_id Feishu returned (identifiers only, for first-time setup); every admitted identity gets full dashboard access; upstream PKCE is not used (confidential client with single-use cookie-bound state); pending logins are in memory, so one dashboard worker only; WebSockets opened before logout may stay open until the session key is rotated and the dashboard restarted.

entries.name: dashboard-auth-ldap
entries.description: LDAP / Active Directory password login for the web dashboard. Verifies credentials with an LDAP bind (direct or search-then-bind), never stores passwords, requires ldaps:// or StartTLS, and supports group restriction. Registers the `ldap` dashboard auth provider once dashboard.ldap_auth is configured. Disclosure — dashboard logins are verified by binding to your configured LDAP/AD server with the user's password (TLS with certificate validation required unless allow_insecure is set); sessions are stateless HMAC tokens (12h access / 30d refresh by default) signed with HERMES_DASHBOARD_LDAP_SECRET or a random per-process key, and logout cannot revoke them; group removal and disabled accounts are not re-checked until the refresh token expires; failed logins count toward the directory's account-lockout policy.

entries.name: dashboard-button
entries.description: One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

entries.name: dashscope-image
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.

entries.name: dashscope-video
entries.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

entries.name: davinci-resolve
entries.description: Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

entries.name: day-panel
entries.title: Today (day panel)
entries.description: A Today page in Hermes Desktop, plus hermes day show and check, built from sections you list in a YAML file: any program that prints JSON (your tracker, a script of yours), your open GitHub pull requests and review requests through gh, one read-only tool of an MCP server you already configured, and your AI providers' limit windows from hermes usage. Items can carry a colour, a progress bar and a relative time; the page follows the Desktop theme. Ships a demo page that needs no login or network. Read-only and no model calls; merging a pull request from the page is off by default and needs a preview and a confirmation pinned to the head commit. Disclosure — runs the programs your sources file names (no shell), plus gh and hermes usage, as your user with your existing logins; calls a configured MCP server's tool only when the server marks it readOnlyHint, in a child process that imports three undocumented Hermes MCP modules (there is no public seam for this yet); reads only the sources file; writes nothing to disk; logs carry section names and exit statuses, not source output. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

entries.name: de-law
entries.description: German federal law, EU law and German federal court decisions for Hermes Agent: read one section or article (§ 203 StGB, Art. 6 DSGVO, Art. 50 AI Act) in the source wording with version status (Stand), gazette reference and a ready source line, search the index of federal laws, list a law's sections, and find and read published decisions of BVerfG, BGH, BVerwG, BFH, BAG, BSG and BPatG. Legal texts, not legal advice. Disclosure: sends HTTPS GET requests only to www.gesetze-im-internet.de (law folder names, the daily index, weekly abbreviation lists), www.rechtsprechung-im-internet.de (the daily index, document ids of decisions you read) and publications.europa.eu (CELEX numbers, text language, one SPARQL query per act listing its consolidated versions); section numbers and search words are not sent, because whole laws are downloaded and searched locally. Public sources, no key. Writes public legal texts and indexes (JSON with ETag, Last-Modified and fetch time; no questions, no session data) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/de-law/cache, capped by the cache_max_mb setting (default 200 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 25 s timeout, 40 MB response cap. rechtsprechung-im-internet.de sends a tdm-reservation header; the plugin fetches its index and single decisions on request only, and case_law: false turns that source off. No hooks, no cron jobs, no background processes. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

entries.name: deadbolt
entries.title: DeadBolt — reviewed artifact writes
entries.description: Review and approve exact text-artifact writes through a local DeadBolt sidecar. Protects this plugin's commit tool only.

entries.name: debug-desk
entries.description: Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the Hermes agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.

entries.name: decisions
entries.description: Predicate Decisions API tools with background jobs and session-owned structured JSON results. Disclosure — each submission sends the model-supplied text and questions with your OpenAI API key to the configured Decisions endpoint (OpenAI by default; billable); jobs run on a background thread and results stay in memory only, lost on restart.

entries.name: deepgram-voice
entries.description: Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for Hermes Agent.

entries.name: deepinfra-sandbox
entries.description: Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.hermes; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

entries.name: deepseek-search-fetch
entries.title: DeepSeek Search & Fetch
entries.description: DeepSeek Search & Fetch as a backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and web_extract URLs to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DeepSeek fetches the pages server-side; billed to your DeepSeek balance per successful request; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access.

entries.name: deepseek-whale
entries.description: Live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing whale for the Hermes desktop titlebar. Blue x0.5 off-peak, grey PEAK at full price, countdown on click, 30s repaint, no backend or API key.

entries.name: deferred-questions
entries.description: Durable non-blocking questions with exact answer binding and gateway continuation. Disclosure — pre_gateway_dispatch sees gateway messages, accepts answers only from the stored recipient and route, and may consume recognized stale/completed inputs; with enable_tool on, the model can send questions to any chat the gateway already authorizes, and continue_agent resumes the target chat with the answer; questions and answers are stored unencrypted in $HERMES_HOME/deferred-questions/questions.sqlite3; profile-local Unix-socket notices wake event-driven workers; pre_llm_call/on_session_end observe current input, turn IDs and terminal status to correlate technical completion for payload retirement, not business success or delivery; automatic header-only repair preserves originals in quarantine, and text-free receipts retain caller-supplied idempotency keys and request hashes; private gateway and adapter APIs can break after a Hermes update.

entries.name: degeneracy-guard
entries.description: Asks the user to confirm a tool call whose arguments look like a repetition loop rather than data, through Hermes' approval gate (denied or unanswered means refused); replaces flagged degenerate output with a short notice; warns when a session grows long. Disclosure — no network, shell, subprocesses, own threads, telemetry or credentials; writes incident records and a session counter to its plugin data directory; a stream-side record keeps the last 800 characters of flagged output.

entries.name: deja-memory
entries.description: Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, receives the turns Hermes compresses so it can hand them back after compaction, and recalled text from those agents is injected into Hermes turns, with lines deja marks "User said (this project)" requiring user confirmation before changing a command, file, rule, or config; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: desensitize
entries.description: Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

entries.name: deskrpg
entries.description: Hermes gateway integration for DeskRPG virtual offices, with profiles, kanban, cron, artifacts and NPC skill management. Install it through the DeskRPG setup wizard. Optional (off by default): when enabled by the operator, links the plugin into every profile so kanban workers and cron runs can save artifacts. Disclosure — NPC skill management runs hermes skills/curator commands as background subprocesses per profile and edits that profile's skills, config.yaml and memory files; creating new review-policy kanban cards needs a review-policy API that upstream Hermes does not ship (the README points at the author's hermes-agent fork for it), and that feature stays inert on upstream.

entries.name: devin
entries.title: Hermes Devin
entries.description: Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Hermes Desktop. Every launch goes through Hermes approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Hermes does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Hermes approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Hermes prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Hermes provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.

entries.name: devkit
entries.title: Scratchpad (devkit)
entries.description: One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.

entries.name: dexio
entries.description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.

entries.name: diaktoros
entries.description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, a `diaktoros/review` check run or commit status at each open loop PR's head, a repository ruleset requiring that check when you run `protect`, a GitHub App's webhook URL and secret when you run `app-webhook --set`, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files or GitHub App private keys you provide (for an App, the host signs a JWT and mints a short-lived installation token for that one repository); its create-apps command opens your browser and runs a one-shot server on 127.0.0.1 for GitHub's App-manifest flow, then writes each new App's private key (mode 0600) to a directory you choose (by default under the Hermes home); edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices and an optional weekly report to the chat you name; opt-in shadow reviews spend a second profile's model tokens on reviews that are recorded but never posted; its optional Desktop page and local dashboard API read loop state and can re-arm a failed run as `hermes dk retry` would, and, after an explicit confirmation, pause or resume a loop's hooks or escalate a PR, and doctor compares the installed commit with the plugin's latest GitHub release (read-only); deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.

entries.name: diff-review
entries.description: Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs, in a diff you pass, the working tree (untracked files included) or a branch against its merge base.

entries.name: digital-marketing-pro
entries.description: Open-source marketing toolkit for agencies and in-house teams, one listing with three skill groups and 207 skills registered as Hermes skills: Digital Marketing Pro (strategy, SEO/AEO/GEO, paid media, CRM, analytics; 164 skills), ContentForge (fact-checked long-form content with a run auditor; 22 skills) and SocialForge (a content calendar to images, carousels, video and copy; 21 skills). Skills only: no tools, hooks or background processes. Disclosure — Skills only (no tools, hooks or MCP servers). The optional scripts the skills run call third-party APIs (ad, CRM, e-mail, Slack, LLM and image/video providers) only when run, using the user's own keys from environment variables. Live writes need the user's typed yes. For writes the plugin sends itself, the script creates a single-use approval record when it prepares the write, and the agent approves that record after the yes, so Hermes does not prompt before those script runs. Writes through MCP tools rely on the typed yes alone. Paid image and video generation is quoted first. refresh_models.py reads your Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and (strategy group) Evolink keys. Keys and data live outside the Hermes profile: SocialForge stores API keys in plain text, plus a copy of any Google service-account file, in ~/socialforge-workspace; brand data goes to ~/.claude-marketing; deliverables are copied to ~/Documents/DigitalMarketingPro and ~/Documents/ContentForge. Nothing installs unless the user says yes; installs are exact-pinned pip packages into the Python that runs the script, plus Playwright's Chromium download. See the README and each group's PRIVACY.md.

entries.name: disciplined-vibe-coding
entries.description: Define/Plan/Build/Verify pipeline with five folded-in practices, for non-engineer builders

entries.name: discord-tps
entries.description: Show live tokens-per-second and the active model on your Discord bot's presence. Disclosure — Replaces the Discord bot's public presence with the live tok/s figure and the model name of the most recent API call in this gateway (any platform or chat), visible to anyone who can see the bot; updates at most every interval seconds (minimum 10) over the gateway's existing Discord connection. Reads no credentials and makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: doc-markdown
entries.description: Convert one local file to Markdown with doc_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc_convert; stop it with hermes tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when Hermes calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no Hermes keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. It stops 8 seconds after its converters load, at 60 seconds if loading never finishes, or above 922746880 bytes. It is not a sandbox: after realpath it may read any allowlisted path it can open. Unpublished Hermes code locates the Hermes home, and a failed check refuses the path. Removal deletes the plugin directory, not the markitdown package. Windows was not tested.

entries.name: doctorpack
entries.description: Local-first diagnostics, safety audit, and incident postmortems for Hermes Agent.

entries.name: document-reader
entries.description: Profile-scoped document OCR for Hermes Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

entries.name: done-bell
entries.description: Ring when a Hermes turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

entries.name: draft-cards
entries.title: Draft Cards
entries.description: Email and chat-message drafts as reviewable cards in the Hermes Desktop chat. The agent's draft_card tool stores each draft and its revisions; the card shows recipients, subject and body, highlights the words each revision changed (removed text on demand), supports inline editing, and offers Copy and Open in Mail. The plugin never sends anything: pressing Send records approval of that exact version and posts it to the chat, then the agent sends it with the user's existing mail or messaging tools and reports the outcome with draft_card_status. Disclosure — stores draft text (recipients, subject, body, versions) in the profile's plugin-data/draft-cards/drafts.db (the 500 most recent drafts are kept); the desktop half appends one scoped stylesheet, removed on disable; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: drag-to-pin-session
entries.description: Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

entries.name: dsers
entries.title: DSers — Multi-platform Dropshipping
entries.description: DSers multi-platform dropshipping plugin for dropshippers, combining eight bundled workflow skills with a remote MCP connection for supplier discovery, product sourcing, listing editing, product publishing, profit and pricing, store management, supplier mapping, order fulfillment, and shipment tracking. The DSers ecosystem includes AliExpress, Alibaba.com, 1688, DVAN, Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, eBay, TikTok Shop, Amazon, Walmart, BigCommerce, Squarespace, Square, Ecwid, Magento, SHOPLINE, Jumpseller, Big Cartel, Cartpanda, Genstore, and LPQV; available operations depend on account and channel access. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugin with eight bundled skills and remote MCP configuration, with no native registered tools. Hermes v0.22.5 requires manual native OAuth connection setup. A DSers Advanced, Pro, or Enterprise subscription is required. Tool arguments and results are exchanged with ai.dsers.com; Hermes manages OAuth credentials. Remote tools include write operations, among them supplier-order placement that spends money through the user's DSers account, pricing changes and listing publication; the package and the documented native entry mark the server untrusted, so non-read-only calls are subject to Hermes's tool approval settings. The remote tool set can change independently of the pinned package. Removing the plugin alone leaves the native MCP connection.

entries.name: duty-board
entries.title: Duty Board
entries.description: Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and hermes duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only HERMES_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process Hermes 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

entries.name: eatwise
entries.description: Eatwise (外卖营养教练) — local-first Chinese dietary coach: deterministic meal nutrition reviews, personal daily energy/nutrient targets, and consented on-device profile and meal history through 9 MCP tools over a bundled open food database (TFND + USDA FNDDS). No network, no accounts, no payments; profile schema rejects name/phone/ID/medical fields by design. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (cbc08f6) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 22.5+ on PATH. Disclosure — the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first.

entries.name: echarts-in-chat
entries.title: ECharts in Chat
entries.description: Render a chart inline in the Hermes Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.

entries.name: edit-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network

entries.name: effortless-hermes
entries.title: effortless-hermes
entries.description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Hermes' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.

entries.name: elevenlabs-music
entries.title: ElevenLabs Music
entries.description: ElevenLabs Music for Hermes: describe a song or paste your lyrics and Hermes writes, generates and sends the track, 3 seconds to 10 minutes, vocals or instrumental. It can redo one section, extend or loop a song, split it into stems (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other) and score a video. Long songs finish in the background and arrive in the chat. Bundles a music skill (prompting, composition plans, edit recipes) and, in Hermes Desktop, an inline music card with synced lyrics, format downloads and a music library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Hermes's ElevenLabs voice; needs a paid ElevenLabs plan, and a restricted key needs the Music permission); compose, plan, upload, stems and video calls are paid generations billed to your ElevenLabs account by length (drafting a plan and listing finetunes are free). Only the prompt or plan, its parameters and any file you name are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set); with store_for_editing on, ElevenLabs keeps generated songs so they can be edited later. Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Hermes home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Hermes).

entries.name: elevenlabs-sound-effects
entries.title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
entries.description: ElevenLabs sound effects for Hermes: one tool, elevenlabs_sound_effect, that turns a text description ("glass shattering on a tile floor", "90s hip-hop drum loop, 90 BPM") into an audio file, 0.5 to 30 seconds, optionally a seamless loop, and sends it to you in chat. Bundles a sound-design skill with a local ffmpeg script (trim, loudness, mono, loop fixing, game variation packs) and, in Hermes Desktop, an inline sound card and a sound library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Hermes's ElevenLabs voice; a restricted key needs the Sound Effects permission); every call is a paid generation billed to your ElevenLabs account. Only the sound description and its parameters are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set). Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Hermes home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Hermes).

entries.name: empiriolabs-media
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI Media
entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI backends for Hermes' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through Hermes' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no Hermes approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into Hermes' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.

entries.name: empiriolabs
entries.title: EmpirioLabs AI
entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI as a Hermes model provider (provider id `empiriolabs`): chat models with tool calling from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog, each with its context window, image input and reasoning support declared to Hermes, a low-cost auxiliary model picked from the same catalog, and `reasoning_effort` sent only when you choose a level and the model accepts it. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests (prompts, tool definitions and tool results) go through Hermes' own client to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, which Hermes reads, and are billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account; the plugin itself only reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models, kept in memory for an hour), writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: enchanted-composer
entries.title: Enchanted Composer
entries.description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from hermes-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from hermes-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Hermes task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Hermes agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.

entries.name: enhance-prompt
entries.title: Enhance Prompt
entries.description: A sparkle beside Send that rewrites the composer draft in place without sending it, deepening it into a clarifier, a task list, then a phased plan on further clicks, with a one-click discard back to the original. Also registers the `/enhance` slash command and the `enhance_prompt` tool for the same rewrite from the agent. Draft read and write go through `host.composer`, so `@file` and `/command` chips survive. Disclosure — every click runs one stateless `llm.oneshot` call on your own gateway with the focused chat's model (the auxiliary title model when no chat is focused), followed by a second short call to score the result, so it spends your model credits. It is not an agent turn: no tools run and nothing is written to a session you cannot see. It overrides no model, sends nothing to a third party, never sends the composer message, and carries no telemetry, no credentials and no self-update.

entries.name: entropicmem
entries.description: Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under HERMES_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to HERMES_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.

entries.name: epistemic-harness
entries.description: Helps a Hermes agent record a prediction before a selected check, compare the result, and track revisions in a local case. Disclosure — the optional epistemic_methods tool (off by default; enable with the plugin's jev setting) sends a capped, redacted projection of the active case (top unknown, decision, stopping condition, a few claim and plan texts, recent event types and the candidate methods you supply) to api.typesafe.ai (or the https endpoint you configure) under your TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your TypeSafe credits; once enabled, the plugin requires a consultation before each committed probe and before closing a case.

entries.name: error-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Hermes could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Hermes's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: escalation-governor
entries.description: Deterministic stuck-detection for Hermes sessions. Watches tool/API failure signals (consecutive tool errors, repeated identical calls, API error bursts, model calls without progress) and, when a threshold trips, injects a structured escalation packet (goal, what was tried, what failed) directing the agent to delegate the remaining work to a stronger model via delegate_task instead of retrying blindly; writes a per-session JSONL report with escalation and token-usage accounting. Disclosure — local code only: injects an escalation packet (the session's first user message and recent tool targets/errors) into tool results and into each following turn's context once a stuck threshold trips, directing the agent to call delegate_task (which spends model usage on a subagent); reads an optional escalation-governor.json and appends one line per session to a shared escalation-governor-reports.jsonl in the Hermes home; adds a /governor status command; opens no network connections, starts no processes and never blocks a tool call.

entries.name: ethics-filter
entries.title: Ethics Filter
entries.description: Universal ethics evaluation engine. Six modules — environmental, fairness, transparency, conscious leadership, ethical framework, compliance — scored against strictness thresholds with tension detection, so any decision comes back GREEN, AMBER or RED with the reasoning attached. Ships the ethics-filter skill (which backs /ethics) and the ethics_evaluate tool; the engine is vendored and needs no pip install. Disclosure — reads the rubrics and constitution templates bundled in the plugin and appends one JSONL record per scored evaluation, including the decision text, context and reasoning it was given, to $ETHICS_FILTER_AUDIT (default ~/.ethics-filter/audit.jsonl, outside the Hermes profile and shared by every profile), which is never rewritten or deleted. With auto_score=true it asks the host agent's own model to score through Hermes, holding no separate key; there are no other network calls.

entries.name: eu-mode
entries.description: EU Mode (beta): HaloGuard EU, Astroware's guard API hosted in the EU, checks each message and each reply (allow or block). EU Mode looks for personal data in what users send and masks what it finds before the request reaches the model, then puts the originals back in the reply, on your machine. Disclosure — on every turn the conversation's user and assistant text (not system prompts, tool results, files or images) goes to api.astroware.ai (or the HALOGUARD_BASE_URL you set) with your own HaloGuard EU key, up to twice per turn (your message, then the reply); fail-open: if the API does not answer, the message goes on unchecked and not masked, and the reply says so; reads two Hermes settings (session titles, context compression) only to say when they are on; stores SHA-256 fingerprints of blocked messages, never their text.

entries.name: evalroute
entries.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start.
