Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under and, since evalroute 0.10.0, whether the arm was an explore draw and which default arm it replaced (arm ids only). Disclosure — since evalroute 0.10.0, setting evalroute.explore.fraction in config.yaml (or EVALROUTE_EXPLORE) makes that fraction of routes recommend the lane's runner-up arm from the bundled explore table instead of the default arm (and "hermes evalroute dispatch" then runs that runner-up model), marked on the route card; off by default. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.10.0,<0.11), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation.

entries.name: event-read
entries.description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. On Hermes 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host a no-argument list_events still returns the next 7 days and does not record uids. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch reads cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Hermes 0.21.6). The printed cron line uses ctx.profile_name. The file write still uses Hermes's write guard. An update can stop the watch if that guard moves. These reads do not ask for approval and do not register a hook. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

entries.name: excel_line
entries.description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

entries.name: fashion-design
entries.description: Fashion design toolkit for drafting ideas, tech packs, size sheets, and manufacturing prep

entries.name: fatetell
entries.title: FateTell
entries.description: BaZi (Four Pillars) charts, the Chinese almanac and the charts saved in a FateTell account, computed by FateTell's hosted MCP server, plus a skill on reading the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — hosted MCP server at https://mcp.fatetell.com/mcp (remote tool list not covered by the pin); the server calls no language model; cast_bazi_chart and get_almanac work without an account and send a birth date and time, IANA time zone, gender, hemisphere and optional longitude (no place name); the other seven tools need a FateTell account (four of them an active membership) and Hermes native MCP OAuth (`mcp_servers.fatetell` on https://mcp.fatetell.com/login/mcp with `auth: oauth`, then `hermes mcp login fatetell`; through the bundled mcp.json alone those tools answer 401), authorization server https://auth.fatetell.com, Hermes stores the OAuth tokens; create_saved_chart is the only write tool: it adds a chart to the user's account from a display name, gender, birth date and time and a birthplace name, and cannot edit or delete charts; the package marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before that call; birth data, saved charts and account details returned by the tools reach the model provider.

entries.name: field-academy
entries.title: Field Academy
entries.description: Learn Hermes by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting Hermes up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own Hermes scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre_llm_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post_tool_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older Hermes it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real Hermes home) and never read Hermes's real ones; on the Guide path reads Hermes's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the Hermes version; no private Hermes imports.

entries.name: file-tray
entries.description: Session file tray — paths the Hermes agent touched via read_file, write_file, or patch. Desktop pane and /files. No API keys.

entries.name: filebox
entries.description: Dual-panel commander file browser for Hermes Desktop — whitelist-guarded file CRUD, copy/move/symlink, media preview, multi-select, rename, and trash. No network I/O, no model tokens.

entries.name: filmease
entries.title: FilmEase
entries.description: Find streamable movies and manage a FilmEase watchlist, ratings, private reviews, viewing history, taste, and streaming preferences. Portable skill plus remote MCP; FilmEase account and Hermes-managed OAuth required (native config step documented). Remote FilmEase service records authenticated activity and service analytics. Disclosure — sends movie queries, titles, filters and requested account changes to FilmEase's hosted MCP service at filmease-mcp.fancy-fire-1eba.workers.dev, which records authenticated tool activity, request summaries, latency and errors as service analytics; needs a FilmEase account and a user-added native `mcp_servers.filmease` entry with `auth: oauth` (Hermes stores the token); write calls ask for approval (`trust: untrusted`).

entries.name: financial-datasets
entries.description: Stock market data from Financial Datasets - financial statements, prices, SEC filings, insider and institutional ownership, KPIs, news, macro data, and a stock screener.

entries.name: finder
entries.title: Finder
entries.description: Sidebar tab that searches and filters Hermes projects and sessions, including by project name, which the built-in search cannot. All, Projects and Sessions views; right-click a project to add a session, copy its folder path, rename, recolour, reorder or delete, and right-click a session to open, copy id, tag, archive or delete; plus per-session and per-project token and cost stats and a live context meter. Desktop only; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: fish-audio
entries.title: Fish Audio
entries.description: Lifelike voices for your agent: Fish Audio's expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, plus transcription, voice cloning and a voice library. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and word-by-word live dictation captions on Hermes 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and hermes fish commands, and four skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to Fish's native realtime speech-to-text at api.fish.audio (transcribe-stream-1, Preview) while you speak, billed $0.36 per hour of open session, per second, including silence; a session opens with the first audio and closes once Fish confirms the last words (the plugin stops waiting after 15 seconds), or 30 seconds after the last audio of a cancelled recording; the live_transcription: compat setting uses Fish's older realtime endpoint instead, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and your own voice ids, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.

entries.name: flashdata-plugin
entries.title: FlashData
entries.description: Web search with Google Search; Google News, Google Images, Google Shopping, Google Video Search and Google Places for research. Use YouTube Search or YouTube Extended Search; retrieve YouTube metadata, YouTube transcripts, YouTube captions and YouTube channel data; get YouTube autocomplete; inspect YouTube trainability as license-label metadata, not training permission. YouTube downloads deliver media to your own storage. One hosted MCP connection and 15 task Skills; bring your own API key and paid FlashData Credits. Disclosure — Connects to FlashData's hosted MCP service (data.flashdata.dev) with your own FLASHDATA_API_KEY; every search, YouTube read or download spends your paid FlashData Credits, and Hermes asks before running only the tools the server does not mark read-only, so most paid searches run without a prompt. The YouTube download tool sends the storage bucket and storage access credentials you supply to FlashData, and those values stay visible in the chat history.

entries.name: fleet-policy
entries.description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`hermes fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks). Disclosure — records only model, reasoning effort and service tier per role (no message content, headers or keys) via the pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call hooks and a pass-through llm_execution middleware, stored in $HERMES_HOME/fleet-policy/observed.json; crons --cost opens cron/executions.db and state.db read-only and checks each cron run's final reply locally for silence; watch is an operator CLI command that calls one MCP tool at the config's server_url (or the admin-pinned watch_server_url) with config headers in which ${VAR} env values are expanded, follows redirects, and writes seen ids to a state file at the config-chosen path; the recurring-tasks skill has the agent write watch configs under $HERMES_HOME/watches, a script under $HERMES_HOME/scripts and a cron job; no other network access, no telemetry.

entries.name: flightlog
entries.title: Flightlog
entries.description: Flight recorder for Hermes. Records every tool call, model call, subagent and approval to local SQLite and flags runs that finish green but went wrong: tool errors the answer hides, loops, token spikes and effort collapse against each cron job's own baseline, failed subagents behind a "done", and "tests pass" claims with no passing check after the last edit. Flagged runs get a short incident report, a footer on the reply, per-step timelines in the CLI, dashboard tab and desktop page, and an opt-in loop tripwire that hands the 5th repeat to Hermes's own approval prompt. Disclosure — local only: no network calls, subprocesses or background services beyond one in-process SQLite writer thread; stores short redacted previews of every tool call's arguments and result in $HERMES_HOME/flightlog/flightlog.db (pruned after 30 days); flagged runs' redacted evidence goes to your configured model via ctx.llm for the incident report; appends a footer to agent replies when a run is flagged, and by default (break_silence) makes a flagged [SILENT] cron job post that note instead of staying silent; the opt-in loop tripwire registers a pre_tool_call hook that sends the 5th identical call to Hermes's approval prompt.

entries.name: flowsery
entries.title: Flowsery
entries.description: Privacy-first web analytics through Flowsery's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.flowsery.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): visitors, sessions, bounce rate, time series, real-time visitors, breakdowns by page, referrer, channel, campaign, country and device, goals and revenue attribution, single visitor journeys, and the bugs and UX problems Flowsery found in session recordings. Bundles the flowsery workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Flowsery's hosted server (mcp.flowsery.com) and acts on the user's Flowsery account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Most tools are read-only; track_goal and track_payment record goal and payment events in the user's analytics (no money moves), delete_goals and delete_payments permanently remove those events, and update_issue_status changes an issue. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: fluxer-platform
entries.description: Fluxer gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Native Fluxer integration using Fluxer's bot REST API for outbound messages, Gateway WebSocket events for inbound dispatches, message edits, agent-requested reactions, pins, reply references, media delivery, and channel-directory enumeration. Component button

entries.name: fmsg-platform
entries.description: fmsg platform adapter for Hermes Agent. Real-time inbound over the fmsg-webapi WebSocket (/fmsg/ws), outbound via its JSON REST routes. Authenticates with an fmsg API key (fmsgk_...) exchanged for a short-lived JWT — run the agent as a derived sub-account such as @alice_hermes@example.com. Only http

entries.name: foresee
entries.title: Foresee
entries.description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

entries.name: fortytwo-provider
entries.description: Fortytwo — Qwen3.8 27B inference; adds Fortytwo to the Hermes model provider list. Disclosure — model provider: Hermes sends prompts, images and tool results to Fortytwo's hosted API (api.fortytwo.network) with your FORTYTWO_API_KEY; requests carry attribution headers naming this plugin.

entries.name: found
entries.title: FOUND
entries.description: FOUND, the AI SDR for LinkedIn and email, through FOUND's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.foundtofind.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): warm leads found from buying signals with the reason for each, pipeline and campaign numbers, account research, new companies and the right contact at a company, work emails, drafted messages, lists, and paused campaigns with their sequences. Bundles the found-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to FOUND's hosted server (app.foundtofind.com) and acts on the user's FOUND account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools spend FOUND credits (FOUND states they quote the price first and spend only on a confirming second call), and FOUND states campaigns created from Hermes start paused; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: freight-reconciliation
entries.description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: freshdesk
entries.description: Generic Freshdesk API v2 tools for Hermes Agent. Unaffiliated community connector, not a Freshworks product. Disclosure — calls the account's native Freshdesk HTTPS origin with profile-scoped secrets FRESHDESK_DOMAIN and FRESHDESK_API_KEY; downloads an attachment into the Hermes cache only from that ticket's own attachment hosts; the five write tools (private note, create ticket, public reply that Freshdesk emails to the ticket's requester, time entry, status/priority update) escalate to Hermes human approval and fail closed when no person is present. No third-party dependencies, shell commands, telemetry, or self-updater.

entries.name: frihet
entries.description: Official Hermes Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical Frihet MCP surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Hermes's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

entries.name: fusion
entries.description: Multi-model fusion router for Hermes: detects the model fleet your harnesses (Hermes, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `hermes fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

entries.name: fxmacrodata
entries.description: FXMacroData macro and FX research with official-source releases, indicator history, release calendars, curves, FX, commodities, positioning and sourced research tasks. 100 native tools: 41 REST, 57 MCP, a USD brief and a version-pinned history snapshot. Disclosure — tool calls send their arguments, including user-entered research or positions, over HTTPS only to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com; optional FXMACRODATA_API_KEY is read through the Hermes profile-scoped secret API and sent in request headers. Public USD catalogue, history and calendar require no key, account or card; other scope depends on data entitlement. No files written, shell commands, background processes or telemetry. Adds research guidance to the system prompt. Finite SSE capture; interactive MCP Apps preserved as data, not rendered. Remote MCP behaviour is not covered by the pinned source SHA. Host/model charges are separate.

entries.name: gadget
entries.title: Hermes Gadget
entries.description: Talk to your Hermes from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Hermes pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny), within Hermes's approval timeout. The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Session hooks feed a dashboard on paired devices with each agent session's platform, a short id and its state (idle, busy, waiting for approval); a device that can switch profiles also sees the offered profiles' sessions. Optional profile switching (off unless `profiles` is set in the default profile's gadget config) lets a device paired on the default profile talk to the listed profiles; each profile approves the device through its own pairing flow (the device shows the `hermes -p <profile> pairing approve` command), the plugin writes nothing into other profiles, and revoking the device in the default profile sends it back there. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg; Opus reply audio uses the host's libopus when installed (loaded with ctypes, not bundled). `hermes gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. Writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Hermes's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: game-dev
entries.title: Game Dev
entries.description: Read-only project inspection and asset audits with playable-slice, asset-production, and verification skills. Disclosure — lists file names and sizes under any absolute project path the agent supplies (skipping hidden, symlinked and credential-named entries), reads that project's project.godot/export_presets.cfg and, on request, hashes asset files; no writes, no shell commands, no network calls.

entries.name: game-editor
entries.description: In the Godot 4 project open in your editor, it places assets into the scene, plays the game, and the next plan fixes each error from its file and line. Disclosure — Needs Godot 4.7 or later, the Godot AI 4.x add-on, and uv. The first start downloads godot-ai==4.3.0 from pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org. There is no API key. The editor is reached only on 127.0.0.1. A server this plugin starts sends no telemetry. The add-on follows godot_ai/telemetry_enabled (on by default) and can send usage to godot-ai-telemetry-v2-pudmurzsnq-uw.a.run.app. plan_change sends only the session list. apply_plan asks once. A plan that deletes, overwrites, drops unsaved work, writes outside the project or runs code it wrote is not made when what is lost exceeds 1,700 characters, and otherwise runs only after confirm_risky_plan. Play and tests ask once and run the project's code. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway, so anyone who can message Hermes there can ask and approve. This plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron, hermes chat -q and unattended runs decline. Data stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-game-editor-<id> after removal. Stop with hermes plugins disable game-editor, or hermes tools for one surface. macOS only.

entries.name: gameforge
entries.title: GameForge
entries.description: Game development toolkit: sound effects, music loops with MIDI, NPC voices, pixel-art sprite sheets and autotiling tilesets, low-poly and AI 3D models (.glb); 4 playable web genres (topdown, platformer, arena, roguelike), Godot 4 and Unity builds; headless Blender and Unreal pipelines; an automated playtester that plays each genre and reports crashes, stuck spots and boring stretches; one-click PWA, itch.io, single-HTML and Capacitor export. Offline by default. Disclosure — runs local Chrome/Chromium for playtests, and Godot, Unity, Blender, UnrealEditor-Cmd, ffmpeg, xvfb-run or butler only when a call asks for them; blender action=script runs a bpy file the caller names. Network only when asked: fal.ai, Tripo or Meshy (FAL_KEY / TRIPO_API_KEY / MESHY_API_KEY, prompt and image sent), ElevenLabs (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, SFX prompt), Edge TTS when edge-tts is installed (dialogue text), Godot export templates from GitHub (~1 GB, target=godot_templates), itch.io via butler (target=itch with an explicit itch_target). Writes only inside the game project directory, plus a temporary browser profile. No telemetry.

entries.name: gbrain-plugin
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Hermes as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

entries.name: gbrain-pointer
entries.title: GBrain Pointer
entries.description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

entries.name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex
entries.description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `hermes plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

entries.name: gemini-live-bridge
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the Hermes desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.

entries.name: gemini-media
entries.description: Google Gemini image (Nano Banana) and video (Gemini Omni) generation backends for image_generate and video_generate, in one plugin built on the google-genai SDK. Image: text-to-image and reference-guided editing (up to 14 images). Video: text-, image- and reference-to-video with native audio. Model picker comes from the key's live models.list. Disclosure — prompts, reference images and the Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY, falling back to GOOGLE_API_KEY, the key Hermes's own Gemini chat provider uses) are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; reference-image URLs are downloaded by the plugin (public hosts only, redirects re-checked) and a local reference path can be any image file the user can read (accepted only after a magic-byte check); generation is billed to the API key's Google project; writes generated media under $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/ and a model-list cache (key hash only) under $HERMES_HOME/cache/gemini_media/; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates. Installs google-genai.

entries.name: genealogy-research-recipes
entries.title: Kinprove Genealogy Research Recipes
entries.description: Fact-checked genealogy instructions for DNA evidence, record searches and proof judgment. Native read-only skill bundle with recipe sources and an offline given-name lookup helper. Disclosure — optional third-party services and commands described by recipes require separately authorized tools and credentials; the adapter itself makes no service calls and registers no tools, hooks or MCP server.

entries.name: genesispay-catalog
entries.title: GenesisPay Catalog
entries.description: Search products, services and shops listed on GenesisPay and read their verified-purchase reviews through the hosted, read-only GenesisPay Catalog MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://catalog.genesispay.finance/mcp/catalog, no sign-in, no key), with a catalog skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — network calls to catalog.genesispay.finance, operated by GenesisPay (Genesis Technologies): search terms, filters and ids reach that server; no credentials are stored; all four tools are read-only and none pays, orders or changes anything; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: gh-ref
entries.description: @gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

entries.name: gigamail
entries.description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Hermes.

entries.name: git-autosave
entries.title: Git Autosave
entries.description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `hermes autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs each backup in a short-lived child process killed at the hook deadline, which runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs and short-lived private index files into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `hermes autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background or long-lived processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.

entries.name: git-hook
entries.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.

entries.name: git-review
entries.title: Git Review
entries.description: Git review pane for Hermes Desktop: every changed file of the agent's last turn, uncommitted, staged or unstaged work, the branch since it left the default branch, or any selection of commits, in one scroll, unified or split, with syntax colours; cites changed lines into the composer as @line: references; and stages, unstages, discards, commits, pushes and opens pull requests from the pane. Disclosure — reads run git subprocesses (rev-parse, status, diff, log, show, cat-file, ls-files, for-each-ref, branch, remote, rev-list, merge-base, symbolic-ref, hash-object) with timeouts and output caps, external diff and textconv drivers disabled. Writes run only when the user clicks: git add, restore, reset, rm, commit and push, on paths validated inside the repository; discard asks first in Desktop's confirmation dialog and deletes only the untracked files it names. By default hooks are skipped and any write that would run a program named by the repository's own config (filter drivers, signing, SSH or credential commands) is refused; the run_repo_programs setting allows them, and the read_only setting hides and refuses every write. Network use: push to the branch's own name on its remote, and the user's own gh or glab CLI for the PR/MR badge and for Create pull request; the plugin itself makes no network requests. Generate commit message sends what the commit will contain and recent commit subjects to the focused chat's model through Hermes's commit_message one-shot template, only when clicked. It reads files and history inside authorized repositories only (the focused workspace, configured repos/roots and the latest agent selection), this profile's config.yaml, and the cwd column of the sessions table in state.db (read-only); it writes $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/select.sqlite3 (agent selection requests), Desktop plugin storage (display settings, turn baselines) and, through the actions above, the user's repository. While the pane is open it polls the local backend every 3 s (agent selections) and 5 s (live diffs); the status-bar count and the commit box's branch state refresh every 15 s; no background processes, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: git-tasks
entries.description: Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — uses your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through Hermes Desktop's shell bridge, or a GitHub token you paste in the panel (stored unencrypted in Desktop plugin storage, sent only to api.github.com); scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos and reads skill names under ~/.hermes; polls the active-session list of every Hermes profile every 10 seconds for status chips; approve, close, reopen, comment and merge act on GitHub from the panel; creates git worktrees and opens Hermes sessions seeded with the issue/PR title and body as fenced untrusted text, and without a shell bridge asks the agent to run the worktree git commands.

entries.name: githermes
entries.description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in Hermes Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `hermes plugins update githermes` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.

entries.name: github-copilot
entries.description: GitHub Copilot model providers for Hermes: `copilot` (the Copilot API with your Copilot subscription: GPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok models, sign in with `hermes auth add copilot` or COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN) and `copilot-acp` (drives your installed GitHub Copilot CLI over ACP). Moved out of Hermes core; profiles that used Copilot get it installed automatically. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — signs in with GitHub's device-code flow using the Copilot editor OAuth app, exchanges your GitHub token for a short-lived Copilot token at api.github.com and sends your prompts to api.githubcopilot.com (or models.github.ai); it calls GitHub only for profiles that chose Copilot, never runs `gh` or reads other tools' token files, and caches the exchanged token in <HERMES_HOME>/.copilot_jwt.json. copilot-acp runs your local `copilot` CLI.

entries.name: github_app
entries.description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or HERMES_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result. Talks only to https://api.github.com or the operator-configured GITHUB_API_URL / settings.api_url (HTTPS, no redirects; no tool argument can change the host). Issue/comment/review/merge writes stay disabled until settings.allow_write_actions is true and each one additionally goes through Hermes's human-approval prompt via its pre_tool_call hook (an 'always' answer does not persist).

entries.name: glass-theme
entries.title: Glass Theme
entries.description: Translucent glass surfaces for Hermes Desktop in light and dark, teal accent, with terminal colors that match. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers one theme through the Desktop plugin SDK and injects no CSS, no DOM access and no stylesheet of its own; the palette ships light and dark sets and the desktop terminal pane takes its colours from them. The package also ships two optional CLI/TUI skins (glass-light, glass-dark) as plain YAML files the user copies into ~/.hermes/skins, plus an inert __init__.py whose register() does nothing so the Agent loader imports the package cleanly instead of reporting a missing module. No network requests, no agent tools, no hooks, no background processes, no settings page.

entries.name: glasser
entries.title: Glasser
entries.description: Glasser's hosted MCP: search, inspect and run 1,000+ paid data endpoints (people and company enrichment, SEO, web, social media, US property, stock quotes) with one key, pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: a stdio bridge through mcp-remote (browser sign-in, no key in the package) plus a bundled skill for setup and the spending rules. Requires Node.js 18+. Disclosure — paid data broker: each run tool call charges your Glasser balance per the endpoint's published price with no in-Hermes confirm step; runs npx mcp-remote@0.14.3 as a local stdio bridge to https://api.glasser.ai/mcp; the sign-in token is cached by mcp-remote under ~/.mcp-auth/.

entries.name: gmail
entries.title: Gmail
entries.description: Hermes Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's Hermes Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (one setting can skip every review dialog, and then the prepare ticket, account/profile binding, exact snapshot validation and readback verification still run); remote email images load only after the user allows them. Attachment metadata listing and bounded read-only attachment download (25 MB cap) are profile/account-scoped.

entries.name: go-whatsapp
entries.title: Go WhatsApp
entries.description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.5.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. The plugin does not ingest incoming messages or configure webhooks.

entries.name: godot-studio
entries.description: Headless Godot 4 workflows for the agent game studio — godot_headless_check (script/resource validation via godot --headless, no editor needed), godot_export (CI builds from named export presets, e.g. a Web build a playtester agent can load), godot_builds (export presets + artifact state: exists/size/modified — gallery data for re-export decisions and attaching fresh builds in chat), godot_setup (read-only install-state report for Godot/godot-ai/uv with the exact registration path). Complements the hi-godot/godot-ai MCP editor bridge by covering the verification and export leg of the loop; bundles the godot-studio skill teaching edit → verify → export → playtest. Ships an optional desktop half (unified package): a Godot version statusbar chip and a builds gallery pane backed by its own read-only dashboard API; opt-in, degrades gracefully when the backend is off. Tools register only when a Godot 4 binary is present (check_fn). Disclosure — runs shell commands (godot --headless against the caller-targeted project; read-only godot --version in the desktop backend; read-only hermes mcp list in godot_setup); godot_headless_check and godot_export execute the target project's own GDScript (autoloads, main scene, export plugins) with no approval prompt — point them only at projects you trust; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no background processes; exports write only inside the target project (the output path is resolved and confined to the project directory, existing files that aren't known export artifacts are never overwritten, and the default is the preset's own export_path from export_presets.cfg); the desktop backend reads export_presets.cfg and artifact metadata inside the project path the user configures in the pane.

entries.name: gondola-provider
entries.description: Gondola, a USDC-settled marketplace API for Venice AI inference

entries.name: gonogo
entries.description: Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim. Disclosure — gonogo_report writes report JSON/HTML to the path the model supplies.

entries.name: good-student
entries.description: Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

entries.name: govee
entries.description: Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

entries.name: greyridge-token-safety
entries.description: Skill that runs a pre-trade safety check on Base ERC-20 tokens (honeypot/sellability, measured transfer tax, owner/mint/pause flags, liquidity, SAFE/CAUTION/AVOID verdict) by curling the Grey Ridge x402 API's free preview endpoint. Skill-only: no tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — the skill has the agent run `curl` against Grey Ridge Signals Group LLC's API (x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev, the same service as api.greyridgesignals.ai) with the token address and, for the swap gate, trade side and USD size; each response carries a paid URL that the skill tells the agent it can call with an x402 client (suggesting `npm i x402-fetch viem`), paying $0.01 USDC per call on Base from whatever wallet that client is given, and it mentions an unpinned `pip install git+https://github.com/rezearcher/greyridge-x402-tools` helper that the user installs themselves. Its verdict is a heuristic, not financial advice.

entries.name: grok-acp
entries.description: xAI Grok subscription as a Hermes model provider, driven over ACP stdio. Disclosure — spawns the vendor grok CLI found on PATH (grok agent over ACP stdio, plus grok models / grok login during setup) and drives your existing Grok subscription login; no API key is stored and Hermes provider secrets are stripped from the child environment.

entries.name: groq-provider
entries.description: Groq as a Hermes model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `hermes model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, Hermes 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that Hermes cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: gurusup-brain
entries.title: Gurusup
entries.description: Your company's memory in Hermes: search decisions, people, customers and projects across every source your team connected to Gurusup (Slack, HubSpot, Notion, uploaded documents and more), with the sources behind each answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1, no local code and no API keys. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Gurusup's server at mcp.brain.gurusup.com under the signed-in Gurusup account (OAuth via `hermes mcp add gurusup-brain --url https://mcp.brain.gurusup.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401), and answers are limited to what that account can see; write tools save knowledge to the company's Gurusup workspace (add_company_knowledge, skills_publish) and send issue reports or feedback to Gurusup (report_issue, send_feedback), and request_human_info can message a teammate on Slack or phone them when its dispatch flag is set.

entries.name: ha-sidebar-navigator
entries.description: Full-power sidebar navigator & uncapped project/session explorer for Hermes Desktop. Bypasses the 3-session overview cap with searchable, scrollable project trees and timeline view. Disclosure — browses and acts on sessions of every Hermes profile and connection you pick (rename, archive, delete with confirmation, branch, move to a project, create, including bulk archive/delete/move of selected sessions; renaming or exporting a session that is not open briefly resumes it on that backend and closes it again), exports a session's full transcript as a downloaded JSON file on request, and keeps its own pins, colours, unread marks, tags and saved views in its plugin storage, mirroring pin and colour changes to the Desktop sidebar for the profile the window is showing.

entries.name: hades-coding-workflows
entries.description: Coding workflow skills — dual-model harness, subagent-driven development, and implementation planning patterns for Hermes Agent

entries.name: handflow
entries.description: Manus-style planning flow — the agent plans in steps and marks them as it works, with a live desktop pane.

entries.name: handydandy
entries.description: Session-size notices and structured handoffs. After each turn it checks the estimated input tokens and message count Hermes reports; when a limit is reached it either adds one notice to the reply (advise, the default) or asks the agent, on your next message, to finish your request and write a HANDOFF-*.md file that you open yourself in a new session. No extra model calls, and it never starts a session on its own. Disclosure — writes state.json, state.lock, events.log and short-lived atomic-save temp files under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/handydandy/ (profile and session ids, paths, thresholds and error details; no conversation text); asks the agent to write handoff files to handoff_dir (default <HERMES_HOME>/handoffs/), which may hold work details from the conversation; optionally appends one row per completed handoff to a session_log_csv the owner sets (off by default). Reads its own state, the first byte and modification time of recorded handoff files, plugin settings via ctx.get_config, and HANDYDANDY_<KEY> and HERMES_HOME environment variables. No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry; it does not auto-approve tools or change safety settings.

entries.name: hardlight-ui
entries.title: Hardlight UI
entries.description: Frontend design guidance with sixteen original style grammars, twelve craft references, dated modern-web capability recipes, explicit direction context, and stateless tools for bounded source inspection, color contrast, and navigation task paths. Disclosure — the hardlight_inspect tool reads frontend source files (.html, .css, .js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx, .vue, .svelte and similar; at most 500 files and 8 MiB) under any local directory the model names, skipping hidden, symlinked, vendor/build and secret-named paths, and returns their design tokens and findings to the model; the plugin adds a short system-prompt section naming its tools to every session; the tools make no network calls, run no subprocesses and write no files; the optional hardlight browser command, run by hand from a shell, launches a locally installed Chromium against loopback or file:// pages only and writes its report to the output folder you give it.

entries.name: harnmem
entries.title: HarnMem
entries.description: Cross-harness long-term memory for Hermes: injects a byte-stable memory snapshot each turn, exposes harnmem_write/search/read/forget/status tools, and can extract new memories when a session ends. Memories are plain Markdown under ~/.harnmem, shared with the pi, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, DSH, Grok, Cursor and omp adapters; the engine itself never opens a network connection. Disclosure — with auto-extract enabled the plugin sends the session transcript to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure, runs a local Node.js child process for every memory operation, and spawns a short-lived detached extractor at session end. The extraction key is read through Hermes' secret scope; the plugin collects no telemetry.

entries.name: hashference-provider
entries.title: Hashference
entries.description: Hashference as a Hermes model provider (`--provider hashference`, or Hashference in `hermes model`): open and frontier models on one balance, funded by mining, QUAI, Qi or staking. Each model's real limits come from Hashference's catalog: the hosted models accept 98,304 input tokens inside a 163,840-token window and cap output at 8,192, so Hermes compresses before an oversized-input refusal; models that cannot call tools are left out of the model list. Disclosure — model provider; chat requests (full prompts) go to https://hashference.com/v1 (or your configured base_url) using HASHFERENCE_API_KEY read by Hermes; the plugin itself only sends an unauthenticated GET of the public model catalog (/v1/models), cached ten minutes.

entries.name: hashtree-git
entries.title: Hashtree Git
entries.description: Git publishing and independent cloning using local Nostr keys and Hashtree. Instruction-only skill; requires separately installed htree and git-remote-htree, invokes shell commands, and can publish repository history. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs git, htree and git-remote-htree in the terminal (installed separately by the user, or by the agent from the project's release binaries or an unpinned `cargo install hashtree-cli git-remote-htree`); a push publishes the repository's history and author metadata to Hashtree storage servers and Nostr relays, publicly unless a link-visible or private URL is used; the CLI creates and stores a local signing key, and an optional htree daemon keeps running until stopped.

entries.name: health-data
entries.description: Local health and daily-context data store for Hermes.

entries.name: health-insights
entries.description: Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills that drive the separately installed health-insights command line tool (installed from the plugin's own pinned copy); the plugin itself contains no executable. Works on a self-hosted HealthRelay or Health Bridge receiver database. Disclosure - it handles sensitive health data, so use a local model or one you trust; personal integrations (medication counts, model wording) are off by default. Disclosure — the skills run a separately installed health-insights CLI that reads your HealthRelay or Health Bridge SQLite database read-only and keeps imported lab and ECG results under ~/.local/share/health-insights; the health values it prints are sent to whichever model provider your Hermes session uses.

entries.name: healthcare
entries.description: Local-first personal health records: encrypted on-device Vault (AES-GCM) for vitals, medications, activities, emotions, sleep, encounters, diagnosis mentions, medication plans and reminders, served through a Keychain-paired local daemon with 24 scoped MCP tools. Zero-config first run: the plugin bootstraps Vault + daemon + agent pairing automatically under PLUGIN_DATA. Engine pinned to an immutable PyPI release (healthcare-mcp==0.2.1) over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), macOS only, Python 3.11+. Zero network by default; the optional LLM report-import endpoint stays off unless the user configures it. Approval-gated deletes, tamper-evident audit chain. Disclosure — personal health record-keeping, not medical advice (the skill forbids diagnoses and dosage changes); first run has uvx fetch healthcare-mcp==0.2.1 from PyPI; the optional report-import path posts report images to Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-max) unless HEALTHCARE_LLM_ENDPOINT points elsewhere, and only when HEALTHCARE_LLM_API_KEY is set.

entries.name: healthrelay
entries.description: Read-only access to your own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one stdio MCP server (ten read-only tools, including intake evidence; no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills for setup, review and troubleshooting. Requires your own HealthRelay receiver (health-bridge) and an iPhone app you sign yourself; the plugin ships neither. Disclosure — exposes your Apple Health data, read-only, from your own receiver database to whichever model you run, so use a local model or one you trust with health data; runs the separately installed health-bridge binary from PATH; the setup skill can install the receiver from the author's git tag with uv tool install.

entries.name: heartbeat2
entries.title: HeartBeat 2.0
entries.description: Your agent follows up on its own: timed check-ins, recurring checks and watchers that wake it in the same chat when something changes. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Hermes event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions). A wake is a turn in the same messaging DM that armed it, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Watchers decide without a model call; the agent answers each wake with a structured verdict (notify or stay silent, never a typed sentinel); a no-op governor slows, then pauses pointless wakes and asks once. Every guardrail is a user setting (quiet hours, daily caps, unanswered mute, floors, lifetimes) that the agent works inside and can never widen. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire, and a wake that could never fire before it expires is refused. It delivers to messaging-gateway DMs only and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Ships the plugin skill `heartbeat2:heartbeat2-report-problem`, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — wakes and watchers run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes and watchers itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote <url>` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Hermes blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-aac
entries.title: Hermes AAC
entries.description: Communication boards, explicit speech, switch scanning and reviewed AI proposals for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Desktop-only page; Speak sends your message text through the Hermes gateway to the TTS provider configured in Hermes (cloud providers receive it) and the audio plays on the gateway host, which may be remote; the AI helpers open a separate Hermes chat session per request and send your topic or message as a normal agent turn on your model provider; saved phrases and approved boards are kept in plaintext in the plugin's Desktop storage.

entries.name: hermes-activity
entries.title: Activity
entries.description: Hermes Desktop session analytics and provider-reported usage: annual heatmaps, token mix, model breakdowns and source-period summaries. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's state.db read-only and, for the Providers tab, an Activity cache under plugin-data/hermes-activity plus the optional Quota quota_cache.json. Fetch provider data runs a local Node.js (22.18+) collector and, only on that explicit click, calls chatgpt.com through Hermes's signed-in Codex request route (requires_auth: openai-codex) and api.commandcode.ai, opencode.ai and ollama.com with the optional API keys you configure as plugin secrets; it stores usage aggregates and hashed key identifiers locally. No other credential reads, telemetry or sign-in flow; remote profiles go through the configured gateway.

entries.name: hermes-adaptive-effort
entries.title: Hermes Adaptive Effort
entries.description: Choose a separate scorer to set the reasoning effort of each Hermes request. Disclosure — off by default; when a mode is enabled (or on an explicit `/hae probe`), sends the latest user message (or the parent-written subagent goal), truncated to 4000 characters, plus any configured guidance to the scorer you select (TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenAI Decisions, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI, Nace at console.nace.ai, or a custom URL) using that service's key; opt-in settings can also send the target model identity, up to 6 earlier user/assistant text messages (1200 characters each) and a separate continuation question to the same scorer; in Hermes Desktop it also sets the focused chat's session reasoning selector through the gateway `config.set` API after each applied change, and it keeps a prompt-free effort-change history (64 changes × 64 conversations), per-conversation mode overrides (at most 256 conversations) and per-route cache verdicts built from provider token counters (at most 128 routes) in its plugin data directory.

entries.name: hermes-agent-builder
entries.title: Hermes Agent Builder
entries.description: Guided Desktop workspace in BOTS: tailored questions, reference files, editable instructions and capabilities, version comparisons, model-only trials, and native Bot Chat handoff. Saves specialists as separate Hermes profiles and installs the Builder companion plugin into its own bot profile. Disclosure — "Talk to Builder" auto-creates a hermes-builder profile cloned from the active profile with copied .env/auth.json and copies+enables this plugin there outside the catalog installer (uninstall does not remove that copy); "Save agent" creates new profiles the same way and rewrites their tool/skill selection.

entries.name: hermes-agent-mixer
entries.title: Agent Mixer
entries.description: A mixing desk for how much a coding agent may change: four enforced dials (edits, write-scope globs, per-turn line budget, new-dependency policy) with /mixer, live presets, a Desktop dial panel in the composer, a web-dashboard saved-defaults bar and a steering-console page. Also drives Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through the agent-mixer hook command. Disclosure — enforces edit/scope/line-budget/new-dependency dials in pre_tool_call (blocks, or escalates "ask" to Hermes approval, which /yolo skips) and adds a one-line rules context via pre_llm_call when a dial is off its default; per-session dial state is stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-agent-mixer/sessions/, and the Desktop panel and dashboard bar write the plugin's own saved defaults into config.yaml (plugins.entries.hermes-agent-mixer.settings); the separately installed agent-mixer CLI keeps its own state in ~/.config/agent-mixer and ~/.local/state/agent-mixer, writes hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/commands/mixer.md, ~/.codex/hooks.json or ~/.gemini/settings.json only when run as `agent-mixer install <harness> --yes`, and `agent-mixer ui` serves a token-guarded console on 127.0.0.1:8377.

entries.name: hermes-anilist
entries.description: AniList tracker for Hermes Desktop — airing countdowns, a season browser, a local or account-backed watchlist, episode alerts and a daily digest, plus agent tools that read your own list and answer about a single show. Disclosure — stores your pasted AniList token in the active profile .env (sent only to graphql.anilist.co); alerts and the daily digest are Hermes cron jobs it creates on the host you pick, and the digest job asks that host's agent to query the public AniList API itself.

entries.name: hermes-asgard
entries.title: Asgard
entries.description: Twelve Norse gods carved in runestone and wood: Odin, Thor, Freyja, Loki, Frigg, Baldur, Tyr, Heimdall, Hel, Skadi, Freyr and Bragi, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named asgard-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-atoll
entries.title: Hermes Notch Plugin
entries.description: Native Hermes Agent plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for Hermes session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every Hermes session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. hermes notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Hermes's npm ci prompt. Run hermes notch stop before removing.

entries.name: hermes-auto-titler
entries.description: Topic-aware session title tracking for Hermes Agent. Hermes generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your Hermes title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.hermes-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

entries.name: hermes-autonomous
entries.description: Proactive follow-ups: reads the recent conversation, finds things worth returning to (care / utility / risk / curiosity) and comes back at the right moment — a check on the weather before a trip, the price of something bought yesterday, or just "did your throat get better?". Event-driven rather than a daily digest: a cheap no-LLM gate runs on the cron tick and only wakes the agent when something is actually due. Sending goes through followups.py send, which enforces the 90-minute cooldown, the 23:00–08:00 quiet window, muted categories, at most three items and six lines per message, and records the receipt immediately. Disclosure — it reads the Hermes session database (~/.hermes/state.db) read-only: only sessions owned by the configured owner, DMs by default, with group/thread/forum/channel sessions (including other members' messages) only after setup --include-groups; it reads the cron job store (~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json) read-only when doctor or setup runs, and writes only its own plugin-data directory (mode 0600). The install step copies two helper scripts into ~/.hermes/scripts/; doctor --fix edits only this plugin's own cron job via hermes cron edit and never creates or deletes jobs. During a review the agent runs the plugin's helper through its terminal tool, and followups.py send delivers the DM with hermes send; the optional offline scripts/decide.py calls hermes -z. No credentials are read and there is no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-axioma
entries.title: Axioma
entries.description: Inline signal color in the agent's normal reply. The agent marks the few phrases that deserve a second look (stop, caution, go, whisper) and the plugin renders them per surface with color, a style cue and a word, never color alone: Desktop through KaTeX color, CLI/TUI through truecolor ANSI, Telegram/Discord/Slack as bold plus the word, SMS and email as the word only. Green renders only when a tool call Hermes reported as successful in this session backs it; a rarity budget caps marks per reply; malformed tags never leak. A color-vision-safe palette and a style-and-words-only mode are one setting away. Secondary: an advisory card (intent, light, signal, question) staged before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls and shown through Hermes's own approval prompt. Each card and notice carries a short card code (a keyed hash of the exact text shown, the tool, its arguments and the card id), logged when shown and again with the answer; /signals verify <code> reports in plain words whether what was staged, shown and answered line up (spec section 5.6, shown equals staged). Advisor, not a gate: it never blocks, approves or executes anything. Disclosure — before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls (by default send_message, email/post/publish tools, payment/checkout tools, cron and kanban creation, delegate_task, terminal deploy and git push/gh pr commands, and terminal rm/mv when no workspace is configured) it escalates the call to Hermes's own approval prompt with an advisory card, using a fresh rule key each time so remembered Session/Always approvals never skip later prompts; under cron and other unattended runs Hermes's approval policy (default deny) then refuses those calls; it never auto-approves or executes anything, makes no network, model or subprocess calls, reads credentials only as presence checks through agent.secret_scope, adds a short markup guide to the system context through pre_llm_call, rewrites the agent's reply text to render the marks, and writes metadata, salted span hashes and keyed card-code digests (no message bodies) to an owner-only SQLite file plus a separate owner-only key file under its own plugin data directory.

entries.name: hermes-band
entries.title: Hermes Band
entries.description: Compose and render original music on your own machine — no music API, no model download, no per-track cost. An arrangement is data (tempo, key, chord progression, parts), rendered deterministically through fluidsynth and a mastering chain to an exact-length wav and mp3, which makes it usable for scoring to picture. Adds band_render, band_validate_score, band_list_presets and band_doctor plus a bundled composition skill.
