Disclosure — renders by running the host's fluidsynth and ffmpeg binaries against a local General MIDI soundfont, and writes the wav, mp3 and per-part midi/wav stems into ~/hermes-band-out/<name>/ (configurable via the plugin's output_dir setting). Long renders take tens of seconds and run in the foreground of the tool call. No network calls, no credentials.

entries.name: hermes-beads
entries.description: Native Beads (bd) work-graph plugin: fixed-argv adapter, scoped ready frontier, claim with read-back, guarded writes. Six tools over an explicit store path + actor; honest exit-code map incl. stale-13; plain bd stays fully sufficient (escape hatch). No desktop pane ships yet.

entries.name: hermes-blogwatcher
entries.title: Blogwatcher
entries.description: A Blogwatcher inbox for Hermes Desktop and web, with themes, read controls and on-demand AI summaries. Disclosure: runs the original Blogwatcher CLI against its database; scans contact subscribed sites; requested summaries fetch public pages and send text to the configured Hermes model after consent, which may incur costs. Summaries are cached locally. No telemetry or self-update.

entries.name: hermes-board
entries.title: Board
entries.description: A Miro-like board the agent draws with its own tools and you edit in a desktop pane, both sides working on one JSON document. board_apply builds a whole diagram in one call from ordered ops (nodes, edges, free lines, groups, notes, captions, layered auto-layout, bus trunks); board_render writes a PNG for chat or the interactive HTML editor; board_watch reports your own pane edits back to the agent. The pane docks beside the conversation with the same editor, saves your edits, and takes agent updates live. Disclosure — board_render shells out to a headless Chrome/Chromium already on PATH (nothing is downloaded; private temp profile, sandbox kept unless running as root) for PNG and self-test rendering; boards live in ~/.hermes/board/ shared across profiles (HERMES_BOARD_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_RENDER_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_WATCH override); serves /api/plugins/hermes-board/ on the plugin host; reads this profile's state.db read-only to find the session board_watch should wake; no external network calls and no stored credentials; board_watch's wake into a messaging chat additionally needs plugins.entries.hermes-board.allow_gateway_injection: true.

entries.name: hermes-boot-screen
entries.title: Hermes Boot Screen
entries.description: Six-act boot animation for the Hermes desktop app — black-screen brand reveal, over-exposed whiteout bridge, a technical-dossier plate, an authorization handshake with identity confirmation, and a welcome finale — with audio cues, theme-aware light/dark plates and Esc/Enter/Space controls. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Fully English UI. Adapted from 6shenhonghong9/dsh-startup-screen (MIT). Disclosure — on every Desktop launch (default: once per session) it covers the whole window with a full-screen animation that plays audio and spoken narration and waits for Enter/Space/click on two steps (Esc skips); while it is up it captures Enter/Space/Esc at the document level. Turn it off or switch to daily in its Startup Animation settings page.

entries.name: hermes-bot-hq
entries.title: Bot HQ
entries.description: Desktop fleet page plus a per-bot Home (status, metrics, alerts, tasks, routines, buttons) published by the bot as JSON. Disclosure — reads each local profile's home files, can run a declared cron routine from the UI on that bot's profile and credentials, and opens chat, a path, or a URL the bot declared; send_prompt buttons send the shown prompt into the bot's Bot Chat. Bot-declared run_action buttons run a script from the bot's home/actions/ folder: a script runs only after the user approves that exact file (SHA-256), is re-approved if it changes, and is limited to 30s and to that folder, but it runs as your user with the Hermes backend's full environment, including provider keys loaded for the profile Hermes was launched with. Approvals are kept under the Hermes root in bot-hq/approvals/. The `hermes hermes-bot-hq setup` command (asks first unless --yes) links the plugin into every profile's plugins folder and enables it there. No database, signup, or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-browser-extension
entries.title: Hermes Browser Extension
entries.description: Connects Hermes to the separately installed Hermes Browser Extension for user-shared page context and opt-in control of explicitly attached browser tabs. Browser control requires Chromium; Firefox supports chat and page context. Serves authenticated routes on the Hermes API server and stores bounded redacted receipts and screenshots in profile-scoped plugin data.

entries.name: hermes-call-ledger
entries.description: Per-call cost ledger for Hermes Desktop: every model call Hermes makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Hermes' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through Hermes's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from hermes-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

entries.name: hermes-chat-share
entries.title: Chat Share
entries.description: Share Hermes Desktop conversations as long PNG screenshots, self-contained HTML, Markdown, JSON, or PDF — per-turn selection with gutter drag range-select, search, collapsing and share-scope control; light/dark theme override with syntax-highlighted code; remembered export preferences; session info (model, thinking level, cache hit, tok/s, Hermes version) in every export header and footer. The Hermes Desktop counterpart of dsh-share. Disclosure — makes no network calls; reads the conversation you share through the gateway's session.history / session.usage RPCs and the session.info gateway event, plus the session list for titles; writes to the clipboard or downloads a file only when you trigger an export. HTML exports keep the conversation's image and link URLs, which load when the file is opened.

entries.name: hermes-cloud-file-manager
entries.title: Cloud File Manager
entries.description: Cloud Files for Hermes Desktop — browse, search and sort by date, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, preview its images, PDFs and code files, download a file, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you press Save in the review, which shows the line diff for files up to 20,000 lines), drag files into the chat, import files from the agent's own Google Drive, and hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Ships one plugin skill, hermes-cloud-file-manager:cloud-file-manager-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders: the configured roots, else terminal.cwd, TERMINAL_CWD or MESSAGING_CWD, else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists, sorts and searches those folders, reads the files you open or preview (Markdown and .txt files up to 1 MiB in the editor; the first 1 MiB of other code and text files; images and PDFs up to 10 MiB), creates folders, and writes uploads, Drive imports and editor saves (staged as hidden .cfm-* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It has no delete action: it removes only its own .cfm-* staging files and folders (aborted ones, and stale ones over a day old) and, when an upload or import fails to publish, the empty file it had reserved for it. It never follows links out of those folders, and its file API never exposes the agent's Hermes home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Download and drag into the chat use Hermes Desktop's own authenticated file download and @file/@folder references; the plugin adds no route for them. Desktop listens for the agent's tool-completion events to refresh the open folder. Apart from Desktop's calls to the gateway and the report skill's GitHub requests, its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's Hermes home, else the copy bundled with Hermes) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys, buffering their output in the gateway's temp directory; the plugin never reads the Google token. While Desktop is open it re-checks the plugin and Drive sign-in about once a minute. The report skill runs hermes --version, hermes plugins list and hermes logs (filtered to this plugin), may save its search words, title and draft as local files, and searches electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager issues with gh or a web tool before drafting; it posts a public issue or comment there only after the user approves the exact title and text.

entries.name: hermes-codex-resets
entries.title: Codex Resets
entries.description: Know the moment OpenAI resets your Codex usage limits. A status-bar chip counts the time since the last reset; when a new one lands, a small card rises out of it (chip-only while you type), with a history page of every reset. Disclosure — polls the public codex-resets.com API every 60 s and loads fonts from Google Fonts; sends nothing about you or your sessions.

entries.name: hermes-context-overview
entries.title: Context Overview
entries.description: Context window usage at a glance: a Context button in the status bar shows tokens used vs. budget, percent full, free space and an estimated breakdown by category, plus context-file sources. Works during a running turn. Read-only token/usage monitor, no backend.

entries.name: hermes-council
entries.description: LLM Council (karpathy/llm-council) as a Hermes plugin. Four fixed advisor seats (First-Principles Analyst, Skeptic, Pragmatist, Researcher) answer in parallel, anonymously review and rank each other, and a Chairman model synthesizes the final answer. Members borrow your existing provider credentials - no API keys. Registers a Council group in every model menu, a council_deliberate tool, /council, hermes council CLI, and a desktop panel. Disclosure — council_deliberate and the Council model fan each prompt (as a session model, the whole conversation) out to every seat, judge and chairman model you assign, up to 2N+1 billed calls per turn on your existing provider credentials; it also adds a non-secret "council" marker row to auth.json and keeps run history in $HERMES_HOME/council/runs/.

entries.name: hermes-cron
entries.description: Operating skill for Hermes cron: lifecycle rules (pause vs disable vs remove, `in 30m` vs `30m`), four ways to avoid needless LLM runs (no_agent, wakeAgent pre-check, monitor, [SILENT]), verify-after-change, a layered runbook and a read-only doctor that complements `hermes cron doctor` and reports one error across several jobs as one scheduler fault and a cron store that cannot be written. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — skill only, no network; the bundled doctor reads ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json, ticker stamps and executions.db (or a named profile's store with --profile) read-only, checks the cron directory's permissions and free space without writing, and runs the local hermes cron doctor (argument list, no shell), whose job loader may repair malformed jobs.json entries (--no-builtin skips it).

entries.name: hermes-desktop-camera
entries.description: A camera button for the Hermes Desktop composer. Open the preview, take a photo, and the frame lands in the composer as an image attachment, ready to send.

entries.name: hermes-discord-rpc
entries.description: Native Discord Rich Presence (RPC) integration for Hermes Agent — real-time session, model, token, and tool tracking with local-only IPC. Disclosure — publishes your most recent session title (or, in full title mode, the workspace folder name), model name and token total to the local Discord client as Rich Presence every 3 s (visible to other Discord users); opt-in settings also publish the git branch and a "View Repository" button with the public github.com/gitlab.com remote URL (credentials, ports and other hosts stripped); reads ~/.hermes/state.db read-only; reads the active workspace's .git/HEAD and .git/config read-only to resolve repository and branch; on Linux may scan running Discord processes' environment via psutil to find XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; writes a small presence-ownership file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or the system temp dir) and, under herdr, queries the local HERDR_SOCKET_PATH socket for pane focus.

entries.name: hermes-dpapi-secrets
entries.description: Resolve Hermes environment variables at startup from a single secret file encrypted with the Windows Data Protection API, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.dpapi.map, an ENV_VAR -> store-name mapping (bare names or dpapi:// names) plus an optional file path (default <HERMES_HOME>/secrets.dpapi). The file is one DPAPI blob keyed by the current Windows user profile, so it is unreadable by another Windows account and worthless off the machine; it is written by the bundled CLI (python -m hermes_dpapi_secrets set NAME, value read from a prompt or stdin, never from argv) and only read at runtime. Mapped names that are missing or empty are skipped with a warning; a file that is not ours, a blob this user cannot decrypt, or a payload that is not a flat string map is reported as an error with nothing injected. Disclosure - this source decrypts a file for every Hermes process that enables it: resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. User-scope encryption only (the machine-wide flag is never used and is not exposed), and the at-rest protection is a bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles, not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no subprocesses, no network calls, no self-update. Windows only. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — decrypts a DPAPI-encrypted secret file (default <HERMES_HOME>/secrets.dpapi) at startup for every Hermes process that enables it, and the resolved values become environment variables of Hermes and its child processes like `.env` entries; the encryption is per Windows user and protects backups, cloud sync and copied files, not against other code running as the same user. Local only: no network calls, no subprocesses.

entries.name: hermes-dreaming
entries.description: Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Secrets and instructions are screened by the dream's own rules plus a verbatim copy of the holographic plugin's screen (scripts/holo_screen.py, MIT, same maintainer), applied to stored facts and human messages before anything reaches memory, the report or the model. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — by default the scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro; with holographic >= 0.15.0 including its fact_versions/fact_confirmations tables, to say who stands behind a fact); they also read Hermes config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror_memory_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote_from). An optional cloud judge (judge in dreaming.json, off by default; off, its code is not even loaded) may, once the owner enables it, send for each mention the rules counted the fact's text and that person's own words (no reply quote, link, id, sender or time; names inside the text may be included; screened for secrets and instructions first), only from the chats, sources and chat stores the owner lists, over HTTPS to the providers the owner lists, in the owner's order: OpenRouter's Decisions API (model typesafe/jev-1.14, Jev by TypeSafe; the data reaches OpenRouter and TypeSafe) and/or OpenAI's Decisions API (model gpt-6-luna); when the first gives no usable answer the same pair may reach the next. A verdict can only remove a counted mention — from promotion, confirmation, fact decay, "said again" after a rejection, the selection of new facts and conflicts, and evidence. Keys OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY are read from the environment or, since Hermes withholds these provider keys from cron scripts, straight from their own line in $HERMES_HOME/.env; the judge's calls are billed to those keys. It keeps a 90-day verdict cache and a 90-day local journal of the pairs sent in $HERMES_HOME/cache (the journal is deleted on nights the judge is off); the nightly spending cap ($0.05 by default) is soft; data already sent cannot be recalled and falls under the providers' retention terms. The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $HERMES_HOME/scripts, seeds $HERMES_HOME/dreaming.json and, through Hermes' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files, judge files and diary without them, deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text) and deletes the set-aside copies of its own broken state files; with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $HERMES_HOME/cache and a diary to $HERMES_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact_store (with holographic >= 0.15.0 marked said or inferred; with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact_store update. Since 3.4.0, with holographic >=0.19.0 and profile scope, it also reads fact_merges and current version ids to propose disjoint duplicate pairs. It saves immutable proposal numbers, both full texts, version ids, origins, keywords and the provider database path in cache/dream-proposals.json; open proposals expire after 180 days and closed ones are removed after 30 days. Full pair texts are included in the agent report and therefore reach the configured agent model. Old facts are merged by fact_store only after the adult memory owner approves the exact proposal; the response checks the database and uses expect to refuse changed versions. Scheduled extraction may merge only a newly added paraphrase from its own session into an existing fact, never old facts from other sessions. The scripts themselves still open the fact store read-only. The sweep also cleans the state of merged copies and archives their hashes so a later forget can remove older untagged diary copies; merging itself does not erase the diary. No new credentials, network providers or tools are introduced. Version 3.4.2 clarifies that forget cleans the store and the skill's own files; Git history, external database dumps, system backups and Hermes session history require separate cleanup. Reports distinguish a successful store deletion from a retained external copy and do not promise that retrying removes a documented history boundary. Version 3.5.0 adds explicit cron maintenance: known stock prompts are synchronized while custom prompts are preserved; --update-existing applies only explicitly supplied settings and --job-id scopes the entire operation. cron.expected_roles controls desired creation without pausing existing jobs. --upgrade validates the request before copying gate scripts and updating cron through public APIs, then checks the result. Checks expose paused jobs, execution modes, missing roles and duplicates; no automatic activation or job deletion. --inherit-model explicitly clears both model and provider pins. The public cron update API has no CAS; avoid concurrent configuration edits during installation. Version 3.6.0 adds opt-in read-only task-outcome summaries and recorded memory-attempt explanations from holographic >=0.20.0 (experience_schema=1). It reads bounded attempt/version references and agent-reported outcomes; usefulness does not change truth, trust, ranking or MEMORY.md. It makes no new model or network calls and keeps no second correction-text cache. Explicit --memory-store must be in chat_stores.promote_from; stores are never joined. task_outcomes: true adds only summary counts to the ordinary nightly result and creates no extra wakeup. Missing capability is reported as unsupported, not as a successful empty journal. Human corrections reported by the agent are not authenticated human confirmation. Version 3.6.1 reuses parsed numbers within a bounded in-memory nightly cache, reducing repeated work without changing contradiction rules. Version 3.6.2 copies the cron gate scripts atomically (an interrupted install keeps the previous gate) and names any cron job the installer refuses to change with the fix. Version 3.7.0 keeps the whole-store duplicate search within its nightly budget on large stores (it also narrows candidates by the numbers and names the pair rule requires; the rule still decides every pair) and names the store in task-outcome summaries. Version 3.7.1 derives each message's data once per nightly pass, with memory bounded by corroboration.memory_mb (default 256 MB; above it data is rebuilt on demand, never changing decisions). Version 3.7.2 makes the quarantine screen about 40× faster on long messages with byte-identical decisions (re-vendored holographic screen 0.22.1). Version 3.7.3 fixes an install-time scanner false positive in that screen's start list (3.7.2 was refused by hermes plugins install) and runs hermes plugins validate in CI. Version 3.7.4 changes no behaviour: the vendored holographic screen is copied whole and checked before it is written. Version 3.8.0 no longer promotes an agent's conclusion nobody confirmed (holographic origin inferred) to MEMORY.md by any corroboration route; people repeating it offer it for confirmation instead, and stores without origins are promoted as before; --explain says why, and --memory-explain keeps the provider's count of candidates that changed before the record. Version 3.8.4 keeps, for each memory entry, hashed word stems and numbers plus a 60-character preview (none for an entry with a secret) in the loss-guard snapshot in $HERMES_HOME/cache, so an entry the agent compressed, reworded or merged is no longer reported as lost; the alert names lost entries by that preview. Version 3.8.5 has the nightly agent change memory entries with the memory tool's patch (Hermes 0.22 removed replace; replace remains only as the fallback for Hermes 0.21), counts a patch staged in the pending/memory approval queue as waiting, and compares a lost entry only with entries the night wrote (also across a split, with numbers compared as numbers); for an entry of fewer than two word stems the snapshot also keeps hashed stems of its short words or, for one with no words and no secret, hashed character trigrams; state files with a UTF-8 BOM are read.

entries.name: hermes-experientiallabs
entries.description: Experiential Labs - OpenAI-compatible multi-model gateway provider (chat, /model picker, aux and curated fallback models, /usage wallet snapshot). All network calls go to api.experientiallabs.ai - /v1 chat + models via Hermes' own transport, /api/v1/credits and /api/v1/key only when /usage runs; no telemetry; credentials resolve through Hermes routes (hermes auth / .env). Disclosure — When you pick Experiential Labs as your model, every prompt, tool result and attachment of that session goes to api.experientiallabs.ai, a third-party gateway that routes to upstream model vendors. /usage sends your key to its Cost API (GET /credits and /key) or to the cost_api_base you set. Independent integration, not affiliated with Experiential Labs.

entries.name: hermes-federated-search
entries.description: Federated web search backend (provider name `federated`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key `ranker`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (`type` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (`reasoning_effort=off`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.hermes-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).

entries.name: hermes-field-notes
entries.description: Field notes for a Hermes install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each hermes update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Hermes core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.hermes/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.hermes/field-notes), ~/.hermes/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.hermes/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.hermes/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py (it reads ~/.hermes/installs/*/facts.json to find Hermes' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.hermes/.env), else local.

entries.name: hermes-finance
entries.title: Hermes Finance
entries.description: Personal-finance tools over your own local hermes-finance database: spending, budgets, transactions, net worth, bills, loans, investments, cash flow, goals and categorization rules (read-only), a bank sync on request, and four writes (file a transaction, add a rule, set a budget cap, track a bill) that each wait for your approval and are blocked under cron and other unattended runs. Needs a separate trusted app checkout prepared with Python 3.12 and `uv sync`, set as HERMES_FINANCE_APP_DIR. Disclosure — reads open the separate hermes-finance app's SQLite database outside the plugin directory, and the plugin imports that app checkout's code into the Hermes process, so it runs whatever that checkout contains, not the catalog pin. `finance_sync` runs the app's sync, which calls Plaid with your optional Plaid keys and fetches security logos from financialmodelingprep.com (ticker symbols leave the machine). `hermes finance completion`, started by the app's Ask panel, sends that conversation and your finance results to your profile's own model. The opt-in report jobs (`hermes finance crons plan/apply`) write profile-owned entry scripts and run the app on a schedule. They call Plaid and, with a live read-only key, Alpaca (GET-only); they look up car and home values through NHTSA, Wikimedia/OpenStreetMap and, only if you switch them on, Carfax (in the local Chrome at 127.0.0.1:9222) and Redfin. The daily job's agent applies transaction categorizations through the app's own CLI without a per-change approval card. The four approval-gated writes stay blocked in cron. Nothing moves money or places trades. The optional Plaid and Alpaca keys are read through Hermes's secret scope only; the plugin opens no key file. Installing starts no server, sync or job. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies in Hermes.

entries.name: hermes-fleet-connector
entries.title: Hermes Fleet Connector
entries.description: Owner-approved universal phone pairing and bundled read-only Live Operations reporting for selected Hermes profiles. Disclosure — paired phones get broad fleet:operator access over the internet, including cron jobs (unattended runs), Kanban task dispatch and media reads, and see live session titles/previews and subagent goals from the profiles you select for reporting; any messaging account you make an owner (with a one-time claim code from `hermes fleet claim`) can create pairing links and approve phones from a private chat, so that account's security is your host's security. Runs an explicitly activated background connector/reverse proxy behind your HTTPS origin and may launch a local Hermes backend; legacy QR flow opens a private local browser. Keeps an owner-only control socket in the system temp directory, plus pairing/owner state and shared local snapshots; reads selected profiles' session registries through private read-only imports. `hermes fleet reporting configure --apply` edits the selected profiles' config.yaml (with a backup). Local idle/retirement maintenance is explicit and not exposed to phones. Reporting adds no control power.

entries.name: hermes-gemini-live
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Hermes. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — hermes_task starts, hermes_tasks reads the call's task board, and hermes_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Hermes needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the Hermes home's .env; delegated work runs as a Hermes run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.

entries.name: hermes-gensyn-delphi
entries.description: Seven read-only tools. Disclosure — Seven read-only tools for Gensyn Delphi prediction markets; no funds move and nothing is signed or sent. Needs Node.js 20.18+ and a manual `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the plugin folder (installs the pinned @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk and its locked npm deps) before the tools work. Runs a local Node subprocess per call (25 s deadline, not a sandbox). Sends your DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY only to delphi-api.gensyn.ai (testnet) or api.delphi.fyi (mainnet); history and quotes read api.goldsky.com and gensyn-testnet/mainnet.g.alchemy.com without the key, and quotes use a throwaway in-memory key the SDK requires. Tools are on for every surface by default, including messaging gateways, where anyone admitted can run these reads on the owner's key (rate limit 30 requests per minute per process); disable per surface with `hermes tools`.

entries.name: hermes-gensyn-ree
entries.description: ree_validate_receipt, ree_verify_receipt, ree_infer. Validate does not re-execute and does not stand behind text_output, finish_reason, token_count, model.name, or ree_version. Verify re-executes on CPU. Infer runs one of three small models and writes one receipt. Disclosure — Starts containers from the local image gensynai/ree:v0.8.0 (pinned by digest) and never pulls it; running docker pull yourself is consent to the REE-Binary-License. ree_verify_receipt and ree_infer mount ~/.cache/gensyn and ~/.cache/huggingface read-write (a Hugging Face token file stored there is visible to the container; no token is passed in the environment), may download Hugging Face weights for any model a receipt names, and their container network is not limited to Hugging Face; they ask for Hermes approval on every call and refuse under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended runs, host isolation, or when the approval API is missing. ree_validate_receipt runs with network none, does not ask, and returns no receipt text. Any person admitted to one of your gateways can call these tools and approve containers on your Docker daemon; disable per surface with hermes tools. Choosing "always" adds one config.yaml allowlist line per call and never covers the next call. New receipts and temporary work files are written under ~/.cache/hermes-ree; nothing is stored under HERMES_HOME. The container is not a hostile-code sandbox. No cron is created.

entries.name: hermes-genui
entries.title: Hermes GenUI
entries.description: Generative UI for Hermes Desktop: the agent answers with interactive blocks drawn inside the chat reply (charts with hover cards, KPI cards, sortable tables, day-by-day plans, photo strips, calculators with sliders and live charts, forms, checklists that keep their ticks, and step-by-step explainers with flow diagrams, simulations and a 3D layer stack). The model sends data only (JSON blocks, never HTML, scripts or SVG); the plugin validates every block and draws it with its own components, in the app's theme. Telegram, the CLI and other chat apps get readable Markdown instead. Ships nine recipe skills (hermes-genui:trip-planner, compare, explain and more). Disclosure — network calls only when the model uses a tool, carrying the model's search words or ticker: market prices from Yahoo Finance (query1.finance.yahoo.com); photos from the Wikimedia Commons and Openverse APIs, from Unsplash or Pexels only when the user adds that key, from Tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set (including one already set for Hermes's own Tavily web search), from the user's configured web search, and from the head (at most 256 KB) of the top result pages; each photo host is contacted briefly to check the picture loads (https only, public addresses only, DNS pinned, redirects re-checked). Boards are saved as JSON under the profile's plugin-data/hermes-genui/ folder; a recipe the user asks to save becomes a profile skill through Hermes's own skill_manage (write approval applies); no telemetry and no account. Adds a short drawing rule to the system prompt and, in Desktop only, a one-line reminder next to messages that ask for something visual, steering answers to blocks instead of Hermes's ::preview widgets.

entries.name: hermes-github-mentions
entries.title: GitHub Mentions
entries.description: Run approved GitHub mentions as Hermes tasks and reply in the original thread. Polls GitHub's API in a gateway worker and sends signed local webhooks granting terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools. Optional Discord copies and read-only Hermes session progress tracking. Disclosure — polls the GitHub notifications API every 60 s or more as the bot account, and when a GitHub user on your allowed_authors list @mentions the bot in any repository the bot can see, starts an unattended Hermes agent turn with terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools on this computer through a signed local webhook route; the mention text and the repository content the agent reads are untrusted input, and the agent acts with the bot's classic `repo` token (the same GITHUB_TOKEN Hermes' GitHub tools use). Hermes' unattended approval mode (deny by default) still governs flagged commands. `hermes github-mentions routes --apply` edits this profile's config.yaml (adds webhook routes, enables the webhook platform on 127.0.0.1). Optional progress notices read Hermes' state.db read-only; optional Discord notices post through Hermes' own Discord adapter.

entries.name: hermes-guide
entries.description: Read-only diagnostics for Hermes configuration: /hermes-doctor in-session and hermes guide in a terminal. Ten read-only health checks (config, mcp, skills, commands, hooks, plugins, memories, sessions, storage, update) and points to 31 troubleshooting skills, installed separately as a skills tap, for what the built-in doctor doesn't cover. Complements — never replaces — hermes doctor. Disclosure — reads config.yaml, SKILL.md frontmatter, skill bundles, plugin manifests, the shell-hooks allowlist and the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md stores read-only (the report quotes short memory snippets); the sessions scope reads the tail of logs/agent.log read-only for runaway-session signatures (session ids, model names and token counts appear in the report); the storage scope stats $HERMES_HOME/state.db for its size only (never opens it); the update scope reads the update-lock record in the co-located hermes-agent checkout under $HERMES_HOME and probes it — owner-PID liveness, then a brief lock acquisition it releases immediately, opening the lock file writable, with a read-only fallback for a root-owned lock on POSIX (writes no content, never deletes the lock); registers one read-only plugin skill, hermes-guide:start, listed in model sessions while the plugin is enabled; /hermes-doctor and hermes guide run hermes config path as a subprocess (argument list, no shell); the default hooks check reads hook configuration, consent state and the exec bit in-process and executes nothing, while hooks --deep runs hermes hooks doctor, which executes every approved shell hook once with a synthetic payload (--fast starts no subprocess and executes no hook); /hermes-doctor and hermes guide (except with --fast or --json) also run git ls-remote once per process against the plugin's GitHub repo to print a newer-release notice (no download, no local writes); with opt-in proactive: true it runs the checks (including the agent.log scan and the update-lock probe) in-process at each session start/end (no hooks executed, no subprocesses, no network). The 31 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover.

entries.name: hermes-handoff
entries.title: Hermes Handoff
entries.description: Profile-bound semantic session handoffs for CLI and Desktop with independent destination and optional summary-writer models. Derived from yuzushi-dev/session-handoff. Disclosure — reads bounded persisted session evidence from the originating profile's state.db and project/Git metadata; runs local Git and foreground Hermes subprocesses without a shell; stores private handoff/journal sidecars under that profile; optional writer and new chat turns use configured model providers and may incur inference costs. No telemetry or plugin-owned credential store. Four internal tool-policy imports remain version-coupled; no runtime overrides or self-updater.

entries.name: hermes-herald
entries.description: Cross-profile agent dispatch for Hermes Agent — 12 tools for agents talking to agents: async dispatch with SSE completion, synchronous multi-turn chat, model-selectable in-process subagents, a durable SQLite run ledger, fail-closed per-target model-route discovery, and host-owned bare LLM inference. Disclosure — sends task text and bearer tokens to the Hermes API servers you configure (plaintext HTTP permitted, warn-only); stores full dispatch text in a local SQLite ledger; delegate_subagent may use any provider credential you have configured.

entries.name: hermes-honcho-plugin
entries.title: Honcho Memory
entries.description: Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, and add confirmed corrections or source files. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Hermes's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-impossibl
entries.description: Impossibl, the AI gateway (100+ models from every major lab behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

entries.name: hermes-insight
entries.description: Selection-definition lookup for Hermes Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless hermes insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `hermes insight` CLI run; no background process remains. When web search is on it also queries your configured searxng instance and fetches result thumbnails from their image hosts, inlining them into the panel; nothing is fetched without a searxng URL.

entries.name: hermes-ios
entries.title: Hermes-iOS-sim
entries.description: Build and visually iterate on native iOS apps in Hermes Desktop through localhost. Runs Xcode commands and a pinned preview server; known dependency security limitations are disclosed in the README. Disclosure — on approval, setup downloads an exact-pinned serve-sim (0.1.49-beta.139.1) and its locked npm tree from registry.npmjs.org into the plugin's data dir. The plugin runs Xcode/simctl commands and keeps background serve-sim preview and watchdog processes on 127.0.0.1, whose simulator stream/input/start/shutdown routes are unauthenticated to local processes (shell execution stays disabled). It reads the local Hermes config to pick its lifecycle mode. Never expose, forward or tunnel the preview port.

entries.name: hermes-iroh-interconnect
entries.description: Authenticated Hermes agent-to-agent tasks and optional file transfer over Iroh QUIC. Disclosure — tasks from a paired peer run in your live gateway agent with its full toolset; pairing is confirmed via the tool's confirm=true argument, not a UI prompt. Uses n0's public relays by default (HERMES_IROH_RELAY=off or a self-hosted URL for LAN-only). iroh_send_file can share any readable path the model names (credential-name denylist only, overridable with allow_sensitive); remote-triggered auto-fetch is off by default and confined to HERMES_IROH_AUTO_FETCH_DIR. The Rust sidecar is built locally with cargo, never downloaded.

entries.name: hermes-jailbreak-kernel
entries.description: Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Hermes Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that, by default (`on`/`full` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); `slim` appends it instead, and `off` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); `/jailbreak dump off` or `HERMES_JAILBREAK_DUMP=0` turns it off. No network, no exec.

entries.name: hermes-jetstream
entries.description: NATS JetStream event bus: agents publish events (nats_publish), pull one batch (nats_fetch), and wake on subject matches — live-session watches or wake routes (config-declared or runtime-registered via jetstream_wake) with durable consumers, manual ack, an idempotent wake ledger and rate rails; an opt-in lifecycle tap mirrors Hermes events onto hermes.> subjects. Disclosure — connects only to the NATS servers in your own config (no third-party calls, no telemetry); the platform adapter holds persistent subscriptions and reconnect loops for the gateway's lifetime; token/nkey/user-pass secrets come from ${VAR} references read via the profile-scoped secret scope and a configured creds file is read from its path, never written or rotated; wake routes render event payloads into prompts that start gateway turns or fire an existing cron job (optionally under another named profile), the agent itself can add up to 16 durable wake routes with jetstream_wake that persist in plugin data across restarts (subject still limited to subscribe_allowed, no cron-job or cross-profile targets), and jetstream_watch injects matching events into the live session when allow_gateway_injection is on, so keep subscribe_allowed scoped to trusted publishers.

entries.name: hermes-jev-routing
entries.description: Per-turn model routing for the request that is about to go out. Jev reads the turn, picks the tier it deserves, and the plugin rewrites the provider request onto that model, including the reasoning level when the request carries one. Shadow by default, with notify, confirm and auto modes, a strip under the composer for the turn that was just routed, and a spend ledger. A pick on another provider is reported rather than sent, because a plugin cannot open a second provider client. Disclosure — once a routing JSON is configured, every turn (shadow mode included) sends the current message, up to 4,000 characters of recent user/assistant turns, the active model name, an estimated context size and the spend/budget snapshot to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai, endpoint overridable in that JSON), and the jev_route tool and /jev-routing route send their text the same way; in auto mode it rewrites the model and reasoning level on outgoing requests, and in Hermes Desktop the auto mode and the approve row also switch the session's model, including onto another provider (core's expensive-model confirmation is shown to the user, never answered automatically).

entries.name: hermes-jina
entries.description: Jina Reader web backend for web_extract (r.jina.ai, works without a key) and web_search (s.jina.ai, needs JINA_API_KEY). Unofficial; not affiliated with Jina AI.

entries.name: hermes-kame-api-rotation
entries.description: Smart API key rotation: the healthiest key for every call, each 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota refusal sized from its own evidence. Install with its companion hermes-kame-provider, which hands Hermes this plugin's rotating client through ProviderProfile.create_client (and create_messages_client where Hermes offers it); no core override. When Hermes has a fallback list, a reply whose model is busy, resting or slow moves down a ladder: the model the reply started on, then the main model (model.default), then the rest of the list; a model of the same provider answers inside the plugin on the same keys and endpoint, a model of another provider is handed to Hermes' own fallback (which walks the list), and a late reply can be raced by the next model of the same provider; nothing moves once part of the reply is on screen, and never_fall_back_to_another_model turns every switch off (the plugin reads the model and fallback_providers from config.yaml, read-only; no new network destination). Disclosure — /kame-keys add|import|split, and on start a key variable holding several comma-joined keys, write one auth.json pool row per key through Hermes' pool API after an owner-only plaintext backup (last 5 kept; switch: resolver_disabled); settings changed from /kame or the Desktop panel are saved as KAME_* lines in Hermes' .env; key-redacted, size-capped owner-only local logs (current file plus one previous) and a status file per profile; the Desktop panel reads that file and queues its settings requests through its own dashboard/plugin_api.py route (GET /state, POST /control, this plugin's plugin-data folder only); after Hermes' own fallback answered a reply, the Desktop page sets that conversation's model back to the model the reply started on with config.set --session (never --global; config.yaml is not written); while every key is resting and no fallback model can take over, chats (CLI, Desktop, messaging gateway) keep waiting with no total limit (each key's rest capped by max_hold_seconds) and cron runs give up after 300 s with the provider's refusal unless max_total_wait_seconds is set. Extra billed requests (chat replies only; hedge_mode off turns them all off): a late reply may also be sent to up to two more keys of the same model (about 10% of replies, 30% in "Faster", bursts of 3), to up to two next models of your fallback list on the same provider, keys and endpoint, and to one more model of the list when it stays silent; a busy best model may be asked again beside a reply at most every 20 s; and when keys keep coming back out of quota the next attempt asks 4, then 8, then up to 16 keys at once (probe_burst_max_legs). Titles and other background jobs are limited to a few requests and are stopped with a timeout so Hermes moves them down your own list.

entries.name: hermes-kame-provider
entries.description: Companion to hermes-kame-api-rotation (install both). A model-provider plugin that re-registers Hermes' bundled API-key profiles unchanged except for create_client and create_messages_client, which return the rotation plugin's key-rotating client; otherwise None and Hermes builds its own. Same endpoints as Hermes, no third-party service, no core override.

entries.name: hermes-kemet
entries.title: Kemet
entries.description: Twelve Egyptian gods in painted relief and gold leaf: Thoth, Ra, Isis, Osiris, Anubis, Horus, Bastet, Sekhmet, Set, Nut, Ptah and Hathor, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named kemet-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-lang-ca
entries.description: Catalan (Català) language pack for Hermes Agent — UI translation for core (CLI, gateway, approval prompts and tips), TUI and Desktop. Covers all text-overridable catalog keys; preserves command syntax and non-text Desktop values. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-cs
entries.title: Czech (Čeština) Language Pack
entries.description: Czech (Čeština) language pack for Hermes Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,515/3,515 keys), the Ink TUI (1,390/1,390) and the Desktop app (5,404 of 5,523). Core and TUI keys match the English source of `main` at 40b566502a (2026-11-02) exactly: no key upstream has since removed and no placeholder divergence, checked by flattening both sides. The remaining 119 Desktop keys are 117 whose English value is a function with branching (plural counts such as `cron.count`, conditional labels such as `assistant.thread.errorSwitchToModel`) plus two array values, which the pack format cannot express as one template — they are omitted so they fall back to English instead of rendering a wrong Czech form. Ships the same text as upstream PR #105503, so if that PR lands the bundled locale and this pack agree. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no network, no dependencies. Disclosure — an `__init__.py` whose `register()` is a no-op is included so the Desktop "Install from Git" flow accepts the pack (#138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language cs`. Česká lokalizace rozhraní Hermes Agent.

entries.name: hermes-lang-el
entries.description: Greek (Ελληνικά) language pack for Hermes Agent — Desktop UI (5,377 of 5,384 keys) plus the 102 most visible core CLI slash-command descriptions; missing keys fall back to English. TUI and the remaining core CLI strings are not covered yet. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-he
entries.description: Hebrew (עברית) language pack for Hermes — core CLI, gateway and tips (3,396 of 3,486 keys on main), TUI (1,331 of 1,356) and Desktop (5,153 of 5,245), with Desktop flipped right-to-left. Hermes bundles no Hebrew, so the pack ships all three catalogs; values identical to English and entries whose English wording depends on an argument (on/off, show/hide) are omitted so they fall back to English. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-it-full
entries.description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for Hermes Desktop covering nearly every Desktop string (firstRun, themePicker, connector accounts and the update-channel picker included; the few array/object leaves the pack format rejects fall back to English). Core, CLI and TUI keep the Italian catalogs already bundled with Hermes. Generated from the hand-reviewed typed catalog maintained in gradia64/hermes-agent (gradia-desktop-it branch); function-backed keys ship as positional {0} templates. Independent community translation, unrelated to hermes-lang-it. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-it
entries.description: Italian (Italiano) language pack for Hermes Agent — UI translation for core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI and Desktop. Coverage: core 3437/3437, TUI 1259/1259 and Desktop ~5,000 keys (missing ones fall back to English). Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Traduzione italiana dell'interfaccia Hermes Agent. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-ko
entries.description: Korean (한국어) language pack for Hermes Desktop — Desktop UI (5,282 of 5,384 keys on v0.22.5 and main cb757fac59; 349 new translations); CLI, gateway and TUI keep the Korean catalogs already bundled with Hermes. Independent translation from the English source; values identical to English are omitted so missing strings fall back to English. Disclosure — text-only catalogs plus an __init__.py whose register() is a no-op (kept so Desktop "Install from Git" accepts the pack, #138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lang-pt-br
entries.title: Brazilian Portuguese (Português do Brasil) Language Pack
entries.description: Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) language pack for Hermes Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,515/3,515 keys), the Ink TUI (1,390/1,390) and the Desktop app (5,517/5,521). Every translatable key exists and every value is translated against the English source of `main` at the revision this release was cut from: zero unknown keys and zero placeholder divergence on all three surfaces, and the four remaining Desktop keys are arrays/structured values a text pack cannot carry. Checked with `hermes plugins validate` and with the pack's own `tools/verify_pack.py`, which also runs as public CI on every push. Core and TUI mirror the bundled `pt` locale, registered as a real `pt-br` variant so it wins over the `pt`/`pt-BR` alias; the Desktop catalog is the original contribution (first proposed upstream in PR #92590, 2026-08-23), since the Desktop app ships no Portuguese at all. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language pt-br`. A weekly drift workflow reports when `main` adds or drops keys; nothing self-updates. Tradução pt-BR da interface do Hermes Agent.

entries.name: hermes-lang-th
entries.title: Thai (ภาษาไทย) Language Pack
entries.description: Thai (ภาษาไทย) language pack covering all three Hermes UI surfaces — Desktop (5,023/5,030), core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,437/3,437), and the Ink TUI (1,259/1,259) — 9,719/9,725 keys total (99.9%). All three catalogs checked against the English reference with `hermes plugins validate`. Manifest-only plugin: flat nested YAML overlays under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language th`. Disclosure — text-only catalogs (no code, network or dependencies); untranslated keys fall back to English: the 7 array/conditional Desktop keys listed in the repo README, plus strings Hermes added after the pack was built.

entries.name: hermes-lang-vi
entries.description: Vietnamese (Tieng Viet) language pack for Hermes Agent — full UI translation across every surface: core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI, and Desktop catalogs. Checked against the English catalogs with hermes plugins validate. Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved; multi-line values use real newlines exactly like the English catalogs. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Ban dich tieng Viet day du cho toan bo giao dien Hermes Agent. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

entries.name: hermes-lcm-x
entries.title: LCM-X
entries.description: Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 16 lcm_* tools for search, recall and expansion (lcm_memory only with LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1). Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from hermes-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace hermes-lcm with hermes-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — local semantic recall is on by default once its dependency companion is installed (hermes plugins install electricsheephq/lcm-x/companions/hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings --ref <the LCM-X commit>; it carries fastembed): summaries and message chunks are embedded in-process with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 after a one-time model download, in the background, and stay on the machine. Without the companion, recall answers from full text and lcm_doctor prints the install command; on hosts with 2 or fewer effective CPUs the default answers from full text unless LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true; LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false turns semantic recall off. Cloud embedding providers (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama) send message text to that provider and run only with LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true and an explicit model. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in); on gateway platforms the sender's platform user ID is recorded with each user message by default (LCM_SENDER_CAPTURE=0 turns it off), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under HERMES_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use.

entries.name: hermes-ledgerline
entries.description: Inspect session costs and usage in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — reads session lists, session detail, search, usage analytics and cron targets from the gateway's core REST API through the raw window.hermesDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no route to those endpoints), and runs hermes version, hermes insights and hermes send --list through the gateway's cli.exec. Only when you start them: explain and audit send the selected session's digest (tool arguments only if you tick that box) to your configured model, as a new Hermes session or a background prompt on the focused one; alerts and test messages are sent with hermes send to a messaging target you pick; scheduled reports create a Hermes cron job (one agent turn per run on the default model, delivered to the target you pick) and are paused, resumed or removed through cron.manage. Budgets, dismissed tips, scans and saved answers are kept in Hermes plugin storage on the desktop. Nothing is sent elsewhere and it exposes no tools to the model.

entries.name: hermes-live-voice
entries.description: Full-duplex Live Voice for Hermes Desktop — GPT-Live-1 on the ChatGPT/Codex subscription via the local Codex app-server, with live transcript, voice tool calls and task delegation to the user chat. Disclosure — subscription voice uses your Hermes openai-codex sign-in through Hermes-signed requests (requires_auth; the plugin never holds or refreshes the token) to mint OpenAI Realtime client secrets, and the usage panel reads Hermes's own account-usage fetcher; the gpt-live-1 lane runs the local codex app-server on the Codex CLI's own login, and the dashboard can run codex login --device-auth, copying ~/.codex/auth.json (or $CODEX_HOME) to a backup before that login, restoring the backup if the login is cancelled, and reading the file read-only for sign-in status; with TALK_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY set it uses that key instead; if hermes-talk is installed it loads that plugin's modules from ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-talk and substitutes its own talk_auth; voice audio goes to OpenAI over WebRTC, and spoken tasks are submitted as messages in your focused chat.

entries.name: hermes-live
entries.title: Hermes Live
entries.description: Multi-provider live voice calls with Gemini, Grok, Qwen, and a Codex subscription in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — voice audio and recent chat go only to the live-voice provider the user picks (Gemini, Grok or Qwen); the Codex option drives the user's own Codex CLI on its own ChatGPT login; tasks the voice model submits run as normal Hermes chat turns with the usual approvals.

entries.name: hermes-loadout
entries.description: Desktop pane to manage skills and MCP connections across agent apps: save named loadouts, review changes, apply them, and undo the latest managed operation. Agent half is inert (no tools or hooks). Disclosure — MCP sync copies your Hermes mcp_servers env/header secrets into ~/.codex/config.toml and claude_desktop_config.json (with 0600 backups).

entries.name: hermes-memory-pane
entries.title: Memory Pane
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop pane for the built-in memory: see what the focused chat remembered, updated or forgot, and edit, delete or undo any entry without leaving the conversation. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — a tool_execution middleware reads MEMORY.md and USER.md around each memory call and logs the entry-level changes to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-memory-pane/; the pane rewrites memory entries only when the user edits, deletes, adds or undoes one, through Hermes's own memory store; no network, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

entries.name: hermes-memory-ui
entries.description: Read-only Hermes Dashboard and Desktop plugin for inspecting built-in, holographic, Mem0, Honcho, Mnemosyne, Hindsight, and ByteRover memory. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memory files, provider configs and provider API keys (keys are never returned to the UI), and on user action sends search/recall/reflect queries with configured bank/peer/user IDs to the configured Mem0, Honcho and Hindsight endpoints (Hindsight Cloud default api.hindsight.vectorize.io) using those keys; ByteRover queries run the local `brv` CLI; for a local embedded Hindsight setup a contents read may start the `hindsight-embed` daemon; no memory is written.

entries.name: hermes-memory-wiki
entries.description: Memory Wiki dashboard tab and opt-in native Desktop page: browsable subject pages and daily logs derived from local session history, plus a read-only Persistent Memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) audit panel.

entries.name: hermes-minimizer
entries.title: Minimizer
entries.description: YAGNI coding and code-review guidance for Hermes: reduce over-engineering, reuse existing behavior, and preserve requirements. One static prompt section; no tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-mobile
entries.title: Hermes Mobile Adapter
entries.description: WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE_CATALOG_AFTER_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE_DELIVER_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $HERMES_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through Hermes's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through Hermes's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.

entries.name: hermes-model-switcher
entries.description: Choose models across Hermes profiles from a Dashboard tab: a per-profile picker built on host-supplied model data (SDK-authenticated GET /api/model/options), a preview of provider/model intent across every supported model-selection slot (main, delegation, auxiliary, judge, fallback, MoA, cron, plugin and specialist), and one-click apply or revert with presets. Main-slot preview shows intended provider/model, not the exact persisted diff; the exact diff is shown only after host readback. Disclosure — its apply route reads and edits the profiles' config.yaml (that is the plugin's function) through public seams only: POST /api/model/set for main and compatible auxiliary slots, and public hermes_cli.config load/save under the target home for other slots; credential presence checks use public profile-scoped secret helpers (agent.secret_scope), and profile discovery uses public hermes_constants. The plugin makes no direct third-party requests and opens no provider caches or pricing registries directly, but its browser tab does call the host's /api/model/* routes through the Dashboard SDK, and the host options route may itself initiate provider or pricing I/O even without an explicit refresh request, so reads are not guaranteed cache-only. It runs no shell commands or background processes and reports nothing. The private undo journal stores a full pre-change snapshot of each config it edits, which can contain sensitive fields including embedded credentials. Saved presets also persist reviewed change values, potentially including inline credentials or credential-bearing base URLs, in presets.json (0600) under get_hermes_home()/state/hermes-model-switcher/ (0700). The host write route has no expected-revision check: readback surfaces many foreign edits as recovery_required, but a concurrent same-key edit can be overwritten undetected and full-state deletions retain an unrelated-write race, so not every foreign edit is guaranteed to surface.

entries.name: hermes-monitor
entries.description: Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every Hermes profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls Hermes' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, Hermes core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress.
entries.maintainer: Hermes Monitor contributors (independent of Nous Research)

entries.name: hermes-monitoring-dashboard
entries.title: Monitoring Dashboard
entries.description: Prompt-customizable desktop dashboard with live host metrics, session activity, clocks, calendars, and text widgets. Disclosure — polls ~/monitoring-dashboard on the desktop device through the Desktop native file bridge, and its Reset command moves only the dashboard's own page/panel marker files in that folder to the OS trash (never dashboard.json or the folder); host metrics and session activity stay on the machine.

entries.name: hermes-mpp
entries.description: Pay supported HTTP 402 MPP challenges on Tempo through mpp_fetch and in-process HTTPX clients. Uses a dedicated wallet. Disclosure — with MPP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset, any supported HTTP 402 MPP challenge returned to core HTTPX traffic (not only mpp_fetch) is auto-paid from the Tempo wallet with no per-payment cap or confirmation; the origin allowlist is the operator's control.

entries.name: hermes-muse-code
entries.description: Muse Spark in Hermes billed to the Muse Code monthly login (device-code login, no API key).

entries.name: hermes-muse
entries.description: A proactive companion for Hermes: follows accepted goals (active/done/cancelled), prepares sourced research and Feed articles, maintains memory, and assembles rolling 30-day or natural-month calendar views. Read-only local Dashboard/Desktop pages show Feed, Ideas and Goals; profile selection cannot install, enable or disable Muse in any profile. One Skill, one state tool and six fixed recurring jobs; selected notices and weekly/monthly reports go to the active profile's Bot Chat and run an assistant turn there. Sources, authorization, quiet hours and actual result/delivery receipts remain distinct; partial coverage is not global availability. Disclosure: first load creates profile-local files/SQLite state and owned Cron scripts/jobs. Private/local input inbox rows retain their first 8000 characters and source identities, with associated chat/user routing IDs when present. The newest 500 remain; older rows are cleaned on later input only after both hourly/nightly cursors cover them. Unprocessed backlog can exceed 500 and has no fixed retention time. Native conversations/tool results are read separately; research records can retain returned payloads. Idempotency journals and oversized tool results stay in the profile state database without automatic expiry and may contain written content or tool output. Bounded conversation previews support full revision-checked paging. Delegates are instructed to remain read-only under inherited permissions, not sandboxed. Workers always use public delegate_task dispatch and follow the user's delegation settings; leave delegation.provider/model empty to keep the parent model. New Cron watches require cron.allow_agent_scheduling; local goal registration creates no job. Watch prompt/stop fields each allow 4000 characters; new repeating watches (interval or cron) must be at least 30 minutes apart, one-off schedules are exempt. Windows is not supported (POSIX file locks) and CI does not cover it. Background work incurs normal model/tool costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory service, core/SOUL replacement or phone/read-receipt guarantee. Native remove retains data/tasks for the documented owned-only cleanup.

entries.name: hermes-newswire
entries.description: Breaking-news ticker for Hermes Desktop: a scrolling RSS/Atom/JSON-Feed strip above the statusbar with per-source favicons, feed search + discovery, grouping modes, offline cache, and in-app reading. Zero API keys, zero model tokens.

entries.name: hermes-nous-prices
entries.description: Browse Nous Portal model prices and account balances in Hermes Desktop.
