entries.name: hermes-office
entries.description: View and manage Bot Mode agents in a shared office in Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-openwhispr
entries.description: Local-first OpenWhispr dictation history and shared notes for Hermes agents: find what the user said, search notes, transcribe local audio. Free local desktop bridge by default, paid cloud opt-in only. Skill-carrier plugin, no tools or hooks registered. Disclosure — skill only: the agent runs the external OpenWhispr CLI (installed with an unpinned `npm install -g @openwhispr/cli`) through the terminal tool to read your dictation history and notes over the OpenWhispr desktop app's authenticated loopback bridge, and, with your consent each time, to create, update or delete notes, transcriptions and dictionary entries and to transcribe local audio files; OpenWhispr Cloud (api.openwhispr.com, including an email-code sign-in that mints an API key kept in the CLI's own config) is used only when you opt in; the agent never opens credential files itself.

entries.name: hermes-opper
entries.description: Opper, the EU-hosted AI gateway (700+ models behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

entries.name: hermes-osint-map
entries.title: Hermes OSINT Map
entries.description: A live situational-awareness globe in Hermes Desktop: earthquakes (USGS), disaster alerts (GDACS), natural events (NASA EONET), US severe weather (NWS), military and nearby aircraft (adsb.lol), satellites propagated live from CelesTrak elements, GDELT news incidents, official traffic cameras (Transport for London, Singapore LTA) and shipping chokepoints on a dithered 3D globe, with satellite orbits, aircraft tracks and live camera stills, country dossiers (World Bank facts, events, headlines), NOAA space weather, markets, a feed of events, headlines and alerts, and a passive recon toolkit (DNS, RDAP, TLS, security headers, CT subdomains, CVE with CISA KEV, IP, GitHub, MAC). Five agent tools (osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news) answer from the same sources in any chat, and the page's Brief me, Ask Hermes and dossier buttons open a chat that uses them. No keys needed; an optional TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (plugin setting, read through Hermes's secret scope) adds equities and commodities. Unofficial; not affiliated with any data provider. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public data from fixed hosts (earthquake.usgs.gov, eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov, gdacs.org, api.weather.gov, data.gdeltproject.org, api.adsb.lol, celestrak.org, services.swpc.noaa.gov, api.tfl.gov.uk and api.data.gov.sg (camera lists), and camera stills from TfL's JamCams bucket on s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com and images.data.gov.sg, fetched only by camera id for a camera the user opens, api.worldbank.org, the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, Guardian and France 24 RSS feeds, api.gdeltproject.org (GDELT article search, only when a news query is given, which sends up to six words of the query), api.coingecko.com, and api.twelvedata.com with the key in a header when set), cached and only while the page is open or a tool is called, with a hermes-osint-map User-Agent; recon sends the domain, IP, CVE id, GitHub name or MAC prefix the user or agent enters to dns.google, rdap.org, crt.sh, cve.circl.lu, cisa.gov, ipwho.is, api.github.com and api.macvendors.com, and the TLS and headers lookups connect directly to the host named, refusing private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other internal addresses on every redirect, on ports 443/8443 (TLS) and 80/443/8080/8443 (headers) only; GDELT incidents are machine-coded from news coverage and labelled as such, incident titles are read from the article URL, and country-centroid locations are flagged as country-level; the page keeps its layer choices in Desktop plugin storage; no files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-output-enhancement
entries.description: Display-only Markdown styling for Desktop assistant replies — theme-aware headings, emphasis and readable tables. Reply content is never modified.

entries.name: hermes-pantheon
entries.title: Pantheon
entries.description: Eighteen Hermes Desktop themes in dithered classical marble, one god each: all twelve Olympians plus Hades, Nyx, Helios, Selene and Medusa. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while a Pantheon theme is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named pantheon-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-pets-all
entries.description: Browse every pet installed for this Hermes profile in its own desktop pane (thumbnails, search, click-to-adopt), plus a read-only list_pets tool for the agent.

entries.name: hermes-pickup
entries.description: Pick up where you left off: up to 10 cards (5 by default) of unfinished work from your recent Hermes chats, project folders and files, each with where you stopped and a one-click next step. Adapted from Herald OS by Luke (iamlukethedev), MIT. Disclosure — after explicit in-app consent (stored per profile), each Refresh reads recent chats from every profile's session store (read-only; profiles the user skips in Settings are never opened) and sends chat excerpts and metadata, project/file names and paths, git branch/changed-file names and recent commit subjects to the current profile's Hermes LLM route (the auxiliary title-generation model, main provider unless configured); runs read-only git and, on macOS, Spotlight `mdfind`; never reads document contents; writes only $HERMES_HOME/pickup/. The "Next step" button can submit a model-written prompt straight into the card's chat in one click. The optional install.sh, when asked, adds the plugin to every profile's plugins.enabled (undone exactly by uninstall.sh).

entries.name: hermes-pii
entries.description: Uses local Presidio and spaCy to redact supported PII in outgoing user text. Disclosure — filters Chat Completions user messages and Responses user input locally; system prompts, tool outputs and tool-call arguments are preserved. Fail-open: detector errors, including a missing model, send original text. Install spaCy en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 separately from its GitHub release wheel in the Hermes Python environment before enabling; Hermes installs only the named PyPI dependencies. No runtime model downloads or remote detection.

entries.name: hermes-plex-music
entries.description: Mini-Plexamp for Hermes Desktop: statusbar player for your Plex music library — likes synced to Liked Songs, custom playlists with rename/delete, shuffle + repeat, sleep timer, queue editing, OS media keys. Needs only Plex Media Server. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — talks only to the Plex Media Server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:32400), sending your Plex token in the request URL as Plex requires; the token is stored in Desktop plugin storage, and the optional "Get token…" button reads the Plex `.LocalAdminToken` file you pick. Likes and playlist create/rename/delete write to your Plex server. No agent tools, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-plexus
entries.title: Plexus
entries.description: Your local markdown vault as a note graph, file tree and tabbed editor in one Hermes Desktop workspace tab, with Obsidian-style wikilinks, nested folder regions in the graph, link rewriting on rename, image and note embeds, and a ::vault chat link. Disclosure — reads and writes markdown files (and images for previews) only inside the one folder you grant, through Hermes Desktop's folder-scoped file API (ctx.files); deletes go to the OS trash. No network calls unless you turn on loading of images that notes link from the web (off by default; the image's host then sees your IP address). No shell commands, background processes, telemetry, agent tools or stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-plugin-chrome-profiles
entries.description: Switch Hermes browser tools to a named Chromium-family profile (Chrome, Edge, Brave), local or remote, over CDP.

entries.name: hermes-plugin-gen
entries.description: Generate, scaffold, and extend Hermes Agent plugins from simple descriptions.

entries.name: hermes-plugin-guard
entries.description: Static review of candidate Hermes plugins; target code is never executed.

entries.name: hermes-plugin-netbox
entries.description: NetBox change management: query DCIM/IPAM objects, build a reviewed field-level diff, apply with a journal and roll back.

entries.name: hermes-pokemon
entries.title: Hermes Pokémon
entries.description: A cozy pixel-art companion garden for Hermes Desktop with three starters, nicknames, fetch, berries, XP, and optional evolution through all nine starter forms. The companion keeps you company on long turns, reacts quietly to failures, to what Hermes is doing and to turns finishing in other chats, and lives through seasons with real day length and moon phases, offline showers, wild visitors it greets in character, old-friend cameos, keepsakes, milestones that leave a bench, a lantern and bunting in the garden, and a sapling that grows with the days. Reachable from the keyboard, the status bar and the command palette. Independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab community contributions; artwork is excluded from the source-code MIT license. Uses local plugin storage and read-only session activity, with no runtime network requests, credentials, backend, or model calls. Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

entries.name: hermes-pr-studio
entries.title: PR Studio
entries.description: Review GitHub pull requests in Hermes Desktop — inbox of your open PRs across repos, diffs with inline threads, line comments and reviews, private-repo images, watched PRs, and one-click Send to Hermes for any comment. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI (and `git remote get-url origin` in the open project); GitHub writes only on explicit click, reviews confirmed; "Send to Hermes" and "review in new chat" submit the PR comment text (written by other GitHub users) to your chat as a prompt immediately; polls watched PRs every 60 s while Desktop is open; no stored credentials, no telemetry. Independent codebase, not derived from githermes.

entries.name: hermes-profile-switcher
entries.title: Profile Switcher & Handoff
entries.description: Composer profile picker with explicit context handoff into a new chat and verified single-folder project inheritance. Disclosure — reads focused session/project metadata; may read the live roster and transcript to verify empty sources, even for Start fresh. Copy context and Brief handoff store selected source text in a new target-profile session. No automatic submission or model call. Cross-gateway handoffs have no inherited project; source chat, composer drafts and profile configuration are not modified.

entries.name: hermes-project-stewardship
entries.description: Durable project ownership and bounded initiative management for Hermes fleets. Disclosure — a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a project's saved rules, decisions and facts to turns of bots assigned to that project; objective checks run allowlisted local programs only at autonomy level 3+ and GitHub objectives shell out to your own `gh api`; it creates and edits Hermes Kanban tasks through Hermes' internal kanban modules (title/body/tenant written directly to kanban.db), keeps its own SQLite DB under `<Hermes home>/plugin-data/hermes-dockyard/`, and its optional HTTP API (`/stewardship/v1`, 127.0.0.1) stays closed until you set a bearer token.

entries.name: hermes-proton
entries.description: Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a Hermes Agent, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `hermes proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by Hermes's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot Hermes cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-pubky
entries.description: Setup helper for managed Pubky agents. The launcher syncs agent state, including conversation database snapshots and portable configuration, to your remote Pubky homeserver.

entries.name: hermes-quest
entries.description: Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real Hermes Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local Hermes data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (HERMES_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <hermes_home>/hermes-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local Hermes backend.

entries.name: hermes-resetwatch
entries.description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Hermes Python interpreter located via HERMES_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the Hermes installer's managed venv (HERMES_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the Hermes .env (through Hermes's get_secret helper, else read directly), the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; Hermes's saved OAuth logins (the credential pool through Hermes's read_credential_pool helper, else auth.json directly, and HERMES_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through Hermes get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. For Codex, a 401 or 403 is retried once with another saved login for the same account. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL (honored only for https grok.com / x.ai hosts), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under HERMES_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.

entries.name: hermes-rich-ui
entries.description: Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop

entries.name: hermes-ros
entries.title: ROS Robot Control
entries.description: Drive and observe ROS / ROS 2 robots from Hermes over rosbridge: list topics, services and nodes, read odometry, grab camera frames for the vision model, publish, call services, drive and e-stop, with every tool call gated by a pre_tool_call safety interlock (speed and duration limits, optional geofence, topic and service write allowlists, a latching e-stop, every blocked call logged). Ships a built-in mock robot (2D sim with a camera and a red cone) so it runs with no ROS at all, a bundled safety skill, and an optional read-only dashboard tab. Disclosure — network: in rosbridge mode it opens one unencrypted websocket to the rosbridge server you configure (default localhost:9090), lazily on first use; mock mode (default) makes no network connections. Files: camera snapshots, a blocked-call audit log, the e-stop latch and the last pose under the plugin data dir. No credentials. One dependency, websocket-client (already in Hermes's lock). With a real robot attached the agent can physically move it; limits default to 0.5 m/s, 1.0 rad/s and 5 s per command and are enforced on this plugin's tools outside the model, but they do not stop other tools (terminal, code execution) from reaching the rosbridge server or changing the limits in config.yaml.

entries.name: hermes-routines
entries.title: Hermes Routines
entries.description: A minimal Routines page in Hermes Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

entries.name: hermes-rss
entries.description: Read RSS and Atom feeds and discuss articles in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — feeds and full articles are fetched with curl through the gateway's shell.exec on the connected Hermes host (public-IPv4 SSRF guard); opt-in AI grading sends article excerpts to your configured model and creates HERMES_HOME/skills/rss-importance-grading/SKILL.md if missing; opt-in image loading fetches publisher images directly from Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-rustpush-imessage
entries.description: Local-only iMessage platform plugin backed by a launchd-supervised OpenBubbles RustPush sidecar over a same-user Unix socket.

entries.name: hermes-security-audit
entries.description: Approval-gated local security audit for Hermes Agent using Gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, and Semgrep CE.

entries.name: hermes-security
entries.title: Security
entries.description: Security review for a local repository. The agent builds a threat model, splits the code into chunks and reviews them with parallel subagents, checks each candidate against the code and traces whether an attacker can reach it. Reports keep evidence, rejected candidates and coverage gaps, export to Markdown, JSON, CSV and SARIF, and get a Security page in Hermes Desktop. Standard, deep and diff modes; `/security` slash command and `hermes security-review` CLI. Optional "Run tests to confirm findings" writes small reproductions and runs them in a temporary copy of the repository; testing a running app needs a per-scan grant (one origin, one hour, 200 requests) that agent tools cannot issue. Apache-2.0 (parts adapted from Apache-2.0 source, see NOTICE). Disclosure — the first scan downloads a pinned osv-scanner release from GitHub (about 55 MB, refused unless its SHA-256 matches) into the plugin data folder; package names and versions go to api.osv.dev and api.deps.dev, declared runtime versions to endoflife.date (`HERMES_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CHECK=off` disables this). Test confirmation runs repository code as your user in a temporary copy with credential-looking environment variables removed; that is not a sandbox. The configured model provider receives the code under review; scan data stays in the profile's plugin data folder. With `plugins.entries.hermes-security.allow_gateway_injection` turned on (off by default), the plugin queues one "Continue security scan" message into the chat when a scan stalls, at most 3 times without progress. No Python dependencies.

entries.name: hermes-self-healing-context
entries.title: Hermes Self-Healing Context
entries.description:
Intercepts runtime errors and dynamically patches the context window 
using local SQLite FTS5 memory for zero-downtime recovery.

entries.name: hermes-seo
entries.title: Hermes SEO
entries.description: Native Hermes port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped hermes_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the hermes_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the Hermes host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `hermes seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in Hermes plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active Hermes profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.

entries.name: hermes-session-diff
entries.description: Persistent session file diffs, run comparisons, and individual edit history in Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-session-reset-policy
entries.description: Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

entries.name: hermes-session-warmer
entries.description: Opt-in bounded idle prompt warming for explicitly allowlisted OpenAI-compatible text-chat endpoints. Sends potentially billable requests; no tool execution or conversation writes. Does not support Codex/Responses or native Anthropic. Authenticated endpoints use optional HERMES_SESSION_WARMER_API_KEY.

entries.name: hermes-sidepulse
entries.description: SidePulse lifecycle status backend; Desktop focus tracking requires the separate companion in the linked setup guide. Disclosure — forwards event names, a hashed agent id, the raw session_id and tool names to a local AF_UNIX socket and a 0600 jsonl log; no network egress.

entries.name: hermes-slash-router
entries.description: Jev-powered routing for misspelled, shortened, and meaning-based slash commands in the Hermes Desktop composer. Preserves drafts when unsure. Requires a TypeSafe API key; every non-exact lookup uses paid TypeSafe API usage. Disclosure — every non-exact slash token is sent through the plugin's local backend to api.typesafe.ai (paid, your TYPESAFE_API_KEY) together with the Desktop command catalog (names and descriptions), any prior route, up to 8 saved correction explanations and any clarification you type into its panel; message arguments and conversation content are not sent; the backend reads HERMES_HOME/.env only to check whether TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set.

entries.name: hermes-snapcompact
entries.description: Snapcompact context engine: archives conversation history as dense bitmap PNG frames that vision models read back at ~1/3 the token cost.

entries.name: hermes-soniox
entries.description: Native BYOK Soniox text-to-speech and asynchronous speech-to-text providers with configurable languages and voices, automatic STT language detection, and Hermes voice-bubble support. Disclosure — TTS sends reply text and synthesis settings to tts-rt.soniox.com; STT uploads audio, optional language hints, and optional prompt context to api.soniox.com, then best-effort deletes the remote transcription and uploaded file. SONIOX_API_KEY is resolved through Hermes' active-profile secret scope. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, or stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-speech
entries.description: Give your agent the voice it deserves. Guided TTS and STT setup for Hermes, with voice search and previews, model switching, testing, and native spoken replies across supported providers. Access 80+ speech models through a single API key with the AllModels router.

entries.name: hermes-ssh
entries.description: Manage SSH connections and remote workspaces in Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-structured-aux-models
entries.description: Routes selected Hermes auxiliary tasks (approval, MCP sampling, compression) through bounded Jev decision calls on OpenRouter instead of free-form chat prompts, failing open to the operator's own auxiliary provider for anything it cannot express as a decision. Disclosure — sends redacted approval prompts, MCP tool names and compression transcript blocks to openrouter.ai using your OpenRouter key (read-only); on any error approvals escalate to you, never auto-approve; the default decision_model is a moving alias, pin it.

entries.name: hermes-stt-enhance
entries.description: Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally. Post-processing is on by default and sends the transcript text to the LLM Hermes routes the stt_enhance auxiliary task to (your main, usually remote, provider unless you point it at a local endpoint or set post_processing.enabled: false). It reads the body of the SKILL.md you configure (never executed) and runs ffmpeg/ffprobe. The opt-in Parakeet backend reads a local model export and, on first use and only when your config.yaml explicitly sets security.allow_lazy_installs: true, installs pinned sherpa-onnx and numpy from PyPI into ~/.hermes/plugin-runtimes/hermes-stt-enhance/ (shared by all profiles). No tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-subscription-meter
entries.description: Provider-neutral subscription quota matrix panel — each provider's subscription window as a single time x quota row (elapsed vs remaining at a glance), with UI-side show/hide per provider row. Disclosure — reads provider keys from the current profile's .env and token presence from its auth.json, and calls each provider's own usage/balance API with that key (Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, Command Code, DeepSeek, xAI management, OpenRouter, Alibaba Cloud BSS, Grok, Codex via Hermes); an optional shared_sources setting reads another profile's .env/auth.json the same way; the token-activity heatmap reads per-day token totals, providers and model names from the state.db of this profile and of every other profile on the install (read-only, no message content, nothing leaves the machine); nothing is written outside this plugin's settings.

entries.name: hermes-switchyard
entries.description: Jev-powered Hermes plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after Hermes redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the Hermes redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of the current user turn after Hermes redact_for_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local_only); light turns (greetings, closed acknowledgements, and read-only listings) skip that hosted call by default. Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after Hermes redact_for_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence_finder_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.

entries.name: hermes-t3-control
entries.description: Bounded tools to list, read, create, and control local T3 coding threads on Linux and WSL2.

entries.name: hermes-tabs
entries.title: Hermes in the Browser
entries.description: Settings page (in the language set in Hermes, nine languages; incl. which browser Hermes works in and its safety level; loosening must be confirmed in the browser) and guard rails for hermes-tabs, which lets Hermes work in individual tabs of your real, signed-in Chromium browser through an extension and an MCP relay. Disclosure — talks only to the hermes-tabs relay you configure (HERMES_TABS_RELAY, default 127.0.0.1:8766) with HERMES_TABS_ADMIN_TOKEN (paths /admin/settings and /admin/select, the latter picks the browser when several are connected); caches the last seen settings in plugin-data/hermes-tabs/settings.json and its own opt-in switch in plugin-data/hermes-tabs/options.json; the pre_tool_call hook rejects the tabs tools while switched off and, only if the user turns that switch on, blocked sites in Hermes' own browser tools and web_extract. No shell, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-tabular
entries.description: Tabular AI that grows with your tables — Hermes skills for honest tabular ML, one entry point. Disclosure — Installing pulls numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow, joblib and pyyaml into Hermes's environment. The skills have the agent run Python on your data files, may ask it to pip install catboost, tabicl/torch, mapie or matplotlib, and the TabICL skill downloads a pretrained checkpoint of a few hundred MB on first use. Saved checkpoints are pickles: load only ones you made.

entries.name: hermes-tag
entries.description: Feishu platform override with per-chat Tier-0/Tier-1 context, standing work, and privacy lifecycle controls. Disclosure — replaces Hermes' bundled Feishu, Slack and DingTalk platform registrations with wrapped adapters; in chats listed in enabled_chats it stores every received group message (text and attachments, including from members who never talk to the bot) plus each @-mention question and reply in a plaintext SQLite file under the plugin's data directory (Tier-0 kept up to 24 h / 500 rows, Tier-1 memories with no time limit), answers /tag commands itself before Hermes' gateway admission (state-changing ones limited to the configured admins), and lets admins create Hermes cron jobs that post to the chat.

entries.name: hermes-tailscale
entries.description: Browse Tailscale devices and connect to remote Hermes instances in Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-talk
entries.description: Realtime voice for Hermes through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Disclosure — Realtime on the ChatGPT subscription uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex); the plugin never reads, refreshes or holds a token. GPT-Live on the subscription (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) starts one local `codex app-server` child per call on the Codex CLI's own login (API-key variables removed from its environment); that call uses the undocumented chatgpt.com Codex realtime endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice. The app-server's Codex thread is ephemeral and fenced (no environment, read-only sandbox, approvals declined, apps, shell, web search, plugins, sub-agents and each configured MCP server disabled, replies only "skip"); Talk reads only the MCP server names to disable them, and each voice request costs one small Codex turn of subscription quota. Voice audio and conversation context go to the selected provider (OpenAI, xAI, Google, optionally ElevenLabs); on Desktop the voice model can list the profile's sessions, read their titles and recent messages, create sessions and queue or steer prompts into them without a per-action confirmation; spoken requests are handed to the user's Hermes agent, whose tools run under Hermes approvals. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-taskbar-badge
entries.description: Windows taskbar badge on the Hermes window when a turn finishes. Calls navigator.setAppBadge on the message.complete event while the window is in the background, and clears it when the window regains focus or another session is opened. Disclosure — no network calls and no data leaves the machine; the badge is drawn by the app's own Electron process, which maps the Chromium Badging API onto the Windows taskbar overlay.

entries.name: hermes-teammates
entries.description: Give your agent a team: named subagents with their own instructions, tools and model, which it assigns work to, checks on and steers mid-task. The operator defines the roster; the agent follows up with a digest of earlier results and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock Hermes; no patched core. Disclosure — adds six tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Hermes subagents using credentials selected by Hermes from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); Hermes can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where Hermes provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion-notice code exists but never injects on current Hermes because the host cannot bind notices to the receiving session; use teammate_wait instead. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.

entries.name: hermes-telegram-business
entries.description: Observe-with-approval Telegram Business Mode (secretary bot): Hermes drafts replies to your customers' messages and DMs each draft to you with Send, Edit and Discard buttons; nothing reaches a customer until you tap Send. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — each customer message is sent to your active Hermes model to draft the reply, and drafts and connection records are stored locally in <HERMES_HOME>/telegram-business/state.db.

entries.name: hermes-telemetry-dashboard
entries.description: Dashboard-only read plugin: visualize the shared-metrics telemetry Hermes collects locally — metric families, drilldowns, milestone timeline, install snapshot, and the exact next package payload. Send stays off.

entries.name: hermes-telemetry
entries.description: Observability + budget guardrails for Hermes Agent — tokens, cost, latency, tool calls per session and cron job. Persists to local SQLite. Exposes /stats and /budget slash commands. Disclosure — records per-session tokens, cost, latency, tool names and sender/profile ids (no message text) in ~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db; fetches public model pricing from openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on first load and at most once a day; in the default enforce mode first load writes a $5/day, $100/month global budget to telemetry/budget.yaml, and a hard breach blocks every tool call and pauses the over-budget cron job until the window resets (set plugins.entries.hermes-telemetry.settings.mode: observe to record without enforcing); the optional standalone dashboard server binds 127.0.0.1 with no auth.

entries.name: hermes-tenuo
entries.title: Tenuo
entries.description:
Security guardrails for Hermes tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — hermes-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $HERMES_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.

entries.name: hermes-terminal
entries.description: Run the Hermes terminal interface in a Hermes Desktop workspace tab.

entries.name: hermes-themes-pack
entries.title: Hermes Themes Pack
entries.description: The 23 Omarchy stock themes (Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord, Rose Pine, Jade Horse and more) as Hermes skins, with one /theme command that switches the CLI, the TUI and Desktop together. Optionally follows the Omarchy theme. Works without Omarchy. Disclosure — registers only the /theme command (plus a `hermes theme` CLI subcommand under plugins.isolation: in_process); nothing runs at load time. /theme writes the pack's skins and a receipt under the active profile's HERMES_HOME (personal or edited skins of the same name are skipped) and selects one by running `hermes config set display.skin <name>`; it never edits config.yaml itself. It reads the current Omarchy theme from ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name. Only after /theme follow on does it write one executable hook into $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy/hooks/theme-set.d/; Omarchy runs it on theme switches and it switches ~/.hermes and every profile under ~/.hermes/profiles that has the pack installed. No network calls, background processes, Hermes tools, hooks or middleware, credentials, telemetry or self-updater.

entries.name: hermes-token-speed
entries.description: Live decode tokens-per-second chip for the Hermes Desktop status bar: 1-second sliding window while the model is still streaming, tool execution time excluded from decode seconds, UI spinner frames never counted, TTFT tracked separately, cumulative totals calibrated against authoritative provider usage at turn end. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: hermes-toolsmith
entries.description: Local developer tools, transformation recipes, and reviewed chat handoff inside Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: hermes-town
entries.description: Local pixel-art town where every Hermes session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. Disclosure — version 0.3.0 bundles the Town Node server and a prebuilt browser app inside the plugin directory and adds a hermes town setup/start/status/stop/open command tree. Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit hermes town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under HERMES_HOME/hermes-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

entries.name: hermes-tripo
entries.title: Hermes Tripo
entries.description: Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer in Hermes Desktop that shows whether a model is really rigged, a library pane that shows where each model came from (the steps behind it, its prompt, a jump back to the chat that made it, and one-click next steps), a local model inspector, and a status-bar chip with the Tripo balance and this chat's spend. Every credit-spending call goes through Hermes's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit (a setting under Settings → Plugins, default 100 credits) makes it ask again past it. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY. Unofficial; not affiliated with Tripo or VAST. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through Hermes's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder (or the folder set in its settings); keeps a local task history in $HERMES_HOME/tripo/history.json (chat id, tool, prompt, parent task, estimated cost, saved file paths; at most 2,000 tasks, never sent anywhere); the Desktop library opens local .glb/.fbx/.obj/.stl files only from inside your home folder, $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or the viewer's download folder, and uploads nothing; the status-bar chip reads your Tripo balance every two minutes and after each Tripo tool call; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-trove
entries.description: DAG-based context engine that never loses a message — full-text search, semantic recall, assertion-backed evidence compilation, and pre-answer sufficiency gating Disclosure — replaces the context engine and stores every turn's full raw transcript in HERMES_HOME/trove.db with secret redaction OFF by default; with TROVE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage, transcript text is sent to Voyage AI for embeddings; as a fallback it reads private AIAgent attributes read-only via frame inspection. No other network egress.

entries.name: hermes-vcc-engine
entries.title: Instant Context Compactor
entries.description: Instant context compaction for Hermes Agent: builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message for recall via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads Hermes's config.yaml through Hermes's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods and two private Hermes helpers, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing; with the opt-in only_local_models setting, compaction for a non-local chat model goes to Hermes's stock LLM summary.

entries.name: hermes-vcc
entries.description: Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $HERMES_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)

entries.name: hermes-verifier
entries.description: Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your Hermes session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in HERMES_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `hermes` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to Hermes's stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-video-editor
entries.title: Video Editor (local FFmpeg)
entries.description: Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in Hermes Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).

entries.name: hermes-vision-inline
entries.description: Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Hermes private vision helpers, so after a Hermes update it may silently fall back to the normal path.

entries.name: hermes-vitals-light
entries.title: Hermes Vitals Light
entries.description: CPU, load, free RAM, Linux PSI CPU pressure, active sessions, running Hermes processes and round-trip time of the connected Hermes server in the Desktop status bar, plus an optional TUI card. Disclosure — the Desktop chip's backend route reads CPU/memory figures via psutil, Linux /proc/pressure/cpu and /proc/meminfo, every process's command line (only per-command Hermes process counts are returned) and the server's own loopback /api/status, and reports the server hostname to the Desktop; the optional TUI card, copied by hand into tui-widgets/, runs the same code as a long-lived `python3 -c` child of the TUI and saves its options to <HERMES_HOME>/vitals.json; no third-party network call, no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: hermes-vpn
entries.description: Named network exits for the agent's browser: ask it to browse from another country and it switches, then verifies by reading back the address the far end actually saw, never trusting a label. Any VPN, WireGuard config or proxy works as a local exit; gluetun containers are discovered automatically and one can be brought up on demand. VPN credentials never reach the agent, the chat or the model. Disclosure -- a root-owned helper, installed out of band by the user through a narrow exact-path sudoers rule, is the only thing that reads the credentials and writes them to a root-only file (the agent names a country, never the key), and it pulls the gluetun image pinned by digest; the helper manages gluetun Docker containers, bringing exits up and down; the plugin registers a tool_execution middleware that holds browser_* calls when no verified exit is up (the kill switch, and optional cross-provider failover); it verifies exits by calling public IP-geolocation services (ipinfo, ifconfig.co, ip2location, cloudflare); credential entry is CLI-only, with no model tool for it -- `hermes vpn provider <name> --set` (interactive) or `--from-ref`, which resolves a WireGuard config from pass/gopass or a host file host-side and never returns it to the model; opening a .onion needs `hermes vpn allow-onion`, a terminal command a person runs (no model tool) that turns off Hermes's own internal-address check so onion names resolve and restarts Hermes, and the plugin never writes that setting itself; the active profile comes from the plugin context (ctx.profile_name), not a private core import.

entries.name: hermes-whatsapp-voice
entries.title: WhatsApp Voice Calls
entries.description: Live voice calls with Hermes over WhatsApp, on the linked-device (personal number) setup most Hermes users already have, with no WhatsApp Business account. Call your bot's number and talk to your Hermes: the voice uses Hermes's own persona (a short briefing fetched from Hermes) and hands real work to Hermes mid-call. Or let Hermes call you for things that matter: whatsapp_call_owner rings only the configured owner number (it has no destination parameter) and reports answered, no answer or declined, so the agent can fall back to another channel, including from cron. A short summary of each call arrives in WhatsApp, and each call keeps a record with timing metrics (hermes whatsapp-voice calls). Speech runs on Gemini Live (gemini-3.8-live by default), reusing the Gemini key Hermes already has; every call setting (languages, pauses, timeouts, any Live setup field) is configurable. Optional chat-session mode (context_mode: core_session, off by default) makes the call part of the owner's WhatsApp chat with Hermes. Setup is a dashboard tab (pairing QR, settings, test call) or an agent runbook skill. Disclosure — runs a separate sidecar process (Rust, built on whatsapp-rust) that the user starts or installs as a systemd/launchd user service; the binary is downloaded from this repo's GitHub release, built and attested by its release workflow, and checked against checksums pinned in the repo (plus the build attestation when the gh CLI is present). The sidecar becomes an extra linked device of the bot's WhatsApp number through an unofficial protocol, stores that session in the plugin's data directory, and answers only the owner's number. During calls it streams audio to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY (read via get_secret), along with the persona briefing, the outgoing call's reason and ask_hermes results as text. It calls the local api_server with API_SERVER_KEY for ask_hermes (a full Hermes turn with the owner's tools), the persona briefing (at startup and after each call) and the post-call summary, a run that may write to Hermes memory and whose result is sent to the owner on WhatsApp. The dashboard tab's backend saves only this plugin's settings (through hermes config set), starts and stops pairing, places test calls to the owner, and restarts the sidecar service (systemctl --user or launchctl). A pre_gateway_dispatch hook sends the owner's WhatsApp DM texts into an active chat-session call instead of a second text reply (slash commands, media, groups and other chats are untouched). Chat-session mode (opt-in) also runs a loopback service inside Hermes's process that reads the owner's WhatsApp DM session (system prompt, recent history, tool schemas) and sends it to Gemini, runs only the tools listed in voice_tools through Hermes in that session, and writes the call into that session. It never answers Hermes approval prompts: a command that needs approval is denied during the call and the owner is told to ask again in the WhatsApp text chat; it imports private Hermes modules (listed in the repo's CORE_PATCHES.md) and falls back to the default mode if they change. Optional recording (record_calls, off) saves the owner's side of each call as WAV in the plugin's data directory, locally only. An advanced voice_api_url setting can point the Live connection at another endpoint, which then receives the Gemini key and call audio. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-wincred
entries.description: Resolve Hermes environment variables from the current user's Windows Credential Manager at startup, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.wincred.map, an ENV_VAR -> generic-credential-target mapping (bare names or wincred:// names); each value is read with CredReadW in the current user's vault and handed to the secret-source orchestrator, which applies it with the usual precedence, provenance and conflict rules. Values may be UTF-8 or UTF-16LE (cmdkey and the Credential UI write UTF-16); anything that does not decode to text, or that contains interior NULs, is skipped with a warning instead of being injected as a mangled key. Disclosure - this source reads your Windows Credential Manager: only the generic credentials named in the map, with no enumeration of the vault. Resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. The package is read-only and stdlib-only (ctypes): it never creates, updates or deletes credentials, writes no files, starts no subprocesses, makes no network calls and does not self-update. Windows only. Credential Manager is user-scoped, so this raises the at-rest bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles; it is not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — when enabled, reads only the Windows Credential Manager generic credentials named in secrets.wincred.map (no vault enumeration) and injects them as environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries; read-only, stdlib ctypes, no subprocesses, no network, no file writes; user-scoped at-rest protection, not a boundary against code already running as the same user.

entries.name: hermes-windows-apps
entries.description: Answer "what is installed on this Windows machine": the software inventory behind Apps & Features, swept straight from the four Uninstall registry keys (the machine's 64-bit and 32-bit views plus the user's), so a program is found even when the Settings page hides it - a per-user install that never shows on the machine page came from the user view on the writing machine. Each row carries version, publisher, size in MB, install date and which view it lives in; the same DisplayName in two views is a 32/64-bit dual install, marked instead of listed twice. Entries the publisher asked to hide (runtime packages, update rollups) are filtered out unless asked for. Details one program with every field its publisher wrote and a reading of the uninstall command (MSI product code, setup executable, appx, script) so the next step is known before anything is run; the install folder is checked against disk. Use it for "what did that installer actually register", for inventory before a cleanup, and for "which of the two installs does uninstalling remove". Read-only: registry keys are enumerated and uninstall strings are reported, never run; no network, no file writes, no elevation. The sweep is pure registry - 102 entries in seven milliseconds on the writing machine, the whole table in ten, no PowerShell, no WMI. The plugin declares no Python dependencies. Windows only. Disclosure - the tools report program names, versions, publishers, sizes, install folders and uninstall commands, and what is hidden from Apps & Features, to the model; treat the output like the machine's own Apps & Features page.

entries.name: hermes-windows-computer-use
entries.description: THEIA — The Human Environment Intelligence Aperture: virtual-desktop capture, fused stage observation, guarded caches, bounded dynamic workflows, and persistent raw-RGB LocateAnything C++/Q5 CUDA grounding.

entries.name: hermes-windows-devices
entries.description: Answer "which device on this Windows machine is unhappy, and what does it need" on Windows: win_device_table lists every present PnP device with its class (System, Net, HIDClass, Display), its status, its manufacturer, its stable device id, and its problem code in words - 28 is one with no driver installed, 10 one that cannot start, 43 one Windows stopped after it reported a failure, 22 one the person switched off on purpose and is not broken - filtering by name or id substring, by class, or to the devices that need attention; devices no longer plugged in are history, left out unless asked for. win_device_detail takes one device by id or name substring and adds the driver behind it from the signed-driver table - name, version, date, provider, signer, INF file, signed or not - or the absence of one, which for code 28 is the same fact said twice; a disabled device gets a note saying it is on purpose, not an alarm. Use it for the Device Manager yellow-mark question without opening Device Manager, for finding what an uninstalled program left behind, and for what changed after an update. Read-only: nothing is enabled, disabled, updated or reinstalled. Both answers come from CIM (Win32_PnPEntity and Win32_PnPSignedDriver, joined by device id), whose property names, enum values and ids do not change with the display language; the human-facing device names localize and are carried through as data, never parsed. The plugin declares no Python dependencies; there is no network call and no file write. Windows only. Disclosure — the tools report device names, manufacturers, device ids and driver versions to the model, and those reveal the machine's hardware inventory and what is plugged into it; treat the output like a Device Manager window opened on their machine.

entries.name: hermes-windows-eventlog
entries.description: Answer "why did this process die" on Windows: three read-only tools over the Windows Event Log. win_crash_events reads Application Error / Application Hang / Windows Error Reporting / .NET Runtime records for a time window, decodes the exception code (0xC0000005 -> ACCESS_VIOLATION and the other codes a debugger would name), reports the faulting module, its path and the fault offset, and groups repeated crashes by app and signature. Records are classified by provider as well as by event id, so unrelated providers that reuse ids 1000 and 1001 for informational events are not reported as crashes. win_shutdown_events reads the System log for Kernel-Power 41 unexpected restarts, bugchecks decoded to names (0x9F -> DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE, accepting the decimal form some providers emit), EventLog 6008 dirty shutdowns, 1074 operator-initiated restarts with the process and comment, and the 6005/6006/12/13 start and stop markers. win_eventlog_query is the general case: any channel, filtered by event ids, levels, an exact provider name or a payload substring, returning structured records instead of raw XML. Queries read newest-first and stop at the window start or at a 5000-record scan cap; a call returns at most 200 records and marks truncated payload text. Channel names, provider names and numeric filters are validated before anything is interpolated into the query. Disclosure - this plugin reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely includes user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...). Treat tool output like any other local diagnostic dump when sharing it. It reads only the channels the current account may read - Security and some operational logs answer with an access-denied error rather than any attempt to obtain elevation - and it never writes to a log, clears one or configures a channel. Stdlib-only (ctypes wevtapi plus xml.etree): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure — reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely include user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...); win_eventlog_query reads any channel the account running Hermes may read, so an unelevated account gets access-denied on Security and some operational logs while an elevated Hermes can return Security-log records (logon events with account names and source addresses). It never requests elevation, never writes to, clears or configures a log, and has no Python dependencies, child processes, network calls, file writes or self-update. Windows only.

entries.name: hermes-windows-ops
entries.description: Windows and WSL triage skills for Hermes: processes that survive a quit (orphaned stdio MCP trees, lingering python/uv/node children), WSL-to-Windows interop where an argument reaches cmd.exe as shell syntax, config and encoding traps (UTF-8 BOM, legacy console code pages), and long-path or reserved-name errors. One skill plus a copy-paste command reference; the process, argv and job-object failure modes are pinned to reports #131561, #132069 and #61059 and re-verified against current main. Disclosure — instructions only: no tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or credentials, and the destructive diagnostics are marked and gated on asking the user first.

entries.name: hermes-windows-ports
entries.description: Answer "who holds this port" on Windows. win_port_owners reads the TCP and UDP owner tables through iphlpapi (the same rows netstat -ano prints, with the owning PID attached) and resolves each PID to its image name and path, returning one structured record per endpoint. Filters cover one port, several ports, a process substring, the protocol (tcp, udp or both), the TCP state (listen, established, any state name, or all; UDP rows report bound) and IPv6 inclusion, with a record cap and a per-process summary of the rows returned. Built for the failure mode that stalls agents on Windows: a gateway, backend or bridge that cannot bind, where the error names a port but not the process holding it. netstat -ano prints columns, not fields, and its PID still needs a second command (tasklist, or a PowerShell round-trip) to become an image name; this tool is one in-process call instead of a shell parse plus a join, with no child process and no dependency on PowerShell being installed or allowed by execution policy. A protected process whose image cannot be queried keeps its PID and reports a null process name instead of failing the call. Disclosure - the tool reports the local and remote addresses, ports, PIDs and process image paths that netstat -ano and Task Manager already show, and those values reach the model; treat the output like any other local diagnostic listing. Read-only: no socket is opened, bound or connected, the only process access is QueryFullProcessImageName with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION to read an image name, and there is no memory reading, no handle inheritance and no injection. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only.

entries.name: hermes-windows-process
entries.description: Answer "what is still running, and who started it" on Windows: win_process_table reads the process table (PID, parent PID, image name) and adds each process's image path and creation time, then marks every row with whether its recorded parent is still the process that spawned it. Windows stores a parent PID rather than a handle, so a child that outlived its parent points at a PID that is either unused or reused by a newer process; a parent that started after its child cannot have spawned it, so both cases are reported as gone or reused instead of a plausible but wrong parent name. Filters cover one PID, several PIDs, a name or path substring, a parent PID, and an orphans-only view of what outlived its parent, with a result cap and an option to leave out Windows session processes. Use it for leftover gateway/backend/server children after a quit, for telling thirty python.exe rows apart by start time, and for checking whether a process started before or after the thing being debugged. Read-only: processes are opened with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION for QueryFullProcessImageName and GetProcessTimes only - no memory reads (command lines are deliberately out of scope), no handle duplication, no writes, no child processes. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure - the tool reports image names, image paths and start times to the model, and those routinely include the user and machine name (C:\Users\<name>\...) and reveal which editor, shell or agent started which process; treat the output like a Task Manager screenshot.

entries.name: hermes-windows-services
entries.description: Answer "what runs as a service on this machine, why did one fail, and what does it depend on" on Windows: win_service_table lists every service with its state (Running, Stopped, Paused), its start mode (Auto, Manual, Disabled, with the delayed flag folded in as "Auto, delayed"), the pid it runs under, the account and binary it runs as, the dependency edges both ways, and what its exit code means - 1077 is one that has not tried to start since the last boot, 1053 one that did not answer in time, 1075 one whose dependency failed first, 2 one whose binary is gone. win_service_detail takes one service and gives what Windows does when it fails (the FailureActions blob decoded: restart the service, restart the computer, run a command, after how many seconds, and when the count resets), whether the registered binary is still on disk, and the Service Control Manager's own event-log record behind the failure - 7000 failed to start, 7009 a start request that timed out, 7024 a service-specific error, 7031 an unexpected end, 7045 an install. Use it for what died after the last update, for finding what an uninstalled program left registered, and for the dependency order before a restart. Read-only: nothing is started, stopped, reconfigured or deleted. The listing comes from one Get-CimInstance Win32_Service call because its property names and enum values do not change with the display language while sc.exe localizes both; dependencies and failure actions are read from the registry, because CIM's DependOnService property is never populated and the failure policy exists nowhere in CIM at all. The plugin declares no Python dependencies; there is no network call and no file write. Windows only. Disclosure - the tools report service names, display names, command lines, logon accounts and the event-log history to the model, and those reveal what the person has installed, what runs as their machine's system accounts, and the paths under C:\Program Files and C:\Users\<name>; treat the output like a Services window opened on their machine.

entries.name: hermes-windows-startup
entries.description: Answer "what launches itself on this machine" on Windows: win_startup_table lists every autostart entry across the six Run/RunOnce registry keys (HKCU and HKLM, plus the 32-bit views) and the two Startup folders, with where each one comes from, whether it is machine- or user-scoped, and whether the person switched it off in Task Manager - Explorer's StartupApproved verdict, with the date it was last changed, a state Win32_StartupCommand has no field for; approval records uninstalled programs left behind are reported as leftovers, their unknown state bytes surfaced as-is rather than guessed into verdicts. win_startup_detail takes one entry and resolves its command the way the loader does - quoting, arguments, environment variables, and unquoted paths with spaces resolved by longest existing prefix - and says whether the binary is still on disk, plus a folder file's size and last change. Use it for what added itself since last month, for slimming a slow sign-in, and for a launcher whose program is already gone. Read-only: nothing is enabled, disabled or deleted; the Startup folders are read through Explorer's User Shell Folders values so OneDrive-redirected folders are found. The sweep is registry and directory reads only - about a millisecond for three Run values and two folders on the machine it was written on, no PowerShell, no WMI. The plugin declares no Python dependencies; there is no network call and no file write. Windows only. Disclosure - the tools report program names, launch commands, binary paths under C:\Program Files and C:\Users\<name>, and what the person chose to keep from starting, to the model; treat the output like the Startup tab of the person's own Task Manager.

entries.name: hermes-windows-tasks
entries.description: Answer "what does this machine run on its own, and did it work" on Windows: win_scheduled_tasks lists the Task Scheduler's tasks with their state (Ready, Running, Disabled), the account each runs as, its first action's command line, its triggers in words (at logon, daily, weekly, at a time, on event), its last and next run with the machine's offset, its missed runs, and what its last result code means - 0x80070002 is a program that is no longer there, 0x800710E0 a task that needed a desktop it did not have, 0x40010004 one that was stopped, 0x80040154 a COM class that is not registered. win_scheduled_task_detail takes one task and gives its triggers with start boundaries and repetition, its actions with arguments and working directory, its principal and the settings that decide whether it runs on battery or when late; a task with no triggers but MaintenanceSettings runs during automatic maintenance and the notes say so rather than leaving an empty list. Use it for why a logon task keeps failing, for finding what an uninstalled program left behind at logon, for telling a disabled task from a broken one, and for reading a task's command line before trusting it. Read-only: nothing is created, started, changed or deleted. Reads through the ScheduledTasks cmdlets rather than the store on disk, because the TaskCache registry tree and C:\Windows\System32\Tasks both answer access denied without elevation, and rather than schtasks /Query /FO CSV, which is localized and interleaves error lines for tasks whose definitions are gone. The plugin declares no Python dependencies; there is no network call and no file write. Windows only. Disclosure - the tools report task paths, command lines, working directories, account names and SIDs to the model, and those reveal what the person has installed, what starts at their logon, and the paths under C:\Users\<name>; treat the output like a Task Scheduler window opened on their machine.

entries.name: hermes-windows-updates
entries.description: Answer "what did Windows install lately, and did it work" on Windows: the update history the Settings app shows - Windows updates, Defender signature and platform updates, driver updates - newest first, with each entry's outcome in words (in progress, succeeded, succeeded with errors, failed, aborted) and, when an entry did not end clean, the failure's error code in 0x form (the agent hands codes over signed; -2145124300 is shown as its unsigned spelling). Filter to the ones that did not end clean, or search titles. The hotfix list (KB numbers, security updates, install dates, newest first) answers "when was this machine last patched" at a glance; it carries OS-level updates only, which the notes say. Use it for "why does it say pending forever", for "did the update that broke something actually install", and for a patch report before assuming a machine is current. Read-only: the history is queried through the Windows Update Agent's session interface and CIM, and nothing else - no update search is run, nothing is downloaded, installed or uninstalled, no elevation. On the writing machine a 723-entry history returns the newest 500 in about a tenth of a second; the first call also starts the COM session, about a quarter of a second. The plugin declares no Python dependencies; there is no network call of its own and no file write. Windows only. Disclosure — each tool call runs one hidden powershell.exe with a fixed read-only script (Windows Update Agent history through COM, Win32_QuickFixEngineering through CIM; no update search, download or install); the tools report update titles, dates, outcomes, failure codes and support links, and hotfix ids, descriptions, install dates and the account that installed them, to the model; treat the output like the Settings app's own update history page.

entries.name: hermes-workbench
entries.description: The Hermes desktop app in your browser. `hermes workbench` serves the desktop interface through the Hermes dashboard, for headless servers, VPSes and tablets. Disclosure — community plugin, not a Nous product. On the first `hermes workbench` run and again after each Hermes update it runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` (guided by Hermes's lockfile) and Vite against your Hermes checkout's desktop sources, writing only under ~/.hermes/hermes-workbench and its own plugin dir (the checkout is only read), and starts `hermes dashboard` on loopback when none is running.

entries.name: hermes-worker-monitor
entries.description: Kanban board groups and worker health in the Hermes Desktop footer: blocked cards first and red, live running state as a coloured dot, hover for the breakdown, one click to open the board. Worker-only fork of hermes-monitor. No credentials are read and there is no network egress; it opens kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only and returns counts only. Zero model tokens.

entries.name: hermes-workflows
entries.description: Agent-owned workflow graphs for Hermes — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock Hermes; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop;
