each agent node is a child hermes chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv and a fan-out's precheck_argv (run once per item before its child spawns) run agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Hermes' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use until_argv to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $HERMES_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through Hermes' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed/run.partial and fan-out straggler events the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml (or API_SERVER_KEY) and POSTs a wake turn to the configured Hermes API server — the gate.held, run.done, run.failed and run.partial wakes state they authorize no choice, repair or additional work, while the straggler wake asks the woken session to take one action (steer the open items, accept the partial, or stop the run); a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $HERMES_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; opt-in settings (all default off) mirror run lifecycle events to an operator-configured https webhook with an optional bearer (outbound_bridge), present held gates into the run owner's own gateway session via plugin message injection (hooks_bridge_allow: approval_bridge, which also needs allow_gateway_injection), and append delegate_task child records to a spool under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-state (hooks_allow: subagent_accounting); state lives under $HERMES_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own.

entries.name: hermes-wsl-terminal
entries.description: Run Hermes' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and hermes doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). HERMES_WSL_DISTRO and HERMES_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and Hermes never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in Hermes is patched or rebound at runtime.

entries.name: hermes-wslc-sandbox
entries.description: Run Hermes' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: hermes-xai
entries.description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to Hermes as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal Hermes turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

entries.name: hermes-zh
entries.description: Simplified Chinese (简体中文) language pack. Declarative locales/zh.yaml overlay for part of approval.* and gateway.*; placeholders match en.yaml.

entries.name: hermes_otel
entries.description: OpenTelemetry for Hermes Agent: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list, an OTEL_* variable, or LANGSMITH_TRACING=true); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $HERMES_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

entries.name: hermesford
entries.title: HermesFord
entries.description: An HD-2D pixel-art village page for Hermes Desktop: every chat is a villager who walks to the forge, library, woods or town hall depending on the tool its agent is running, waits at the town hall when the chat needs you, and goes home to sleep when the chat is not active. Click a villager to open its chat. Built on the Luminati engine (MIT). Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface, read-only session.list / session.active_list polling every 3 s); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network calls.

entries.name: hermesvault
entries.description: Keep secrets out of plaintext .env files: a local encrypted vault (FloorVault, AES-256-SIV) whose items Hermes loads as environment variables at startup (mapped source "hermesvault", hv: references), with a hermes hvault CLI to manage items. The vault key lives in your OS key store (Keychain, Secret Service, DPAPI), a key file, a systemd-creds credential, or HERMES_VAULT_KEY. Disclosure — reads an encrypted store under <HERMES_HOME>/agent-vault (or secrets.hermesvault.dir) at startup; hermes hvault commands write to it and hermes hvault setup creates it; reads its own master key only from the variable named by token_env (default HERMES_VAULT_KEY) in the environment Hermes scopes to the profile being fetched, else from the custody set in secrets.hermesvault.custody: os (default; macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service or Windows DPAPI, service floor-vault, shared with other FloorVault apps on the same account), key_file (the file named by secrets.hermesvault.key_file, which must not be writable by group or others), or systemd-creds (master.key.sdcred beside the store) — never from FLOOR_VAULT_KEY, VAULT_MASTER_KEY or FLOOR_VAULT_KEY_FILE, which it also protects from being overwritten; a configured custody that fails is reported, never replaced by another; startup never prompts and never creates a key, a credential or a store (a locked or missing key is reported and Hermes starts without those variables), and only hermes hvault setup may unlock the key store or create the key; reads Hermes' own command line (sys.argv and sys.orig_argv, no other process's) to compare with the command bindings stored on an item by floorvault secrets allow, and resolves a bound item only when Hermes was started with one of them (secrets.hermesvault.require_binding, default off, also skips items with no binding); resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, like .env entries; installs floorvault>=0.2.8,<0.4 from PyPI (plus secretstorage on Linux, pyobjc-framework-Security on macOS); one subprocess, only with custody: systemd-creds: the system's own systemd-creds (decrypt --user at startup; encrypt and decrypt in hermes hvault setup), found only in system directories, run as an argument list with no shell and a minimal environment, the key passed through a pipe; otherwise no subprocesses; no network calls, no self-update; protection is at rest, not against code already running as the same user.

entries.name: hermetic
entries.title: hermetic
entries.description: Status-bar popover for Hermes Desktop with three views: Costs (spend, cache, pricing drift, OpenRouter provider routing), AAI (skill changes, ratings, tests and replays) and HDR (a guard for risky tool calls, hooks, destinations, sensitive paths, what runs on its own). Disclosure — reads this profile's sessions (and other profiles' when you pick them) to audit tool calls, paths and hosts; can edit and save config.yaml and rewrite skill files when you ship or revert a version, and once you give background tasks your routing rules, rewrites those tasks' entries in config.yaml by itself (from a background thread, at most once a minute) when the main provider changes; adds your data_collection and zdr routing rules to requests sent to Nous Portal; AAI replays and judge runs resend conversation context and tool definitions to OpenRouter with your OpenRouter key and incur cost (Nous Portal profiles are refused); HDR lists listening TCP ports via ps/lsof; HDR's guard (off by default) checks each tool call through a pre_tool_call hook and, when you turn it on, holds calls Hermes does not check itself (reading keys and logins, writing startup items or key places Hermes does not list) and asks you in its own card, blocking without an answer in time (6 seconds inside Hermes' plugin hook limit: 24 seconds by default, 120 seconds when that limit is off) or at once when hermetic is not open, or blocks them outright; the guard is a best-effort match on the paths a call names, not a sandbox; questions from every profile wait in the default profile's hermetic folder; HDR also lists shell and gateway hooks and flags hook scripts edited after approval, keeping a copy of each script to compare; Costs reads public model price lists (OpenRouter, and hopscotchlabs.ai model pages for models a profile is billed for through Hopscotch) and, at most once a minute, asks Hermes for the profile provider's account report (OpenRouter usage and limits, Anthropic and OpenAI Codex plan windows, Nous credits and spend cap), with Hermes looking up the credential, and reads OpenRouter workspace and guardrail budgets itself with the profile's OpenRouter key, sent only to OpenRouter.

entries.name: hicortex
entries.description: Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

entries.name: hindsight
entries.description: Hindsight long-term memory provider — knowledge graph, entity resolution and multi-strategy retrieval (recall/reflect/retain tools plus automatic per-turn capture). Maintained by Vectorize; cloud, local external and local embedded modes are available. `hermes memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main). Disclosure — in cloud mode (and local external) every turn's conversation, and every entry the agent adds or replaces in Hermes's built-in MEMORY/USER stores, is sent to api.hindsight.vectorize.io or the URL you configure, into every bank it writes to; local embedded mode starts a background Hindsight daemon (fetched with uvx, version-pinned, on first run when hindsight-api is not installed) and keeps its LLM settings in ~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env; setup writes the keys you enter to the profile .env; repositories under folders you list in trusted_project_dirs may choose their bank with .hindsight/config.toml; `hermes memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main).

entries.name: holographic
entries.title: Holographic
entries.description: Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless an optional online feature is switched on: search by meaning (embeddings: on) or rescoring by a cross-encoder (rerank: on), both off by default. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.hermes-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `hermes update` moves existing users onto it; a file without merges keeps history schema 1; the first merge raises it to schema 2, after which writers of 0.15-0.18 refuse it until 0.19.0 or a pre-merge backup is restored. Taken over from Nous Research's handoff copy (NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, hermes_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Since 0.18.0 an optional, experimental second stage reorders the recall candidates with a cross-encoder at a /v1/rerank endpoint that answers in Cohere's shape without a key, such as llama-server (rerank: on, off by default). It does not raise hits: on the maintainer's held-out set (126 questions) it cut non-target facts in the top five by about 40 % and lines per turn by about a third, and lost about one target per hundred questions. Disclosure — local only unless an optional online feature (search by meaning or rescoring) is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact_store rebuild_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry (at the debug log level the recall stages log fact ids and scores, never text), and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on or rerank: on (both off by default). With embeddings: on, the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; with rerank: on, before a turn the user's message and up to rerank_top_k (40) candidate fact texts, and for a fact_store search its query and results, go to the rerank endpoint the user configures (rerank_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name), with no credentials and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject or that look like they hold a secret, and queries that hold one, are not sent; a failure or a slow answer gives the recall of rerank: off and pauses the endpoint (60 s, doubling to 900 s); nothing the endpoint returns is stored; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored. Since 0.19.0, fact_store merge combines duplicate facts in one transaction while keeping each copy's history, sources and confirmations under its original id. The retained fact keeps its own text, trust and origin; copies leave current search and recall. Optional expect pins the exact shown versions and refuses changed participants without a write. Scheduled jobs can merge only copies created in their own session. Forgetting the retained fact also erases its merged copies. Merge is local and makes no new network or model calls. Version 0.19.1 adds strict tooling for comparing recorded margins; the normal RECALL_MARGIN remains 1.0. Version 0.19.2 closes a timed-out rerank or embeddings request socket so a server dripping response headers does not keep its worker alive. During TLS wrapping, cancellation is retained but the handshake can continue until its own socket timeout; DNS resolution is outside socket cancellation. Version 0.20.0 adds an opt-in local task-outcome journal and the memory-provider tool fact_experience: emitted and candidate fact/version identifiers, an optional short task and correction, outcome/reason and optional corrected-source references. It is separate from trust, origin and ranking. Agent reports are not authenticated human confirmations. Collection and detailed tracing are off by default; retention is bounded to 30 days and 1000 attempts per store, with up to 10 revisions per attempt. Forgetting any referenced fact removes the dependent attempt and outcome from the store. No new model, network or credential use; synchronous local writes add latency. PR #45 also loads NumPy on first use outside the plugin-loader lock; concurrent first callers wait for import completion. Version 0.20.1 limits SQLite busy waits for the optional journal and retries transient contention once. Failed receipts are reported and are not queued; the SQLite timeout is not a full search deadline. Version 0.20.2 writes no receipt for a prefetch that emits nothing, applies journal retention whenever a writer opens the store (also with the journal off) and scrubs removed outcome text from the file like a forgotten fact. Version 0.20.3 adds one system-prompt line, only with the journal on, asking the agent to record an outcome when the person corrects an answer that used recalled facts (an agent report, not human confirmation). Version 0.21.0 adds an opt-in prefetch_max_tokens budget for the recalled block: facts that do not fit are left out whole, never cut; off by default. Version 0.22.0 keeps entity links honest on a text change: a new entities list replaces the declared names, and a declared name the new text no longer says is dropped; revert restores a version's declared names from an additive version_names table (names with keyed hashes, removed with the version and by delete_entity in every spelling a tombstone covers, including by older releases through triggers). Version 0.22.1 makes the secret/instruction screen about 30× faster on long texts with the same decisions (patterns unchanged; a prefilter chooses where they are tried). Version 0.22.2 sends a slow reranker only as many of the first candidates as its measured speed answers in half rerank_timeout (at least two), so a large pool no longer times out and pauses the endpoint; the candidates not sent keep their order behind the scored ones. Version 0.23.0 stops feedback (helpful/unhelpful) from refreshing a fact's age: optional temporal decay counts from when the current version was recorded, and updated_at changes only when the fact itself does; a correction with a new text (correct / update content) starts at its origin's trust without the old text's helpful marks, recalls and confirmations, like change, while a date-only correction keeps them and revert restores the old trust. Version 0.23.1 takes a correction that journal retention removed off the disk on the open connection (the file rewrite runs after the receipt write, with busy timeout 0 at every step) and clears only the rewrite mark it served. Version 0.24.0 adds two experimental features, both off by default and with no new network, model or credential use: memory_map.py, a command-line exporter nothing in the provider calls, which prints one store as a read-only JSON snapshot for a person to read (opened mode=ro in one read transaction; a forgotten fact is its id and date only; corrected versions and texts the safety screen hides carry no text; with --config it reads config.yaml's search settings, with --hermes-home the hermes-dreaming files about the profile store), whose output holds the facts' texts and so is personal data; and prefetch_clause_coverage: on, which gives each of two separate Russian or English questions in one message a second look at the facts the coverage gate left out. Version 0.25.0 limits the memory map export to 1000 facts and 300 names by default (--max-facts / --max-entities, 0 for none) and says what it cut in SNAP.limits; nothing else changes. Version 0.25.1 fixes recall by meaning dropping a fact that names a short Russian name in another grammatical case than the message (Eva as «Ева» / «Еву»): the name now also meets a capitalized word of the fact that may be a case form of it. Version 0.25.2 reads that word by its case ending rather than a short stem: names whose stem changes meet their forms («Лев» / «Льва»), and different names that only shared a short stem («Аня» / «Анна») no longer meet; nothing else changes. Version 0.25.3 no longer imports NumPy when the provider starts (the first search that needs it does, as does opening a store whose vectors need re-encoding) and treats a NumPy that is installed but fails to import as missing, so recall goes on by words; finds a Latin word written into Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Thai text by itself; refuses at write, and leaves out of recall, a prompt addressed to an assistant and the agent's report of its own steps; and auto_extract (off by default) no longer stores a reply such as "I like that" as a preference; no change to defaults, schema or network behaviour. Version 0.26.0 adds an experimental presence gate, prefetch_presence_gate (off by default): with it on, a fact this provider injected is held back past the six-turn repeat window only while the model can verifiably still see it (its exact recall line inside a <memory-context> block the core fenced, or its fact id and text in a fact_store result), reading only the messages the core already passes to sync_turn, with no new storage, network, model or credential use; tool results now carry raw Unicode instead of Unicode escape sequences (a payload that cannot be encoded keeps the escaped form); change names the keywords it drops and correct writes the keywords it is given; with the gate off, recall is unchanged. Version 0.26.1 fixes that gate after an independent review: a sync the core queued before a compaction no longer counts as the current view, a fact the compaction removed is recalled again once a fresh view no longer shows it, a compaction that fails no longer switches the gate off for the session, a late sync keeps its own turn, and a fact_store history result counts as the fact being visible; with the gate off nothing changes. Version 0.26.2: with the task-outcome journal on (off by default), a prefetch that only refreshes facts the session already holds records no new attempt and carries no Memory attempt line, so a repeated block adds nothing new to the context. Version 0.26.3: with the journal and the presence gate on, a delivery whose attempt could not be written after a compaction no longer stops that fact from recording attempts later. Version 0.26.4 fixes the presence gate after a second independent review: two late syncs in a row each keep their own turn, a quiet session that compacted leaves no lasting state, and a refresh no longer keeps token-budget room for an attempt line it does not carry.

entries.name: home-dashboard
entries.description: Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Hermes Web and Desktop.

entries.name: homeassistant-statistics
entries.description: Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access.

entries.name: homeassistant
entries.description: Home Assistant gateway platform (state-change events in, persistent notifications and cron notify delivery out) plus the homeassistant toolset (ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically.

entries.name: honcho
entries.description: Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (Hermes version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers that Honcho records for usage attribution. Links the plugin opens or prints to app.honcho.dev and docs.honcho.dev carry static utm_source=hermes, utm_medium=plugin and utm_content=<placement> parameters; nothing user-, machine- or session-identifying is added.

entries.name: hopper
entries.description: Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in Hermes without modifying the core catalog.

entries.name: hud-teach
entries.description: Click-through numbered marks on any live Mac window — chess, games, Photoshop, Settings — so Hermes can teach on the real UI without clicking for the user.

entries.name: huddo
entries.description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, answer or close polls and forms, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.10.2, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, and when a message contains a link it fetches that page once from this machine (public hosts only, skipped for links carrying a token or signature) and uploads a small preview image with the message; huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; Hermes does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_answer/huddo_close_choices/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar/huddo_rename run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, and, if Hermes can schedule recurring tasks, to schedule one that does the same between turns, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; the server also tells the agent to read the remote guide at https://huddo.ai/SKILL.md before starting (vendor-hosted, not pinned), and the skills point to npx -y huddoai@latest (unpinned) for identity export and app publishing; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) and a local copy of your rooms' messages (used by huddo_search/huddo_show/huddo_files; huddo_sync fetches older history from api.huddo.ai) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry; requests to api.huddo.ai carry an x-huddo-client header (cli/mcp/<version>) that the server counts for usage statistics, with no identity or content in it. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skills tell the agent to get confirmation in your own Hermes chat before anything sensitive.

entries.name: hwiki
entries.description: Markdown wiki as Hermes long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside HERMES_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Hermes's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at HERMES_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in HERMES_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to hermes backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

entries.name: hyatlas
entries.title: HyAtlas Memory
entries.description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `hermes memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Hermes's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through Hermes's get_secret and reads no Hermes credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as Hermes auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `hermes memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Nous Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `hermes hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `hermes hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with Hermes's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Hermes starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `hermes hyatlas start` keeps running after Hermes exits until `hermes hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `hermes hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads Hermes auth.json). No telemetry.

entries.name: hydradb
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes, backed by HydraDB. Relevant context is recalled before each turn, and completed turns are saved in the background. Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

entries.name: hypd-ai-ads
entries.description: Read-only paid-media analysis for Google Ads, Meta (Facebook) Ads, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics (GA4), Search Console and Merchant Center through the hosted HYPD MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with four skills (setup, tool rules, overview, ready-made analyses). OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Read-only: never changes campaigns, budgets or ads. Disclosure — runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (downloaded from npm on first run) as a local bridge to HYPD's hosted MCP server at mcp.hypd.ai; tool arguments and the ad, analytics, Search Console and Merchant Center data HYPD returns pass through HYPD's servers; sign-in is a browser OAuth flow whose tokens mcp-remote stores in ~/.mcp-auth; read-only is HYPD's server-side guarantee, and the analysis templates the skills follow are fetched from HYPD's server at run time.

entries.name: icarus
entries.description: Self-memory and replacement models for Hermes agents. Remember your work. Train your replacement.

entries.name: idealphase-elevenlabs-audio-tags
entries.title: IdealPhase Audio Tags
entries.description: Hermes plugin that adds a few honest ElevenLabs delivery tags so speech sounds more human. It does not replace the built-in ElevenLabs voice provider, and it does not change the chat transcript. Disclosure — sends the prepared speech, voice ID, model ID, and any pronunciation-dictionary locator to api.elevenlabs.io with your ELEVENLABS_API_KEY; synthesis is billed to your ElevenLabs account. When automatic tags are on, the untagged transcript is also sent to the model configured for auxiliary.idealphase_elevenlabs_audio_tags, or your normal chat model if you did not pin one. Audio is written only to the path Hermes requests. No tools, hooks, or middleware. Does not store the key, phone home, or log the transcript.

entries.name: identity
entries.description: View and edit the identity files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, AGENT.md/HERMES.md) from chat, switch the active profile, and see per-line usage with colour-coded staleness timestamps. Adds six tools, /identity, /identity-switch and /identity-dashboard commands, and a utilization dashboard pane. Disclosure — reads and writes the identity files and a line-utilization record inside the selected profile directory under HERMES_HOME, and can change which profile is active; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — the model-callable identity_edit tool rewrites SOUL.md/MEMORY.md/USER.md/AGENT.md and identity_switch_profile writes HERMES_HOME/active_profile.

entries.name: image-utils
entries.description: Inspect, resize, crop, rotate, convert and re-encode image files in-process with Pillow - no shell, no ImageMagick, no network.

entries.name: inbox
entries.description: hermes inbox: one read-only view of everything in flight for the active profile: failed or paused cron jobs, stalled or dropped delegations, orphaned background processes, blocked kanban tasks, running work, undelivered delegation results, upcoming cron runs and open chat sessions, with --json for scripts. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — reads processes.json, cron/jobs.json, runtime/active_sessions.json and state.db (SQLite read-only) in the profile's home, plus the shared kanban board's kanban.db (read-only); it never writes, repairs or prunes them, adds no model tools or hooks, and sends nothing anywhere.

entries.name: index-network
entries.title: Index
entries.description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `hermes index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Hermes env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Hermes model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $HERMES_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Hermes env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Hermes sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.

entries.name: index-search
entries.description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. It searches a Meilisearch server you run, so notes or local files can be found only after you index them there; it does not search files on disk itself. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can search with your key. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. On Hermes 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. index_watch save stores one query and prints a hermes cron create line for every 15 minutes. You run that line. A run is a model turn, and a tool call is another model request, with no daily cap. The watch covers only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. This plugin does not create or remove the cron job and it does not ask. Writes use the guard in agent.file_safety. An update can stop the watch.

entries.name: infisical
entries.description: Secret source plugin that resolves environment variables from an Infisical secret store (cloud or self-hosted) at Hermes startup. Registers a mapped source ("infisical", inf:// references) and a bulk source ("infisical_bulk").

entries.name: inkbox
entries.description: Inkbox email, SMS/MMS, iMessage, voice, and A2A platform plugin for Hermes Agent.

entries.name: inline-platform
entries.description: Use Hermes Agent from Inline work-chat DMs, chats, and reply threads. Disclosure — the setup wizard can, on explicit opt-in, download https://inline.chat/cli/install.sh and pipe it to sh without a checksum, then run the vendor inline CLI login; on connect the adapter publishes your Hermes slash-command list and the names and descriptions of installed skills to the Inline server (INLINE_SYNC_COMMANDS=false disables); error telemetry is off unless a Sentry DSN is set.

entries.name: innernet
entries.title: innernet
entries.description: One memory for every AI tool: load a project's context, answer from what was decided before, save new decisions back, and pick up where the last session left off, in the same memory Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Grok read and write. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at innernet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with CIMD and DCR); the two bundled skills load as innernet:innernet and innernet:innernet-handoff. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code, hooks, background process, telemetry or self-update. Every tool call goes to innernet.live, signed in as the user through innernet's own browser sign-in (a first sign-in creates a free innernet account); what a call carries (a project name, a question, text the user asks to save) is sent there, and what the memory holds comes back into the session context, so it reaches the user's model provider. Some tools write to the user's innernet account (save context, capture a note, write a handoff, update a task, forget on request); every write is versioned and can be read, edited or deleted on the user's dashboard. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with an `mcp_servers.innernet` entry in config.yaml (url https://innernet.live/api/mcp, `auth: oauth`) and `hermes mcp login innernet`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: inspeximus
entries.title: Inspeximus
entries.description: Memory provider with keyed corrections you can undo. A correction retires the old value by key, so it stops being recalled, and inspeximus_revert puts the previous value back from the key alone, without anyone retyping what the record used to say. Recall before each turn returns retrieval minus what a later correction retired, so a value corrected three sessions ago cannot come back as context. Adds inspeximus_remember, inspeximus_correct, inspeximus_revert, inspeximus_forget and inspeximus_forget_me. Disclosure — installs the inspeximus package from PyPI (inspeximus>=3.23.1,<4, including its `inspeximus` command-line tools) into the Hermes environment; the provider makes no network calls and carries no telemetry: memories live in a local JSON file under the profile's Hermes home (or a path you set), recalled memories are added to each turn's context and to the compression summary prompt, and writes made with the built-in memory tool are mirrored into the store.

entries.name: intelligent-tool-break
entries.description: Abort a stalled in-flight tool call with /break, send a note with /break {message}, or retry it with /again without cancelling the rest of the task.

entries.name: intelligent_memory
entries.description: Local-first Arabic/English intelligent memory with canonical facts, conflict lifecycle, bounded recall, and selective Hermes cloud enrichment.

entries.name: interim-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). Counted even where display.interim_assistant_messages hides them. Disclosure — writes message metadata (model, provider, surface, step of the turn, length in characters, 12-digit hashes of the session and turn ids; never the message text) to plugin-data/interim-ledger/interim.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay, change or hide a message; no network

entries.name: invinoveritas-receipts
entries.description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

entries.name: iowap
entries.description: Fleet control for Hermes Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). The task watcher posts stage/final task updates into the app's chat composer with user-typed authority (fail-closed, never a broadcast; switchable + persisted, a one-time long-run hint for tasks actually claimed beyond 5 minutes) and warns about fleet anomalies (node up/down, relay reachability) under the same toggle. Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the node-cli, and the plugin makes no raw HTTP calls of its own. Node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files, and tracked task ids are stored in your Hermes home under plugin-data/iowap/. The task and fleet watcher is off by default. When you turn it on, it drafts task-event lines (task name, id and stage status, never node output) into the chat composer, or, in direct mode, which you must choose, sends them with your typing authority into the session that submitted the task or the session you configured. No third-party endpoints.

entries.name: iris-chat-channel
entries.title: Iris Chat
entries.description: Chat with Hermes through Iris Chat: Signal-like messaging using Nostr Double Ratchet end-to-end encryption, without phone numbers or signup. Iris also supports nearby messaging over local networks and Bluetooth. The native channel supports one approved contact, text replies, seen receipts and typing. Disclosure — invokes the separately installed Iris CLI and runs its background service when needed; Iris stores its own dedicated identity and message history and connects to configured message servers/transports. Plaintext requests pass through Hermes and its selected model. No telemetry, automatic software downloads, imported personal keys, or added tools. Not filesystem isolation.

entries.name: iris-chat
entries.title: Iris Chat
entries.description: Private messaging through the separately installed Iris CLI. Instruction-only skill; uses a selected local identity and message history, connects to Nostr relays, and may run a persistent sync service. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs the separately installed iris CLI in the terminal, which creates a local messaging identity (secret keys and message history stored on disk), connects to Nostr relays and peers, can run a persistent sync service until stopped, and sends messages on the user's behalf; messages received from other people are read into the agent's context.

entries.name: iteration-budget-meter
entries.description: Status-bar chip for the focused session per-turn iteration usage (N/60), with a hover tooltip and a click popover of per-request stats.

entries.name: iwork-studio
entries.title: iWork Studio
entries.description: Create, edit, design and export Apple Numbers, Keynote and Pages files: designed Keynote decks from data and the user's brand kit, spreadsheet cells, formulas and formatting, Pages text and tables, exports to PDF, Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Every write is backed up, made on a copy, re-read and checked, then swapped in; any change can be undone in one call. Arabic and right-to-left text round-trip exactly. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/): a local stdio MCP server (65 tools) and a workflow skill. macOS. Disclosure — first start downloads iwork-studio==2.6.1 and its Python dependencies from PyPI with uvx (about 60 MB; built from the v2.6.1 tag by the repo's release workflow through PyPI trusted publishing; the server code is that release, not the pinned tree); Pages, exports, render checks and Keynote slide operations drive Numbers, Keynote and Pages through osascript, and macOS asks once for Automation access; it reads and writes the iWork files and export targets the agent names, anywhere on disk unless IWORK_STUDIO_ROOTS is set to fence it, and Hermes does not prompt before its write tools; it keeps backups in ~/.iwork-studio/backups (last 10 per file) and saved design kits in ~/.iwork-studio/kits; no network calls after the download, no telemetry, no self-updates.

entries.name: ja-writing-guard
entries.description: Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform_llm_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only Hermes helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.

entries.name: jackal-verified
entries.description: Typed adapter for the reproducible JACKAL v1.7.3 release: 41 catalog-derived verification tools (exact, numerical, Lean-checked bounded lanes, claim replay).

entries.name: jekyll-hyde
entries.description: Context optimization and execution alignment for agent sessions.

entries.name: jet-browser
entries.description: Verify Jet Browser startup, native input, DOM agreement, and PNG capture inside a network-isolated WPE WebKit container. Disclosure — runs `docker run` (Docker access is root-equivalent on the host) on the digest-pinned image ghcr.io/masakaai/jet-browser@sha256:540a1fec…, pulled from GHCR on first use; the container has no network and only SETUID/SETGID capabilities, but runs with AppArmor and systempaths unconfined and a seccomp profile that allows user-namespace and mount syscalls for WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox; the tool takes no arguments and loads only a built-in local test page.

entries.name: jev-agent-router
entries.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (agent_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

entries.name: jev-approvals
entries.description: TypeSafe's Jev decision model as Hermes' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.

entries.name: jev-cron-gate
entries.description: Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.

entries.name: jev-curator
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Hermes' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Hermes retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

entries.name: jev-effort-router
entries.description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing Ollama:Cloud provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. Every other catalog router picks a model and stops, and the two entries that touch reasoning effort move it by hand; this one decides both per turn. Ollama:Cloud only — no other provider is routed, and every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev, billed to your OpenRouter key) on every routed turn.

entries.name: jev-judge
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

entries.name: jev-mcp-router
entries.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (mcp_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

entries.name: jev-memory-selector
entries.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (memory_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

entries.name: jev-model-router
entries.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (model_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

entries.name: jev-skill-router-mcp
entries.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (skill_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Suggests at most one skill per request via the TypeSafe (Jev) cookbook pattern; roster is read live from the profile skills dir. Note: the portable loader does not interpolate env in mcp.json — JEV_TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be present in the server's inherited environment (native mcp_servers declaration works too).

entries.name: jev-skill-router
entries.description: Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads Hermes' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

entries.name: jev-typesafe
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

entries.name: jev
entries.description: Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

entries.name: jira-browser
entries.description: Jira workspace for Hermes Desktop, linking tickets to Hermes Projects, worktrees, and conversations. Disclosure — reads a Jira API token from JIRA_* env vars or ~/jira-config/config.json (owner-only, read-only) and sends it only to your configured https Jira origin; agent tools are read-only but return Jira text (untrusted) to the model; Start work / Draft update create chats seeded with ticket descriptions (Draft update auto-runs a turn); PR/CI status is read through your local gh CLI login.

entries.name: job-search
entries.description: A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

entries.name: jot
entries.title: Jot
entries.description: Notes, checklists and documents beside Hermes that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.

entries.name: jp-address
entries.description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Give it a Japanese postal address as written, such as 東京都千代田区霞が関2-1-2, and it returns the prefecture, city and town as separate fields. Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL is read for the active profile on each call, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Called from Hermes with five models in a small sample of 18 sessions (see CHANGELOG.md).

entries.name: jp-charts
entries.description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure: no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Hermes home); writes PNGs to the Hermes image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default).

entries.name: jp-chatwork
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Hermes in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Hermes commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Hermes commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

entries.name: jp-corporate
entries.description: Japanese corporate lookup (法人照会): find or verify a company by name or corporate number and read its gBizINFO record (basic info, subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents, workplace data). Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN in a request header; no other host, nothing written to disk.

entries.name: jp-edinet
entries.description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. It finds a Japanese company's annual securities report (yuho) and other financial reports filed on EDINET, and reads headline figures such as revenue and total assets from a filing. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. Each call reads EDINET_API_KEY for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Hermes. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false only means the figure is missing from the consolidated current-year rows the plugin reads, not that the document has no number. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Hermes internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup.

entries.name: jp-egov-law
entries.description: Japanese laws for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Ask for one Japanese law article, such as Article 32 of the Labor Standards Act, and it returns the official law text with the law number and the date that version took effect. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Hermes tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until hermes cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint.

entries.name: jp-estat
entries.description: Japanese government statistics from the e-Stat API: search tables and fetch figures such as population, households, wages, and prices, with estat_search_tables, estat_table_info, and estat_get_data. Disclosure — It needs a free e-Stat application ID, set as ESTAT_APP_ID in the .env of each profile. Each call sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp and puts ESTAT_APP_ID in the request URL. The ID is read for the active profile on each call. An HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used, and no other host is called. Nothing is written to disk, and this plugin creates no cron job. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call them with your ID. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

entries.name: jp-kokkai
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Posts new Diet meeting hits as metadata and the official meeting URL, with kokkai_search, kokkai_speech, and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key. kokkai_speech requests speech text and returns a short excerpt. Speech text is not stored. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, read a speech excerpt, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. kokkai_watch add writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/jp-kokkai-watch.py and creates one cron job that does not call a model, once a day, at the hour you pick in Hermes's own timezone. Each run costs 0 tokens and has no daily cap. Empty script output sends nothing. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch returns one pre_tool_call approve line, as does a repeat add that switches the saved job. Hermes shows it. An unchanged repeat add returns none. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt when a person is present. A cron job, hermes -q, and a separate plugin process cannot add or remove a watch even after always. A webhook or API-server turn inside the gateway is refused by Hermes unless "always" was already given for that exact add plan. plugins.isolation: host still blocks add and remove. Answering "always" on add covers only the same add plan. That choice adds one plugin_rule:kokkai_watch: line to config.yaml, and the line stays after the plugin is removed. A different add plan asks again. Remove builds a new rule key on every call, so answering always on remove does not cover the next remove, including the call that deletes the cron job.
