While the read-meetings skill is enabled, Hermes adds one line to the skill index of every session, including a session whose tools are turned off. The scheduled script does not run inside plugins.isolation: host, so that setting does not stop the watch. kokkai_watch run still cannot save seen speech IDs under plugins.isolation: host and says so on every run of the tool. The cron mark is cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Hermes 0.21.6). The daily job is created with the public hermes cron command using --no-agent and --script. hermes cron create on 0.21.6 cannot pin a toolset, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Running add again asks, then switches a model job onto the script and clears its prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next add. An update can stop the watch if the cron mark or that command moves. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data. The script timeout is 3600 seconds unless it was changed. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Hermes 0.22.2, not in a live chat.

entries.name: jp-reinfolib
entries.description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Use it for Japanese real estate and property prices in one city: it returns the number of recorded sales, the median trade price and the first 20 rows for a quarter. These are transaction prices, not the official land prices published as 地価公示. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. hermes tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until hermes cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」

entries.name: jp-subsidies
entries.description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. The /subsidies command is outside hermes tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run hermes cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows.

entries.name: junie-acp
entries.description: JetBrains Junie coding agent as a Hermes model provider over ACP.

entries.name: jwt-ref
entries.description: @jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.

entries.name: kanban-empowered
entries.title: Kanban Empowered
entries.description: A redesign for the Hermes kanban: per-board project status, a dashboard that explains what is really happening across your boards, a live summary of what each agent is doing right now, a chain view that shows where a block starts, and a fast way to answer what the kanban needs from you, by Telegram or Desktop. Cards waiting on a person get a structured ask, reminders and an escalation; cards held by guards or parked by host failures are reported or undone within a budget. No card stays silently stuck. Disclosure — a coordinator runs inside the gateway's kanban dispatch tick (coordinator profile only, leader lock, no extra process); it reads every board's kanban database and metadata through Hermes' kanban functions and writes only through them (comments, unblocking a waiting card when its owner answers, undoing an infrastructure park, reassigning a card on the release command); its SQLite state lives under the coordinator profile's plugin-data/kanban-empowered and is read by the plugin in every other profile, and its doctor command reads every profile's config.yaml read-only; it consumes Telegram replies from the configured owners to its own messages before they reach the agent, reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (the gateway's bot) only through Hermes' secret scope, and, apart from the auxiliary model below, calls only the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage, editMessageText, pinChatMessage to the configured owner chats, one pinned panel; never getUpdates) plus Hermes' own IPv4 fallback path (DNS-over-HTTPS lookups of api.telegram.org at dns.google and cloudflare-dns.com); to show what a running card is doing, the Desktop backend reads that worker's recent session from its profile's state.db read-only (what the agent wrote, including reasoning, and tool names; never commands or tool output), redacts secrets and sends it to the Hermes auxiliary model the user configured, only when the session changed and at most once a minute per card; no shell commands and no telemetry; imports private Hermes kanban, i18n, profile, plugin and Telegram-network modules (listed in its README); ships an optional core patch adding kanban veto hooks that the user applies by hand to the Hermes checkout (the plugin never applies it, and `hermes update` drops it), and registers kanban_pre_claim only on a Hermes build that exposes it.

entries.name: kanban-gantt
entries.description: One board, three views, and each answers a different question: List says what the work is, Timeline says when it happened, Graph says what hangs off what. The Graph view draws a card per task and an arrow per dependency, laid out top-down by longest path (or left to right, by status, or as a compact grid), with a transitive reduction that counts the arrows it implies instead of hiding them, links you draw, move and delete where they are drawn, and a click that lights the whole upstream and downstream lineage of a task. The Timeline renders any board as real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a period selector from 6 hours to 7 days. The List view trades the bars for a dense table — task, assignee, status, last activity. Quick scopes (Running, Blocked, Open, All) narrow the board in all three views alike, and a lineage switch widens any of them to what leads to the selection and what follows it. Tasks are created from the page (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parented by drag & drop or from the drawer, and moved between boards with their children; any task with files carries a paperclip, its files listed on demand — the board payload carries only a count — and previewed by type (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or downloaded. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download; read a task's worker log from the kanban worker-log folder); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.

entries.name: kanban-graph
entries.description: Live, read-only dependency graph of the Hermes kanban boards in Hermes Desktop: every board as a band, tasks as cards, dependencies as arrows with implied ones folded away. Click a task to light up its whole lineage with runs, last failure and the running worker's latest tool calls; deep links open a task directly, and a stdlib CLI renders the same graph as a standalone HTML file. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — reads every kanban board database and, for running tasks, the assignee profile's state.db (the kanban worker session's latest assistant messages and tool-call arguments), read-only, and shows them in Desktop through its own local dashboard routes.

entries.name: kanban-live-gantt
entries.description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the Hermes kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.

entries.name: kanban-stream
entries.title: Kanban Stream
entries.description: Live-stream Hermes kanban worker activity to a Telegram ops channel: one edit-in-place message per task with rolling tool-call history, elapsed timer, tokens/sec, thinking indicator, and a pinned final state (done/blocked). Mid-task steering via task comments — /steer from Telegram through the bundled companion daemon, or straight from the board. Ships disabled by default; needs a dedicated ops bot (KANBAN_STREAM_BOT_TOKEN + KANBAN_STREAM_ALLOWED_USERS). Outbound calls go only to api.telegram.org; reads the kanban DB read-only; no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — sends kanban task titles, summaries and tool names with command/path snippets to the Telegram chat you configure via your own bot; the optional steer daemon posts allowlisted Telegram users' /steer text as task comments that reach the running worker.

entries.name: kanban-task-threads
entries.description: Give every Hermes kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

entries.name: keenable-plugin
entries.title: Keenable
entries.description: Web search and page fetching through Keenable's hosted MCP server, with search and research skills: single-site and publish-date filters, result and snippet limits, and page fetches that return only what a prompt asks for. Works without an API key; an optional KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limits. Adds direct MCP tools beside Hermes's built-in Keenable web backend and leaves web_search / web_extract provider selection unchanged. Disclosure: connects to Keenable's hosted MCP server at `api.keenable.ai` and sends it the search queries, URLs and fetch prompts the agent issues, labelled with the header `X-Keenable-Title: hermes-plugin`; sends `X-API-Key` only when the user adds the optional config.yaml entry with their key.

entries.name: kfchow-llm-value-router
entries.description: Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.

entries.name: kimchi-acp-provider
entries.description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Hermes model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes.

entries.name: kimchi-provider
entries.description: Kimchi (kimchi.dev) models via the OpenAI-compatible API — live catalog from the metadata endpoint, API-key auth, gateway unknown-model 400s classified as model_not_found, and an identifying User-Agent (hermes-agent/<version>) on every gateway request.

entries.name: kimi-code-delegate
entries.description: Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for Hermes Agent

entries.name: kinocut
entries.title: Kinocut
entries.description: Guardrailed local video editing: Kinocut's MCP server plus two workflow skills (editing and short-form repurposing). Trim, caption, reformat and check quality with local FFmpeg. Portable Agent Plugins v1 configuration and skills, no plugin code. Requires uv and FFmpeg on PATH; launches uvx kinocut==1.16.4 over stdio. First launch downloads Kinocut and dependencies from PyPI. URL inputs download the requested media; font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub. Explicit Revideo dependency installation runs npm ci and may download renderer dependencies. Local FFmpeg editing and color grading need no account or API key. Kinocut's optional vision calls default off and require explicit configuration: legacy product descriptions use an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, while sampled-frame QC uses Anthropic. The README explains how to use the host's image model instead, including local models. Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry default off. Unverified Hyperframes browser previews and Docker renders require explicit telemetry consent. Hyperframes capture/snapshots disable implicit model analysis. These controls are not a network sandbox; see the plugin README for configuration and remaining network use. Disclosure — launches `uvx kinocut==1.16.4` over stdio, which downloads Kinocut and its dependencies from PyPI on first launch; edits and writes local video files with FFmpeg; URL inputs download the requested media, font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub, and an explicit Revideo install runs `npm ci`; optional vision features (off by default) send selected images or sampled frames to an Anthropic-compatible endpoint or Anthropic; Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry stay off unless the operator enables them.

entries.name: kiro-acp
entries.description: Kiro CLI (AWS) as a Hermes model provider, driven over ACP stdio.

entries.name: kiro-provider
entries.description: Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS with AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `hermes-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in Hermes' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool.

entries.name: kiwi
entries.description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.

entries.name: klipper-print-watch
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. While a person is in the session, pause, resume and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Hermes shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt. Choosing always adds one config.yaml command_allowlist line. For pause and resume, answering "always" covers only the same action at the same Moonraker origin, and only while a person is in the session. Cancel asks every time. Its rule_key changes on each call, so a saved always line does not approve the next cancel. It does not move the printer in cron, hermes -q, webhook, or plugins.isolation: host. cron, hermes -q, and unattended sessions default to deny, and this plugin also refuses the move after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a move and approve it. A different action or origin asks again. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. schedule writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/klipper-print-watch.py and creates the job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. Running schedule again switches an existing job with hermes cron edit --script --no-agent and clears the stored prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until that next schedule. On that leftover turn, pre_tool_call allows klipper_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool name. A deferred tool named inside tool_call is checked under that inner name. Pause, resume, and cancel stay refused on it. Removing the plugin leaves the script job. Run unschedule first, or hermes cron remove after. The scheduled script does not call the vision model. vision_check, off by default, still applies when klipper_watch itself runs on a cron turn, and it does not cancel the print. The plugin host cannot run that tool watch. The scheduled script is started by Hermes cron, so plugins.isolation: host does not stop it. Not tested on real hardware.

entries.name: kokoro-tts
entries.title: Kokoro TTS (local)
entries.description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon (MLX) and Linux (PyTorch on CPU): adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Brazilian Portuguese and English (tested by the author) and Italian (not yet tested by the author), and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus hermes kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — hermes kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB on macOS or 1.3 GB on Linux from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release and, on Linux, the CPU-only torch wheel from download.pytorch.org, both pinned by SHA-256), downloads the model at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 on macOS, hexgrad/Kokoro-82M on Linux, about 340 MB), and installs a background service that keeps a local server running (a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux, both named dev.hermes.kokoro-tts). The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. Writes the environment, model cache and log under ~/Library/Application Support/hermes-kokoro-tts (macOS) or ~/.local/share/hermes-kokoro-tts (Linux), the requested audio files, and the profile's config.yaml only when you run hermes kokoro words add or remove. No API keys, no telemetry.

entries.name: kubernetes
entries.description: Write one namespace in cluster.json to approve the scope, then use four reads: list pods, get one pod, list events, and read logs. Kubernetes is a registered trademark of The Linux Foundation. kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 is the GitHub release binary. The plugin downloads kubernetes-mcp-server-<os>-<arch> from https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.0.68/ into the plugin data directory, checks the sha256 against constants taken from that release's GitHub asset digest, and starts that file. MCP initialize and tools/list are answered before that download. A partial download is kept and continued with HTTP Range. A mismatch, including a file that was already there, is refused. read_only is true, toolsets stay core, and only pods_list_in_namespace, pods_get, events_list, and pods_log are enabled. Helm is not offered. Secret, ConfigMap, and ServiceAccount are denied. configuration_view is not listed. prod, production, live, and prd names are refused unless allow_production is true. Public and link-local hosts are always refused. The host must be local, and DNS is not resolved. readOnlyHint is true, so no approval card is shown. Before the call, name the namespace, the object, and that it only reads, because status, events, and logs reach the model. This plugin does not create a cron job. Disclosure — reads the kubeconfig you name in cluster.json (read-only) and sends its token only to that kubeconfig's API host (plain http sends it unencrypted); on the first tool call downloads the kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 GitHub release binary (~90 MB) into the plugin data directory, refuses it unless its sha256 matches the pinned release digest, and runs it as a subprocess (a file swap between the check and the start is not fully excluded); pod status, events and logs reach the model, with password-like env values and last-applied-configuration redacted; no HTTP proxy is used; gateway users can call these read tools with that kubeconfig; stop with hermes plugins disable kubernetes or hermes tools disable mcp-kubernetes.

entries.name: kuma
entries.description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

entries.name: kumiho-memory
entries.title: Kumiho Memory
entries.description: Recall and save decisions, preferences and facts in your Kumiho Cloud workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with hosted OAuth MCP and six skills. Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by Hermes); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring Hermes cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.

entries.name: lancedb-suite
entries.description: Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

entries.name: lancedb
entries.description: LanceDB hybrid memory — embedded vector + FTS recall, workspace facts, transparent forget.

entries.name: langfuse
entries.description: Langfuse observability for Hermes: one trace per turn, one generation per LLM call (usage and cost from Hermes' own pricing, cache and reasoning tokens included), one observation per tool call and subagent. Content capture is sanitized by default (metadata-only and full are opt-in); sends traces only to the Langfuse project whose keys you set. Formerly built into Hermes core as observability/langfuse; existing users are migrated automatically.

entries.name: laso-finance
entries.description: Spend USDC in the real world from Hermes: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Hermes approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 19 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for Hermes approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in Hermes (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order); all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

entries.name: ld-workbench
entries.title: Debate Workbench
entries.description: Practice Lincoln-Douglas debate. A case workbench helps a student build their own case section by section (resolution analysis, value and criterion, contentions, evidence, blocks) with a coach that gives real help and asks hard questions but never writes the case. A topic briefing maps a new resolution for both sides. A full NSDA practice round (AC, cross-examination, NC, 1AR, NR, 2AR, with prep time) runs against an AI opponent at three levels, followed by a ballot from a lay, traditional or flow judge. A fallacies guide, drill and spotter work on the student's own case and on other people's arguments. Cases are kept in a library with Word, text and backup-file export. Every model call goes to the user's own Hermes model through the plugin LLM helper. Debate Workbench is an independent community plugin. It is not made or endorsed by Nous Research or the National Speech & Debate Association. Disclosure — one network call of its own: when the user adds a topic source link, it fetches that one public web page (http or https, public addresses only, checked on every redirect, 20-second timeout, first 30,000 characters of text kept); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers no tools, hooks or middleware, only a Desktop page and a dashboard API; stores cases, rounds, ballots and briefings in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ld-workbench/; reads a .docx or .txt case file or a backup file only when the user picks one; writes an export only to a path the user picks in the save dialog, inside their home folder; the optional dictation button uses the speech recognition built into the desktop app's browser engine when that engine provides it, which may send the audio to that engine's speech service; no private Hermes imports.

entries.name: letsfg
entries.title: LetsFG
entries.description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

entries.name: levea-video-editor
entries.title: Levea Video Editor
entries.description: Agentic AI video editing via Levea: describe an edit in plain language (trim, 9:16 reframe, viral clips, captions, B-roll, multicam, audio cleanup, color, motion graphics) and get a verified MP4. Disclosure — Prompts, source video URLs/assets and project ids go to api.livecore.ai with your LEVEA_API_KEY; edits and exports consume your Levea account quota with no Hermes approval prompt; levea_video_edit and levea_job_status (wait) can block up to 10 minutes. No telemetry, no shell, no background processes.

entries.name: lfg-alarm
entries.title: LFG Alarm
entries.description: Put a real alarm on your phone from Hermes, and on your friends', family's or community's phones, ringing together: for a time, an event, a post, a stream going live, a token price, or anything that can call a link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), with one workflow skill bundled. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to LFG Alarm's MCP server at mcp.lfg.gm, signed in as the user through LFG Alarm's sign-in. Alarm titles, times, notes, links and the people added are sent there, and what the tools return, such as the user's alarms and friends, enters the session and reaches the user's model provider. Tools make, change and delete alarms and can ring every phone on an alarm the user made. The tool list comes from LFG Alarm's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add lfg-alarm --url https://mcp.lfg.gm --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. That command replaces the package's server entry and its trust setting, so the README's next step sets it again: `hermes config set mcp_servers.lfg-alarm.trust untrusted`.

entries.name: lib-docs
entries.description: Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

entries.name: lightkeeper
entries.title: Lightkeeper
entries.description: An Obsidian-compatible map of how your codebase works (modules, flows, integrations, platform traps, decisions), kept outside the repo and kept honest by hooks: a primer on the first turn, pointers to the notes that own what you are asking about or editing, and a reminder through the verify gate when code moved but the map did not. Eight lightkeeper:* skills carry the procedures (init, seed, tidy, trace, release, knowledge-vault, vault-sync, vault-tidy); the vault CLI (find, check, sync, status, log, export) works from any shell. Not a memory provider. Disclosure — each hook runs python3 on the plugin's own scripts as a synchronous subprocess with a 10 s timeout (on every user message, after every write_file and patch, at the verify step and at session end), and those scripts run read-only git commands (rev-parse, remote get-url, worktree list, ls-tree, status, log) in the session's checkout and in the vault folder; the session primer and prompt hints put text from the vault's notes into the model's context; the hooks read the vault registry ~/.claude/vaults and the vault folders it lists, and write only inside the vault (_meta/index.json), a small per-session state file in the system temporary directory ($TMPDIR), and the plugin's own data directory; the init, seed, sync, tidy, trace and release procedures run the vault CLI through the terminal and commit to the vault's own git repository, and vault init appends the vault to ~/.claude/vaults and, only when you pass its opt-in flags, copies a vault launcher to ~/.local/bin (--install-cli), installs report-only post-merge and pre-push hooks in your code checkouts (--git-hook), or adds a post-commit hook that pushes every vault commit to the remote you name (--backup-remote); vault export writes an HTML map that loads d3 7.9.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com when opened; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no dependencies beyond Python 3.9 and git. Silent until a vault covers the session's working directory.

entries.name: lightningai-rate-limit
entries.description: Per-process throttle for Lightning AI (https://lightning.ai/api/v1) keeping LLM requests within the ~15 requests/min limit, using an in-memory token bucket. Gates only calls whose provider or base_url points at Lightning AI; no-op otherwise. Disclosure — registers one llm_execution middleware and nothing else; no network calls, files, or processes of its own.

entries.name: lightningai
entries.description: Lightning AI as a Hermes model provider (--provider lightning, lightning-ai, lightningai): OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://lightning.ai/api/v1, models fetched live from /models. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to lightning.ai through Hermes' own client with LIGHTNING_API_KEY (or LIGHTNING_AI_API_KEY), optional LIGHTNING_BASE_URL overrides the endpoint; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads/writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: limbic
entries.description:
Local long-term memory for Hermes agents. Everything stays on your machine: an SQLite store plus bundled embedding and NLI models, no telemetry, no LLMs.
Limbic is designed on the physiological brain, opaque and organic. Memories strengthen or atrophy with use, corrections replace what they superseded — all deterministic background mechanisms, zero LLM calls.
Algorithmic forgetting keeps atrophied memories out of the database. Recall is calibrated: when nothing in memory is confident enough, it abstains instead of guessing, so the agent answers honestly rather than surfacing near-misses. First start downloads ~1 GB of pinned models once, then runs fully offline. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license). Disclosure — the agent-facing tools are remember, recall and forget (forget lists candidate facts for a query, then deletes the one fact id the user picks, scoped to the current user, and appends a hash-only receipt of the content's sha256, length, user id and fact id to limbic.db.deletions.jsonl beside the database); on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside HERMES_HOME; %USERPROFILE%\.cache\limbic on Windows); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache_dir at a shared folder; spaCy NER models are optional: `hermes limbic languages --set <lang>` and `hermes limbic setup` run `python -m spacy download <model>`, which pip-installs each model package (~14.5MB, version picked by spaCy, not hash-pinned) from spaCy's GitHub releases into Hermes's own Python environment, and `hermes limbic setup` also pre-downloads both ONNX models; memory stays local in limbic.db under HERMES_HOME, facts whose trust decays to zero are deleted automatically, and hermes backup adds VACUUM snapshots under HERMES_HOME/backups; no telemetry.

entries.name: limits-monitor
entries.title: Limits
entries.description: Read-only Hermes Desktop quota pane showing provider allowance windows exposed by Hermes across reachable profiles. It uses the public Hermes RPC surface and deliberately avoids direct vendor usage endpoints and credential-file access.

entries.name: lineage
entries.title: Lineage
entries.description: Provenance for everything the agent produces: every file Hermes writes gets a receipt (what it was made from — files read, pages fetched, searches run — by which tool call, model and agent, with SHA-256 hashes) and a Desktop page draws the graph back to the sources, with observed / evidenced / inferred links labelled, never blended. Verify a file and its sources against recorded hashes; export Mermaid/DOT. Disclosure — hooks only (post_tool_call, pre/post_llm_call, post_api_request, api_request_error, post_auxiliary_call, subagent_start/stop, on_session_start/end); no tools, middleware, LLM calls or credentials; runs no commands. Hashes files the agent read or wrote, scans files the agent wrote (bounded text scan) and stats the working tree once after terminal/execute_code calls; receipts only for files the agent produced. Writes under plugin-data/lineage/ (SQLite, install.key) and, on request or with sidecar: true, <file>.receipt.json beside artifacts. Stores redacted, bounded previews of prompts, tool arguments and results (store_previews: false keeps ids and hashes only). Network only on an explicit `verify --refetch` (GET to the recorded source URLs, public hosts only; redirects are followed). No telemetry.

entries.name: linkedcamp
entries.title: LinkedCamp
entries.description: Plan, build and run LinkedIn and email outreach in LinkedCamp through LinkedCamp's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.linkedcamp.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the account's API key, no keys in config): campaigns, audience search URLs, multi-step sequences, leads, unified inbox and AI-drafted replies, sending-account health, analytics, reply agents, and agency sub-accounts. Bundles the linkedcamp-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to LinkedCamp's hosted server (mcp.linkedcamp.com) and acts on the user's LinkedCamp account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools reach real people (campaign_launch starts outreach, message_send delivers at once); the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and blocks them in unattended runs.

entries.name: linkup
entries.description: Linkup web search: live cited search (fast/standard/deep), URL-to-Markdown fetch with JS rendering, async deep research, and a Linkup backend for the built-in web_search / web_extract tools. Disclosure — sends search queries, fetch URLs and research briefs to api.linkup.so with your LINKUP_API_KEY (Linkup fetches pages server-side); when selected with hermes linkup use-as-web-backend it also handles the built-in web_search and web_extract calls; large fetched pages are cached under $HERMES_HOME/cache/linkup for 24 hours.

entries.name: liquid-inference-provider
entries.description: Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a Hermes model provider (provider id `liquid`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model `liquid.auto`) and the model list go through Hermes's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID_BASE_URL) with LIQUID_API_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. Each request is billed up to its `x-liquid-cap-usd` cap (1 USD by default, set with `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd`) and carries `X-Title: Hermes Agent`. A top-level `reasoning_effort` is sent only when you select a level.

entries.name: lithermes
entries.description: Adds lit to Hermes Agent so a request is planned, built with tests and recorded checks, reviewed, and closed with a handoff note. 40 skills. MIT. Disclosure — adds per-turn workflow context and output marks through Hermes hooks and writes its plans, goals, run state and default-on knowledge capture under the workspace's .hermes/lithermes/ (capture opt-out: LITHERMES_WIKIFY_CAPTURE=0); /lit-adhd reads recent Hermes session titles, asks and tool names from ~/.hermes/state.db read-only with the sqlite3 CLI; /lit-hijack downloads the URLs and files you name (web pages, PDFs, X posts via api.fxtwitter.com, git clones of github.com repos and gists) into the workspace; bundled skill runtimes install from their own lockfiles when a skill asks; reads Hermes internals read-only (context compressor, config defaults, model metadata, command registry), which can break on a Hermes release.

entries.name: little-canary
entries.description: Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.
entries.maintainer: roli-lpci (Hermes Labs; independent of Nous Research)

entries.name: live-time
entries.description: Inject live current time into every LLM call via the pre_llm_call hook — fixes stale session-start timestamps in long/cross-day conversations.

entries.name: llm-antidote
entries.description: Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for Hermes Agent: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Hermes's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `hermes antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose.

entries.name: llmslim
entries.title: LLMSlim
entries.description: Context engine that compresses older tool output and turns locally with LLMSlim instead of asking a model for a summary: no LLM call, deterministic output, and the start of the prompt is sent unchanged, so prompt caching keeps working. Select it with context.engine: llmslim. Disclosure: installs llmslim==0.12.0 from PyPI (with numpy, scikit-learn and jsonschema); registers no tools, hooks or middleware; makes no network calls, runs no shell commands, needs no credentials, writes no files and sends no telemetry; reads its settings from config.yaml through Hermes's config loader. Token counts use a character estimate unless tiktoken is already installed in Hermes's environment, in which case tiktoken may download its encoding file once.

entries.name: loaded-skills-indicator
entries.title: Loaded Skills Indicator
entries.description: Status-bar chip, popover and dockable pane showing which skills are read into the active Hermes Desktop conversation's context: full bodies bold with an accent dot, compression-pruned ones ghosted, never-loaded ones not listed. A second pane view lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions and a loaded marker, and clicking a skill drops /<skill> into the composer for you to send (it never submits). A small local backend reads the profile's state.db read-only to tell a live skill body from a [SKILL_PRUNED] marker, and reads SKILL.md frontmatter for the descriptions. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no writes. Disclosure — the local backend opens state.db read-only for the requested session in this profile, the default root and, as a fallback, every other profile's state.db, and returns only skill names and load state; it reads SKILL.md frontmatter under the Hermes skill directories and makes no network calls or writes.

entries.name: local-system-one-hermes
entries.title: Local System One
entries.description: Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

entries.name: local_knowledge
entries.description: Native Hermes tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

entries.name: long-conversations
entries.description: Persistent long-term conversations across session boundaries via structured handoff briefs and token monitoring. Disclosure — stores handoff briefs (topic, work in progress, decisions, open questions, next step; in aggressive mode auto-built from the first 200 characters of recent user messages) as plain JSON under HERMES_HOME/long-conversations/ and injects the pending brief into the first turn of the next session for the same chat or user (CLI briefs stay in one local scope and are not shown to messaging users); the model can change the plugin's settings with long_conv_config_set; an opt-in HERMES_LONG_CONV_BETA_LOG writes a local event log; no network calls.

entries.name: looot
entries.description: looot gives Hermes one sign-in and one prepaid balance for 2,500+ data API endpoints from 90+ providers: work emails and phones, company and people search, Google results, web pages as markdown, news, local businesses. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and 21 skills. Disclosure — the run tool spends your prepaid looot balance (Hermes asks before each paid call and refuses them in unattended runs); the names, domains and emails you look up are sent to looot.ai and its upstream data providers; a `looot` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

entries.name: loreconvo
entries.description: LoreConvo memory provider: cross-surface persistent session memory with search, recall and structured memory items. Disclosure — stores end-of-session transcripts (truncated, including tool output) and Hermes memory writes in ~/.loreconvo/sessions.db, a store shared across all Hermes profiles and other LoreConvo clients, and injects context from those sessions into each turn; when LoreDocs is installed its session_link_doc tool writes session-to-document links into the LoreDocs database; a Pro license enables a one-time Hugging Face embedding-model download; installs the loreconvo package (BUSL-1.1) with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime into the Hermes environment.

entries.name: lowrouter
entries.description: LowRouter as a Hermes model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `hermes model`). The picker shows the `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of every ID from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Hermes' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Hermes shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour per key and base URL) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Hermes' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes.

entries.name: lumberroom
entries.description: lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

entries.name: machine-library
entries.title: Machine Library
entries.description: Research search for web_search and web_extract — papers, books, patents, standards and Wikipedia, with citable source links (Machine Library API key).

entries.name: machine-spirit
entries.title: Machine Spirit
entries.description: A Warhammer 40k shrine pane docked under the sessions list: the cogitators recite original Adeptus Mechanicus-style litanies, and the cog-skull, candle and binary stream animate while Hermes works. Just for fun. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network or file access.

entries.name: made-shelf
entries.description: Everything Hermes made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

entries.name: magi
entries.description: Review pending Hermes memory writes and inspect, add, edit, delete, or AI-compact stored memory from Desktop. Disclosure — while the Agent plugin is loaded it runs a profile-local Unix socket (owner-only 0600, same-OS-user peers only; under $TMPDIR/magi-ipc for very long profile paths) through which its Dashboard backend sends structured AI-compaction requests to Hermes' configured model, so any process running as the same OS user can make model calls through it; explicit model overrides additionally require the llm.model_override capability.

entries.name: make-parts-now
entries.title: Make Parts Now
entries.description: Quote and order custom 3D printed and CNC machined parts from your CAD files through the hosted Make Parts Now MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in to quote), with the quote-parts workflow skill bundled: upload an STL, STEP, 3MF or OBJ file, get the price and ship date for each production speed (SLS nylon, FDM plastic, CNC aluminum and brass), change the quantity, material or speed, and get a checkout link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to makepartsnow.com. To quote a local file the agent uploads that one CAD file with curl through the terminal tool (Hermes approvals apply) to a one-time upload link, or gives the user an upload page. Nothing is charged in chat: checkout links open Stripe Checkout on makepartsnow.com where the user pays. US shipping only.

entries.name: maqami-travel
entries.title: MAQAMI Travel
entries.description: Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

entries.name: mariadb-dev
entries.title: MariaDB
entries.description: Work with MariaDB from Hermes: 85 skills on MariaDB SQL, functions, schema management, REST services, connectors and migration from MySQL, plus the native mariadb-shell MCP server (run SQL, inspect schemas, dump/load/copy data, deploy local sandbox servers, manage REST services). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — the MCP server is the local mariadb-shell binary, started by scripts/mariadb-mcp-launcher.sh. If no mariadb-shell of the required version (26.10.4) or newer is on PATH or in ~/.local/bin, the launcher downloads the official installer from a fixed github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-shell commit and installs exactly release v26.10.4 into ~/.local/share/mariadb-shell, linked into ~/.local/bin. The package is verified against scripts/mariadb-shell-v26.10.4.SHA256SUMS, committed at the pinned sha; a mismatching package is refused. The launcher reads no GitHub credentials and sends none. Tools run SQL against the databases the user registered with mariadb-shell, whose passwords stay in mariadb-shell's own OS secret store and never pass through the agent; the sandbox tools download and run local MariaDB server instances. No telemetry.

entries.name: mariadb-guard
entries.title: MariaDB Guard
entries.description: Companion to mariadb-dev; install it together with mariadb-dev, whose MCP server it redirects to. A pre_tool_call hook that blocks the agent from running the mariadb/mysql command-line clients (and similar) for what the mariadb MCP tools do, so no database password reaches a command line, plus a short system-prompt rule saying so. Pure Python, no dependencies, no network calls, no file access. Setting MARIADB_PLUGIN_ALLOW_CLI=1 disables it.

entries.name: markdown-new
entries.description: Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in Hermes. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the Hermes process environment.

entries.name: markifact
entries.description: Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Hermes.

entries.name: max-platform
entries.title: Hermes MAX.ru Integration
entries.description: MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

entries.name: mcp-plugin-creator
entries.title: MCP Plugin Creator
entries.description: Turn any MCP server into a portable Agent Plugin (mcp.json + workflow skill) built from evidence: the server's self-description, your past sessions with it, its docs and a read-only probe. Validates and installs the package in linked mode, and checks a built plugin for server drift and new errors in use. Disclosure: starts the target MCP server to introspect it; reads this profile's state.db read-only; logs redacted mcp__* call summaries locally (log_calls: false turns it off); inline server launches, writes outside its data dir and installs ask for approval.

entries.name: mcp-serve
entries.description: Run Hermes as an MCP server: `hermes mcp-serve` lets any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex) list and read your messaging conversations, poll live events, send messages and answer approvals over stdio. `--tools` (off by default) also exposes Hermes' web, browser, vision, image generation, skills and TTS tools; terminal, file and kanban tools are never exposed. Formerly built into Hermes core as `hermes mcp serve` (MCP clients change their args to ["mcp-serve"]). Disclosure — the connecting MCP client reads the active profile's conversation history (state.db) and can send messages as your connected platform accounts; with `--tools` it also runs Hermes tools under your configured provider credentials, which can spend provider credits. The plugin itself makes no network or model calls beyond those tool calls and sends.

entries.name: mdvault
entries.title: Markdown Vault
entries.description: Memory provider that treats a folder of Markdown notes as the agent's long-term store: BM25 retrieval with CJK bigrams over an in-memory index, relevant notes injected before every turn (prefetch), four tools (mdvault_search, mdvault_note, mdvault_recent, mdvault_remember), built-in memory writes mirrored into a human-readable vault note, a `hermes mdvault` CLI and a dashboard config panel. No network, no database, no dependencies; the store is plain .md files the user can edit, git and back up. Disclosure — reads only the configured vault folder (file symlinks skipped, excluded directories ignored), writes only inside that folder (new notes with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, plus the ownership-marked mirror note), no telemetry, no self-updater, no background process, no subprocesses. The vault itself lives outside $HERMES_HOME, so `hermes backup` does not copy it.

entries.name: mediarag
entries.description:
Multimodal local search over documents and media: pdf, office files, notes, images,
audio and subtitles in one corpus, queried by meaning from any MCP-capable agent.
Documents and media sit level in the same index, so "which file mentions the landing"
and "where is the clip where I said it" are the same kind of question. Retrieval is
hybrid — semantic vectors fused with an FTS5/BM25 keyword lane — and results carry
snippets, timestamps and image thumbnails.

Everything runs locally: the corpus is a SQLite file you own, the embedding weights
download once (~285MB) and every search after that runs offline. Nothing is uploaded
and there is no telemetry — the only network calls are ones you ask for: an http(s)
source you add, or the optional Raindrop adapter.

Ships as an Agent Plugins v1 package — a stdio MCP server for conforming clients, plus
five native Hermes tools so one gateway serves every agent with the model loaded once.
Linux and Windows. Disclosure — downloads the ~285 MB EmbeddingGemma-2 ONNX weights from Hugging Face (pinned revision) on first setup; `mediarag_add_source` fetches user-supplied http(s) URLs (public hosts only, re-checked on every redirect) and runs packaged or user `sources.d` adapters as local subprocesses, including the optional Raindrop.io adapter, which sends RAINDROP_API_TOKEN to Raindrop's API; the standalone MCP launcher can build its own Python environment with `uv` from PyPI (~1.7 GB incl. torch) only when MEDIARAG_AUTO_BOOTSTRAP=1.

entries.name: meeting-overlay
entries.description: Disclosure — sends meeting transcripts to Nous inference with your Hermes login (fallback OpenRouter key from ~/.hermes/.env; optional OCTOPUS_DESK_URL); installs a launchd agent that records mic/system audio; writes and deletes under your Obsidian vault; macOS + source install only. Native desktop pane showing the live meeting transcript, answer, and daemon status.

entries.name: mem-os
entries.description: Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

entries.name: mem0
entries.description: Mem0 memory provider — server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, automatic deduplication and opt-in reranking, in platform, self-hosted or local OSS mode. Maintained by Mem0; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries go to the configured Mem0 backend (api.mem0.ai in platform mode); at this pin the mem0ai library's anonymous PostHog usage telemetry stays on unless MEM0_TELEMETRY=false is set; `hermes memory setup` can start Docker (pgvector) and Ollama containers for local mode.

entries.name: memanto
entries.description: Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, Hermes memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $HERMES_HOME/memanto.json.

entries.name: memex8
entries.description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.1.0 adds optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.

entries.name: memlock
entries.description: Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same HERMES_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

entries.name: memobase
entries.description: Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

entries.name: memoria
entries.description: Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Hermes profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.

entries.name: memory-review
entries.description: Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

entries.name: memory-rewind
entries.description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `hermes memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

entries.name: memory-shaper
entries.title: Dynamic Memory (keyword index)
entries.description: Keyword-index memory for Hermes: a small resident index of 'keyword,keyword -> file.md' routing lines stays in the system prompt while verbose topic files stay on disk and are read only when the conversation touches their keywords. Retrieval is done by the model reading a literal index — no embeddings, no vector store, no retrieval service. Disclosure — a pre_tool_call hook and a tool_execution middleware refuse a non-memory tool's write to the memory index across the recognised write vectors (write_file, patch, shell redirects, tee, sed -i; best-effort against arbitrary shell indirection) and refuse malformed index lines with a fix message rather than fixing them silently (including the keyword count: an entry outside the documented 5-20 keywords is refused, and the ASCII arrow is refused on every code path), while read-only commands and reads through a pipe always pass so the agent can audit the file it maintains; the same guard refuses any memory-tool remove, replace or patch whose old_text lands inside the index header, because on the stock store the whole preamble is a single §-joined entry and such an edit would rewrite or delete every header line at once; a documented escape hatch lets a scripted rewrite proceed when the sentinel file $HERMES_HOME/state/.memory_shaper_rewrite_approved exists or MEMORY_SHAPER_ALLOW_REWRITE=1 is set. Beyond $HERMES_HOME/memories/, the guard reads one thing: when a shell command invokes python3 on a script file, it opens that script (and the execute_code payload is already in args) to check whether the code would write the index; no file content is retained or sent anywhere. The repo also ships an optional core patch (scripts/patches/0001-flat-memory-separator.patch, changes tools/memory_tool_store.py) that the plugin does not need and never applies; a user who applies it by hand must re-apply it after every Hermes update. No network calls, no subprocesses, nothing spawned in the background.

entries.name: memory-shield
entries.title: Memory Shield
entries.description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Hermes' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Hermes' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Hermes' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Hermes' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.

entries.name: memory-zvec
entries.description: Community Zvec memory backend for Hermes Agent - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

entries.name: memtomem
entries.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.9) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside Hermes's MCP environment filtering.

entries.name: mermail
entries.description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `hermes mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in Hermes.

entries.name: meshy
entries.title: Meshy
entries.description: Meshy AI's own MCP server (pinned @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server@0.6.5) for text, image and multi-image to 3D, texturing, remeshing, rigging, animation, concept images and 3D-print prep, with a bundled meshy-3d workflow skill. In Hermes Desktop: inline 3D cards with a download and convert menu, a gallery of recent generations and saved models (with a "Made from" history), image sets, and a credit chip in the status bar. Every credit-spending call goes through Hermes's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a 200-credit limit per chat makes it ask again. Needs MESHY_API_KEY and Node.js 18+.
