Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned server from npm through npx; it sends prompts and the images or models you or the agent name to Meshy's API (api.meshy.ai) under your key, gets only MESHY_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics (its User-Agent names Hermes and its version). Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or the folder the agent names (never over an existing file); the Desktop backend fetches only from Meshy's asset hosts. The skill's helper scripts (model stats, preview render, optional Blender hand-off) run locally through the terminal tool.

entries.name: metamask-wallet
entries.description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for Hermes — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

entries.name: metronix
entries.description: Metronix memory provider for Hermes with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

entries.name: microsoft365
entries.description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

entries.name: mindgraph
entries.description: MindGraph typed knowledge-graph memory: bounded per-message recall, session transcript capture, and the mindgraph-mcp general tool surface (capture, reason, commit, plan, retrieve, remember, ingest, synthesize, ontology). Disclosure — every tool call, recall and capture goes to the MindGraph API (api.mindgraph.cloud, or MINDGRAPH_BASE_URL) under MINDGRAPH_API_KEY; with automatic capture on (default; MINDGRAPH_AUTO_CAPTURE=off disables it) the user and assistant text of completed turns is sent for extraction, tool calls and outputs are not; every add or replace made with Hermes's built-in memory tool is mirrored to MindGraph (and the replaced entry is forgotten there); each tool call first sends its name, action and target node uids to the server's governance check (MINDGRAPH_GOVERNANCE=off skips it); automatic writes run only in the primary agent, never in subagents or cron; no telemetry, no background processes, no credentials stored outside Hermes.

entries.name: minecraft-platform
entries.description: Minecraft gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the Hermes agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

entries.name: minimalist-themes
entries.title: Minimalist Themes
entries.description: Eighteen warm, readable palettes for Hermes Desktop, assigned natively per profile, with one embedded type system (Figtree + Geist Mono), matching terminal colors and a CLI banner painted per palette. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and its stylesheet adjusts a few Desktop surfaces (profile-rail glyph contrast, Capabilities metadata, the MCP JSON editor and the Manage Profiles overlay) only while a Minimalist theme is active. It also ships optional CLI/TUI skins as plain YAML files the user copies; the Desktop side never reads them. Fonts are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks, no background processes. The package also ships an inert Agent entrypoint whose register() does nothing, so Hermes Agent imports it cleanly instead of reporting a missing module.

entries.name: minimax-image
entries.description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

entries.name: minimax-search
entries.description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

entries.name: minimax-video
entries.description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

entries.name: mistral-vibe
entries.description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models. Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "hermes auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Hermes credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

entries.name: mixar
entries.title: Mixar
entries.description: Mixar's own desktop MCP server over stdio, with a Mixar workflow skill: build and edit 3D scenes, generate models, textures, rigs and animation with AI, render, and export game-ready assets for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as Hermes. Disclosure — runs the launcher the installed Mixar app writes at ~/.mixar/connector/mixar-mcp (%USERPROFILE%\.mixar\connector\mixar-mcp.cmd on Windows), which reads Mixar's own files under ~/.mixar/; tools execute arbitrary Python inside Mixar with your privileges; a tool call can start the installed Mixar app, which stays open after Hermes exits; calls go over loopback to Mixar, which forwards them to api.mixar.app under the signed-in account; generation prompts and reference images go to the AI provider running the chosen model; Mixar's backend keeps diagnostic records of MCP tool calls (inputs and results) and deletes them within 30 days; AI generation and create_layered_material spend Mixar credits, declared to Hermes as cost ranges with a 500-credit spend limit per chat; the plugin stores no credentials, ships no binaries, sends no telemetry and never updates itself; the optional MIXAR_MCP_LAUNCHER variable makes it run the program it names; at install Hermes looks for Mixar (macOS: Mixar.app in /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows: the installed-apps entry or %ProgramFiles%\Mixar; Linux: a mixar command on PATH or Mixar's launcher) and refuses the install when it is missing or, on macOS and Windows, older than 4.2.1.

entries.name: mnemostack
entries.description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (hermes-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the Hermes venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

entries.name: mnemosyne-dashboard
entries.description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

entries.name: mnemosyne
entries.description: Local-first memory layer for Hermes Agent — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

entries.name: mnemoverse
entries.description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Hermes runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by Hermes, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

entries.name: mock-review
entries.title: Mock Review
entries.description: Review boards for UI mockups. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Four mock_review tools, the `hermes mockreview` CLI and slash command, and a bundled usage skill. Boards are served from your computer (loopback by default, or your tailnet) or published on here.now, behind a random per-review password by default (`herenow_password` setting, `--no-password` per review, `hermes mockreview password <id> on|off` on a live board). Plain http(s) links in mocks stay clickable and open in a new tab; every other link scheme is stripped. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `hermes mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes every review to your network with no login. Outbound calls: a signed POST to the local Hermes webhook (localhost:8644) on Send, and, only for reviews hosted on here.now, https://here.now/api/v1 with your HERENOW_API_KEY (publish, Site Data reads, a metadata PATCH that sets or removes the board password, delete on close). Secrets are read through Hermes's secret scope only. Runs `bash publish.sh` from the official here-now skill (key in the child environment), and for a password-protected here.now prototype launches your installed Chrome, Chromium or Edge headless (throwaway profile, credential-named variables removed from its environment, `--no-sandbox` only when run as root) to load the board behind its password before the link is shared; runs `tailscale status --json` and `tailscale serve status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes) for tailnet hosting, and from `setup` the hermes subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. The opt-in `wake_toolsets` setting lets the session woken by Send use the toolsets you list (for example terminal and file), so board feedback reaches those tools; setup refuses it while any waking board is ungated and only prints the `toolsets` line for you to add to the wake route by hand (re-add it after every setup run). Reviews are stored under $HERMES_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies.

entries.name: model-drift-watch
entries.description: Scheduled check that the model you use in Hermes has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through Hermes cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real Hermes cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through Hermes's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one Hermes cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.

entries.name: model-fallback-heuristic
entries.title: Fallback — Model Switching Heuristics
entries.description: Multi-provider heuristic model fallback and automatic failover routing across all configured providers (parameter count, context window, release recency, flash tier, tool support, provider preference, and reasoning effort) — works seamlessly with or without an LLM call. Disclosure — session-start and API-error hooks rewrite fallback_providers and plugin settings in ~/.hermes/config.yaml (primary model replacement is opt-in via auto_switch_primary_when_unavailable); queries public model catalog endpoints (models.dev/api.json, openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, and inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/portal/models) to rank candidate models and check free-tier availability; optional interactive CLI setup saves user-entered provider API keys via hermes_cli.config.save_env_value when explicitly requested.

entries.name: model-leaderboard
entries.description: Model leaderboard for Hermes Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen Hermes profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed Hermes profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; keeps its state in <hermes home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; no API keys of its own, no writes outside its data directory.

entries.name: model-picker
entries.description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $HERMES_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

entries.name: model-presets
entries.title: Model Presets
entries.description: Named model, provider and reasoning presets for gateway /model commands. Uses only the pre_gateway_dispatch hook; no network calls, credential access, shell commands, background processes or self-updating.

entries.name: model-router
entries.title: Model Router
entries.description: Explicit per-profile readiness and native missing-profile preparation; Python installation remains per profile, never automatic on refresh. Profile model settings, default-on Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Hermes profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Hermes children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — after you trust and enable the plugin, routing defaults ON for every installed profile without a saved choice, including profiles that installed an earlier version and never saved one (the update turns it on); existing saved OFF and explicit skill opt-outs remain OFF. On enabled profiles, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background Hermes agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. The Desktop "prepare profiles" action, after you select profiles and confirm, installs and enables this same catalog pin in up to 32 other local profiles through Hermes's plugin manager, where routing then defaults ON. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.

entries.name: model-usage-status
entries.description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the Hermes Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through Hermes core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

entries.name: model-usage
entries.title: Model Usage
entries.description: Minimal triple-ring status-bar gauges for Claude and Codex — outer thin ring = context of the current chat, middle = 5-hour session, inner = weekly window, colored by remaining share — with a click-through detail popover and one-shot 30%/10% limit alerts (in-app toast + OS notification while Hermes is unfocused). Duplicate pool rows of the same login are merged. EN/KO/JA. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (reads the gateway's model.options usage cache and the focused chat's usage stats), never reads or stores credentials, no subprocesses, no telemetry; stores only the list of alerts already shown in plugin storage.

entries.name: modernisation-engine
entries.description: Controlled migration engine: maps an existing codebase, turns the behaviour that must survive into reviewable contracts, prepares a separate candidate and records old/new evidence before any production change. Disclosure — 27 tools plus a `hermes modernise` CLI and `/modernise` slash command; `assess`, `plan`, `record` and `recipe` read source trees and files at absolute paths the agent supplies (refusing symlinks, `.env`, `auth.json`, `credentials.json` and SSH keys) and never import or run repository code; `recipe` creates a new directory at an agent-chosen absolute path holding a copy of the source with fixed metadata edits; job records live under the plugin's data directory; only after you set `operator_config` and sign a one-use Ed25519 owner grant do `run`, `cancel` and `recover` invoke the local `docker` CLI, outside Hermes's command-approval prompt, to run, inspect and remove rootless, network-disabled, read-only, resource-limited containers from digest-pinned images you allow-list (never pulled); no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater.

entries.name: modular
entries.description: Modular Cloud model provider: open models (MiniMax, DeepSeek, Gemma) on an OpenAI-compatible API, with per-model reasoning controls.

entries.name: monid
entries.description: Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a Hermes approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

entries.name: morning-briefing
entries.description: Personal daily newspaper for Hermes: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

entries.name: mqtt
entries.title: MQTT
entries.description: MQTT as a Hermes platform: one authenticated broker connection, per-topic routing (deliver, agent, job, drop) and JSON replies published outside the consumed namespace; ships its own standard-library MQTT 3.1.1/5.0 client over TCP or TLS (verified by default, optional private CA/mTLS) with keepalive, reconnect and opt-in burst coalescing, and drops unmatched topics. Disclosure — holds one outbound broker connection and its reconnect loop, reads the MQTT username/password through Hermes's scoped secret route and optional TLS files at operator-provided paths, and enables trusted_inbound (the broker's authentication is the trust boundary): any publisher the broker's ACL admits can start agent turns, and on topics you map to deliver or job it can post text to the chat you name on another connected platform or run the cron job you name, while payload text can never issue gateway commands; job and cross-platform delivery go through Hermes internals (tools.cronjob_tools, the gateway runner), so a Hermes update can disable them; no telemetry, no shell, no writes.

entries.name: mrscraper
entries.description: MrScraper page retrieval, Google search, and account usage via direct HTTP APIs. Disclosure — page and search requests can consume paid account tokens; target URLs, search queries, and request options are sent to MrScraper.

entries.name: ms-decision-provider
entries.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Hermes's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

entries.name: muse-harness
entries.description: Drive local Muse Code over MSP so Wonder Full can call MCP tools. Disclosure — runs your locally installed `muse` (Muse Code) binary as a child process with an allowlisted environment and sends the prompt to Meta through it; if the Muse Code subscription allowance is exhausted, the same prompt is retried once on pay-as-you-go billing with the Meta API key stored in Hermes secrets (MODEL_API_KEY, META_API_KEY or META_MODEL_API_KEY) when one is set; with `approval_mode: allowAll` Muse runs its own shell and file tools in the session directory without asking; MCP servers the model passes are limited to loopback HTTP.

entries.name: my-github
entries.description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

entries.name: mybot-farm
entries.description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall Hermes packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party Hermes profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

entries.name: myeline
entries.title: Myeline
entries.description: Myeline is a remote MCP memory server: every memory is a single fact with its source attached, AI proposals land in a human review queue, and removing a fact takes a written reason kept in an audit log. One retraction stops a stale fact in every connected assistant at once. Maintained by Sandbox Group, the Myeline vendor. Disclosure — registers the vendor-hosted remote MCP server cortex.myeline.si/mcp, signed in through Hermes's remote MCP OAuth with your own Myeline account; the queries and facts the model sends in Myeline tool calls are stored and processed on Myeline's servers, and the server defines its own tool list, which can change without a new catalog pin.

entries.name: myswarm
entries.title: MySwarm
entries.description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Hermes default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Hermes loads into every session's system prompt) after a Hermes approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

entries.name: nachos
entries.description: Durable memory and context compression for Hermes Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under $HERMES_HOME/nachos/.

entries.name: needs-you
entries.description: Hermes is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

entries.name: nerve
entries.description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Hermes Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and Liquid D1 Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and D1 can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The Operator/Lean/Marie Kondo/Fat Cat presets (Operator is what `nerve setup` / the control panel picks for new homes) rewrite each outgoing model request to trim deferred tool schemas and skill descriptions to the current task, which can change the prompt-cache prefix between turns. The operator-only `nerve ui` control panel (127.0.0.1, per-run token) can replace the installed Nerve plugin with a local source checkout and run `hermes plugins validate/enable`, and, after an explicit confirmation, can create a Python venv under HERMES_HOME, pip-install Laya or PyTorch/transformers from PyPI, download model weights, and start a long-running localhost model server (D1 runs Hugging Face `trust_remote_code` model code). The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local HermesContextBus checkout into HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-context-bus and runs hermes plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger any of this.

entries.name: netmind-provider
entries.title: NetMind
entries.description: NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through Hermes' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: netplane
entries.description: Install, configure and operate a self-hosted Headscale control plane from Hermes. netplane_setup previews a configuration and, after approval, installs the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB on a fresh Debian 12+ or Ubuntu 22.04+ systemd host (amd64/arm64). Installation runs on the Hermes host, requires root or noninteractive sudo, refuses existing deployments, and verifies the package SHA-256. It configures SQLite, MagicDNS, embedded DERP/STUN, local admin gRPC, and either Let's Encrypt HTTPS or a loopback backend for an existing reverse proxy. It starts the system service, creates the first user, and saves a 90-day API key and connection settings through Hermes's active-profile APIs. netplane_status reports health, netplane_nodes lists devices, and netplane_preauth lists metadata without stored join secrets or creates an approval-gated, single-use-by-default join key with a 1–168 hour lifetime. Desktop includes setup preview/confirmation, health, nodes, join keys and confirmed node expiration, with a FastAPI backend. Management requires NETPLANE_APIKEY; setup works before a key exists. Bundled protobuf stubs use pinned sources and a compatible toolchain. Disclosure — the netplane_setup tool (after Hermes approval) and the Desktop pane (after confirmation) install the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB as root through noninteractive sudo on the Hermes host, downloading it from GitHub (SHA-256 verified) and possibly contacting configured APT repositories; it writes /etc/headscale, /var/lib/headscale and a systemd drop-in, and enables a persistent headscale service that in Let's Encrypt mode listens publicly on TCP 80/443 and UDP 3478 (admin gRPC and metrics stay on loopback); Let's Encrypt receives the chosen domain and email; setup saves a new 90-day Headscale API key as NETPLANE_APIKEY in the active Hermes profile; management reads credentials only from Hermes and uses TLS with system trust off-host; approved join-key creation returns the key into the chat; status runs systemctl is-active headscale and tailscale serve status; no telemetry and no automatic software updates.

entries.name: network-xray
entries.title: Network X-ray
entries.description: Compare DNS, TCP, verified TLS and HTTP HEAD captures of one URL from two machines, find the first observed difference and export a local evidence report. Read-only and local-first, with native agent tools, a Desktop workbench and a stdlib-only portable collector for the second machine. Disclosure — the network_xray_probe tool, the CLI and the Desktop page connect from the Hermes machine to a URL the model or user names, including private and loopback addresses (link-local, multicast and unspecified are refused): DNS, TCP, verified TLS and one HTTP HEAD request, with no query, credentials, redirects or body, run in an isolated Python child with a minimal environment; it saves the target, resolved IPs, certificate fingerprint and the server/content-type headers under the profile's plugin-data/network-xray/ folder, and imported bundles from a second machine are unauthenticated; no telemetry.

entries.name: neuralmind
entries.title: NeuralMind
entries.description: Code memory on every Hermes turn, with no tool call. Before the model runs, the plugin looks the user's message up in a local NeuralMind index of the project and appends the matching files and symbols (with line numbers), the code linked to them in NeuralMind's synapse graph, and decisions recorded in commit trailers. A session's first turn also gets a recap of the previous session in that project. The plugin is a stdlib-only shim around the separately installed NeuralMind CLI: install NeuralMind 4.9 or later yourself (`pipx install neuralmind`, `uv tool install neuralmind` or `pip install neuralmind`) and run `neuralmind build` in the project; in any other directory it does nothing. Not a memory provider: it registers no `memory.provider` and runs beside whichever one is configured. Disclosure — runs `neuralmind _hook <action>` as a child process once per turn (twice on a session's first), once for each file a write_file or patch call wrote, and once for each read_file of a file inside the project; each call is stopped after NEURALMIND_HERMES_TIMEOUT seconds (default 8) and the turn goes ahead without its context. A session's first turn can leave a detached NeuralMind process running after the hook returns, which writes the project's graph cache or, on a large synapse store, runs the decay tick and memory export, then exits. NeuralMind runs read-only git queries in the project (rev-parse, ls-files, log, diff --name-only). Reads the project, and reads and writes its .neuralmind/ directory, including each session's prompts (secret-redacted and truncated) and the paths of the files it edited, for the recap. On a session's first turn it copies .neuralmind/SYNAPSE_MEMORY.md into Claude Code's memory directory for the project (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/) when that directory already exists. The added context is part of the user message, so it is sent to the model provider with that turn and stays in the session history. The plugin makes no network requests and NeuralMind sends no telemetry; NeuralMind downloads its embedding model once when it has no cached copy, normally during `neuralmind build` (ChromaDB's all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX archive from chroma-onnx-models.s3.amazonaws.com, SHA-256-checked, cached in ~/.cache/neuralmind/). Subagent and cron turns are skipped. MIT.

entries.name: neuralwatt
entries.description: Check NeuralWatt service health, available models, account balance, request costs, energy use, and session activity from Hermes. Includes seven read-only tools. Health and public model discovery need no credentials; account analytics use your NeuralWatt API key. Disclosure — makes GET requests to the NeuralWatt API (api.neuralwatt.com, or the host you set in NEURALWATT_BASE_URL, which then receives your API key), reads account usage, cost and energy metrics rather than prompt or completion text, writes nothing, and loads the optional API key through Hermes's secret scope.

entries.name: next-prompt
entries.description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

entries.name: next-steps
entries.description: Next-step suggestions under the Hermes Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

entries.name: nextcloud-talk-platform
entries.description: Nextcloud Talk platform adapter for Hermes Agent, in two modes behind one plugin: a webhook bot (Nextcloud Talk Bot API, HMAC-SHA256 signed, with an explicit body-size cap and a nonce-replay cache ahead of payload parsing) and a real Nextcloud user account (app password, long-polling the Chat REST API, with federation-invite support, per-room mention/watch/free modes, and an agent-to-agent loop guard plus active-listening context for multi-agent rooms). Mode is picked automatically by which credential is configured. No extra SDKs -- aiohttp for bot mode, httpx for user mode, both already Hermes dependencies. Disclosure — Connects to your Nextcloud server either as a Talk bot (HMAC-verified webhook listener, 127.0.0.1:18797 by default) or as a real Nextcloud user with an app password (long-polls the Chat API and auto-accepts federation invites only from NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ALLOWED_INVITERS); in user mode, unanswered room messages from allowed senders (up to 40 per room by default) and, for rooms listed in NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ROOM_MODES or with room_rules_all_rooms on, the room description are added to the agent's next turn in that room.

entries.name: nextcloud-talk
entries.title: Nextcloud Talk
entries.description: Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for Hermes, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.

entries.name: nextdns
entries.description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

entries.name: nexus-recovery-peer
entries.title: Nexus Recovery Peer
entries.description: Optional bounded peer-model suggestion after repeated tool failure or a failed delegated child. Disclosure — when an administrator explicitly configures a provider/model route and grants the required LLM override capabilities, the plugin sends a redacted excerpt of the task and failure to that provider via Hermes ctx.llm. Redaction is best-effort, not a confidentiality guarantee; host routing/fallback may change the actual recipient. Empty routes (the default) make no peer requests. The plugin does not replay tools, run shell commands, read files independently, store credentials, or send telemetry.

entries.name: nexus
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Hermes and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Hermes config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to Hermes's own default model through local Ollama; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon that sends memory text to the Ollama endpoint at 127.0.0.1:11434 or NEXUS_OLLAMA_BASE under the model named by NEXUS_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL, nexus-memory.consolidation_model or Hermes's model.default, which can be an Ollama cloud model), and the service keeps running after Hermes exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Hermes config.yaml, and the opt-in recall reranker (nexus-memory.rerank or NEXUS_RERANK=1) defaults to sending each query plus up to 20 memory snippets to that same endpoint using the provider API key it reads from config.yaml; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.

entries.name: ngrok-ai-gateway
entries.title: ngrok AI Gateway
entries.description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `hermes model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto Hermes' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: nine-balance-widget
entries.title: Nine-Balance Widget
entries.description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not Hermes' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

entries.name: node-search
entries.description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

entries.name: nord-theme
entries.title: Nord Theme
entries.description: Unofficial Nord theme for Hermes Desktop with hand-tuned Polar Night (dark) and Snow Storm (light) palettes, Nord terminal colors, Nord code-block syntax colors, and Aurora status colors. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — its stylesheet recolors Desktop surfaces, code-block syntax colors, status colors, selection and inline code only while Nord is selected, and it switches the active theme to Nord once on first enable; no network calls, file reads or shell commands.

entries.name: nostr-vpn
entries.title: Nostr VPN
entries.description: Private mesh networking through the separately installed nvpn CLI. Instruction-only skill; connects to relays and peers and starts a persistent daemon. Tunnels need elevated host networking privileges. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs the separately installed nvpn CLI in the terminal (installed by the user, or by the agent from the project's latest GitHub release or an unpinned `cargo install nvpn`), which creates local device keys, connects to Nostr relays and peers, starts a persistent daemon that with elevated privileges creates tunnel interfaces and routes, and on an admin host can approve devices into the user's private network.

entries.name: nous-girl-theme
entries.title: Nous Girl
entries.description: Warm monochrome ink-and-paper theme for Hermes Desktop in real light and dark palettes, with terminal colours that match and a CLI banner painted from the theme's own palette. Disclosure — theme-only plugin: it registers one theme through the Desktop plugin SDK and injects no CSS, no DOM access and no stylesheet of its own; the two Desktop palettes ship as light and dark sets, and the Desktop keeps its own typography. The package also ships two optional CLI/TUI skins (nous-girl-light, nous-girl-dark) as plain YAML files the user copies into ~/.hermes/skins, plus an inert __init__.py whose register() does nothing so the Agent loader imports the package cleanly instead of reporting a missing module. No network requests, no agent tools, no hooks, no background processes, no settings page.

entries.name: nowstamp
entries.description: Give the agent a clock. Appends the current date and time, plus the real gap since the previous message, to every user turn. Optional spaced-out timestamps on tool results for long runs.

entries.name: ntfy-approval
entries.description: Answer Hermes' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Hermes' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: nvidia-app
entries.title: NVIDIA App
entries.description: NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

entries.name: nvidia-broadcast
entries.title: NVIDIA Broadcast
entries.description: NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. Disclosure: the tools change live audio and video effects on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

entries.name: nyx
entries.description: Nyx: local, single-user long-term memory with no LLM on the write path. Every turn is logged verbatim and indexed (SQLite FTS5, optional embeddings); on top of that log Nyx keeps bi-temporal facts (what is true now, and what you believed on a given day), source trust (tool, delegation and bot output never becomes a fact about you), two-stage forgetting with a restorable quarantine, and secrets filtering before anything is stored, with an optional encrypted vault that hands a pasted key back to its owner only after human approval. Disclosure — memory is stored locally in ~/.neurobase (configurable); no network calls by default. Opt-in only: a configured embedding API receives memory text and queries; l3_llm sends profile, scene and recent-decision snippets to DeepSeek or OpenRouter; LLM extraction sends the sentence being extracted to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set (default 127.0.0.1). Keys are read through get_secret. The optional vault stores secrets encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a master key in ~/.config/nyx/vault.key, or optionally in the OS keychain under Nyx's own service name; revealing one asks for approval through Hermes and is refused under cron and subagents. Adds a hermes nyx CLI (vault, doctor, scrub, repair, status). A separate opt-in companion plugin shipped in the same package, nyx-reveal, registers one transform_llm_output hook.

entries.name: obscurify-provider
entries.title: Obscurify.ai
entries.description: Obscurify.ai as a Hermes model provider (`--provider obscurify`, or Obscurify.ai in `hermes model`): a privacy-focused, OpenAI-compatible API to 200+ models with zero-data-retention routes and account-number sign-up (no email). The model list leaves out decision models and models under Hermes' 64K context minimum, context windows come from the catalog, and reasoning effort is sent as `reasoning_effort`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://obscurify.ai/v1 through Hermes' own client with OBSCURIFY_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself only fetches the public model catalog (GET https://obscurify.ai/v1/models, no credentials) at most once an hour per process, reads and writes no files and starts no processes. Usage is billed from the user's prepaid Obscurify.ai balance; the plugin makes no payments.

entries.name: obsidian-memory
entries.description: Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the Hermes dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

entries.name: oc-free-provider
entries.description: Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for Hermes. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and Hermes tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while Hermes executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

entries.name: office-3d
entries.title: Office 3D
entries.description: A live isometric office for Hermes Desktop: every profile is a person at a desk — a profile doing real work sits typing with a lit terminal screen, an online-but-idle one relaxes in the lounge with tea, an offline one leaves an empty desk with a dark monitor. Click a desk to inspect that profile (state, sessions, tokens, cost) and open its chat or latest session; a cost/tokens leaderboard ranks the profiles; plus a global Total/Working/Idle/Offline overview, a status-bar chip, a palette command with keybind, a settings page, and an office_status agent tool that reports the same status to the model. Disclosure — the backend and the tool read each profile's gateway_state.json and open its state.db read-only, running aggregate queries only (COUNT/SUM/MAX over the sessions table: counts, token totals, cost, last-activity); they never read message content, system prompts or titles, make no network calls, and need no credentials. Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. POSIX only (platforms: [linux, macos]) because the process-liveness check uses os.kill(pid, 0), which on Windows would terminate the target process.

entries.name: office-desk
entries.title: Office Desk
entries.description: Guarded Word, PowerPoint and Excel editing: tracked Word changes and comments, slide and deck edits, and Excel edits with LibreOffice recalc. Every write gets a backup and a revertible receipt, and you review it all on a Desk page in the Desktop app. Settings are in Settings > Plugins. Disclosure: reads any Office file the agent is pointed at but writes only inside folders the user puts on the Desk (backups and receipts live in the plugin's own data dir). xlsx_recalc runs the user's installed LibreOffice (soffice, headless) on a temporary copy. The Desk page reads the session store read-only to show a workstream's chat. No network calls, telemetry, credentials or background processes. Depends on the paper-docx, paper-pptx and paper-xlsx forks. They provide the docx, pptx and openpyxl import names, so they must not share an environment with python-docx, python-pptx or openpyxl.

entries.name: offpeak-bekci
entries.title: Off-Peak Watch (offpeak-bekci)
entries.description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in Hermes: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger, its own JSONL measurement log, and a read-only look at the profile's cron/jobs.json. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires Hermes >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; it reads the profile's cron/jobs.json read-only (on `/offpeak-durum`, `/offpeak-kaldir` and at every session end) to count enabled queue-consumer jobs; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

entries.name: olympus
entries.title: Olympus
entries.description: Manage your Hermes agents from one dashboard tab: every agent (profile) on one list with its status, current task and tool, helpers and a week of runs; one Needs-you queue of questions waiting on your answer, failed or overdue cron jobs, stalled or failing Kanban workers, blocked or unassigned tasks, offline gateways and looping or expensive runs, each with its action; an inspector per agent; a Live view of every open run with its subagents and their last tool; a Floor with every agent at a fixed place, moving only on recorded tool calls; a Pop out window of the roster that stays on top; and a Performance view of run success, run time, tool failures and cost per agent, each compared with the days before, with the runs behind any day a click away. Controls (pause, resume or run a cron job; answer, retry, reclaim or reassign a Kanban task) are confirmed, logged and executed by Hermes' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off. Opt-in alerts run as a Hermes no-agent cron job. Disclosure — reads Hermes' own stores read-only across every profile under HERMES_HOME (sessions and messages in state.db, cron jobs, run output and the usage ledger, the Kanban database, gateway state, config.yaml and profile.yaml, skills, the agent/gateway/error log tails and subagent live transcripts under cache/delegation/live) and writes to plugin-data/olympus/, plus `$HERMES_HOME/scripts/olympus_alerts.py` when you run `hermes olympus install-alerts`; controls (on by default, each confirmed; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off) pause, resume or run cron jobs and answer, retry, reclaim or reassign Kanban tasks through Hermes' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; no network calls to third-party services, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials and no self-updater; never opens a profile's .env (configured gateways come from Hermes' own helper, a private import the validator warns on); local labels, task titles, questions and message previews stay hidden unless `dashboard.olympus.expose_local_labels: true`; the Desktop page uses the plugin SDK only.

entries.name: omh
entries.description: Oh My Hermes (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a Hermes Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider, a dag-ulw run keeper (omh_dag) whose nodes the parent dispatches with Hermes' own delegate_task, a data-only search planner (omh_search, no retrieval), and language-server navigation tools (lsp_definition, lsp_references, lsp_diagnostics, lsp_rename) over Hermes' own LSP service. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without Hermes' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed, which the plugin imports from the directory OMH's own installer recorded) asks once through the Hermes approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; the pre_tool_call hook refuses skill_manage edits and deletes of skills OMH installed; lsp_rename applies the language server's workspace edit all-or-nothing, only to files inside the session workspace root Hermes' file tools resolve (apply=false previews), and the lsp_* tools (off until OMH_LSP_TOOLS or the lsp_tools setting) drive Hermes' agent.lsp service through its private loop, answering lsp_unavailable when that seam is absent; omh_dag reads delegation.max_concurrent_children and state.db async_delegations read-only to size each ready batch and, on a Docker or SSH terminal, runs fixed read-only file and $HOME checks in that terminal without Hermes' approval prompt; the memory provider reads the profile's .env, config.yaml and pairing files to find the gateway allowlist when classifying DMs; adds system-prompt sections for delegated children and a per-model calibration block; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

entries.name: omnivoice
entries.description: OmniVoice TTS provider for Hermes Agent

entries.name: onebot-platform
entries.title: QQ (OneBot)
entries.description: QQ bot via the OneBot 11 protocol: connects Hermes to your own self-hosted NapCat, Lagrange, LLOneBot or go-cqhttp deployment over WebSocket — the plugin hosts a reverse-WS server inside the Hermes gateway, or dials an existing forward-WS endpoint — and adds the qq toolset (qq_send_image, qq_send_voice, qq_send_video, qq_send_file, qq_send_forward, qq_napcat_api, qq_group_history) for DM and group chats with admin allowlists, group mention gating, per-member soft limits, and cron/notification delivery to a configured home channel. Inbound images are downloaded and (with Pillow) downscaled before the vision tool sees them; long replies are split at sentence boundaries or rendered locally into a text image with fonttools/Pillow. Disclosure — talks only to the user's own OneBot deployment; the plugin's listener (default port 8643) is a long-running background server inside the Hermes gateway process that accepts the bridge's reverse WebSocket and also serves the qq_* tools' local HTTP API, refuses a non-loopback bind without an access token, and limits tool sends from a QQ session to that chat or the configured home channel unless the session is an admin user's private chat; inbound message images are downloaded from that deployment into the plugin's data directory for the vision tool; text-to-image rendering runs locally (fonttools, Pillow, system CJK fonts) with no third-party calls; credentials (the OneBot access token, allowed-user lists, home channel) reach the plugin only through Hermes's secret scope and ONEBOT_* config and go nowhere but your own OneBot deployment; no telemetry or usage reporting.

entries.name: opaque-composer
entries.description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

entries.name: openai-compatible
entries.description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

entries.name: openalex
entries.description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

entries.name: opencode-free-acp
entries.title: OpenCode Free (ACP)
entries.description: Real OpenCode CLI over ACP as a Hermes model provider, with curated free-model selection and Hermes-owned tool execution and approvals. Independent stdlib transport using only the documented provider API, not an HTTP compatibility client or a handoff to OpenCode's autonomous tools. Disclosure — starts the separately installed opencode acp executable for discovery/inference in the included restricted workspace; forwards the conversation, tool schemas and results to OpenCode and its selected upstream model. The CLI uses its normal HOME/configuration/login and may load user-configured vendor plugins/hooks; its normal network calls, local records and vendor terms apply. Child environment is allowlisted; Hermes/provider keys and YOLO settings are not inherited. Plugin code reads no credential stores, writes no runtime state, makes no direct network calls, installs no binaries and sends no telemetry. Native ACP permission/file/terminal requests are refused, native tool events abort the request, and selection must be confirmed before inference. This is not an OS sandbox or an authorization to use OpenCode; broader vendor policies can override workspace restrictions, and free availability/pricing/privacy can change.

entries.name: opencode-shepherd
entries.description: Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.

entries.name: openinvest
entries.title: openInvest
entries.description: Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.

entries.name: openltm
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in HERMES_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

entries.name: openmail
entries.description: Gives a Hermes agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

entries.name: openpaths
entries.title: OpenPaths
entries.description: OpenPaths model provider for Hermes: OpenAI-compatible inference at openpaths.io with auto, auto-easy-task, auto-medium-task, auto-hard-task and auto-think task-tier routes plus GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models, live /models listing, and Hermes reasoning effort mapped to OpenPaths reasoning_effort. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results and conversation context are sent to openpaths.io with your OPENPATHS_API_KEY and forwarded to the upstream model vendors it routes to; the plugin makes no other network calls and registers no tools or hooks.

entries.name: openrouter-picker
entries.description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Hermes secret store or HERMES_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

entries.name: openrouter-spend
entries.title: OpenRouter Spend
entries.description: OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the Hermes root.

entries.name: openrouter-voice
entries.description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for Hermes Agent (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

entries.name: openspec
entries.description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

entries.name: openviking
entries.title: OpenViking
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.5.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active Hermes static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after Hermes exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `hermes openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus Hermes bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

entries.name: operations
entries.title: Operations
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads hermes-metrics-dash's <hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <hermes root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through hermes send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. From the setup checklist's Connect GitLab step it can also adopt this profile's own login - its environment read through Hermes' secret scope, or the host the gitlab-mr plugin names - or take a host and token typed on the page; the host goes through the plugin-settings writer and the token through Hermes' .env credential route as OPERATIONS_GITLAB_TOKEN, and the token is never sent back to the page. No other credential store is read: a login that exists only in another profile's .env or in the glab CLI's config is typed in instead. Since 0.3.5 the plugin keeps its own metrics store: it tails <hermes root>/metrics/requests.jsonl and moa-refs.jsonl, guardrail lines in logs/agent.log, logs/model-router-requests.jsonl and clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl (all read-only, offset-tracked) plus its own host probes (CPU and memory via sysctl/vm_stat or PowerShell, LM Studio's lms ps, and every five minutes the local conformance.yaml's install-stamp, launchd/scheduled-task, loopback-port and key-name checks), and reads session titles and costs from <hermes root>/state.db and every profile's gateway_state.json (read-only), into <hermes root>/metrics/operations.db, which this plugin alone writes and prunes to the metrics_retention_days setting (30/60/90 days or forever, chosen on the page and written through Hermes' plugin-settings writer); hermes-metrics-dash's metrics.db is then only a read-only fallback until the own store holds data. It probes the local metrics dashboard's /api/about (METRICS_DASH_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8899, cached five minutes) to link to it rather than duplicate it, and every Hermes process that loads the plugin starts a daemon timer: when no kanban dispatcher tick has arrived for two minutes it runs the same sweep itself every 30 seconds (collection, alerts and, with drift_action: automatic, the fix cards), and the page says so; OPERATIONS_HEARTBEAT_TIMER=0 turns that timer off. Since 0.3.4 a failed model call is classified with the host app's own error classifier and shown with its cause and remedy commands; no new outbound call is made for that.

entries.name: optchat
entries.description: OptChat-style endless memory for Hermes: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Hermes's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $HERMES_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

entries.name: optmem-hermes
entries.description: Independent Hermes integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under HERMES_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

entries.name: orbit-desktop
entries.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments.
