Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: orcaslicer
entries.title: OrcaSlicer for Hermes
entries.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/HERMES_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.hermes-orca (HERMES_ORCA_HOME), outside HERMES_HOME.

entries.name: orquehelx
entries.description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider Hermes already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with Hermes' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.

entries.name: osv-ref
entries.description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

entries.name: otari
entries.title: Otari
entries.description: Use Otari, the open-source LLM gateway by Mozilla.ai, as a model provider, with one key for every model your gateway serves.

entries.name: parallel-search
entries.description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside Hermes's native web providers.

entries.name: parcel-deliveries
entries.description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

entries.name: parlor
entries.title: Parlor.sh
entries.description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

entries.name: parrotnotes
entries.description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: pass-secrets
entries.description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

entries.name: pastdotdev
entries.description: past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-hermes/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

entries.name: patsnap
entries.title: Patsnap
entries.description: Patent and scientific-literature search through Patsnap's own hosted MCP server: prior-art and landscape searches across WIPO/EPO/USPTO/CNIPA/JPO/KIPO and more, paper search (PubMed, Nature, arXiv and others), assignee resolution, corporate trees and a patent's legal lifecycle, with a bundled patsnap-search workflow skill. Needs PATSNAP_API_KEY from the Patsnap Open Platform. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — connects to connect.patsnap.com over HTTPS and sends your queries and record ids there under your key (every call spends Patsnap credits); gets only PATSNAP_API_KEY from your profile and sends it in a request header, never in the URL; no local processes, files or telemetry.

entries.name: pay-cli
entries.title: Pay CLI
entries.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: Hermes starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

entries.name: pay
entries.title: Pay
entries.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`hermes mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a Hermes profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: pcs-security-tls-posture
entries.description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

entries.name: pdf-surgeon
entries.description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Hermes installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.

entries.name: pending-queue-monitor
entries.description: Desktop-only, read-only monitor for pending memory and skill write approvals. Disclosure — the pane's API reads pending/memory/*.json and pending/skills/*.json under the default Hermes root and every named profile directory beneath it (all profiles, not only the active one), and returns only counts, age buckets, oldest age, and per-item profile/subsystem/id/action/origin/created_at/age_seconds. It never returns or displays summaries, payloads, or record content; it exposes no approve, reject, or delete actions; it registers no tools, hooks, or middleware, performs no network I/O, and holds no credentials.

entries.name: penny
entries.title: Penny
entries.description: Penny core memory and private notes for Hermes. Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a Hermes approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <HERMES_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.

entries.name: pep-ref
entries.description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

entries.name: perf-hud
entries.title: Perf HUD
entries.description: Live performance HUD for Hermes Desktop: a status-bar chip with core-compatible TPS (sum of output tokens over sum of API durations for the last 10 completed calls, the same window and arithmetic as Hermes' own status bar) in `tps`, `tps_ttft` or `calls` form, and a statistics popover with TPS, a separately labelled Session Avg TPS (the same ratio over every call in the session), median TTFT from `first_chunk_at`, LLM calls, an `Agent steps*` compatibility alias (equal to LLM calls, footnoted inside the snapshot by `agent_steps_note`), turns, errors, input, output and cache-read tokens, cache hit rate on Hermes' `cache_read / (cache_read + input)` buckets, tool calls and tool time, tool time share, wall-clock session duration, and the model and provider. Two controls — Reset current statistics (clears the plugin's own in-memory counters, never Hermes session state) and Clear history — plus local performance history for the last 50 sessions. Observes only: nine observer hooks, no tool or message is ever blocked, rewritten or reordered, no Hermes core file is touched, the aggregation layer is pure with no I/O and no host imports, all handlers are fail-open so a telemetry bug cannot break a turn, and a corrupt history file is quarantined instead of raised. Disclosure — reads only from the observer payloads: token usage buckets (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning), API and tool timings, first-chunk timestamps, model and provider names, session ids, and tool names plus error status for the counts; prompts, model responses, conversation contents, tool arguments and tool results are never read and have no field in its snapshot, its desktop event or its history record. Writes exactly one JSON file per profile at `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-perf-hud-*/history.json` containing only session_id, model, provider, started_at, updated_at, duration_ms, ttft_ms, tps_core, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_hit_pct, tool_time_ms and llm_calls, allow-list enforced, atomic, capped at 50 sessions; no other disk writes, and no config change beyond the documented `plugins.entries.perf-hud.settings.*` keys (chip_enabled, chip_metric, history_enabled, history_max_sessions, poll_ms, broadcast_min_interval_ms). Desktop updates travel over Hermes' in-process plugin event bridge (`broadcast_plugin_event`, topic `plugin.perf-hud.stats.update`, throttled to 400 ms) and its REST routes are served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/perf-hud/ (snapshot, sessions, history, config, reset, clear-history, status), which requires the dashboard's auth ticket. Executes no subprocess, no shell command, no systemd unit, no Task Scheduler task; makes no network request; has no credentials, no OAuth and no telemetry. Standard library only, no third-party dependencies.

entries.name: personae
entries.description: A messenger-style roster for Hermes Desktop: one row per profile with its live sessions, per-profile colour, status lights, search, groups, multi-select and an Apropos beta that starts a new session already knowing the ones you picked. Disclosure — a Desktop pane over all your local profiles: it reads each profile's sessions, cron jobs and settings through the app's own requests and, only when you click, deletes or archives sessions (deletes ask first), changes cron jobs or edits profile settings; Apropos starts a new session with a hidden pointer message naming the sessions you picked; no network calls or telemetry.

entries.name: pethost
entries.title: Pethost
entries.description: Deploy and run Docker Compose projects on Pethost with its skill and Pethost's hosted MCP server: deploys, logs and requests, rollbacks, backups and restores, domains and commands in containers. Disclosure — connects Hermes to Pethost's hosted MCP server (mcp.pethost.dev), signed in by OAuth through `hermes mcp add pethost --url https://mcp.pethost.dev/mcp --auth oauth`, with no key or token in the package; the package marks its server untrusted, but that native entry replaces it and runs at trust: full unless mcp_servers.pethost.trust is set to untrusted, as the README's install does; tools act on the account's machine (deploys, restarts, restores, deletions, commands in containers); to move files the skill has Hermes run tar and curl in commands the skill writes, only to https at the machine's own hostname (*.pethost.network) under /transfer/, never a command the server returns, and says before an upload that the project folder goes as it is, .env included; it also has Hermes generate app secrets with openssl in the user's shell and fetches a deployed site to check it.

entries.name: phone-harness
entries.title: Phone Harness
entries.description: Drive a real phone from Hermes with one phone_exec tool: an iPhone via iPhone Mirroring on a Mac, an Android over adb, or a cloud phone from Phone Harness Cloud. Disclosure — runs model-written Python on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package (installed from PyPI); every phone_exec call goes to Hermes's approval prompt unless you opt in to classifier auto-run, a heuristic, bypassable check that decides which scripts ask first; taps and types into your real phone and its apps and accounts; screenshots go to the system temp folder and are attached to the tool result for vision models; a cloud phone streams its screen to Phone Harness Cloud and uses phone-harness's own cloud sign-in (~/.config/phone-harness/auth.json), and the push_file helper uploads a file from this computer to Phone Harness Cloud's file store to open it on the cloud phone; a cloud Android bills by the minute, and a cloud iPhone is a per-phone subscription; phone-harness's PostHog telemetry (script text, script output, helper arguments, errors, an install ID, and your cloud account and session IDs when signed in) is off under Hermes unless you opt in.

entries.name: photofresco
entries.title: PhotoFresco
entries.description: Edit images in a PhotoFresco window you approve: layers, masks, selections, adjustment layers, previews and PNG/PSD export. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with a local stdio MCP server and bundled skill; needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium 120+. Disclosure — opens https://photofresco.com/app/ (remote web editor, live code not covered by this pin) in a separate Chrome/Edge/Chromium profile under ~/.local/share/photofresco-connector (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/PhotoFresco Connector), with cookies/sign-in/autosave kept there; previews and document state the agent requests go to your model provider; with the Send/Spend permissions granted in the PhotoFresco window, AI ops spend PhotoFresco credits up to the budget you set and cloud/feedback ops send document data to PhotoFresco, and Hermes does not prompt before those calls; with Export granted, quick-export ops save to the browser's download folder; no local folders are readable or writable unless you add --read/--write yourself.

entries.name: pidgeon
entries.title: Pidgeon
entries.description: Email for Hermes through Pidgeon: mail to your agent's own address starts a conversation, one per email thread, and the agent's answer goes back as a reply in that thread. The agent reads Pidgeon Firewall's clean text, mail flagged as prompt injection is held before it reaches the agent, mail whose From fails DMARC never reaches it, and the agent can only reply, never write to a new recipient. Standard library only. Disclosure — while the gateway runs it polls pidgeon.ai (or `PIDGEON_BASE_URL`) every five seconds with `PIDGEON_API_KEY` and sends the agent's answers as email replies through Pidgeon; mail from senders in `PIDGEON_ALLOWED_USERS` that passes DMARC becomes agent turns with the agent's full toolset (Firewall-flagged mail is held by default; setting `PIDGEON_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` also admits mail whose From is not authenticated, so anyone who knows an allowed address could instruct the agent), and a cursor/message-id state file is kept under `<HERMES_HOME>/pidgeon/`.

entries.name: pinned-folders
entries.description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

entries.name: pixel-worlds
entries.description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Hermes Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

entries.name: plan-mode
entries.title: Plan mode
entries.description: Claude Code-style plan mode for Hermes: the agent explores and writes a plan, and edits nothing else until you approve it. It works on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Hermes approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets Hermes' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions, and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 recommended. On the interactive classic CLI, Hermes' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Hermes' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .hermes/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Hermes core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that Hermes printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.

entries.name: pocket-watch
entries.description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under HERMES_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

entries.name: post-cortex
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author hermes:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when Hermes knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Hermes secret scope; the only local state is $HERMES_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on Hermes' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.

entries.name: postel
entries.title: Postel
entries.description: Find posts that went viral in your niche, write your version in your own voice, and save, schedule or publish it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Mastodon, through Postel's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with the postel-writing workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Postel's server at www.postel.app; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Research (search-viral-tweets) works without signing in; every other tool acts on the user's Postel account after `hermes mcp add postel --url https://www.postel.app/api/mcp --auth oauth`, and a first sign-in can create a Postel account. Viral posts, drafts, voice profiles and the posting schedule join the session context, so they reach the user's model provider. Write tools change drafts, generate-post and refine-post spend Postel AI credits, and schedule-post and publish-post post to the user's connected networks. The package marks its server untrusted, but the `hermes mcp add postel` sign-in entry replaces the package's server entry, trust included, so after sign-in Hermes does not ask before write, schedule or publish tools and does not block them in unattended runs unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.postel`. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens.

entries.name: postroom
entries.title: Postroom
entries.description: Prepare social previews, schedule explicitly approved posts and inspect delivery in your own Postroom workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — hosted MCP server at https://social.notacompanynameyet.com/mcp (remote tool list not covered by the pin); needs a Postroom account and Hermes native MCP OAuth (`mcp_servers.postroom` with `auth: oauth`, then `hermes mcp login postroom`; the bundled mcp.json alone gets 401), Hermes stores the OAuth tokens; write tools import media (made publicly accessible), save previews, schedule an approved preview to the user's connected social accounts and cancel queued posts; the package marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before write-capable calls; workspace data, drafts and analytics returned by the tools reach the model provider.

entries.name: ppq
entries.description: PayPerQ (ppq.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider for Hermes — per-response cost estimation from ppq's published rate card, chat model discovery from GET /v1/models, automatic per-request Zero Data Retention opt-in, and a 3-layer picker pin strategy (user-local pins file → live top chat models from ppq's public stats dashboard → generic static fallback; generic installs never get the author's personal pins). Disclosure — model provider; PPQ_API_KEY and all prompts, tool schemas and responses go to ppq.ai (PayPerQ; terms https://ppq.ai/terms, contact matt@ppq.ai), a relay that routes requests to third-party inference partners, some outside the user's jurisdiction, and frontier providers still see prompts; usage is billed per request from the user's prepaid PayPerQ balance (funded by card or cryptocurrency on ppq.ai; the plugin itself makes no payments). Privacy protections are opt-in per request: for models badged privacyLevel 'zdr' the plugin automatically sends provider={"zdr": true, "data_collection": "deny"} so requests route only to endpoints with a Zero Data Retention policy that do not collect data (the zdr model set refreshes hourly from an unauthenticated GET /v1/models with a pinned fallback); models badged 'e2e' run inside TEE enclaves with no opt-in flag needed — enclave coverage applies to chat by default, not to image/video/audio, and true end-to-end encryption is only available via the optional local ppq-privacy-verifier proxy. Building the model picker, for any provider, starts a background unauthenticated POST to stats.ppq.ai at most hourly to fetch the top chat models; cost estimates and personal picker pins read optional local files under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ppq/ (prices.json, pins.json) that the plugin does not create, so costs show as unknown without a price snapshot. Additional caveats: Claude Opus 4.8 with web search enabled drops the ZDR guarantee, and some Anthropic/Gemini models may override the provider routing fields (order/only/ignore).

entries.name: precleared
entries.title: Precleared
entries.description: Checks cold email against the law before it goes out: when the agent sends an email with a send tool, one of Hermes's email skills (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace) or an email API call, Precleared checks each new recipient against UK PECR and UK GDPR, US CAN-SPAM, Canada's CASL and German, French, Australian, Irish and Dutch rules; anything not cleared goes to Hermes's approval prompt (or is refused in block mode) with the rule, its source and a signed receipt. Adds precleared_check and precleared_verify_receipt tools and a cold-email-check skill. Disclosure — when the agent sends email through a send tool, an email skill (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace), a mailer command or an email-API call, and on every precleared_check call, the plugin sends each new recipient's address with the configured sender country, address source, pitch and optional prospect country to precleared.dev over HTTPS; Precleared keeps a signed receipt of each check that anyone holding the receipt id can open at precleared.dev/r/<id>. The optional PRECLEARED_API_KEY is read through Hermes's secret scope and sent only in the Authorization header; without a key, checks draw on a free allowance shared by everyone on the same network. Emails not cleared go to Hermes's approval prompt (or are refused in block mode), and verdicts are cached under hashed addresses in plugin state for 30 days. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry; maintained by the operator of Precleared.

entries.name: preview-text-size
entries.title: Preview Text Size
entries.description: Larger or smaller text in the Hermes Desktop file preview pane: scales the rendered Markdown from 90% to 175%, independent of Chat Text Size and UI Scale, through a row in Settings → Appearance, three command-palette entries and rebindable shortcuts (⌘⌥=, ⌘⌥-, ⌘⌥0 on macOS; unbound by default on Windows and Linux, where Ctrl+Alt is AltGr). The Source and Diff views keep their size. Disclosure — desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); appends one stylesheet that sets CSS zoom on the preview's [data-preview-markdown] element, removed on disable, so a Desktop release that renames that attribute turns the plugin into a no-op; stores the chosen size in plugin storage; no network calls, credentials, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: pricewin
entries.description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

entries.name: print-job-watch
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Hermes shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt while a person is present. cron, hermes -q, webhook, and unattended sessions refuse the move, including after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" on pause or resume adds a permanent allowlist line to config.yaml, so a later pause or resume of that same action at the same origin runs without asking while a person is present, until you remove that line. Each cancel asks again. Answering always on cancel does not cover the next cancel. cron, hermes -q, and webhook do not use that line. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. hermes print-job-watch schedule writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/print-job-watch.py and creates one cron job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. This is the same when HERMES_HOME is HOME/.hermes and when HERMES_HOME points somewhere else. unschedule removes that job and that script in both places. The job does not call a model. Empty script output sends nothing. The script binds the profile secret scope and then reads the URL and API key, and it does not print the key. The default schedule is every 5 minutes. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. Running schedule again switches an existing job in place with hermes cron edit --script --no-agent. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. The create command cannot set a tool list, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Under plugins.isolation: host, the print_job_watch tool cannot watch the printer. Set plugins.isolation to in_process. The scheduled script is not that form, so that setting does not stop the watch. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run unschedule, which removes both. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam. A request that sent the API key is not followed on a redirect, including one that stays on the same origin.

entries.name: print3d
entries.description: Turn an idea, a photo of an object, or a shop listing into a sliced Bambu Studio project. The agent writes a Blender script, print3d checks the mesh (overhangs, thin walls, fits between parts, likeness to the photo), slices it and says what to fix, until it prints clean; each run also writes a 3D view the agent opens in the Desktop preview pane. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill and a stdio MCP server run through uvx, so Blender 4.2+, Bambu Studio and uv are required; at install Hermes looks for Blender in the standard locations (/Applications and Steam on macOS; PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install without it. Disclosure — runs Blender and the Bambu Studio CLI as local child processes; Blender runs the agent-written Python with your user's permissions, outside Hermes's terminal sandbox, and the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that runs a script or changes a job (the read-only tools still write preview images and the 3D view under ~/print3d/jobs without asking); installs Pillow and mcp from PyPI; the 3D view loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; the optional `print3d setup` command (not needed for a catalog install) edits Hermes, Codex, Claude, Cursor and Gemini config files, with backups. Never contacts the printer; no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: priors
entries.title: Priors
entries.description: Pay HTTP 402 (x402) APIs on credit: when the agent's wallet is short, it borrows the gap in USDG from its Priors credit line on Robinhood Chain, pays, and repays; before paying another ERC-8004 agent it reads that agent's repayment record. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for Priors: the priors-wallet server runs the local priors-mcp command (npm @priors/mcp, installed by the user, not bundled; the README pins 0.14.1) and signs payments, loans, repayments, savings, stock and market trades and Autopay allowances in USDG on Robinhood Chain mainnet with the key named by PRIORS_KEY_FILE (or PRIORS_KEY) in the profile's .env; both servers are marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write-capable call, and where nobody can answer (chat -q, cron, the gateway without a prompt) the call is declined and nothing is paid; pay_url pays only https hosts listed in PRIORS_PAY_HOSTS when it is set (any public https host when it is not), at most max_price_usd a call, and borrows only when max_borrow_usd is given (a loan is at least the pool's minimum, 5 USDG today); a loan more than three days late can be marked defaulted, which ends the agent's record on Priors; the hosted read-only server (https://mcp.priors.trade/mcp) receives the tools' public arguments (agent ids, addresses) and counts connections by the client's runtime name only; the tool sets are served by @priors/mcp and the hosted server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: prism
entries.description: Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

entries.name: privacy-gateway
entries.description: Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for Hermes model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the Hermes plugin DB under HERMES_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

entries.name: profile-models
entries.title: Profile Models
entries.description: Read-only Desktop model map for main, auxiliary, sub-agent and MoA routes. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's full config.yaml through the host's `config.get` (the response includes any credential fields it holds); only model-routing fields are kept and nothing is stored or sent off the machine.

entries.name: profile-pane
entries.description: Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

entries.name: profile-picker
entries.description: Pick the profile for a new chat right in the composer, next to the model pill, and see which profile a running chat belongs to.

entries.name: profile-switcher
entries.title: Profile Switcher
entries.description: The Alt+Tab gesture for Hermes profiles. Hold Ctrl+Alt and tap Tab to cycle through your profiles, release to land on the highlighted one — the same hold-tap-release rhythm as the OS app switcher. (Alt+Tab, Win+Tab and Cmd+Tab are owned by the window manager and cannot be bound by any application, so the gesture lives on ctrl+alt+tab, unclaimed by the OS and by Hermes core.) Each row shows the profile's model and most recent conversation; a working profile shows a spinner. Also opens with a single contributed keybind (Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P, rebindable in the app's own keybind panel), a status-bar chip, and a palette command. The switch goes through the Desktop's own profile path, so the target profile's backend is activated and its chrome is scoped onto it. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls, or stored credentials.

entries.name: progress-squash
entries.description: Collapses carriage-return progress bars (tqdm, git clone --progress and similar) in terminal output to the frame a terminal would show, so the model reads one line instead of every redraw: a 300-step tqdm loop goes from 17,396 characters to about 120. Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.

entries.name: project-manager
entries.title: Project Manager
entries.description: Git workbench for the Hermes Dashboard and Desktop: discovers the git repositories under the folders you watch, and inspects or changes them per file — stage, unstage, diff and discard — plus commit, push, pull, branches, commits and worktrees. Disclosure — reads the watch paths from its own SQLite table (under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/project-manager) and git metadata (branch, remote, ahead/behind, commit subjects, status and diff text) from the repositories under them, and lists folder names under any path you type when adding a watch folder; file contents are read only as diff text returned to the requesting UI; the five agent tools are read-only. Writes on request only from the Dashboard/Desktop UI: git add, commit, push, stash (including stash -u before a branch switch), fetch, merge --ff-only (also as "pull all" across every watched repository), restore, clean -f, git switch, and git worktree remove (including --force and remove-all). Discard on a tracked file restores it from HEAD and drops the uncommitted edits; on a file in no commit (untracked or staged-new) it leaves the bytes on disk but nothing here can restore a version of it, and both sit behind a confirmation naming which one you are doing. The Desktop Chat button starts a new Hermes session whose working directory is that project's folder, and the project name and branch chip open the repository's remote URL in your system browser. The optional standalone server (project_manager_server.py, 127.0.0.1:9120) requires a per-run token printed to its log. No outbound network, no model call, no API keys; git fetch/push contact the remote named in the request (the UI sends the repository's own remote).

entries.name: promoat
entries.title: AI Clone Videos
entries.description: Make realistic AI videos of yourself, with your own face and voice, from inside Hermes. Powered by Promoat. Disclosure — sends your scripts, prompts and the public media URLs you supply to Promoat's hosted API (promoat-platform-plugins.vercel.app) with your PROMOAT_KEY; video, character, voice-clone and speech tools spend paid Promoat credits; clone_voice and create_character build a reusable voice or face from the samples you pass; delete_character and delete_voice permanently remove account assets.

entries.name: prompt-enhance
entries.description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

entries.name: prompt-enhancer
entries.description: A composer button for Hermes Desktop that first repairs dictation typos in the draft, then rewrites it into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape); one click back restores the original typing, and ⌥-click repairs without enhancing. Two stateless gateway calls, preserves @file and /command chips, per-session state. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

entries.name: prompt-optimizer
entries.description: Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.

entries.name: prompt-pocket
entries.description: Local prompt library for Hermes Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

entries.name: prompt-queue
entries.description: Kanban-style prompt queue for the desktop: Play drains cards one at a time into per-card target modes — new session, existing session, project, or a profile's canonical Bot Chat — gated on the global model slot, background-review completion, and context compaction. Queue/Done/Skipped/ Failed tabs, two-row target picker, markdown ingest (Windows), and a trust-aware ::enqueue directive (ask-first by default). Disclosure — Desktop pane that runs queued prompts as full agent turns (all tools the session allows) in new or chosen existing sessions, projects it can create, or a hidden per-profile "Bot Chat" session while Play is on; reads recent agent.log lines to detect background reviews and context compaction; on Windows the markdown-ingest menu runs local shell commands (mkdir, dir, certutil, explorer, and python on a small bundled reader script it writes into the chosen folder) through Hermes's shell.exec; an opt-in Auto-add setting lets ::enqueue directives in a live assistant reply queue prompts that run without a click.

entries.name: prompt-snippets
entries.description: Prompt snippet library for the Hermes Desktop composer: a quick-pick overlay styled after the app's own slash menu (own shortcut), plus a management view with drag reordering, group tags and import/export. Inserts into the focused session, not the active one. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體. v1.8.0 is fully SDK-only: the quick-pick overlay renders as an official Popover anchored to the plugin's own contributed node and all draft writes go through the host composer draft API. No local network; v1.6.0+ adds local JSON import/export via the system clipboard.

entries.name: prompt-studio
entries.description: Step-by-step prompt builder for Hermes Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (Hermes Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns (plus any compaction summary) of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions; draft and form answers go to the same auxiliary model; no other network.

entries.name: prompt-tray
entries.description: Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the Hermes composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

entries.name: proofable-mcp
entries.title: Proofable
entries.description: Context and control for any AI. Agent identity, scoped access, and proof across tools. Disclosure — skills-only package: its workflow skills steer the agent to Proofable's hosted MCP server at mcp.proofable.me (which you add yourself with `hermes mcp add … --auth oauth`) to check identity proofs and agent permissions, create wallet-signed proofs, and store, list or revoke secrets in Proofable's hosted vault, so secrets you store and proof/agent data go to Proofable; Hermes does not prompt before those MCP tools run unless you give the server a trust setting; the skills also suggest Proofable's own optional `proofable` CLI, which edits MCP/project config.

entries.name: proofgate
entries.title: ProofGate
entries.description: No proof, no done. Verifies an agent's completion claims (file created, message sent, command ran, tests passed, figures quoted) against the tool evidence recorded in the same session, before the final reply is delivered. Unproven claims are flagged as unverified or withheld, fail closed, and every verdict is written to an append-only ledger stored locally in $HERMES_HOME/proofgate/. Disclosure — observes every tool call and final reply in profiles where it is enabled and stores tool arguments (sensitive-named keys redacted) and the first 800 characters of every tool result, unredacted, in append-only files under $HERMES_HOME/proofgate/ with no rotation; makes no network calls; in the default enforce mode it holds reply streaming and may append warnings to or entirely withhold a reply judged by keyword heuristics to contain unproven claims.

entries.name: protean-model-sync
entries.description: Fleet-wide provider and model presets with CLI and Hermes Desktop support. Disclosure — writes model/provider keys into the config.yaml of the profiles you select (backup taken first).

entries.name: protean-ordaprompt
entries.description: Jev-style comparative classifier for OrdaPilot. It compares all topic labels and session choices in one batch, including new-topic, ambiguous, and new-session options. It uses calibrated score and margin gates, weighs continuity against context cost and contamination, and abstains when uncertain. OpenRouter is optional for provisional new-label proposals and disabled by default.

entries.name: protean-subagent-viewer
entries.description: Read-only Hermes Desktop pane for live and past delegated subagent workers.

entries.name: protonpass
entries.description: Proton Pass secret source: resolves pass://vault/item/field references (mapped source "protonpass") or every env-var-titled item of one vault (bulk source "protonpass_vault") into environment variables at startup through the user's own pass-cli, beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources, with a hermes protonpass setup/status/token/set/remove/sync/disable CLI. Stdlib-only, no Python deps. Disclosure — when enabled, runs the user-installed pass-cli (argv only, allowlisted env, 30 s per call), which talks to Proton's API; a personal access token or AI-agent token is read from Hermes' env and passed only to the pass-cli login child's environment (never argv); writes a 0700 session dir under cache/protonpass and a 0600 value cache (cache_ttl_seconds: 0 disables); no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry, no background process.

entries.name: provenance-gate
entries.title: Provenance Gate
entries.description: Flags memory and skill_manage writes that state a user decision ("the user decided ...", "用户决定 ...") without the user's own words: each such sentence needs a quote that appears verbatim in text the user typed in this session, shares key words with the decision and does not drop a negation. A patch is checked by the text it produces. Observe mode (the default) records flagged writes and `hermes provenance-gate report` lists them; block mode refuses them and tells the model how to fix the write. Measured on an independent blind set of 133 lines: precision 1.000, recall 0.694. Disclosure — two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call); keeps a local copy of the text the user types, with its sender_id and session link, and an evidence log of checked claims under plugin-data/provenance-gate (30-day default retention, `hermes provenance-gate purge`); reads MEMORY.md, USER.md and skill files to reproduce what a patch produces; no network, no credentials, never asks for approval.

entries.name: provider-copy
entries.description: Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. Per-profile missing/present badges, fill-missing by default with an explicit overwrite opt-in. OAuth sign-ins and messaging bot tokens never travel; values never cross back in responses.

entries.name: provider-status
entries.description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Hermes environment keys on exhaust, and an expired OAuth token asks for a new login. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent. Disclosure — Reads provider API keys from the Hermes .env and its own config.json and calls each enabled provider's own usage or billing endpoint; Codex and Grok sign-ins use those CLIs' OAuth client identity and user-agent, keep the plugin's tokens in its install folder, and ask for a new login on expiry. When the Discord gateway runs, the bot's Discord presence (visible to everyone in servers the bot shares) is updated every 20 seconds by default with tokens/sec, context-window use and the active provider's name with its remaining quota or dollar credit balance (model and running tool are opt-in); turn it off with plugins.entries.provider-status.settings.discord_presence_enabled: false. /pulse and the agent_pulse tool report process-wide telemetry (model, provider, current tool, quota) to anyone allowed to call them on a gateway. Writes a secret-free quota-cache.json into its install folder and reads Hermes config.yaml for the active model.

entries.name: provider-usage
entries.description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Hermes desktop status bar. Per-provider chips with eye toggles, a popover with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, near-limit amber tint, a desktop notification per threshold crossing, and burn-rate projections (ETA to reset or depletion). Providers: OpenCode Go, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers and profile secrets, else the profile's .env and the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity. No subprocesses, no telemetry.

entries.name: proxy
entries.title: Proxy
entries.description: Creative strategy and marketing engineering on live ad-library data through the hosted Proxy MCP: a brand's live ads from the Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, LinkedIn Ad Library and TikTok's EU ad library, keyword search on Meta, video ad transcripts, image analysis and competitor discovery, for creative briefs and scheduled competitor radars (Hermes cron). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one research skill; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — read-only (no ad-account access, no spend); every tool call, with its brand names, keywords and ad URLs, goes to mcp.useproxy.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth, so sign in from an interactive chat before scheduling cron runs. Free tier 20 credits/day.

entries.name: pstack
entries.description: Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 17 playbooks, plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, unslop, and 46 other skills and principles. Disclosure — skills only, no tools or network calls of their own; when the user asks, the setup-pstack skill changes Hermes `delegation` model/provider/reasoning settings via `hermes config set`, the autopilot, shipping and babysit playbooks push and force-push the agent's own branches, squash-merge pull requests and arm hourly Hermes cron jobs to watch them, and the reflect skill files backlog issues in your team's tracker without asking per item.

entries.name: public-holidays
entries.description: Public holidays for 200+ countries and their regions, plus workday checks, workday counts and deadline math (N working days after a date), computed in code instead of by the model. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to date.nager.at (Nager.Date, free, no key) carrying only a country code and a year; no redirects, 10 s timeout, responses cached in memory only. No credentials, no files written, no shell commands, no hooks, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: pulldown
entries.title: Pulldown
entries.description: Read public pages as bounded Markdown with source metadata and explicit Chromium rendering. Disclosure — fetches model-chosen public web pages (and, with render=true, their subresources in headless Chromium) through a separately installed Pulldown Python runtime; private addresses and redirects to them are refused, and fetched pages are cached in the plugin data directory.

entries.name: pushary
entries.description: Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native Hermes approval transport, with optional per-tool gates. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/hermes-commands; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when Hermes marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Hermes.

entries.name: pushover-hermes-plugin
entries.description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Hermes's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by Hermes; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $HERMES_HOME/logs and settings.json under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data, and $HERMES_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.

entries.name: qdrant-memory
entries.description: Durable native memory for Hermes with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Hermes-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; a restart-interrupted remote write stays retryable with the same request identifier, and a deterministic extraction failure is quarantined without stopping unrelated writers. Optional shared memory runs through one authenticated Owner over loopback or HTTPS MCP with provisioned device grants, fixed scopes and one writer per destination; the default stays private under a local ownership lock. scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — optional shared memory runs one authenticated Owner service (off by default, loopback or HTTPS MCP only, token-checked device grants with fixed scopes).

entries.name: qdrant
entries.description: Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.hermes/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/hermes_default, ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Hermes home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate hermes_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Hermes session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.

entries.name: quota
entries.description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the hermes-quota-plugin User-Agent, caching Anthropic usage responses and rate-limit cooldowns in the Hermes root directory keyed by a token hash so profiles sharing one Claude login share them; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Hermes' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; when a Codex account is configured, each refresh also fetches public Codex reset announcements from the third-party site codex-resets.com (anonymous request, no credentials sent); the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Hermes' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check first sends Hermes' own xai-oauth access token (read via Hermes or from auth.json, read-only) to grok.com's billing endpoint with a browser User-Agent, and on an authentication failure falls back to local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux, the macOS Keychain or Windows DPAPI for the browser's cookie key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or every saved commandcode credential in Hermes' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.hermes/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage, /api/balance and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Hermes' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints. The opt-in (default off) Agent Monitor reads this profile's Hermes session database and the local process list to show running sessions, spend estimates and model health, locally only.

entries.name: quote-ask
entries.title: Quote & Ask
entries.description: Codex-style ask-about-selection for Hermes Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: quotum
entries.description: A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in hermes dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops Hermes web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token

entries.name: radio-dm-gateway
entries.description: Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until hermes tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until hermes cron remove. Hermes main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.

entries.name: ram-first-context
entries.description: Read-only RAM-first context memory — FTS5 keyword recall over the live Mnemosyne SQLite database; no embeddings, no network.

entries.name: rea-captcha
entries.description: Inspect captured browser verification evidence locally when an agent task is interrupted by a CAPTCHA. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (pinned stateless mcp.json + skill); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ with npx on PATH. Disclosure — on first start Hermes runs `npx rea-captcha@0.3.1`, which downloads that exact npm package and its dependencies (incl. Playwright) from the npm registry; the catalog config is stateless, so only the read-only, local captcha_analyze works and the browser-session tools fail closed until you configure a separate stateful server; no telemetry, hosted solver, browser-profile copying, or cookie/token transfer.

entries.name: rea
entries.description: Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.7.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for Hermes. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation.
