Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and Hermes does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs.

entries.name: reaction-feedback
entries.description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.

entries.name: reaction-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with Hermes: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). Only reactions the gateway authorizes reach it. Disclosure — subscribes to gateway_platform_event as an observer only and ignores every event but a reaction change; writes the emoji a message has after the change, a count of custom emoji and 12-digit hashes of the chat and message ids (never a user id, user name or message text) to plugin-data/reaction-ledger/reactions.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

entries.name: read-only-mode
entries.title: Read-only mode
entries.description: Ask/read-only toggle beside the Desktop composer (Cursor Ask-mode equivalent): while it is on, each send is prefixed with a read-only instruction so the agent answers from reading only, and asks before changing anything. Per-chat state, palette command, no agent tools or hooks. It is a prompt-level constraint, not a sandbox: Hermes has no session-level read-only policy, so the model can still disobey. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no tools, hooks, env vars.

entries.name: reading-buddy
entries.description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.

entries.name: reasoning-switch
entries.description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

entries.name: recency-anchor
entries.description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

entries.name: recued
entries.title: Recued
entries.description: Connect Hermes to your own self-hosted Recued server on the same computer: your notes, tasks, mail, calendar and records, through the tools a Recued contract grants. Reads run at once, and every change waits for your approval in Recued. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json and one skill), no plugin code: Hermes starts the installed `recued --mcp` as a local stdio MCP server. Disclosure — the tools reach the services you connected to Recued, such as your mail, only as the contract allows. The contract's key is saved in Recued with `recued mcp-key set`, never in Hermes or the plugin. The plugin makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: redaction-pack
entries.description: Teaches Hermes's built-in secret redactor 71 more vendor credential formats (HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Amazon Bedrock, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Tailscale, Docker Hub, JFrog Artifactory, CircleCI, HubSpot, PostHog, Grafana, Sentry, Shopify and others) through register_redaction_patterns, so those tokens are masked in logs, tool output and model-bound text like the built-in ones. Disclosure — register() makes one call, ctx.register_redaction_patterns; no tools, hooks, network access, subprocesses, files or environment variables; the patterns can only add masks, and security.redact_secrets: false still turns redaction off.

entries.name: redline
entries.description: Guided Markdown and source-code review in Hermes Desktop — annotate passages or line-numbered code in a docked pane and send comment/question/change-request batches back to the opening chat session; cards are offered automatically for qualifying delivered Markdown or source files. Disclosure — reads any user-selected local .md/.markdown or source-code path (.py .sh .js .ts .tsx .c .h .cpp .go .rs .rb .yaml .yml .json .toml .sql, so config files such as config.yaml or auth.json are shown if you open them) up to 1 MB (symlink-resolved), writes only a <file><ext>.redline.json sidecar beside it, and reviewed paths and sidecars are on the gateway host; in Hermes Desktop chats the transform_llm_output hook appends a ::redline directive line to qualifying final agent responses; source selections carry L<n> anchors, annotations re-anchor by saved offsets or quote with a margin fallback, and code highlighting uses Pygments in the local gateway host with plain-text fallback; no network beyond the local gateway, no credentials, no telemetry, no subprocesses; the pane polls the local backend every 3 s while open.

entries.name: redreplier
entries.title: RedReplier
entries.description: Find leads in public conversations through RedReplier's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.redreplier.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): keyword mentions on Reddit, Hacker News, X, Bluesky and Facebook, each scored 0-100 for relevance, with filters by score, keyword, source and date, the reason behind a score, approve and reject triage, monitored websites and keywords, and alert settings. Bundles the redreplier workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to RedReplier's hosted server (mcp.redreplier.com) and acts on the user's RedReplier account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Keywords count against the user's RedReplier plan. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: reduck
entries.title: Reduck
entries.description: Run tested browser scripts on any website, in your own Chrome signed in as you or on a Reduck-hosted browser, through Reduck's MCP server (https://mcp.reduck.ai). Configuration only: plugin.json + mcp.json. Disclosure — every Reduck tool call and its arguments go to mcp.reduck.ai with your REDUCK_API_KEY; runs act on websites as you (in your paired Chrome or a Reduck-hosted browser) and can submit forms, post or buy when a script does that, and Hermes does not ask before these remote tools run; runs, traces and scripts are stored on your Reduck account and hosted-browser runs use plan credits; the tool set comes from the server at runtime, not from the pinned sha.

entries.name: refusal
entries.description: Detects when a model refuses a request or deflects to an educational alternative, and retries the turn on the next model in your fallback_providers chain; optionally appends your own text to the retry's system prompt after a refusal. Detection is local and rule-based (regex patterns over the response prose); tool-calling responses, code blocks and partial answers are treated as genuine answers. Disclosure — an llm_execution middleware inspects every model response before the agent loop uses it, and when it detects a refusal it sets finish_reason to content_filter (Anthropic: stop_reason to refusal) so Hermes activates its fallback model; this is logged and counted identically to a real provider-signalled refusal (reason=content_policy_blocked), with no way for a plugin to register a distinct reason, so the detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id to let the two be told apart by hand; a triggered fallback resends the full conversation to the fallback provider and spends tokens there; with no fallback provider configured, Hermes replaces the response with its standard safety-refusal notice, so a false positive discards a valid answer. Optional (off by default, empty preprompt/preprompt_escalated settings): an llm_request middleware appends your configured text to the system prompt of requests in an armed session, so a same-route retry of the same model carries it; armed state is memory-only unless persist_state is enabled, in which case session ids/levels/turn ids (never text or credentials) are kept in Hermes's plugin state. No network calls, no files read or written outside the plugin package (and, if persist_state is on, its own plugin-data file), no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry sent anywhere.

entries.name: reka-provider
entries.title: Reka
entries.description: Reka as a Hermes model provider: Reka's agent-capable models on Reka's OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Reka's top-level reasoning_effort. Pick Reka in `hermes model` or use `--provider reka`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access); chat requests (prompts, tool schemas and results, supported user images) and the model list go to https://api.reka.ai/v1 (or REKA_BASE_URL) through Hermes's own client with REKA_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; usage is billed to your Reka account; the plugin itself opens no connections.

entries.name: remarkable
entries.description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.hermes/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

entries.name: reme
entries.description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.

entries.name: remesher
entries.title: Remesher
entries.description: Bounded image-to-GLB jobs using an isolated Remesher CLI, with existing ComfyUI/Comfy3D or native TRELLIS.2 and Pixal3D runtimes. Four Python SDK tools provide health, generation, persistent job status and hashed GLB assets, plus a setup/generation skill. Apache-2.0 for Remesher code; third-party terms remain separate. Disclosure — reads selected local images and configured files, uploads images to the configured ComfyUI server, launches local CLI subprocesses and detached supervisors, optionally owns a GPU runtime, and stores inputs, logs and assets in profile plugin data. Client/runtime installation and model downloads require separate explicit opt-ins; no model weights are bundled. No credentials or telemetry are required. No Desktop viewer or hosted service is included.

entries.name: render-platform
entries.title: Render
entries.description: Deploy, debug and manage Render applications with 20 unchanged skills from render-oss/skills and Render's hosted MCP connection. Disclosure — connects Hermes to Render's hosted MCP server (mcp.render.com) with your RENDER_API_KEY; the server is marked untrusted so tools without a read-only annotation need approval; account permissions apply and changes can incur Render charges; bundled skills guide shell commands, file edits and Render CLI installs (including the vendor's curl | sh installer).

entries.name: rentahuman
entries.title: RentAHuman
entries.description: Find people and coordinate real-world work through the RentAHuman marketplace. Disclosure — runs the third-party `rentahuman-mcp` server via npx, which sends your requests and your RentAHuman API key to rentahuman.ai and stores agent identity keys in `~/.rentahuman-identities/`; its tools can post and fund tasks, accept workers, send messages and release real money to people — write-capable calls ask for approval because the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, but each approval moves money or commits you to work.

entries.name: replaid
entries.description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

entries.name: requesty
entries.title: Requesty
entries.description: Requesty LLM gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `hermes model`). The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the Hermes session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.

entries.name: revamp
entries.description: Winamp-style music, audiobook and radio player for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — starts a token-protected HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 for as long as Hermes runs (Host-checked); scans `~/Music` (or the configured library folders) and stores its library index, playlists and a credential-masked agent-activity ticker in its own data dir, with automatic backups every 10 minutes under `~/.local/share/revamp/backups/`; contacts Radio Browser for station search, the radio stations (and their redirect/playlist/favicon hosts) you or the agent pick, `api.webamp.org` / `r2.webampskins.org` for the Skin Museum and `lrclib.net` for lyrics; may run `ffprobe` for audiobook chapters; the optional pop-out launches a local Chrome/Chromium with a private profile and, on Linux, writes desktop entries and icons under `~/.local/share`; its hooks observe tool calls and approvals without answering or changing them; no telemetry.

entries.name: rex
entries.title: Rex
entries.description: Rex terminal integration: Hermes sessions started in a Rex pane learn which session and pane they run in and get Rex's own agent skill (rex:rex), the same context `rex skill setup` gives Claude Code and Codex. Adds status marks on the window title, a macOS alert when Hermes waits for you, /title and /resume label sync, and follower panes for subagents and kanban workers. Needs terminal.client_env_passthrough set to the REX_* variables (see README).

entries.name: rfc-ref
entries.description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

entries.name: rocketchat-platform
entries.description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Hermes dependency) — no extra packages needed.

entries.name: rply-platform
entries.title: rply
entries.description: rply gateway platform: talk to Hermes from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Hermes as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Hermes' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `hermes rply` setup command; credentials read through Hermes' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: rss-lite
entries.title: RSS Lite
entries.description: Lightweight RSS, Atom and YouTube reader page for Hermes Desktop: folders, unread/saved, search, a sanitized reader view, and optional AI summaries on your configured model. Disclosure — the gateway fetches only the feeds you add (and a pasted web page or YouTube @handle page once, to find its feed) through the plugin's own SSRF-guarded backend route, sending YouTube's anonymous consent cookie SOCS=CAI to YouTube hosts only; Desktop loads thumbnails and article images directly from publishers (can be turned off) and a YouTube video only after you press Play, through Desktop's own embed; Summarise sends the article title and up to 12,000 characters of its text to your configured model; subscriptions are stored in HERMES_HOME/rss-lite; no shell commands, background processes, credentials or telemetry. Independent implementation, not derived from hermes-rss or rss-reader.

entries.name: rss-reader
entries.description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite-docker
entries.description: Community plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Hermes host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/hermes/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

entries.name: ruapi
entries.title: RuAPI
entries.description: RuAPI as Hermes model providers on one key: `ruapi` serves Claude models over RuAPI's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `ruapi-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, leaving out image and video models, and context windows and image input are declared for the main models. Maintained by RuAPI. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and RUAPI_API_KEY go to https://www.ruapi.ai (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and RuAPI forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Hermes' standard GET https://www.ruapi.ai/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

entries.name: runa
entries.title: Runa
entries.description: Bring your Runa meetings into Hermes: prep for what's next, recap decisions and who owes what, draft the follow-up, and find the exact words behind a claim, through Runa's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with four workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Runa's MCP server at mcp.joinruna.com, signed in as the user through Runa's sign-in (Google or Microsoft), and a first sign-in creates a Runa account. Meeting titles, summaries, transcripts, action items, people and company notes, and reads from apps the user connected to Runa are pulled into the session context, and so reach the user's model provider. No tool changes data in Runa or in those apps; Runa logs each call's metadata. The tool list comes from Runa's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add runa --url https://mcp.joinruna.com/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: runbox
entries.title: runbox
entries.description: Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In Hermes Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without Hermes' dangerous-command approval like Hermes' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: runcrate-provider
entries.title: Runcrate
entries.description: Runcrate (runcrate.ai) open models via the OpenAI-compatible API at api.runcrate.ai/v1: live model list from /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default, and Hermes reasoning settings sent as reasoning_effort. Disclosure: model provider; prompts, tool schemas and RUNCRATE_API_KEY go to api.runcrate.ai, and free requests can be served by third-party model providers under their own terms (runcrate.ai/privacy).

entries.name: s2docs
entries.title: s2docs
entries.description: Source 2 documentation and mod tooling for CS2 and Deadlock from a local index of Valve's own game data: convars, Hammer entities with their inputs and outputs, schema classes and enums, game events, the cs_script and Pulse APIs and Source2Wiki pages, plus the mod pipeline — scaffold addons, validate scripts and .cfg files, start map builds on a registered Windows host over SSH, deploy and verify hashes, and record evidence, test runs and job state. Needs uv and an index built with s2docs sync; every write-capable call asks for approval. Disclosure — runs its MCP server with uvx from the pinned git commit, resolving its PyPI dependencies on first start as of a fixed 2026-10-10 snapshot; nothing is sent to a third party, but SSH/scp go to any host registered through register_host, build_start runs agent-written shell commands on that host and its builds keep running after the session ends, deploy_push and job_attach copy local files the agent names, and it writes its own index and addon workspace; write tools ask for approval through the package's untrusted server trust.

entries.name: s3
entries.description: Generic S3-compatible backup and restore operations for Hermes

entries.name: sabi-metadata
entries.description: Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on Hermes 0.21.3.

entries.name: safeailabs-provider
entries.title: Safe AI Labs
entries.description: Safe AI Labs as a Hermes model provider (`--provider safeailabs`, or Safe AI Labs in `hermes model`): an OpenAI-compatible API with one endpoint per region, the model list from its /v1/models and the context window of its fallback model declared. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://us.api.safeailabs.ai/v1 (or SAFE_AI_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with SAFE_AI_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: salesforce-chatter
entries.title: Salesforce Chatter
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. Disclosure — authenticates as a dedicated bot user with the OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer flow, reading the private key file at SF_CHATTER_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH; talks to the configured Salesforce login host and the org instance (attachment downloads follow Salesforce redirects); image URLs in the agent's replies are fetched from the gateway host over HTTPS (any public host; private, loopback and metadata addresses are refused) and uploaded to Chatter; polls the To Me feed every 60 s and, for allowlisted groups, runs a SOQL probe every 5 s by default (counts against the org API quota); writes Likes, comments, files in the bot user's Files and optional home-channel posts; keeps its ledger in plugin-data/salesforce-chatter/inbox.sqlite. dry_run defaults to true (no Salesforce writes, no outbound image fetch); with SF_CHATTER_ALLOWED_USERS unset nobody is answered. Optional, off by default: html_preview renders model-generated HTML to PNG with Chromium in a network-isolated Docker container (digest-pinned image, pulled if missing). No telemetry.

entries.name: say-do-gate
entries.description: Checks agent claims against what actually ran this turn. Deterministic, zero tokens.

entries.name: scalekit
entries.title: Scalekit
entries.description: Call any Scalekit connector from Hermes: 500+ connectors and 20,000+ tools. Disclosure — HTTP calls go to the Scalekit environment URL you paste; the three Scalekit values are read with get_secret; one person id is stored at plugin-data/scalekit/identifier; the model can request an approval link, run a named tool, or proxy one HTTP request. Provider tokens stay in Scalekit; no shell, no background process, no telemetry.

entries.name: scaleway-provider
entries.description: Scaleway Generative APIs as a Hermes model provider (`--provider scaleway`, alias `scw`): European, OpenAI-compatible, pay-per-use, with a curated tool-calling model list led by deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (the default) that stands in when the live catalog probe fails, the cheapest vision-capable aux model, and real context windows and pricing through models.dev. The credential is SCW_SECRET_KEY, the same secret key the Scaleway CLI and SDKs use; because it is ambient, the provider is never auto-detected and turns on only when explicitly selected. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and SCW_SECRET_KEY go to api.scaleway.ai (or SCALEWAY_BASE_URL), plus a GET /v1/models catalog probe with the same key

entries.name: scamgate
entries.description: Offline scam gate. Blocks known-bad links and payments before a tool runs, and asks a human when it cannot see the destination. Disclosure — blocks agent tool calls that would edit Hermes config/profiles/plugins/hooks or Claude Code settings/hooks/plugins, turn approvals off, or disable a Claude Code plugin or its hooks, and asks before an agent installs or enables a plugin; with approvals off it turns its "ask" into a block (setting when_approvals_off: allow restores asks); keeps its signing key and ask log under ~/.local/state/scamgate and phishing feeds under ~/.cache/scamgate (not per-profile); downloads phishing feeds (openphish.com, Phishing-Database on GitHub, optional urlhaus) in the background every 6 hours while Hermes runs (auto_update_feeds: false turns this off) and on /scamgate update, hermes scamgate update-feeds or its no-argument scamgate_update_feeds tool; the downloads carry nothing about the links being checked; optional SCAMGATE_RDAP=live sends each checked link's domain to its RDAP registry.

entries.name: scar
entries.description: scar keeps the tool-call shape you denied on a Hermes approval card and stops that shape before it runs. scar does not call a model. hermes chat --cli stores only the choice id deny. The shape is the tool, the argument keys that held an rm command, and the danger tokens, including an rm inside a shell -c body and an rm after env flags, so rm -rf and rm -fr are one scar. Only a tool that has a scar is compared, and only under the argument keys that scar kept, so read_file, write_file, web_search, a sentence, and a touch of nine files are not stopped. A bare rm that dropped a token is not this scar. A path is not part of the match. The block line names the scar, the weekday, the numeric offset, and the words you pressed deny, and it tells the agent not to paraphrase the command and not to run it again. Disclosure — A deny is written only under this profile plugin-data/scar/ledger.json after secret-shaped text is removed by the plugin patterns and then by the Hermes redactor. A secret shape that neither knows can stay in the preview. The ledger is read on every foreign tool call, up to 800KB and 200 scars. An unreadable file stops only a terminal command that carries an rm danger token, and it is left in place. On a tool that has a scar, a kept value over 200,000 characters, a shell nested past 8 levels, or more than 8 wrapper words is not compared and is not run. The block applies on every surface, including yolo, cron, the gateway, and approvals off, once a scar exists. A scar stays until scar_forget removes it or the plugin is disabled. scar_forget asks on the Hermes approval card when it fits in 7 lines of 63 columns. A longer question is not sent, and the scar stays. Each forget asks again. Its rule key changes on every call, so always does not cover the next forget. Yolo and approvals off skip that card when it fits, so that scar can be forgotten with no second prompt. Cron, a single query, a webhook, msgraph_webhook, api_server, and a plugin host do not forget a scar: the hook blocks scar_forget before Hermes's gate, including after always and including when yolo is on. Hermes checks a permanent allowlist before its own cron deny. Those sessions do not store a new scar. scar_list returns each scar, including the redacted preview, on any platform that can call the tool. hermes tools disable scar --platform <platform> hides the tools on that platform and does not stop the block. Disable the plugin to stop the block. A running gateway keeps the hook until it restarts. The plugin registers scar:keep-a-scar. A skills-tool session adds one system prompt skills index line. -t terminal,scar adds none. Nothing is sent off the computer. Yolo and approvals off skip the Hermes prompt, and this plugin does not add a second prompt. Setting isolation to host blocks new scars. This plugin creates no cron job. The install scan is safe, with 15 medium findings, all in the test tree.

entries.name: scribase
entries.description: Provision a hosted Postgres backend project on Scribase (api.scribase.com) and get back its connection string and API keys. Disclosure — calling scribase_create_project creates billable Scribase resources (a project and a Postgres environment) in the user's organization without a confirmation prompt, and returns the new environment's Postgres connection URI and anon/service-role/secret API keys into the conversation, where they reach the configured model provider and the session history; network only to api.scribase.com or the user-configured api_base_url, authenticated with SCRIBASE_API_KEY.

entries.name: search-sources
entries.title: Search Sources
entries.description: Shows the pages a turn searched or fetched as a 'Searched N pages' capsule under the reply and a Sources side panel in Hermes Desktop; cited pages first. Reads web search / fetch tools of Hermes, the plugin catalog and common MCP servers, JSON or Markdown output. Disclosure — stores page URLs/titles/summaries under plugin-data/search-sources; appends one ::search-sources paragraph to Desktop replies; the Desktop half looks up site icons via Google and DuckDuckGo icon services and the site's /favicon.ico unless set to Off; no telemetry.

entries.name: search1api
entries.description: Live web search, news, Ask, page crawl, sitemap, and trending via Search1API

entries.name: secret-drop
entries.description: Store a secret on the gateway host without showing it to the model. Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_hermes_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).

entries.name: secret-handoff
entries.description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the reply is typed into the focused field of the page whose origin matches the requested service, over the endpoint from BROWSER_CDP_URL or SECRET_HANDOFF_CDP_URL; the answer is visible in the CLI scrollback or the chat history of the surface that asked, and the value is never written to disk, the tool result, or the session transcript.

entries.name: secure-env-ingress
entries.description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, retained exact-parent login/password and saved TOTP filling, protected payment-field filling, nested verification codes/passcodes and guarded indexed code groups, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. Interactive Telegram secret entry uses secure_env_vault; secure_login_fill consumes existing native Vault handles without registering a login backend. Browser writes require an explicitly selected existing parent and the public captured-CDP dispatch API, retain the original transport and exact document/control guards, and fail closed on reconnect, profile or human-control lease changes; tab creation ownership is not required. No native fill fallback or explicit site-form submission occurs. Payment filling requires separate native consent; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Card storage includes encrypted CVC. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer. Setup bootstrap reads the profile .env directly to obtain TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS owner IDs.

entries.name: sem-weave
entries.description: CLI-backed skills for local code discovery and entity-diff review with Sem, plus optional Weave branch-merge previews. Requires user-installed CLIs; does not apply edits or merges, install binaries, or change Git configuration.

entries.name: sendblue
entries.description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

entries.name: senler-io-user
entries.title: Senler.io
entries.description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — Hermes installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Hermes) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass Hermes allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Hermes approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<HERMES_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native Hermes messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.

entries.name: serpapi
entries.title: SerpApi
entries.description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for Hermes Agent.

entries.name: session-dashboard
entries.description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the Hermes desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

entries.name: session-find
entries.description: A search window over your Hermes session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. Finds a session by an exact word, identifier or phrase through the gateway's own full text index, and by meaning as well when a session-find service answers on loopback; typed filters (in:, -in:, after:, before:, me:, repo: and quoted phrases) are mirrored as chips under the box. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. The window half ships off by default and is switched on in the app's plugin inventory. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your Hermes session database read-only.

entries.name: session-flow
entries.description: Session pane for Hermes Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local Hermes gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.close, session.delete); captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.

entries.name: session-lens
entries.title: Hermes Session Lens
entries.description: Read-only observability for Hermes Desktop: what each session cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron/gateway state, config.yaml and .env (key names, and the values of keys an adapter uses); with the credentials Hermes' own resolvers return, calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README), sending Grok CLI client headers to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and a Claude Code user-agent to api.anthropic.com; Hermes' resolvers may renew Hermes' Codex, Nous and xAI logins and, when Hermes holds no other Anthropic credential, Claude Code's login; runs the local monid CLI when installed; an Anthropic one-token Claude Haiku probe is off by default; writes no Hermes state itself and sends no session content anywhere.

entries.name: session-mirror
entries.description: Mirrors Hermes Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Hermes's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $HERMES_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `hermes session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

entries.name: session-ref
entries.description: Reference another Hermes session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

entries.name: session-relay
entries.title: Session Relay
entries.description: Hands a long-running conversation over to a fresh session before the context window fills up: a ⚡ chip in the status bar shows live context usage, and at the threshold (45% by default) the agent writes a hand-off note while the plugin opens a new chat, seeded with that note as its first message and named after the current one (+1). On Telegram and other messaging platforms the gateway half provides a session_relay_handoff tool; after /new it attaches that chat's note to the first message of the new session, so the fresh session opens with the hand-off. Disclosure: each relay runs one extra agent turn and therefore uses model tokens.

entries.name: session-token-counter
entries.description: Accumulated input/output token totals and context-window occupancy for the focused session, in the Hermes Desktop status bar.

entries.name: severian
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory for Hermes agents: a canonical append-only store (SQLite or PostgreSQL+pgvector) with five-dimensional tenant/profile/collection/agent/session scope, hybrid BM25+vector retrieval with a re-ranker, memories that cite the observations they came from, per-turn user facts, real dates next to relative times, truth resolution when a newer fact replaces an older one, and a conflict note when two returned memories disagree. Fully offline by default; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B semantic embeddings opt-in, locally or in a user-owned sidecar. On OmniMemEval's public long-term-memory leaderboard (its own models, prompts and full public sets) it scores 90.6 LongMemEval (1st), 87.3 LoCoMo (2nd) and 71.6 BEAM 100K (2nd, within noise of the lead); it re-ran LCM-X to check the board's records, and per-question results, a strict second marker and scripts are published in the repo. Disclosure — stores every conversation turn in one SQLite database under the Hermes root (`<hermes root>/severian`) shared by all profiles with rows scoped per profile, or in the PostgreSQL database named by `SEVERIAN_DSN`; the opt-in Qwen/Granite embeddings download a model from Hugging Face on first use, and the opt-in embedding sidecar sends memory text to the URL you configure.

entries.name: sgme
entries.description: SGME (拾光记忆) self-hosted long-term memory engine — tagged memories with provenance, per-turn recall, automatic session refinement, a skills library, wiki knowledge base, care signals, communication roles and a three-pool task system (ideas/demands/projects), all behind one HTTP service you own. The plugin is a thin bridge: no LLM, no database, everything heavy runs in your SGME server (local or remote). Disclosure — the plugin talks only to the SGME server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:9910, SGME_BASE_URL for a remote server), sending SGME_AGENT_KEY / SGME_ADMIN_KEY read through Hermes's secret scope; each session's user, assistant and tool messages are appended to that server and refined into memories at session end by an LLM you configure on the SGME side; its sgme_* tools let the model read and change memories, skills, wiki pages and tasks on that server and write skill packages under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/sgme/skills/ on the SGME host; credential names in the SGME vault can be listed, and reading a credential value into the conversation is off by default (credential_get_enabled / SGME_ENABLE_CREDENTIAL_GET); no third-party services, no telemetry.

entries.name: shipframe
entries.title: ShipFrame
entries.description: AI coding workflows for teams that plan, prove, and ship — 44 read-only skills covering project context refresh, feature discovery, planning, implementation, TDD, two-phase code review, release evidence, PR/MR creation, project wiki knowledge, and accessibility/security auditing. Native plugin: a plugin.yaml manifest plus a dependency-free Python entrypoint that registers every skill through ctx.register_skill (no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars). Disclosure — the skills themselves instruct the agent to run shell commands (git, gh, project test suites, occasional installer commands) as part of the workflows they describe, and some skills write project context files such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the user's repositories; the plugin code makes no network calls, spawns no processes, reads no credentials or files outside its own tree, ships no telemetry, and contains no self-updater (updates arrive only through sha-bump PRs in this catalog).

entries.name: shodan
entries.description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

entries.name: showly
entries.title: Showly
entries.description: Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from Hermes Agent, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to hermes` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

entries.name: sidebar-cycle
entries.description: Step through Hermes Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

entries.name: sidebar-manager
entries.description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

entries.name: signal-notify
entries.description: Signal texts when a Hermes turn pauses, fails or is interrupted, and when Hermes waits on a clarify question, approval or sudo prompt. Sends through the user's own signal-cli HTTP daemon (the same SIGNAL_* settings as the core Signal gateway); skips Signal-origin, cron and subagent turns, and dedupes identical texts within 60s. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled turns POST to SIGNAL_HTTP_URL (plain HTTP unless that URL is https), which signal-cli delivers as a Signal message; by default each text includes up to 300 characters of the final reply (not secret-redacted) or of the redacted question/command (include_text: false or reply_chars: 0 sends none); each event has its own on/off setting; sudo passwords and clarify answers are never seen; nothing is stored on disk, at most 64 clipped reply previews are kept in memory, and each send runs on a short-lived daemon thread with a 20s timeout.

entries.name: sigrex
entries.description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skills instruct the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data; connecting an exchange or prediction-market account gives Sigrex that account's API key or wallet private key, which the skills tell the agent to leave to the user in the Sigrex dashboard.

entries.name: simular-sai
entries.title: Sai by Simular
entries.description: Give Hermes a computer: hand tasks that need a screen (web apps behind a login, admin consoles, desktop software, forms with no import) to Sai, Simular's computer-use agent, which does them on a cloud computer Simular hosts and reports back in text. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only; the MCP server runs as npx @simular-ai/sai-mcp@0.4.0 over stdio, so Node.js 22.12+ and npm are required. Needs a Sai API key (from platform.simular.ai), set in Settings > Plugins or as SAI_API_KEY in the profile .env. Disclosure — Runs the npm package @simular-ai/sai-mcp@0.4.0 through npx; every task, its results and the SAI_API_KEY go to api.simular.ai and spend the account's Sai credit or free computer time; the agent can upload any local file it chooses (up to 25 MB) to Simular with sai_upload, run code on the Simular cloud computer (sai_control_exec), and approve Sai's own permission requests, without a Hermes prompt; a local task view is served on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run token, and sai_live_link returns a link that lets whoever holds it control the cloud computer until it expires.

entries.name: singularity
entries.description: Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend: Hermes's terminal, file and code tools run inside a hardened, rootless container on this machine (--containall --no-home), with CPU/memory limits and an optional per-session persistent overlay (`hermes config set terminal.backend singularity`; image from `terminal.singularity_image`). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it drives the `apptainer` (or `singularity`) CLI you install, which pulls the configured image (default `docker://nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`) and caches a SIF under your scratch directory. Your skills and registered credential files are bind-mounted read-only into the container, and because the container is a disposable sandbox Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as for its other container backends.

entries.name: sketch-pad
entries.description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next Hermes chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

entries.name: skill-integrity
entries.description: Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre_llm_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot | check | show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get_hermes_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.

entries.name: skill-lineage
entries.title: Skill Lineage
entries.description: Records where each skill version's content came from, so a skill that rewrites itself can be audited afterwards. For every skill write — a foreground skill_manage call, a background-review edit, or a curator consolidation — it stores the skill content fingerprint before and after, the sources present earlier in the same session (the text the user typed, tool results such as a fetched page or a file, and skills that were read), how each source is linked to the added lines — strong (at least three shared 8-word shingles), anchor (a shared operative token: a URL or host, a shell command with its first argument, a package install, a file path, an environment variable, an IP or e-mail address, that is not common across sources), or context (seen in the session, nothing measurable shared; recorded, not followed by default) — and a seq -> prev_hash -> hash chain over the entries. Text is never stored: hashes are keyed per install and the key stays in plugin-data/skill-lineage. `hermes skill-lineage trace <skill>` shows where the newest version came from, `descendants <url|skill>` lists every skill a source produced, `report` lists versions carrying operative lines of no traceable origin, `verify` re-walks the chain, and `head` prints a value to record elsewhere so a later `verify --head` can tell truncation from an intact chain; a key reset is recorded in the chain and shown in `status` rather than happening silently. The plugin does not stop a write and does not judge a skill: it records and it verifies, and it does not claim a source caused an edit. Prior work on memory lineage (MemLineage, arXiv:2605.14421) is acknowledged in the README. Measured on 2026-10-22 against Hermes 3166d61: Python 3.14 62 passed; Python 3.11 54 passed, 1 skipped; `hermes plugins validate` reports no warning other than one known false positive (a test template that quotes a "curl | sh" instruction as data and never runs it). Evaluation (generated scenarios and 120 real-model runs) in the README; raw output in eval/. A manual end-to-end run in an isolated HERMES_HOME (one real session creating a skill through skill_manage, then status/trace/descendants/report/verify/head) passed, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-10-21.txt. Disclosure — four read-only hooks (on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call); reads tool results, user messages and skill files (in this profile, every other profile's skills folder, the project's .hermes/skills and the skills.external_dirs it reads from config.yaml) to compute keyed hashes; keeps hashes (no text) for 7 days per session and the lineage chain (hashes and skill names) under plugin-data/skill-lineage; no network, no credentials, never blocks or changes a tool call.

entries.name: skill-retrieval
entries.description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $HERMES_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

entries.name: skill-router
entries.description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

entries.name: smolmachines
entries.title: smol machines
entries.description: smol machines' own plugin: runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools in a smol machine, a microVM with its own Linux kernel on this computer (macOS on Apple Silicon, or Linux with KVM), as a terminal backend (`hermes config set terminal.backend smolmachines`). It needs no Docker and no account. Disclosure: installs the `smolmachines` Python SDK (>=1.27.2,<2), which carries the VM engine. Everything runs on this computer: the plugin always asks the SDK for a local machine, so nothing is sent to smol machines' cloud, even with SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN set or the smol CLI signed in (Hermes strips SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN from the commands it runs). Creating a machine pulls its image (default `python:3.12-slim`, from Docker Hub), and the engine pulls with this computer's Docker registry login when one is configured (`~/.docker/config.json`, including a credential helper such as the macOS keychain), read-only and sent only to the registry being pulled from. A machine has outbound network access and mounts nothing from this computer. With `terminal.container_persistent` (the Hermes default) each Hermes home and session keeps one machine, which keeps running after Hermes exits until stopped or deleted with the smolvm CLI, otherwise the machine is deleted when the session ends. Because the machine is a disposable sandbox, Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends.

entries.name: snag-shelf
entries.description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

entries.name: snyk
entries.description: Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

entries.name: soul-finder
entries.title: Soul Finder
entries.description: Build or refine your agent's SOUL.md — the personality file loaded into every conversation. NEW flow interviews you over a few plain questions and drafts a soul from scratch; REFINE audits an existing one against the gold-standard structure, asks only the gap questions, and ships a diff. Adds a /soul command, the soul_finder_status and soul_finder_complete tools, a once-per-profile first-run offer, and a bundled workflow skill. Disclosure — reads $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md and writes it only through the agent's own file tools after the user approves the draft (its bundled skill can also suggest copying the approved file into other profiles' SOUL.md, again only on approval); on a profile with no real SOUL.md it makes a one-time offer through a system-prompt section and an injected first-run message, and writes two booleans (nudge_sent, flow_complete) to its own plugin-data state file so the offer happens once and never repeats. It performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

entries.name: source-tray
entries.description: Session source tray — URLs the Hermes agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

entries.name: specstream
entries.title: SpecStream
entries.description: SpecStream gives Hermes finished lists from the live web: describe the list in plain words and get every matching row with the page it was read from, priced per match with a maximum you approve before anything runs. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and four skills (compile, review-work, approve-work, continue-work); no Python, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure — your request text and your answers to the price are sent to api.specstream.ai; approving a price spends your SpecStream balance (new accounts get $10 free) and the plugin marks its server `untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `specstream` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

entries.name: spectator
entries.description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

entries.name: speechify
entries.title: Speechify
entries.description: The official Speechify text-to-speech provider (tts.provider: speechify), maintained by Speechify. Simba 3.5 voices in 48 languages with low-latency streaming in voice mode, Opus voice notes for messaging platforms, and a hermes speechify command to list voices and hear a test line. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice and model, the plugin's name and version (Speechify-Caller attribution headers), and your SPEECHIFY_API_KEY to api.speechify.ai (or the base_url / SPEECHIFY_BASE_URL you configure); synthesis is billed to your Speechify workspace; generated audio is written to Hermes's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry.

entries.name: spotify-desktop
entries.description: Spotify Connect remote for Hermes Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the Hermes Spotify login (Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

entries.name: spotify
entries.description: Spotify for Hermes: seven tools (playback, devices, queue, search, playlists, albums, library) over the Spotify Web API, plus `hermes spotify login|status|logout` (loopback PKCE with your own Spotify developer app; Premium needed for playback control). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically.

entries.name: squad-hub
entries.title: Hermes Agent Squads Hub
entries.description: One Desktop list for Hermes Agent Squads: bot, project, folder, worktree and chat, several bots open at once without a profile switch; the squad's cron jobs; a bell for what waits on you; live Kanban cards in chat; squad managers ask with clarify buttons; the empty chat names the squad and project. Disclosure — reads and manages other profiles' chats (list, start, rename, archive), projects and cron jobs (pause, resume, remove) through Hermes RPC on running backends, and reads Kanban boards through its own read-only dashboard route built on Hermes' internal kanban_db module; adds a system-prompt section telling agents to ask with clarify buttons and appends Kanban card lines to Desktop replies; writes its own desktop_cards setting on manager profiles and applies its Squads theme on every bot by default (switchable in its settings); git worktree create/remove is only copied as a command unless the separate repo-only squad-hub-plus companion handles it; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, never reads .env or credentials.

entries.name: stablelens
entries.title: StableLens
entries.description: Read-only tools for Arc Network, the stablecoin-native L1 where USDC is the gas token: native USDC and Circle token balances (USDC, EURC, USYC, cirBTC, WETH, plus any ERC-20) read at one block, transaction status with the USDC fee and decoded ERC-20 transfers, the current cost of a transfer, and token, address and block lookups, on mainnet (chain 5042) and testnet (5042002). Standard library only; never signs, sends or holds keys. Disclosure — each tool call sends JSON-RPC requests carrying the addresses, transaction hashes, token addresses and block numbers asked about to Arc's public RPC endpoints (rpc.mainnet.arc.io / rpc.testnet.arc.io and the Blockdaemon, dRPC and QuickNode endpoints Arc publishes), or first to a private endpoint the user stores as a Hermes secret (STABLELENS_MAINNET_RPC_URL / STABLELENS_TESTNET_RPC_URL, read through the secret scope); registration makes no network calls, and there are no other network calls, file writes, shell commands or background processes.

entries.name: stack
entries.description: Git-backed Markdown memory with background curation and model-based recall. Disclosure — runs a background curation agent with terminal, file-read and patch tools on your configured auxiliary model, fed raw conversation turns; it commits and pushes the memory store to whatever git remotes you configure, and pulls shared submodules at session start; the engine runs via uv run, which fetches pyyaml==6.0.2 from PyPI; an optional dataset file (memory.stack.dataset_enabled, off by default) stores full transcripts locally with no rotation.

entries.name: stacktree
entries.description: Publish what Hermes builds (reports, dashboards, briefs, proposals) to a private link that opens in any browser with no account for the viewer, set a passcode or limit it to a company's email addresses, update it in place, and see who opened it and what they commented. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Stacktree's remote MCP server at api.stacktr.ee (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, token kept by Hermes); the HTML the model passes to publish_html or update_site is stored in the user's Stacktree account and served at the returned link (unlisted by default, public when a public_slug is set); page titles, open counts and third-party reader comments from that account are read into the session; the remote tools that publish, update, gate, delete pages or email approval requests run without a Hermes approval prompt; the required sign-in step `hermes mcp add stacktree --url https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp --auth oauth` writes a config.yaml server entry that replaces the package's own.

entries.name: stalkchain
entries.title: StalkChain
entries.description: Crypto research in plain English through the official StalkChain Data MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://data.stalkchain.com/mcp/directory, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check a coin before you buy, vet a trader before you copy them, see what smart money is buying, review a wallet and set price alerts, across Solana, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Monad, Hyperliquid and Robinhood Chain, plus the StonkFun launchpad. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + 18 skills), no Python or executables; needs a StalkChain account with credits. Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything; the only write is the user's own price alerts, after they confirm. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; each tool call sends the tool name and its inputs to data.stalkchain.com and spends the account's credits; price alerts are stored by StalkChain with their destination (account email or a user-given Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook URL, which can embed a bot token) until deleted or fired.

entries.name: statejar
entries.title: StateJar
entries.description: Verifiable memory for Hermes Agent (memory.provider statejar): typed facts with one value per field, append-only content-addressed versions, recall of only what a message needs with the handle of the state it came from, and an audit trail of every disclosure. Disclosure — the user's current message (first 2,000 characters) is sent to api.statejar.com as a recall query on every turn, and the user's own messages (three words or more), every entry Hermes's built-in memory tool saves, and the text or query the agent passes to the statejar_* tools are sent there with STATEJAR_API_KEY; assistant replies and tool output are not captured, and API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords and card numbers are removed locally first (best effort). StateJar's server sends each captured message to a cloud model provider it uses for extraction (today Google Gemini and OpenRouter). A capture queue is kept under the Hermes home (created mode 600; a queue rewritten after a failed send uses default permissions). Only the primary agent writes; cron and subagent runs only recall.

entries.name: sticky-notes
entries.description: In-window sticky notes for Hermes Desktop.

entries.name: stop-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the turns you stopped while Hermes was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, Hermes's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network

entries.name: storm-fusion-research
entries.description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through Hermes's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

entries.name: stream-speed
entries.description: How fast each model starts answering and how fast it writes: /speed shows the median and p90 time to first text and the median characters per second per model, provider or day, or lists the newest streams (ten, or up to 100 with /speed recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded, from the streaming hooks. Disclosure — writes per-response stream timings (ids, model, timings, character count, no text) to plugin-data/stream-speed/streams.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; atexit waits up to 1 s; no network

entries.name: stt-vocab
entries.description: Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt Hermes sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters Hermes keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; Hermes uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.

entries.name: sugar
entries.description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.
