entries.name: sunshine-moonlight
entries.title: Sunshine / Moonlight
entries.description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run Hermes. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a Hermes approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

entries.name: super-artifacts
entries.title: Super Artifacts
entries.description: Publish pages, forms, trackers and proofs as live URLs that open on a phone, and read back what visitors submit, through the hosted Super Artifacts MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the super-artifacts workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to superartifacts.app/mcp; published artifacts and what visitors submit to them are stored on Super Artifacts' servers. Artifacts are private by default, and the skill tells the model to publish private and never widen who can open one unless the person asked; Hermes does not prompt before these tools run unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the server. No telemetry. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add super-artifacts --url https://superartifacts.app/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: superlocalmemory
entries.title: SuperLocalMemory
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory for Hermes, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into Hermes config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.

entries.name: supermemory
entries.description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

entries.name: surp-hermes-x402-llm
entries.description: Marketplace-aware LLM routing for Surp — live prices for all models, provider TPS and trusted flags, mid-chat seller switching, secret masking, and approval-gated paid chat. Disclosure — the messages passed to surp_chat and SURP_API_KEY go to the surp.ivc.lol gateway, run by the individual developer ivcained (operator page https://surp.ivc.lol/operator, terms https://surp.ivc.lol/terms; not affiliated with Surplus Intelligence), which forwards them to third-party sellers on the Surplus Intelligence marketplace, including sellers not flagged trusted unless trusted_only is set; paid surp_chat calls spend from the user's prepaid Surp balance (USDC on Base, 5 % gateway markup), each behind a per-model Hermes approval prompt (denied in cron and other unattended runs by default) plus a per-request ceiling (max_spend_usd, default $0.05); the price, provider, quote, combo and cache tools call the same gateway without a key; routing preferences are stored under HERMES_HOME/cache/surp-hermes-x402-llm/.

entries.name: surplus-intelligence-seller
entries.title: Surplus Intelligence seller
entries.description: Sell the full daily Venice DIEM allowance on Surplus Intelligence before 00:00 UTC. Seller-only and Venice-only: lists DIEM-funded Venice inference as Surplus offers, rebalances discount and caps through the epoch, and deepens price late in the day so leftover DIEM (which does not roll over) is avoided. Earnings settle in USDC on Base. Disclosure — Venice API key is sent to Surplus Intelligence (encrypted at rest) so Surplus can proxy buyer traffic; Surplus seller API and Venice billing/rate-limit endpoints are called to manage offers and read remaining DIEM; the tools create, reprice, pause and cancel offers without an approval prompt (price floor 0.10x), and if the Venice account also holds paid USD credit, buyer traffic past the DIEM can bill it unless the key's USD limit is 0; SIWE mint uses a throwaway wallet whose private key is discarded after signing, and the minted seller key is shown in the conversation.

entries.name: switch402
entries.description: switch402 web data tools: public page to markdown (full and lite), site map, page metadata, screenshots and web search, plus a free price and health quote. Disclosure — tool inputs (URLs and search queries) go to api.switch402.com, run by the switch402 team that maintains this plugin; the six paid tools spend USDC on Base ($0.001–$0.012 per call, charged only on success) from the wallet in SWITCH402_WALLET_KEY, which is used only locally to sign one x402 payment per call through Hermes' secret scope and is never sent or logged; every paid call needs a fresh human answer to the Hermes approval prompt (session/always answers do not carry over), stays under a per-request cap (max_spend_usd, default $0.02), and is refused in cron, yolo, approvals-off, smart-approval and other unattended runs; screenshots are saved under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/switch402/; no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: switchbot-control
entries.description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. The watch does not report Plug Mini on or off. A command can still turn a Plug Mini on or off. The published card sentence ("No Plug Mini on/off.") does not describe a command on this pin. Locks off unless enabled. When safety_devices is on, each lock or door command asks again. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. On this pin, yolo and approvals off skip the prompt only when a person can answer. A cron job, hermes -q, and a webhook cannot send a command, even after always. Each watch run costs 0 tokens. The unmanned run holds no tools. schedule writes a script under HERMES_HOME/scripts and creates the job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. A 0.1.x job stays a model turn until the next schedule. That turn allows switchbot_devices, switchbot_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool. The script drops every other profile .env key. If hermes cron fails, unschedule still removes the script and says the job was not removed. hermes cron create has no per-job tool list, which does not matter here because the unmanned run holds no tools. switchbot_command is a separate toolset. A cron turn hides it and refuses it, even after always. The published lines ("Every command asks for Hermes approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions."), (Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time.), and ("The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule.") are not this pin. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. When they are enabled, each of those commands asks again, so always does not cover the next one. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a command and approve it. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a toolset off per surface with hermes tools. On this pin, answering always in an interactive chat covers the same device id, command, and parameter, and it does not send from cron, hermes -q, or a webhook. The optional watch is a no-agent cron script (every 5 minutes by default, 0 tokens a run) that stays after uninstall. While the plugin is installed, remove that job with hermes switchbot-control unschedule. After uninstall that command is gone, so remove the job with hermes cron remove. Not tested on real devices. Saved files are under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/switchbot-control for the active profile. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

entries.name: t3-code-theme
entries.title: T3 Code Theme
entries.description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Hermes Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

entries.name: tabella
entries.description: Document lifecycle for agents in one package: create .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf/.odt/.ods/.odp from structured JSON or raw HTML/CSS, convert between formats via pandoc + LaTeX, and read any document — anydoc (Rust, office formats and text PDFs to Markdown, in-process) with LiteParse + Tesseract OCR fallback for scanned PDFs and images, plus PDF text editing with output-directory guards. Ships as an Agent Plugins v1 package (auto-discovered plugin.json + mcp.json declaring a stdio MCP server — the client spawns it per the v1 lifecycle, PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA injected — plus an optional self-host streamable-HTTP server; first run of either bootstraps the dependency venv). The HTTP lane binds to 127.0.0.1 only and requires Bearer auth out of the box: a random token is generated into PLUGIN_DATA on first run (TABELLA_TOKEN overrides); requests with an Origin header or a non-JSON body are rejected, and model-supplied HTML cannot fetch network or local-file resources (data: URIs only — the same fetcher now also guards CSS input, not just HTML). Pandoc invocations are argument-safe: extra_args is allowlisted (--toc, --number-sections, -V key=value) and from_format/to_format are validated against the built-in format-name grammar (^[a-z0-9_]+([+-][a-z0-9_]+)*$), closing pandoc's *.lua reader/writer code-exec path; both servers re-exec into the dependency venv after bootstrap. Disclosure — Python deps (python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, weasyprint, odfpy, Pillow, lxml, PyMuPDF, firecrawl-anydoc, liteparse — 10 direct packages, transitives included in a 25-package closure) are pinned to exact versions with sha256 hashes in requirements-pinned.txt and installed with --require-hashes into a venv under PLUGIN_DATA or ~/.venvs/docs (scripts/setup.sh on Linux/macOS; on Windows the venv is built with the standard library's venv module — no bash or MSYS2 needed); system pandoc is required for conversion, a TeX engine (e.g. texlive-xetex) only when the output format is PDF (weasyprint for HTML->PDF); OCR needs the tesseract binary (UB-Mannheim build on Windows); all conversion, reading, OCR and PDF editing run locally with no network or telemetry; nothing is uploaded; read, convert, and PDF-edit tools access exactly the filesystem paths you pass; doc_create_document additionally containment-checks its output paths against the configured output directory (escape warns). Linux and Windows are CI-tested platforms (five-lane smoke battery on windows-latest: stdio lifecycle through a natively bootstrapped venv, create, read, pdf-from-html via the GTK runtime, pandoc convert).

entries.name: tailgate
entries.description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Hermes hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

entries.name: talaria-webui
entries.description: Extends Hermes Agent API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the Hermes API server (cross-session history search, rewind/compress of API sessions, branching any session into a new API session, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $HERMES_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.

entries.name: tallybuy
entries.title: Tallybuy
entries.description: Price comparison for Germany and Austria through Tallybuy's public MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://tallybuy.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): product search, shop offers with delivery cost and delivered total, price history and side-by-side comparison. Bundles the tallybuy-shopping skill: unknown prices stay unknown, every price carries its shop and time, no basket totals, and the person is sent only to the offer's own link. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — connects to the hosted Tallybuy MCP server at tallybuy.com (no key); search words, market and destination country go to it and it sees the caller's IP (used for rate limits); shop links it returns are affiliate links and Tallybuy may earn a commission; the six tools are served by the remote server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: tam
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: Hermes provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside HERMES_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; hermes memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

entries.name: tamahermes
entries.description: Grow a local TamaHermes pet from real Hermes agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $HERMES_HOME only; the optional python -m tamahermes CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

entries.name: tameru
entries.title: Tameru
entries.description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses Hermes's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Hermes's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default.

entries.name: taskwatch
entries.title: TaskWatch
entries.description: Background-task watchboard for the Hermes Desktop status bar and a side pane: every process the focused chat dispatched through terminal(background=true) (claude, opencode, codex, a build, anything) with live output tail, runtime, a silence heartbeat, a two-click stop, and OS notifications when a task goes quiet past a configurable threshold or exits (success/failure by exit code). Agent-agnostic by construction — it renders the gateway's own process.list projection for the focused session. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars or network. Everything is local.

entries.name: tavily-plugin
entries.title: Tavily
entries.description: Search, extract, map, crawl, and research through Tavily hosted MCP, with Tavily skills. The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports Hermes-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a Hermes-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.

entries.name: teamorouter
entries.title: TeamoRouter
entries.description: TeamoRouter as Hermes model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: hermes-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.

entries.name: telegram-client
entries.title: Telegram Client
entries.description: Telegram client pane for Hermes Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's Hermes secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in HERMES_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).

entries.name: telegram-notify
entries.description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Hermes agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/telegram-notify.

entries.name: telegram-stickers
entries.title: Telegram Stickers
entries.description: Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through Hermes' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Hermes answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Hermes. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Hermes' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Hermes like any tool. Uses Hermes functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.

entries.name: telegram_dashboard_probe
entries.title: Telegram Dashboard
entries.description: One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Hermes on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, whether the agent sees its rules and whether its memory writes stand unapproved, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Hermes' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Hermes' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through Hermes' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Hermes itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save Hermes' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of HERMES_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; with a memory provider configured, the last 256 KB of the same log are also read for the engine's warnings about that provider, of which only the time and whether one says unavailable are kept; every tick HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; every tick HERMES_HOME/state.db is opened read-only the same way for the newest saved system prompt of each platform the running gateway lists in HERMES_HOME/gateway_state.json, and the project context files the engine would load (.hermes.md or HERMES.md in that directory and each parent up to the git root, the AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / agents.md chain from the git root down, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc; up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .hermes.md, HERMES.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and HERMES_HOME, which may be outside HERMES_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick HERMES_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in HERMES_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of HERMES_HOME/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private hermes_cli.version_info._cached_version_info and the signature of agent.prompt_builder._read_text_with_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through Hermes' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write_approval and each platform's skip_context_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Hermes' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Hermes release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/.

entries.name: telesec
entries.title: Telesec
entries.description: Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat, with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export), correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend Hermes is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the Hermes model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; an optional message check on the same gateway and optional Cloudflare fact extraction are off by default); an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) into the Business chat for the contact to read; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; opt-in dossiers run a gateway background thread; modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; no telemetry.

entries.name: telnyx-provider
entries.description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

entries.name: terraform-drift
entries.description: Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every Hermes surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with hermes tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with hermes plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.name: thomas
entries.description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under HERMES_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

entries.name: thott-bot
entries.title: thott.bot
entries.description: thott.bot makes your AI an expert on World of Warcraft: Forever, from Blizzard's own game files for the build you're playing, current to the latest hotfix, with Blizzard's news and credited community data, drawn right in the chat. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to thott.bot's server (mcp.thott.bot), which records the queries your agent sends it (not your conversation, and not used to train models); its tool set is served remotely and is not covered by the pinned sha; it requires a free thott.bot account, signed in by running `hermes mcp add thott --url https://mcp.thott.bot/mcp --auth oauth`, whose config entry replaces the package's own server definition.

entries.name: tidal
entries.title: TIDAL
entries.description: TIDAL for Hermes Agent: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (hermes tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the Hermes machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the Hermes machine.

entries.name: time-gap
entries.description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

entries.name: timestamp-ref
entries.description: @ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

entries.name: tinyfish
entries.title: TinyFish
entries.description: TinyFish: the web, built into Hermes. Free Search and Fetch power Hermes's own web_search and web_extract, and when a site needs clicks, forms or a login, a remote browser and the tinyfish_agent web agent handle it, signed in through saved TinyFish profiles when needed. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Hermes's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `hermes tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Hermes .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking. Profile tools manage TinyFish Browser Context Profiles (saved website sign-ins) over the same API; you sign in to sites yourself at an agent.tinyfish.ai link and never give Hermes a password; the agent can create, rename and re-default profiles without asking, and deleting a profile goes through Hermes's approval prompt for each profile unless approvals are off (YOLO). Setup telemetry is off by default: only if you opt in (`hermes tinyfish setup --share-usage`, `tinyfish.telemetry: true`, or answering yes to setup's y/N question) does each setup run send one event to agent.tinyfish.ai with its outcome, where the key came from, the plugin version and OS, plus a one-way hash of the key (never the key). TINYFISH_NO_TELEMETRY=1 turns it off regardless.

entries.name: tirith
entries.title: tirith
entries.description: Check every terminal command with your installed tirith before it runs: lookalike and homograph URLs, pipe-to-shell, obfuscated execution, credential and .env exfiltration, malicious packages and terminal injection. tirith blocks and required policy approvals go to Hermes's approval prompt, critical findings are refused, warnings run with the warning added to the result; unattended runs follow approvals.*_mode. Disclosure — runs the user-installed tirith binary (0.5.0 or later; never downloaded, installed or updated by the plugin) on every terminal command and completed shell command sent to a background terminal, in the command's working directory, with the command on stdin; tirith logs each check locally and, unless offline is set, may refresh its signed threat database, query OSV.dev, deps.dev and ecosyste.ms, download the CISA KEV feed, and query Google Safe Browsing (only with your key); fails closed (asks, or refuses when unattended) if tirith is missing, older than 0.5.0, times out or gives no verdict.

entries.name: titanos-mcp
entries.description: Connect Hermes to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.

entries.name: together
entries.description: Together AI model-provider plugin — OpenAI-compatible API, 270+ serverless open-weight models, live catalog discovery.

entries.name: token-cost-meter
entries.description: Live token usage, model-aware USD cost and prompt-cache savings in the Hermes Desktop status bar, with a persistent per-day ledger that survives restarts. Disclosure — Desktop only; no network calls of its own (prices come from the gateway's model.options and a bundled models.dev rate table); stores per-day token totals, per-session counters and last-known rates in its own Desktop plugin storage; costs are list-price estimates, not billing data.

entries.name: token-dashboard
entries.title: Token Dashboard
entries.description: Token cost and usage dashboard for Hermes Desktop: a right pane with the focused session's live input and output tokens, session cost (backend-reported cost_usd when available, otherwise a labelled estimate from a built-in per-model price table), API calls and context usage bar, plus a recent-sessions overview with message counts and a status bar cost chip. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Disclosure: reads the focused session usage state and the session list through the Desktop host API and renders them locally; no network calls, no storage.

entries.name: token-lens
entries.description: Token consumption analytics for Hermes: records exact per-call usage from pre/post_api_request hooks, decomposes every request into categories (system prompt, built-in and per-MCP-server tool schemas, skills, memory, history, tool results, output, reasoning) calibrated to billed totals, and adds a Token Lens dashboard tab plus a Sessions-page card with deterministic and AI-evaluated token-reduction suggestions; `hermes token-lens refresh` runs a suggestion refresh from the CLI. Disclosure — records per-API-call token counts (no message text) from pre/post_api_request hooks into token_lens.db at the Hermes home root (per-call rows kept 90 days, rollups kept), and reads Hermes's state.db read-only for session token totals and, during the optional dashboard history import, message text for estimation only; after 10 recorded sessions it automatically calls your configured main model through Hermes's plugin LLM facade every 5 sessions (up to two calls per refresh, capped at 50,000 tokens by meta_budget_tokens), sending aggregated token statistics plus the names of your enabled MCP servers and plugins, and auto-applies the model's proposed category regex rules and rubric changes (logged to token_lens.EVOLUTION.md; evolve_rules: false turns this off); the dashboard's refresh button spawns a detached `hermes token-lens refresh` process that logs to logs/token-lens-refresh.log; its data paths follow the HERMES_HOME environment variable rather than the active profile, so in a multi-profile gateway every profile records into the launch profile's database; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.

entries.name: token-rate
entries.title: Token Rate Monitor
entries.description: Live output/input tokens-per-second chip in the Hermes Desktop status bar for a local llama.cpp server. Hermes itself reads the server's log ($HERMES_HOME/logs/llama-server.log, last 200 lines: `tg = X t/s` for output and `prompt eval time ... X tokens per second` for input) and serves it at /api/plugins/token-rate/; the chip polls that route once a second. The counter starts off — click the chip, or run the palette entry "Token Rate: start/stop the tok/s counter" (Ctrl/Cmd+K), to start it; the on/off flag is a file ($HERMES_HOME/cache/token-rate-state.json). It also registers the get_token_rate agent tool, so the model can read its own speed. Disclosure — it reads one local file (the llama.cpp log) and nothing else: no network calls, no external process, no extra port, no API key, no credentials, no telemetry. UI is English by default, Italian when the app locale is Italian.

entries.name: tokenjuice
entries.description: Compact successful terminal output locally before model consumption. Disclosure — runs the separately installed `tokenjuice` CLI (from PATH or `TOKENJUICE_BIN`; installed outside the pinned commit with `npm install --global tokenjuice`) on every successful foreground terminal command's output and replaces what the model sees with its shorter summary; the plugin sends nothing over the network.

entries.name: tokenwatch
entries.description: Monitor Hermes token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

entries.name: tokstat
entries.description: Live token usage in the Hermes Desktop status bar: cumulative total, a real-time this-turn counter, last-turn delta, context occupancy, and prompt-cache hit rate. Event-driven (no polling, no RPC); English and Chinese, follows the app locale.

entries.name: toll
entries.title: Toll
entries.description: Read-only safety checks before an agent buys a coin, signs a transaction or pays another agent, through Toll's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://t0ll.xyz/mcp, no key, no sign-in): who is behind a coin (snipers, bundles, linked wallets, the dev's funding and record), whether the LP can be pulled, whether the product a coin claims exists, ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK before signing a transaction, EIP-712 message or x402 payment, and an ERC-8004 agent's registration and x402 terms, on Robinhood Chain (4663) only; plus Robinhood Stock Token market data (debt securities, not shares), SEC fundamentals, insider trades, 13F institutional holders, earnings guidance, the Stock Token event feed and US macro figures. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to t0ll.xyz, which receives the tool's arguments (token contracts, wallet addresses, agent ids, tickers, the unsigned transaction passed to check_tx); every tool is annotated read-only and the server never signs, sends transactions or moves money; the package marks the server untrusted; no key is stored or sent (free daily quota of 10 new coins and 50 market calls, more with a Toll key the user sets in their own config); past the quota answers end with a paid x402 URL the plugin cannot pay; no telemetry (the quota is counted per caller with a daily-rotated keyed hash of the IP, deleted after 3 days). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: tool-call-salvage
entries.title: Tool Call Salvage
entries.description: Removes tool-call markup that a model wrote into its final reply as text instead of calling the tool (Qwen <function=...>, <invoke>, DeepSeek DSML and tool tokens, Harmony, Kimi, Mistral and Llama formats). Only complete markup that ends the reply is touched; code blocks and markup followed by more text are left as they are. An optional salvage mode, off by default and limited to the models you list, turns the markup into a real call to a tool offered in that request. Disclosure: no network, files, shell, subprocesses, telemetry or stored state; logs name the format and tools, never arguments; in salvage mode text the model wrote can become a real tool call (tools offered in the request, or Hermes's tool_call bridge when deferred_tools is on), run through Hermes's normal approvals.

entries.name: tool-slimmer
entries.description: Reduce Hermes tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Hermes core on older Hermes and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

entries.name: toolaria
entries.description: Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

entries.name: totem
entries.title: Totem
entries.description: Connect a Totem agent for peer discovery, durable messages, shared tasks, Missions, persistent memory, and activity. Agent Plugins v1 configuration-only package with six workflow skills and Streamable HTTP MCP. Disclosure — the agent's Totem tool calls (message text, attachments, memory, task and Mission records) go to Totem's hosted MCP server at https://totemlayer.com/mcp under your Totem agent identity, authenticated with TOTEM_NETWORK_API_KEY from Hermes's secret scope (or Totem OAuth); messages and files from other Totem agents enter the conversation as untrusted content; Hermes does not prompt before Totem write tools (send/reply, attachment upload, task and Mission delegation); remote tool behaviour is not covered by the pinned SHA; the package licence is proprietary.

entries.name: touchdesigner
entries.description: Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

entries.name: tracekit
entries.description: Tracekit's signer decides every tool call before it runs (deny blocks, ask waits for a person) and signs each call and its outcome into a run you can verify offline. Disclosure — every tool call's name and arguments, plus its result (in full for tools Tracekit's policy marks untrusted, otherwise a SHA-256 digest), go to a Tracekit signer: by default a same-user dev signer (`python -m tracekit signer serve --dev`) that the plugin starts on first use as a detached background process, which keeps running after Hermes exits until 15 minutes idle and stores signed runs plus each call's redacted arguments and results (encrypted, kept 7 days) under your user's data directory (~/.local/share/tracekit on Linux), or a remote signer when you set TRACEKIT_SIGNER to an https:// URL. The plugin fails closed: when tracekit-ai can't load or the signer refuses or can't be reached, tool calls are blocked (including every tool an execute_code script calls), and an `ask` decision holds the call until someone approves it in Tracekit or Hermes's hook timeout runs out.

entries.name: traceverse_hermes_otel
entries.title: Hermes OTel + Eval Metrics
entries.description: Hermes Agent OpenTelemetry traces and dashboard logs, with local-model cost estimates and optional in-process evaluation, GPU, energy, and CO2 metrics via genai-otel-instrument. Disclosure — Sends OpenTelemetry traces and log records for every turn, LLM call and tool call (session ids, models, token counts, costs, tool names, errors) to an OTLP endpoint, `http://localhost:4318` unless `HERMES_OTEL_ENDPOINT` points elsewhere; prompt, response and tool argument/result text is included only when `HERMES_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`; if `genai-otel-instrument` is installed it is activated in-process and instruments the LLM client libraries Hermes uses.

entries.name: transcription-dashscope
entries.description: Speech-to-text for Hermes via DashScope (Qwen) — voice messages and live dictation. Needs a Qwen AI Platform API key. Disclosure — voice messages and live dictation audio are uploaded to Alibaba's Qwen AI Platform (DashScope, maas.qianwenaiapi.com by default, or the base URL set in stt.dashscope.base_url / TRANSCRIPTION_DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL / DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL); the API key is TRANSCRIPTION_DASHSCOPE_API_KEY, falling back to the HERMES_CUSTOM_DASHSCOPE_API_KEY custom-provider key or the built-in Alibaba provider's DASHSCOPE_API_KEY; clips are converted with the local ffmpeg into a temporary wav that is deleted afterwards.

entries.name: tripwire
entries.description: Logs every refused agent action (a tool blocked by a guardrail or plugin, or a dangerous command denied, cancelled or timed out at approval) as one JSON line, so a no-agent cron script can send the owner one short alert. Observer only: it stores no tool arguments, results or message text, and fails open. Disclosure — appends one JSON line per refused action (profile, tool name, block type or approval choice, session id, and the first 120 characters of the block reason or approval rule) to ~/.hermes/tripwire/events.jsonl, shared by all profiles (path overridable with TRIPWIRE_EVENTS); a pre_tool_call hook reads ~/.hermes/tripwire/TEST_BLOCK and, only while that file exists, blocks the single tool it names for the single profile it names (a drill switch to prove the alarm). No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: true402-swap-guard
entries.title: true402 swap guard
entries.description: Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Free edition: it never pays, holds no wallet key and has no payment code. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Hermes approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: tsubasa
entries.description: Tsubasa OpenAI-compatible model provider (tool calling not supported yet). Disclosure — sends prompts and your TSUBASA_API_KEY to api.tsubasa.sh, operated by PalmAndWand; the API currently serves Canada only and answers HTTP 451 to requests from elsewhere.

entries.name: ttsbuddy
entries.title: TTS Buddy
entries.description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Hermes voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `hermes ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

entries.name: turn-bell
entries.description: A bell in the Hermes desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic Hermes already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic Hermes is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).

entries.name: turn-usage
entries.description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

entries.name: twenty-crm
entries.description: Twenty CRM for Hermes Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

entries.name: typesafe-skill-router
entries.description: TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

entries.name: umt
entries.description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

entries.name: unbrowse
entries.description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

entries.name: understudy
entries.title: Understudy
entries.description: Audition cheaper models on your real Hermes history before you switch. Understudy replays a sample of your past decisions (replies and tool calls) on candidate models through Hermes's own credentials, has a blind judge compare each step with what your current model actually did, and reports how often each candidate could have taken over (with a 95% confidence interval), its critical misses, a per-category breakdown and projected monthly cost. Two tools, /understudy, hermes understudy, and a Desktop page with an inline scorecard. Disclosure — reads this profile's session history read-only; sends redacted excerpts of past conversations (plus, by default, an excerpt of the agent's system prompt; `include_persona: false` stops it) to the candidate models and the judge model you pick, through ctx.llm on your existing provider credentials; each audition is capped by budget_usd only when Hermes reports the call cost (unpriced models are bounded by the sample size, not the budget); the agent tool spends without its own confirmation prompt (the bundled skill tells the model to dry-run and ask first; /understudy asks unless --yes); reads Hermes's local models.dev cache (active profile, then the default root) for list prices; writes run records and reports under plugin-data/understudy; runs a background worker thread only while an audition runs; requests the llm.model_override and llm.provider_override capabilities; no telemetry, no other network calls.

entries.name: undo-effects
entries.title: Undo Effects
entries.description: Puts back files an agent deleted or overwrote: before write_file, patch and destructive terminal commands (rm, mv, cp, redirects, tee, sed -i, find -delete) it saves the affected files to a local store and lets the tool run unchanged; /undo-effects lists the effects and restores them, refusing to overwrite later edits unless forced and keeping a safety copy so a restore can be undone. Disclosure — no network; reads the contents of the files and directories a covered tool call is about to change; writes unencrypted copies of them under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/undo-effects/ (files named like credentials, files above 50 MB, node_modules, .venv and .git are skipped and reported); runs no shell command and no background process; never blocks, rewrites or approves a tool call, and runs the tool even if a snapshot fails; covers the local terminal backend only; no telemetry.

entries.name: unibaseio-membase
entries.title: Membase
entries.description: Long-term memory for you and your AI from Membase (membase.com, by Unibase): one memory every connected AI shares. Searches the user's Membase memory before each turn (8 s, fail-open) and adds membase_search, membase_save and membase_profile. Disclosure — user prompts are sent as search queries to the Membase API (api.app.membase.com); with the opt-in capture_turns setting the user's messages are saved there too; on a Hermes build with memory.user_store: provider, what Hermes' memory tool records about the user is saved to their Membase profile instead of USER.md. MEMBASE_API_KEY comes from the Hermes secret scope; the only local file is $HERMES_HOME/unibaseio-membase.json. No background processes, shell commands or telemetry.

entries.name: unicode-ref
entries.description: @unicode: context references that spell text out character by character for the model: @unicode:"text" attaches a table of every character of the quoted text (code point, Unicode name, category) with notes on what does not show on screen: invisible characters and their positions, text-direction controls, spaces other than the ordinary one, Unicode tag characters (decoded), words that mix Latin letters with lookalike Cyrillic, Greek or fullwidth ones, and private-use or unassigned code points; @unicode:U+200B describes up to 20 code points (name, category, UTF-8 bytes, decomposition); the TUI and Desktop composer suggest characters by name. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's unicodedata; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @unicode: reference provider

entries.name: unitares
entries.description: Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

entries.name: unraid
entries.title: Unraid
entries.description: Read-only Unraid monitoring for Hermes Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through Hermes secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.

entries.name: upstash-box
entries.title: Upstash Box
entries.description: Terminal backend that runs Hermes terminal, execute_code and file tools in an Upstash Box cloud container, paused and resumed by name per task or created per session and deleted when it ends. Disclosure — requires an Upstash Box API key (UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY); every command and the files the file tools touch are sent to Upstash Box; your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files are uploaded to ~/.hermes in the Box and skill and cache files changed in the Box are copied back to your machine; SDK telemetry is turned off; Boxes are created, paused and deleted in the key's account and billed to it; persistent mode keeps one paused Box per task (each Hermes Desktop chat is its own task), and paused Boxes count toward the account's Box limit; if the Upstash account has GitHub connected, every Box holds those GitHub credentials in ~/.git-credentials, and every Box has an UPSTASH_BLOB_TOKEN environment variable, both readable by the commands the agent runs; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the Box.

entries.name: upstash
entries.title: Upstash Memory
entries.description: Long-term memory and searchable chat history for Hermes on Upstash Redis Search (BM25, no vector database or embeddings). Recalls related memories into each turn, saves every session as a searchable transcript, mirrors the built-in memory tool (adds, corrections and removals), and gives the model upstash_memory_save / upstash_memory_search / upstash_memory_forget and upstash_chat_search. Memories use the same keys as @upstash/agentkit-sdk, so they are shared with AgentKit apps on the same database. Works on the Upstash Free plan (one search index). Disclosure — memories and full chat transcripts are written to the Upstash Redis database you configure (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN) and sent to it over HTTPS on every turn; nothing else is contacted. Telemetry is opt-in and off by default: UPSTASH_HERMES_TELEMETRY=1 adds SDK, Python version and platform tags to request headers sent to that same database.

entries.name: usage-flame
entries.description: Pinned glowing chip + fire-themed panel with live subscription-quota windows (remaining %, reset countdown, burn-rate pace and run-out forecast with sparkline history) for every provider Hermes reports usage for. 12 color themes and fonts, RU/EN, zero dependencies, works on Windows. Disclosure — runs hermes usage --json through the Desktop gateway (cli.exec) every 1–15 minutes and sweeps up to 8 providers every 15 minutes; each run queries that provider's usage endpoint with the credential Hermes already holds. Reads the composer's selected provider from Desktop localStorage. No network calls of its own.

entries.name: usage-guard
entries.description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage Hermes already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent`, and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through Hermes's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated. Borrowing is off by default: when `hydrate_from_paths` names files, the guard may read those JSON snapshots instead of reading the endpoint, validating every window and never writing them into its own cache.

entries.name: usage-ledger
entries.description: Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows and macOS beta).

entries.name: usage-stats
entries.description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the Hermes Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Nous.

entries.name: uuid-ref
entries.description: @uuid: context references that decode a UUID or ULID for the model: @uuid:<id> takes a UUID in any common spelling (hyphens or not, braces, upper case, urn:uuid:) or a ULID, and attaches what its bits say, read the way RFC 9562 lays them out: version and variant in words, the creation time a v1, v6, v7 or ULID carries in UTC with how long ago, the clock sequence and node of a v1 or v6 and whether the node is random or looks like a network card (MAC) address, the local id and domain of a v2, a ULID's 128 bits written as a UUID, and the Nil, Max and RFC namespace UUIDs by name; up to 10 identifiers in one reference are compared by creation time; the TUI and Desktop composer preview an identifier as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's re, datetime and fractions; nothing is looked up; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the identifiers, but the @uuid: reference and the decoded text become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @uuid: reference provider.

entries.name: ux3-product-design-harness
entries.title: UX3 Product Design Harness
entries.description: MIT-licensed product judgment across User, Evidence and Business flows, with one portable Agent Plugins v1 skill and all 91 original skill files. Disclosure: skill instructions run bundled local Python/jsonschema validators and read/write user-controlled local briefs, context packs and review outputs, which can contain personal data. Optional evidence gathering uses explicitly user/host-authorized tools, including external search and connectors; selected claims, queries or evidence go to the chosen services under their policies. There is no publisher-operated receiving endpoint, retention service, telemetry or background process. The bundled jev_gate.py runs offline; connecting a remote decision service needs separate configuration and consent. No MCP server, native plugin entrypoint, registered tools, hooks or middleware.

entries.name: vault-view
entries.title: Vault View
entries.description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Hermes Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in.

entries.name: vaultknox
entries.description: Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

entries.name: vaultwarden
entries.description: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

entries.name: vector-platform
entries.description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Hermes becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `hermes gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `hermes gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

entries.name: vercel-agent-desktop-support
entries.description: Vercel Agent Desktop Support: operate Windows apps through the accessibility tree instead of the screen. Reads a window's real UI as roles, names, states and refs, then clicks, fills a field, selects an option, toggles a checkbox, scrolls, sends a key combo, and manages windows and the clipboard. Actions are semantic and headless by default, so they do not take focus, move the cursor or synthesize keystrokes, and they fail closed rather than guess. desktop_install downloads the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release for the running Windows target, verifies the archive against a sha256 pinned in the plugin, and proves the install by running version and status. Disclosure — the plugin runs the agent-desktop executable as a child process with arguments it builds, using the copy it installed or one already on PATH, in the npm global folder, AGENT_DESKTOP_BIN or the bin_path setting (those are not checksum-checked); starting or closing a program, installing the binary, and the first call that auto-installs a missing binary (auto_install, off by default) go through Hermes's approval prompt (Hermes Agent 0.18.1 or newer), while key presses, field values and clipboard writes into any window, a terminal included, run without a prompt; desktop_install is the only tool that uses the network, downloading the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release from GitHub, and a release without a digest pinned in the plugin is refused; it reads window titles, labels, field values and the clipboard on request, which can contain private content. Windows only.

entries.name: verifyum
entries.title: Verifyum
entries.description: Privacy-preserving file proofs on Solana Mainnet through Verifyum (no account, no key): the agent hashes a file on the user's machine, anchors only a domain-separated commitment, follows the proof until it is finalized, and verifies public proofs, with one skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: the package contains no code and declares two MCP servers. verifyum is Verifyum's hosted server at api.verifyum.com (Streamable HTTP). verifyum-local runs npx -y verifyum-mcp@0.1.1, which downloads that exact npm release (MIT, JavaScript source, published by aisenseapi) on first start and needs Node.js 20 or later. verifyum_anchor_commitment and verifyum_create_proof_from_file write a real, public and permanent Solana Mainnet transaction, so plugin.json marks both servers untrusted and Hermes asks first. The file tool reads only regular files inside the directories listed in VERIFYUM_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS, which the package does not set, so it refuses every path until the user sets it. It writes a private draft the user must keep. Verifyum receives only the commitment, the idempotency key and proof IDs, never the file, filename, raw hash, nonce or private manifest. Tool arguments, local paths included, still reach the user's model provider through the session. Verification also reads from a public Solana RPC endpoint. At most ten new anchors per IP address per rolling hour. The tool lists come from the servers at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover them.

entries.name: vet402
entries.description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. ALLOW, and a WARN that only says vet402 has not bought there yet, let it run. Any other WARN, a URL with no record for the paying HTTP method, and a vet402 outage ask for approval, and the call is refused when nobody can answer (yolo, approvals off, cron). vet402 only knows endpoints in public x402 and MPP discovery, so an unlisted URL asks. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside Hermes HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

entries.name: veyrul-media
entries.title: Veyrul Media Knowledge
entries.description: Saved media workflows, code and references for captions, editing, audio and production troubleshooting. One portable skill and five remote read tools. Disclosure: enabling the anonymous HTTPS MCP connection sends chosen queries or record IDs and request metadata to veyrul.com; keep private briefs and assets out of queries. No account, API key, executable, dependency installer, background worker, file upload, self-updater or separate analytics sender. Existing agent-provider usage and public-service rate limits apply.

entries.name: viajante
entries.description: Flight and hotel search from your own machine through a local MCP server and one skill that tells the agent how to read the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). No API keys and no account. Disclosure — mcp.json runs `npx -y @viajante/mcp@1.5.2`, which downloads the pinned npm shim and then `uvx` installs the same-version `viajante` package from PyPI on first start, so it needs Node.js, uv and Python 3.10+. Searches read Google Flights and Google Hotels public pages from your IP address (Booking.com and Skiplagged are opt-in). Optional local state (price-history log, cooldown file) is written under the viajante state directory. Nothing is booked and no credentials are stored.

entries.name: vidiq
entries.description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with hermes mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

entries.name: vk-platform
entries.description: VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.

entries.name: voice-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the voice messages and recordings Hermes transcribes (voice messages from messaging platforms, CLI voice mode): /voice-log shows how many recordings there were, how much audio in total and typically, and how long ago the last one was, per speech-to-text provider, model, source, language or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days or everything recorded; /voice-log recent lists the newest recordings (ten, or up to 100 with /voice-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes recording metadata (source, provider, model, language, file size read from the file system; no audio, file path, prompt or transcript) to plugin-data/voice-ledger/voice.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, always returns None so the transcription request is unchanged; no network

entries.name: voicestudio
entries.description: Client for the local VoiceStudio text-to-speech app (debpalash/VoiceStudio): speak short text, design or clone voices, browse voices, render chaptered long-form audio, dub videos, and check server status. Six tools with mirrored slash commands plus a bundled skill. Disclosure — sends the text, script files, videos and voice samples you point it at to the VoiceStudio server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP) and saves the returned audio under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/voicestudio; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: vornik-companion
entries.description: Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon.
